signals.title: fix(proxy): preserve timezone offsets when resetting multi-window budgets
signals.text: ## Summary `ResetBudgetJob.reset_budget_windows()` drops the timezone offset stored in `budget_limits[].reset_at`, then compares it with a naive UTC timestamp. This delays resets for non-UTC configured budget timezones. ## Current code In `litellm/proxy/common_utils/reset_budget_job.py`: ```python reset_at = datetime.fromisoformat(reset_at_str.replace("Z", "+00:00")).replace(tzinfo=None) if reset_at > now: return False # ... now = datetime.utcnow() ``` ## Reproduction Configure a non-UTC budget reset timezone, for example `Asia/Shanghai` / `Asia/Singapore` (UTC+8), and create a multi-window budget: ```json { "budget_duration": "24h", "max_budget": 100, "reset_at": "2026-08-20T00:00:00+08:00" } ``` At `2026-08-19 16:00:00 UTC`, the window is due, because this is exactly `2026-08-20 00:00:00+08:00`. The current code removes `+08:00`, yielding `2026-08-20 00:00:00` (naive), then compares it to `2026-08-19 16:00:00` (naive UTC). It considers the window unexpired and delays the reset until `2026-08-20 00:00:00 UTC` (08:00 local time). ## Impact This affects `budget_limits` / Budget Windows for Keys and Teams. A daily or monthly window configured for local midnight may continue enforcing the previous window for up to the timezone offset after its intended reset boundary. ## Expected behavior - Preserve the parsed offset for `reset_at`. - Use `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` for `now`. - Convert both values to aware UTC before comparing. - Define a compatibility policy for legacy offset-less values (for example, interpret them as UTC and log a warning). - Reset only the expired window; other windows (e.g. `30d`) must remain untouched. ## Suggested tests 1. `2026-08-20T00:00:00+08:00` does not reset at `2026-08-19 15:59 UTC`. 2. The same window resets immediately at `2026-08-19 16:00 UTC`. 3. A `Z` timestamp resets at the correct UTC boundary. 4. Legacy offset-less timestamps follow the documented compatibility behavior. 5. With `24h` and `30d` windows, expiring `24h` only clears its matching memory/Redis counter. The current test coverage constructs only `Z` timestamps and therefore does not cover this offset-preservation case.

signals.title: [Feature]: Publish Windows ARM64 wheels
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature Publish a native Windows ARM64 (`win_arm64`) wheel for each LiteLLM PyPI release alongside the existing `win_amd64` wheel The latest release provides native wheels for macOS ARM64, Linux ARM64, and Windows AMD64, but no Windows ARM64 artifact ### User Flow Before this feature (today): Windows on Arm users cannot install a released LiteLLM binary wheel with native ARM64 Python 1. The user runs `python -m pip install --only-binary=:all: litellm==1.97.0` 2. pip finds no compatible distribution because PyPI contains a `win_amd64` wheel but no `win_arm64` wheel 3. The workaround requires source builds and Rust plus C/C++ compiler toolchains After this feature (ideal user flow): the same command installs a native wheel without compiler toolchains 1. The user runs `python -m pip install --only-binary=:all: litellm==1.97.0` 2. pip downloads `litellm-1.97.0-cp310-abi3-win_arm64.whl` 3. `python -c "import litellm"` succeeds without Rust, Clang, or Visual Studio build tools Config / setup: ```text Windows 11 10.0.26200 ARM64 CPython 3.12.10 ARM64 pip 25.0.1 ``` Version: ```text litellm==1.97.0 from PyPI ``` Commands and output: ```powershell > python -c "import platform, sys; print(sys.version); print(platform.platform()); print(platform.machine())" 3.12.10 (tags/v3.12.10:0cc8128, Apr 8 2025, 12:31:18) [MSC v.1943 64 bit (ARM64)] Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0 ARM64 > (Invoke-RestMethod https://pypi.org/pypi/litellm/1.97.0/json).urls.filename | Where-Object { $_ -like '*win*' } litellm-1.97.0-cp310-abi3-win_amd64.whl > python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --only-binary=:all: litellm==1.97.0 ERROR: No matching distribution found for litellm==1.97.0 ``` What stopped me there: PyPI has no Windows ARM64 wheel, so native ARM64 Python cannot select a binary distribution ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? signals.title: [Feature]: Native NeuralTrust TrustGuard guardrail
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate Searched open and closed issues for `neuraltrust`, `trustguard`, and `neural trust`. No existing issue ### The Feature Add NeuralTrust TrustGuard as a named LiteLLM guardrail, configurable from Guardrail Garden and from `config.yaml`, so a proxy admin can enforce TrustGuard policy on chat completions without a generic HTTP workaround TrustGuard already exposes `POST /v1/evaluate` ([Evaluate API](https://docs.neuraltrust.ai/trustguard/api/evaluate)). The missing piece is a first-class LiteLLM option that sends input and output, then applies `block` / `transform` / `report` / `allow` ### User Flow Before this feature (today): a proxy admin cannot add NeuralTrust from Guardrail Garden, so they either skip TrustGuard or keep a generic HTTP workaround that does not map TrustGuard verdicts onto LiteLLM 1. They open `http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=guardrails` and switch to Guardrail Garden 2. They search NeuralTrust 3. No card is shown 4. Their workaround is a generic HTTP guardrail aimed at `POST https://trustguard.neuraltrust.ai/v1/evaluate` ([docs](https://docs.neuraltrust.ai/trustguard/api/evaluate)) 5. They send `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` with a policy-violating prompt 6. The completion returns 200 from the model. A TrustGuard `block` or `transform` is not applied as a LiteLLM verdict unless they maintain custom mapping outside LiteLLM After this feature (ideal user flow): the same admin adds NeuralTrust from Garden and TrustGuard enforces policy on the same chat call 1. They open `http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=guardrails` and switch to Guardrail Garden 2. They search NeuralTrust 3. The NeuralTrust card is on screen. They click Create Guardrail 4. They set Always On, modes `pre_call` and `post_call`, a TrustGuard `tgk_…` API key, optional `tgcol_…` collector key, and API base `https://trustguard.neuraltrust.ai` 5. They send `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` with the same prompts 6. A blocking collector returns HTTP 400 `Violated guardrail policy` with `trace_id` / `request_id` only. A DLP collector returns HTTP 200 with `[MASKED_EMAIL]` instead of the raw address ### How far you got Config / setup the proxy ran with: Revision: `origin/litellm_internal_staging` (`973329e986`). Stock LiteLLM, no NeuralTrust settings. Docs page checked: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/guardrails/quick_start Version or commit: `973329e986` Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends: ```bash python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, re text = subprocess.check_output( ["git", "show", "origin/litellm_internal_staging:litellm/types/guardrails.py"], text=True, ) m = re.search(r"class SupportedGuardrailIntegrations\(Enum\):(.*?)(?=\nclass )", text, re.S) values = re.findall(r'=\s*"([^"]+)"', m.group(1)) print("neuraltrust_in_enum", "neuraltrust" in values) print("hiddenlayer_in_enum", "hiddenlayer" in values) print("count", len(values)) PY ``` ``` neuraltrust_in_enum False hiddenlayer_in_enum True count 55 ``` ```bash git show 'origin/litellm_internal_staging:ui/litellm-dashboard/src/app/(dashboard)/guardrails/_components/guardrail_garden_data.ts' \ | rg -n -i 'neuraltrust|trustguard' || echo NO_GARDEN_HIT ``` ``` NO_GARDEN_HIT ``` What stopped me there: There is no NeuralTrust card in Guardrail Garden, and `guardrail: neuraltrust` is not a supported value on current `litellm_internal_staging`. After step 2 of the ideal flow, the create form cannot be opened TrustGuard itself already returns `allow` / `block` / `transform` on `POST https://trustguard.neuraltrust.ai/v1/evaluate` ([Evaluate API](https://docs.neuraltrust.ai/trustguard/api/evaluate)). The After flow is implemented in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/37165 and was run against that prod evaluate endpoint (live TrustGuard, mock model on the proxy) ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No

signals.title: [Bug]: /v1/messages → vertex_ai/gemini drops tool_result blocks with no text (tool_reference, empty list) → Vertex 400 function-response part count
signals.text: ### What happened Any Claude Code turn that calls `ToolSearch` (deferred tool loading) dies against a Gemini model routed through `/v1/messages`: ``` litellm.BadRequestError: Vertex_aiException BadRequestError - { "error": { "code": 400, "message": "Please ensure that the number of function response parts is equal to the number of function call parts of the function call turn.", "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT" } } . Received Model Group=claude-gemini-flash ``` Retries cannot help — the malformed turn is already in history, so every retry replays it and the session is stuck until the user clears it. The error message is misleading: the client's Anthropic request is well-formed. Every `tool_use` block has exactly one matching `tool_result` block. The mismatch is introduced by LiteLLM's own translation. ### Root cause `ToolSearch` returns a `tool_result` whose content is a list of `tool_reference` blocks, with no text anywhere: ```json { "type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "call_1", "content": [{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "Read"}] } ``` `translate_anthropic_messages_to_openai` only recognises `text` and `image` blocks inside a `tool_result` list. Anything else produces **no `role:"tool"` message at all**, so the `tool_call` it belongs to loses its result. Two places, both in `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/transformation.py`: - single-item list — the `if c.get("type") == "text" / elif ... == "image"` chain has no `else`, so nothing is appended - multi-item list / `[]` — `if combined_content_parts:` skips the append when nothing rendered Downstream is innocent: `convert_to_gemini_tool_call_result` has no empty-content skip, and `_gemini_convert_messages_with_history` appends 1:1 over whatever messages it is handed. It simply never receives the tool message. Vertex then sees N `functionCall` parts answered by N-1 `functionResponse` parts and rejects the whole `contents`. An empty *string* `content: ""` is handled correctly (`elif isinstance(content.get("content"), str)` matches and appends) — only the list form drops. ### Reproduction No credentials needed — the defect is in the adapter: ```python from litellm.llms.anthropic.experimental_pass_through.adapters.transformation import ( LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter, ) messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "search"}]}, {"role": "assistant", "content": [ {"type": "tool_use", "id": "call_1", "name": "ToolSearch", "input": {"q": "read"}}, {"type": "tool_use", "id": "call_2", "name": "get_weather", "input": {"city": "Paris"}}, ]}, {"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "call_1", "content": [{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "Read"}]}, {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "call_2", "content": "20C"}, ]}, ] out = LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter().translate_anthropic_messages_to_openai(messages=messages) print([m["tool_call_id"] for m in out if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("role") == "tool"]) # actual: ['call_2'] <- call_1 has no result # expected: ['call_1', 'call_2'] ``` End to end against a proxy with `model: vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash`, POST `/v1/messages` with that same body → 400 as above. ### Evidence Sent to a LiteLLM proxy `v1.98.0-rc.1` → `vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash`. Two `tool_use` blocks, two `tool_result` blocks, only the first result's shape varies: | `tool_result.content` of the first result | outcome | |---|---| | `"20C"` (plain string) | 200 | | `[{"type": "text", "text": "20C"}]` | 200 | | `[{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "Read"}]` | **400 function-response part count** | | `[]` | **400 function-response part count** | Replaying a real failing Claude Code request reproduces it, and rewriting *only* the `tool_reference` block of that body into text — leaving everything else byte-identical — makes the same request return 200. Same failure on `vertex_ai/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. A single-call turn hides the bug: with one `tool_use` and one dropped result, the response turn collapses entirely and Gemini never runs the pairing check. It only surfaces on parallel tool calls where at least one sibling result does render. ### Suggested fix Guarantee the invariant at the adapter: **every `tool_result` block emits exactly one tool message**, and unknown blocks degrade to text instead of disappearing. `tool_reference` renders as `[Loaded tool: <name>]`; other unrecognised types get a `[<type> block]` placeholder rather than a JSON dump, since they may carry base64 payloads. Their semantics do not need to survive — Claude Code re-injects the discovered tool schemas into `tools` itself, so the block is a history marker. What must survive is the item. PR follows. ### Relevant log output ``` File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/anthropic_endpoints/endpoints.py", line 97, in anthropic_response result: Final = await base_llm_response_processor.base_process_llm_request( File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/litellm_core_utils/exception_mapping_utils.py", line 1205, in _map_vertex_exception raise BadRequestError( litellm.BadRequestError: Vertex_aiException BadRequestError - {"error": {"code": 400, "message": "Please ensure that the number of function response parts is equal to the number of function call parts of the function call turn.", "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT"}} ``` ### Related - #36540 — same `tool_reference` blocks dropped on the `/v1/messages` → Responses API transform. Same class of defect, different downstream path; that report's "any unknown block inside a `tool_result` should degrade, not delete" applies verbatim here. - #22841 — `v1/messages` tool_result messages lost. ### Environment - LiteLLM proxy `v1.98.0-rc.1`; code paths above verified unchanged on `main` (`1.99.0`) - Route: `model: vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash`, `vertex_location: global`; also `vertex_ai/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` - Claude Code against the proxy with tool search active (deferred tool loading — needs `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=1` on non-first-party hosts) and enough MCP servers to trigger deferral - Non-streaming `/v1/messages`

signals.title: [Bug]: `cache_control_injection_points` incorrectly invokes Dotprompt prompt management and requires `prompt_id`
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Requests to `/v1/chat/completions` return HTTP 500 when a cloud model is configured with: ```yaml cache_control_injection_points: - role: system location: message ``` This has been observed with `gemini-3.6-flash`, `claude-opus-4.8`, and other cloud models configured in a local LiteLLM deployment. The same model and request work when `cache_control_injection_points` is removed. When this parameter is enabled, LiteLLM unexpectedly calls the Dotprompt prompt-management integration while constructing the chat prompt. The request is an ordinary chat-completion request and does not reference a managed prompt, so it does not contain a `prompt_id`. `PromptManagementBase.get_chat_completion_prompt()` consequently raises: ```text ValueError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` LiteLLM wraps this local preprocessing exception as an `APIConnectionError`, retries it five times, attempts fallback handling, and ultimately returns HTTP 500. This appears to occur because cache-control injection is incorrectly activating, or being handled by, the Dotprompt prompt-management callback. Configuring cache-control injection should not cause an unrelated prompt-management integration to require `prompt_id`. ### Expected behavior LiteLLM should add the requested cache-control metadata to the matching system message and submit the completion to the provider without requiring prompt-management fields. If the selected provider or model does not support cache-control injection, LiteLLM should return an appropriate validation or unsupported-feature error. It should not invoke prompt management or require `prompt_id`. ### Actual behavior An ordinary completion enters the Dotprompt prompt-management path and fails before a provider response can be obtained because the request has no `prompt_id`. ### User Flow - Run a local LiteLLM Proxy deployment with a cloud-backed model such as `claude-opus-4.8` or `gemini-3.6-flash`. - Configure the model with `cache_control_injection_points` under `litellm_params`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-opus-4.8 litellm_params: model: <provider/model> api_key: os.environ/PROVIDER_API_KEY cache_control_injection_points: - role: system location: message ``` - Send a normal request containing a system message, without specifying `prompt_id` or any managed-prompt parameters: ```bash curl http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "claude-opus-4.8", "messages": [ { "role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant." }, { "role": "user", "content": "Hello" } ] }' ``` - Observe that the request returns HTTP 500 with: ```text prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` - Remove the following configuration: ```yaml cache_control_injection_points: - role: system location: message ``` - Restart or reload the proxy and repeat the same request. - Observe that the prompt-management error no longer occurs. ### Proof the bug occurs | Test Result | Outcome | | --- | --- | | Cloud model without `cache_control_injection_points` | Request proceeds without this error | | Same model and request with `cache_control_injection_points` | HTTP 500 | | Request without any managed-prompt fields | Dotprompt is still invoked | | Models observed | `gemini-3.6-flash`, `claude-opus-4.8`, and other configured cloud models | The stack trace proves that an ordinary completion unexpectedly enters Dotprompt prompt management: ```text litellm.main.completion -> litellm_logging_obj.get_chat_completion_prompt -> custom_logger.get_chat_completion_prompt -> dotprompt_manager.get_chat_completion_prompt -> PromptManagementBase.get_chat_completion_prompt -> ValueError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` Relevant trace excerpt: ```text File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/main.py", line 5076, in completion ) = litellm_logging_obj.get_chat_completion_prompt( File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py", line 701, in get_chat_completion_prompt ) = custom_logger.get_chat_completion_prompt( File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/integrations/dotprompt/dotprompt_manager.py", line 201, in get_chat_completion_prompt return PromptManagementBase.get_chat_completion_prompt( File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/integrations/prompt_management_base.py", line 168, in get_chat_completion_prompt raise ValueError("prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class") ValueError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` The error is then incorrectly surfaced as a provider connection failure: ```text 500 litellm.APIConnectionError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` LiteLLM retries the deterministic preprocessing failure: ```text LiteLLM Retried: 5 times, LiteLLM Max Retries: 5 ``` Fallback handling cannot recover from it: ```text No fallback model group found for original model_group=claude-opus-4.8 Error doing the fallback: litellm.APIConnectionError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` This evidence shows that: 1. The exception originates in LiteLLM prompt preprocessing rather than in the cloud provider. 2. Dotprompt is invoked even though the request does not use a managed prompt. 3. Enabling `cache_control_injection_points` makes `prompt_id` incorrectly mandatory. 4. The issue is provider-independent because it occurs with multiple cloud models. 5. Retries and fallbacks cannot resolve the issue because every attempt encounters the same local preprocessing error. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.2 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: Responses API transformer strips cache_control unconditionally, unlike Chat Completions' custom-endpoint carve-out
signals.text: ### What happened? When a model is configured with `custom_llm_provider: openai` and a self-hosted `api_base` (an OpenAI-compatible gateway that understands Anthropic-style `cache_control` markers — e.g. a local proxy bridging to Claude via OAuth), the **Chat Completions** transformer preserves `cache_control` for that self-hosted endpoint, but the **Responses API** transformer strips it unconditionally, with no equivalent carve-out. `litellm/llms/openai/chat/gpt_transformation.py` has `_should_preserve_cache_control_for_endpoint()`: ```python def _should_preserve_cache_control_for_endpoint( self, custom_llm_provider: str | None, api_base: str | None, ) -> bool: """ The generic `openai` provider also reaches OpenAI-compatible endpoints (a LiteLLM proxy, vLLM, an Anthropic-compatible gateway) via a custom api_base. Those can understand cache_control, so it must survive there. Real OpenAI cannot, so it is still stripped for an openai.com host. """ ``` This is called from `transform_request`/`transform_request` async path, and when `custom_llm_provider == "openai"` with a non-`api.openai.com` `api_base`, `cache_control` on messages/tools is preserved. `litellm/llms/openai/responses/transformation.py` has no equivalent check. `transform_responses_api_request` (and the sync counterpart) unconditionally calls `remove_cache_control_flag_from_input_and_tools`, regardless of `custom_llm_provider`/`api_base`: ```python """Strip Anthropic-only `cache_control` markers before sending to OpenAI. OpenAI's Responses API rejects unknown fields on input content blocks with HTTP 400 ("Unknown parameter: 'input[0].content[0].cache_control'"). Chat Completions strips these in `remove_cache_control_flag_from_messages_and_tools`; mirror that here. """ ``` Net effect: a client sending Anthropic `cache_control` breakpoints (e.g. Claude Code, which enables extended thinking by default and in our setup causes LiteLLM to route through the Responses API transformer rather than Chat Completions) through a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible + Anthropic-capable backend gets its `cache_control` silently dropped on the Responses path, while the same request would have survived on the Chat Completions path. Prompt caching (`cache_read_input_tokens`) never fires — measured 0% hit rate across all live traffic in our deployment — even though the pricing config (`cache_read_input_token_cost` etc.) and the downstream bridge both support it correctly when the field is present. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.96.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response*

signals.title: additional_drop_params strips fields from message content blocks, not just top-level request params
signals.text: # Bug: `additional_drop_params` strips fields from message content blocks, not just top-level request params ## Description `additional_drop_params` is intended to drop top-level request parameters (e.g., `thinking`, `temperature`) before they're sent to the provider. However, it also recursively strips fields with the same name from **inside message content blocks**, breaking valid conversation histories. ## Reproduction ### Config: ```yaml - model_name: "claude-opus-5" litellm_params: model: "anthropic/claude-opus-5" api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY additional_drop_params: ["thinking", "temperature", "top_p", "top_k"] ``` ### Request: ```python import litellm response = litellm.completion( model="claude-opus-5", messages=[ {"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": [ {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "The user asks about 2+2. The answer is 4."}, {"type": "text", "text": "4"} ]}, {"role": "user", "content": "And 3+3?"} ], max_tokens=100 ) ``` ### Expected behavior: - The top-level `thinking` request parameter (if present) should be stripped. - The `thinking` **field inside message content blocks** (`messages[].content[].thinking`) should be left intact — it's part of the conversation history, not a request parameter. ### Actual behavior: The `thinking` field is stripped from inside the assistant message content block, turning: ```json {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "The user asks about 2+2. The answer is 4."} ``` into: ```json {"type": "thinking"} ``` Anthropic then rejects this with: ``` messages.X.content.0.thinking: each thinking block must contain thinking ``` ## Impact This breaks **fallback routing** in production. When a primary model fails and LiteLLM falls back to a model with `additional_drop_params: ["thinking"]`, the conversation history (which may contain thinking blocks from prior reasoning model responses) gets corrupted, causing the fallback to also fail. Error observed: ``` Error doing the fallback: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error", "message":"messages.27.content.0.thinking: each thinking block must contain thinking"}} ``` ## Environment - LiteLLM version: v1.93.2 - Deployment: LiteLLM Proxy (Docker/K8s) - Provider: Anthropic (claude-opus-5) - Router with fallbacks enabled ## Suggested Fix `additional_drop_params` should only strip keys from the **top-level request body** (the kwargs dict passed to the completion call), not recurse into nested structures like `messages[].content[]`. The stripping logic should be scoped to: ```python # Only strip from top-level params for param in additional_drop_params: kwargs.pop(param, None) ``` And should NOT traverse into: - `messages[].content[]` (message content blocks) - `messages[].tool_calls[]` (tool call arguments) - Any other nested message payload structures ## Workaround Remove `"thinking"` from `additional_drop_params` on models that are used as fallback targets. This means clients sending the unsupported `thinking` parameter will get a raw provider error, but fallback routing won't break.

signals.title: [Bug]: Missing Basic credentials return 500 on /langfuse/{endpoint:path}
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate ### What happened? An unauthenticated request without an `Authorization` header to the built-in Langfuse pass-through returns HTTP 500 instead of a controlled authentication error The route reads the Basic authorization value and decodes it before calling the normal virtual-key authentication function. With no header, the value becomes an empty string, base64 decoding produces an empty string, and indexing the second element of `decoded_str.split(":")` raises `IndexError` The affected route registers GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE at `/langfuse/{endpoint:path}`. Missing credentials and several malformed Basic values can therefore generate an unhandled exception and a server-side traceback before credential validation Expected behavior is a controlled 401 response for missing or malformed credentials, with no unhandled traceback No authentication bypass, upstream forwarding, protected-data access, or client-visible traceback was observed. The established impact is avoidable 500 responses and exception-log volume from unauthenticated requests Relevant source in v1.98.0: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.98.0/litellm/proxy/vertex_ai_endpoints/langfuse_endpoints.py#L167-L176 ### User Flow Before a hypothetical fix: an anonymous caller receives a 500 when the Langfuse pass-through should reject the missing credentials cleanly 1. The proxy administrator runs LiteLLM 1.98.0 with a master key, PostgreSQL, and Redis 2. An anonymous caller sends `GET http://localhost:4000/langfuse/zzz` without request headers 3. The caller receives HTTP 500 with `Internal server error` 4. The administrator sees an `IndexError` traceback in the proxy logs After a hypothetical fix: the same anonymous request is rejected as an authentication failure without an unhandled exception 1. The proxy administrator runs LiteLLM 1.98.0 with a master key, PostgreSQL, and Redis 2. An anonymous caller sends `GET http://localhost:4000/langfuse/zzz` without request headers 3. The caller receives HTTP 401 with the normal authentication error shape 4. The administrator sees a controlled authentication rejection rather than an `IndexError` traceback ### Proof the bug occurs Config and setup used for the live proxy: ```text Image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-latest Version reported by the image: 1.98.0 Master key: configured and redacted Database: PostgreSQL Cache: Redis LANGFUSE_HOST: unset LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY: unset LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY: unset ``` The Langfuse environment variables are not needed to reach this failure because it occurs before upstream configuration or forwarding Command and full client-visible output: ```console $ curl -s -w "\n[HTTP %{http_code}]\n" http://localhost:4000/langfuse/zzz {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"internal_server_error"}} [HTTP 500] ``` Relevant server-log excerpt: ```text File "litellm/proxy/vertex_ai_endpoints/langfuse_endpoints.py", line 174, in langfuse_proxy_route api_key = decoded_str.split(":")[1] IndexError: list index out of range ``` The same handler is registered for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE A robust fix should validate the Basic scheme, decode base64 strictly, handle decoding failures, require a colon and nonempty secret, and return a controlled 401 before invoking virtual-key authentication. A plain `Depends(user_api_key_auth)` is not sufficient unless it is wrapped or extended to decode the Langfuse Basic credential format Regression coverage should include missing headers, invalid base64, decoded values without a colon, empty secrets, and a well-formed Basic value containing an invalid virtual key ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on? 1.98.0
signals.author: emerzon

signals.title: [Bug]: vercel_ai_gateway streaming drops prompt_tokens_details (cached_tokens) — regression since v1.95, overcharges cache-heavy streaming workloads
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? # [Bug]: `vercel_ai_gateway` streaming drops `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` — regression since v1.95, massively overcharges cache-heavy streaming workloads ## What happened? For `vercel_ai_gateway` models, **streaming** responses lose `prompt_tokens_details` (it comes back `null`), so LiteLLM cannot see `cached_tokens` and bills the entire prompt as fresh input. **Non-streaming** requests to the same model, same prompt, are fine (`cached_tokens` populated correctly). This is a **regression**: it works in **v1.89.3** and is broken in **v1.95.0, v1.97.0, and v1.98.0-rc.1**. Impact for us: a real production window billed by Vercel at **$0.50 (97% cache read)** was recorded by LiteLLM at **$3.71 (4% cache detected) → 7.4x overcharge**, because ~97% of traffic is streaming and the cache read tokens are counted as fresh input. ## How to reproduce Config (a `vercel_ai_gateway` model with a discounted cache-read rate): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: minimax litellm_params: model: vercel_ai_gateway/minimax/minimax-m3 api_key: os.environ/VERCEL_AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY input_cost_per_token: 0.0000003 output_cost_per_token: 0.0000012 cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.00000006 ``` Send the **same large prompt several times** to warm Vercel's prompt cache (vary only a short trailing user message so the client-side response cache doesn't short-circuit it), once **non-streaming** and once **streaming**: ```bash # NON-STREAMING -> prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens is POPULATED curl -s $LITELLM/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"minimax","stream":false,"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<large repeated prompt>"},{"role":"user","content":"reply OK 1"}]}' # STREAMING (even with include_usage) -> prompt_tokens_details is NULL curl -s $LITELLM/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"minimax","stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true},"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<large repeated prompt>"},{"role":"user","content":"reply OK 2"}]}' ``` Inspect the final `usage` object of each (or the SpendLogs `metadata.usage_object`). ## Expected Streaming `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` should be populated (as in non-streaming), so cache reads are billed at `cache_read_input_token_cost`. ## Actual - Non-streaming: `prompt_tokens_details: {"cached_tokens": 33121, ...}` ✅ (billed at cache rate) - Streaming: `prompt_tokens_details: null` ❌ (all tokens billed at input rate → overcharge) Note: `stream_options.include_usage: true` **is** set and usage totals do arrive — only `prompt_tokens_details` is dropped during streamed usage reassembly. ## Version regression (reproduced with identical prompt/model, only version changed) | LiteLLM version | non-streaming | streaming | |---|---|---| | v1.89.3 | cached populated ✅ | **cached populated ✅** | | v1.95.0 | cached populated ✅ | **null ❌** | | v1.97.0 | cached populated ✅ | **null ❌** | | v1.98.0-rc.1 | cached populated ✅ | **null ❌** | ## Cross-check against the provider's own billing (ground truth) Same 1-minute production window, streaming traffic: - **Vercel AI Gateway usage log:** Input = 186,021 tokens, **Cache Read = 6,545,053 tokens (97.2% cached)**, cost **$0.50**. - **LiteLLM (same window):** only 4% of requests had `cached_tokens` populated, recorded spend **$3.71 (7.4x)**. So the provider **does** return cache-read usage for streaming; LiteLLM discards it on the streaming path. ## Possibly related PR #34812 ("keep OpenAI prompt cache token details through streaming usage reassembly") appears to target this class of bug but does not cover `vercel_ai_gateway` streaming — the regression persists through v1.98.0-rc.1. ## Environment - LiteLLM Proxy (Docker, `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:<version>`) - Provider: `vercel_ai_gateway` (models: minimax/minimax-m3, zai/glm-5.2 — same behavior) - Reproduced on v1.95.0, v1.97.0, v1.98.0-rc.1; **not** present on v1.89.3 ### User Flow 1. Configure a vercel_ai_gateway model with cache_read_input_token_cost set. 2. Send the SAME large prompt twice (vary only a short trailing user message): once with "stream": false, once with "stream": true + stream_options.include_usage=true. 3. Inspect usage.prompt_tokens_details of each response. Expected: cached_tokens populated in both. Actual: populated in non-streaming, NULL in streaming (cache read billed as fresh input). Regression: works in v1.89.3, broken in v1.95.0 / v1.97.0 / v1.98.0-rc.1. ### Proof the bug occurs PROOF 1 — A/B, same prompt & model, only version/stream changed: | LiteLLM version | non-streaming | streaming | |-----------------|---------------|-----------| | v1.89.3 | cached OK ✅ | cached OK ✅ | | v1.95.0 | cached OK ✅ | NULL ❌ | | v1.97.0 | cached OK ✅ | NULL ❌ | | v1.98.0-rc.1 | cached OK ✅ | NULL ❌ | Non-streaming usage_object: "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 33121, ...} (billed at cache rate) Streaming usage_object (same prompt, stream_options.include_usage=true): "prompt_tokens_details": null (all billed as fresh input) PROOF 2 — Cross-check vs the provider's own billing log (ground truth), same 1-minute production window, streaming traffic: Vercel AI Gateway usage log : Input 186,021 | Cache Read 6,545,053 (97.2% cached) | cost $0.50 LiteLLM (same window) : cached_tokens present in only 4% of requests | recorded spend $3.71 => 7.4x overcharge. The provider DOES return cache-read usage for streaming; LiteLLM discards prompt_tokens_details on the streaming reassembly path. PROOF 3 — Fixed by downgrading to v1.89.3 in production: Before (v1.97): cached populated ~2-4% of requests, $/req ~$0.06-0.12 After (v1.89.3): cached populated ~100% of requests, $/req dropped ~2x ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? _No response_ ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.95.0 / v1.97.0 / v1.98.0-rc.1 (broken), v1.89.3 (works) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: Per-user authorization-code credentials are omitted from MCP prompt and resource operations
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? For an MCP server configured with per-user OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code credentials, LiteLLM applies the stored user credential to tool operations but not to prompt or resource operations. After the user completes OAuth, `tools/list` and `tools/call` work. The same upstream server returns 401 for `prompts/list` and `resources/list`, and LiteLLM turns those failures into empty lists. `prompts/get`, `resources/read`, and `resources/templates/list` use the same unauthenticated client-construction path and are affected as well. Expected behavior: every protected MCP operation should resolve and send the same stored per-user OAuth credential. Actual behavior: only the tool paths pass `user_api_key_auth` into `_create_mcp_client`, which is required by the Authorization Code credential resolver. The difference is visible in the v1.97.0 source: - Tool listing passes `user_api_key_auth`: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/server.py#L1965-L2025 - Prompt and resource listing do not pass it to the manager: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/server.py#L2130-L2305 - The manager constructs prompt and resource clients without `user_api_key_auth`: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py#L3480-L3682 ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure an upstream Streamable HTTP MCP server that requires the same bearer token for tools, prompts, and resources. 2. Configure that server in LiteLLM with `auth_type: oauth2` and `oauth2_flow: authorization_code`. 3. Complete the per-user OAuth connection and verify that the credential status reports `has_credential: true`. 4. Connect an MCP client through LiteLLM and call `tools/list`. The protected upstream tools are returned. 5. Call `prompts/list` and `resources/list` through the same connection and user identity. 6. Observe upstream 401 responses in the LiteLLM logs and empty prompt and resource lists at the client. 7. Call a protected prompt or resource directly. These operations also create an MCP client without the per-user credential. ### Relevant log output ```text Failed to get prompts from server protected-mcp: Client error '401 Unauthorized' Failed to get resources from server protected-mcp: Client error '401 Unauthorized' ``` ### Suggested fix Pass `user_api_key_auth` through every prompt and resource manager method and into `_create_mcp_client`, using the same Authorization Code credential-resolution path as tool listing and tool calls. Please cover list, get, read, and resource-template operations with regression tests. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.97.0
signals.author: frdeng

signals.title: [Bug]: MCP OAuth disconnect leaves cached credentials usable on other proxy replicas
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? In a multi-replica LiteLLM deployment, disconnecting a per-user OAuth MCP server can delete the database credential and shared Redis entry while another replica continues using its local cached access token. The credential-status endpoint then reports `has_credential: false`, but requests routed to a replica with a warmed local cache can still list or call upstream tools until that cache entry expires. Expected behavior: after the disconnect endpoint succeeds, the credential must no longer be usable by any proxy replica. Actual behavior: the Authorization Code token backend is built on `user_api_key_cache`, which has a process-local cache in front of Redis. The disconnect endpoint invalidates through the worker handling that request, but does not broadcast invalidation to other workers. Relevant v1.97.0 source: - The per-user token backend uses `user_api_key_cache`: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/outbound_credentials/per_user_oauth_store.py#L118-L160 - The OAuth disconnect endpoint deletes the row and invokes local cache invalidation: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/mcp_management_endpoints.py#L2041-L2078 - `DualCacheTokenCacheBackend.delete` delegates to the supplied cache: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/outbound_credentials/dual_cache_token_backend.py#L50-L74 - LiteLLM has cross-worker auth-cache invalidation pub/sub, but the MCP OAuth disconnect path does not publish an invalidation: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/common_utils/auth_cache_invalidation_pubsub.py#L53-L72 This is distinct from #33072. Authorization Code refresh exists in v1.97.0. This report is about cache coherence and disconnect semantics across replicas. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run two or more LiteLLM proxy replicas with the same database and Redis configuration. 2. Configure an upstream MCP server with per-user OAuth Authorization Code credentials. 3. Connect one user to the server. 4. Route `tools/list` through each replica so each process reads and caches the user's upstream token. 5. Send `DELETE /v1/mcp/server/{server_id}/oauth-user-credential` through replica A. 6. Verify that the status endpoint reports `has_credential: false` and that the database credential row is gone. 7. Route `tools/list` or `tools/call` through replica B. 8. Observe that replica B can continue using the cached upstream credential until its local entry expires. ### Relevant log output ```text OAuth credential status: has_credential=false Replica B still returns protected upstream tools after the disconnect request succeeded. ``` ### Suggested fix Make the per-user Authorization Code token cache coherent across replicas. Two possible approaches are: 1. Use a Redis-only backend for these short-lived upstream credentials when coordination Redis is available. 2. Publish and consume cross-worker invalidation for the exact `(user_id, server_id)` token key on connect, refresh, and disconnect. The disconnect response should not report success until the authoritative shared credential has been removed. Local caches must not continue granting access afterward. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.97.0
signals.author: frdeng

signals.title: [Bug]: OAuth discovery can hang on a Streamable HTTP MCP GET response
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? OAuth endpoint discovery performs an ordinary buffered `GET` against the configured Streamable HTTP MCP resource URL. If that endpoint supports the optional server-to-client SSE stream and keeps the GET response open, LiteLLM can remain stuck while loading or reloading the MCP server. This is a valid Streamable HTTP behavior. A server may return an SSE stream for GET, while servers that do not support that stream may return 405. Expected behavior: OAuth discovery must be bounded by `MCP_METADATA_TIMEOUT` and must not wait for an indefinite MCP event-stream body. Actual behavior: `_discover_metadata_recording_attempts` creates the MCP HTTP client without the metadata timeout and calls `await client.get(server_url)`, which buffers the response. The helper used for subsequent well-known metadata requests does apply `MCP_METADATA_TIMEOUT`. Relevant v1.97.0 source: - Well-known discovery applies `MCP_METADATA_TIMEOUT`: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py#L3712-L3723 - The initial MCP resource GET does not: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py#L3758-L3801 ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run a Streamable HTTP MCP server whose `GET /mcp` returns `200 OK` with `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and keeps the stream open. 2. Configure that URL as an OAuth-protected MCP server in LiteLLM, with `auth_type: oauth2` and `oauth2_flow: authorization_code`. 3. Start LiteLLM or trigger an MCP server reload that performs OAuth discovery. 4. Observe that server loading remains in the initial resource GET instead of completing well-known protected-resource and authorization-server discovery within `MCP_METADATA_TIMEOUT`. 5. Change the test server to return 405 immediately for `GET /mcp` and observe that discovery proceeds without hanging. Minimal upstream behavior: ```python async def events(): while True: yield b": keepalive\n\n" await asyncio.sleep(10) @app.get("/mcp") async def mcp_get(): return StreamingResponse(events(), media_type="text/event-stream") ``` ### Relevant log output ```text No terminal discovery error is emitted while the client waits for the non-terminating response body. ``` ### Suggested fix Apply `MCP_METADATA_TIMEOUT` to the initial resource request. Prefer streaming the response, inspecting the HTTP status and `WWW-Authenticate` header, and closing it without consuming an indefinite event-stream body. Then continue RFC 9728 well-known discovery as normal. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.97.0
signals.author: frdeng

signals.title: Exa AI search: highlights, score, and response metadata (costDollars, requestId) silently dropped in transform_search_response
signals.text: ### Bug description `ExaAISearchConfig.transform_search_response` (`litellm/llms/exa_ai/search/transformation.py`) only reads `result.get("text")` when building each `SearchResult`, so a request with `contents: {highlights: {...}}` returns HTTP 200 with `snippet` empty on every row — the `highlights` Exa actually returned are discarded entirely. `highlightScores` and `score` are dropped the same way, and the response envelope (`costDollars`, `requestId`, `resolvedSearchType`, `searchTime`) is discarded too, even though `costDollars` is the only in-band way to reconcile billed spend against Exa's actual charge. ### Reproduction Measured against `v1.93.0`, but the relevant code path looks unchanged on `main` as of this writing: ```python import litellm resp = litellm.search( model="exa_ai/search", query="...", contents={"highlights": {"numSentences": 2}}, ) print(resp.results[0].snippet) # "" -- empty, even though Exa returned highlights ``` ### Expected behavior - `snippet` should fall back to the joined `highlights` when `text` is blank (Exa returns only the content type you request, so in practice one or the other is populated, not both). - `highlights` / `highlight_scores` (from `highlightScores`) / `score` should be attached to `SearchResult` when Exa returns them — `SearchResult` already declares `model_config = {"extra": "allow"}`, so this is purely additive and doesn't change the shape of a text-only response. - The response envelope (minus `results`) should be attached to `SearchResponse` (e.g. as `provider_metadata`), so callers can reconcile billed cost against `costDollars`. ### Fix We have a fix for this (not yet upstream) that does exactly the above. Happy to open a PR if useful.
signals.author: deepanshululla

signals.title: search_provider_cost_per_query only ever looks up <provider>/search — per-mode price entries (search-advanced, search-deep, search-pro) are unreachable
signals.text: ### Bug description `search_provider_cost_per_query` (`litellm/search/cost_calculator.py`) always calls `get_model_info(model=model, ...)` where `model` is constructed as `<provider>/search` — it never varies by the request's actual mode/depth parameter. But litellm's own `model_prices_and_context_window.json` already ships mode-specific entries for several of these providers — e.g. `tavily/search-advanced` ($0.016 vs $0.008 for `tavily/search`), `linkup/search-deep` ($0.05867 vs $0.00587), `parallel_ai/search-pro`. None of these are ever reachable today, so every mode bills at the base mode's price — under-reporting cost by 2x-10x depending on provider/mode. ### Reproduction ```python import litellm # search_depth="advanced" should resolve tavily/search-advanced ($0.016/query), # but resolves tavily/search ($0.008/query) instead -- a 2x under-report. cost = litellm.search_provider_cost_per_query( model="tavily/search", custom_llm_provider="tavily", optional_params={"search_depth": "advanced"}, ) ``` ### Expected behavior When the request carries a provider's mode/depth parameter (`type` for Exa, `mode` for Parallel, `search_depth` for Tavily, `depth` for Linkup), the cost lookup should prefer a `<provider>/search-<mode>` entry, falling back to the plain `<provider>/search` entry only when no mode-specific entry exists. ### Fix We have a fix for this (not yet upstream) that adds a per-provider mode-parameter lookup before falling back to the base entry. Happy to open a PR. One open design question for maintainers: our fix uses a small provider → param-name table living in `cost_calculator.py`. It might fit the existing architecture better as an attribute on each provider's own `SearchConfig` class (parallel to the existing `get_provider_search_config` dispatch) rather than a second lookup table that has to be kept in sync with the first whenever a new provider is added — open to whichever pattern you'd prefer before we put up a PR.
signals.author: deepanshululla

signals.title: Anthropic /v1/messages adapter maps metadata.user_id to 'user' only, never to OpenAI's prompt_cache_key
signals.text: ## Summary When bridging Anthropic `/v1/messages` requests to OpenAI-compatible targets (Responses API and Chat Completions), `metadata.user_id` is only mapped to the deprecated OpenAI `user` field. It is never used to populate `prompt_cache_key`, which is the field OpenAI's GPT-5.6+ prompt caching actually keys routing/matching off of. This is documented explicitly in the `/v1/messages → /responses` mapping reference: | Anthropic (`/v1/messages`) | Responses API | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `metadata.user_id` | `user` | Extracted from the metadata object and truncated to 64 characters | Relevant code: `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/responses_adapters/transformation.py` (Responses path) and the equivalent chat-completions adapter path both only set `responses_kwargs["user"]` / the chat-completions `user` param from `metadata.user_id`. Neither sets `prompt_cache_key`. ## Why this matters Per OpenAI's own prompt-caching docs: - `user` is being replaced by `safety_identifier` and `prompt_cache_key`; OpenAI explicitly recommends using `prompt_cache_key` instead of `user` to maintain caching optimizations. - For GPT-5.6 and later, you must set `prompt_cache_key` to get reliable exact-prefix matching for both implicit and explicit caching. Without it, requests may still get automatic cache hits, but without the improved matching. Anthropic-native clients that talk to LiteLLM's `/v1/messages` endpoint — Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK, other Anthropic-shaped tools — already send a stable, per-session `metadata.user_id` on every request (Claude Code specifically sends a value that's stable for the lifetime of one CLI session and only changes on restart). This is exactly the kind of value `prompt_cache_key` is designed for (OpenAI's own docs list "session IDs and user IDs" as common `prompt_cache_key` values), but it's currently discarded for caching purposes and only forwarded to the deprecated `user` field. The practical effect: any Anthropic-shaped client routed through LiteLLM to an OpenAI GPT-5.6+ backend gets no cache-routing stickiness benefit from a value it's already sending on every call, with no client-side change possible to fix this (the client has no notion of `prompt_cache_key`, only `metadata.user_id`). ## Request Populate `prompt_cache_key` from `metadata.user_id` (in addition to, or as a config-gated alternative to, the existing `user` mapping) when translating Anthropic `/v1/messages` requests to OpenAI-compatible Responses API / Chat Completions targets. ## Related - Closed issue #28354 and open issue #36091 cover the reverse-direction gap (OpenAI cache-hit usage not being reported back in the Anthropic response shape) — fixing this request-side mapping without also fixing the usage-reporting side would leave callers unable to verify caching is actually happening. Flagging for context, not asking to bundle the fixes.
signals.author: jimmychen-p72

signals.title: cache_control_injection_points has no equivalent for OpenAI prompt_cache_breakpoint on OpenAI-compatible targets
signals.text: ## Summary `cache_control_injection_points` (via `AnthropicCacheControlHook`, introduced in #9996 and extended to the `/v1/messages` path in #30341/#30615 for issue #30293) lets an admin configure, at the deployment level, where a stable-prefix cache boundary should be placed. Today this hook only ever produces Anthropic-shaped `cache_control` blocks. There is no equivalent path that emits OpenAI's GPT-5.6+ `prompt_cache_breakpoint` (per content block) plus `prompt_cache_options` (request-level `mode`/`ttl`) when the deployment actually routes to an OpenAI-compatible target. ## Why this matters OpenAI's GPT-5.6+ caching model supports the same concept — an explicit marker on the last content block of a reusable prefix — as `prompt_cache_breakpoint`, combined with `prompt_cache_options.mode` to control whether the automatic implicit breakpoint stays active alongside it. This is functionally the same admin intent `cache_control_injection_points` already expresses for Anthropic, just via a different wire format on a different provider. Without this, admins running mixed model fleets (Anthropic + OpenAI GPT-5.6 deployments behind the same proxy config pattern) have a working, centrally-configured caching primitive for Anthropic-backed deployments and *no* equivalent centrally-configured primitive for OpenAI-backed ones — caching for OpenAI targets is left entirely to either the client (which, for Anthropic-shaped clients like Claude Code, has no notion of `prompt_cache_breakpoint` at all — see openai/codex#35300 for the same gap in another Anthropic-shaped client, Codex CLI) or to OpenAI's default implicit-mode caching, which the docs note is exact-match-only on GPT-5.6+ and does not do the longest-matching-prefix fallback earlier models had. This means a stable prefix (e.g. a large system prompt + tool definitions, sent identically by an Anthropic-shaped client on every turn) that would reliably cache on Anthropic never gets the same reliable treatment on OpenAI targets, purely because of a proxy-side config gap rather than a client or model limitation. ## Request When a deployment configured with `cache_control_injection_points` routes to an OpenAI-compatible target that supports explicit prompt-cache breakpoints (GPT-5.6+), translate the configured injection point(s) into: - a `prompt_cache_breakpoint: {"mode": "explicit"}` marker on the corresponding outgoing content block, and - `prompt_cache_options` at the request root (at minimum enabling explicit mode; `ttl` currently only supports `"30m"` per OpenAI's docs so may not need to be configurable yet). Leaving the specific implementation approach (extend `AnthropicCacheControlHook` with provider-aware branching vs. a new parallel hook) to maintainer judgment — filing this to capture the gap, not to prescribe the fix. ## Related - #30293 / #30341 / #30615 — established the pattern this issue is asking to extend to OpenAI-compatible targets - #32669 — adds `prompt_cache_breakpoint` as a passthrough param for GPT-5.6 models (request-shape plumbing this issue would build on) - openai/codex#35300 — the same underlying gap (no way to emit `prompt_cache_breakpoint`) from the client side, for a different Anthropic-shaped client
signals.author: jimmychen-p72

signals.title: [Bug]: Routing Issues
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? We are not able to get proper routing behavior. We have tried / experimented with many options ‘default’ , fallbacks enabled/disabled, tag filtering on/off, with and without ‘default’ tags – never could get expected or consistent behavior. Our need is tags enabled, routing_strategy: latency-based-routing, Below are lots of details – we need to know what is the right combination of configuration to get basic routing behavior. model_list: # Existing, unmodified, working model group - model_name: reasoning-complex litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY max_tokens: 8192 tags: [default, provider:anthropic, paid] model_info: input_cost_per_token: 3.0e-06 output_cost_per_token: 1.5e-05 - model_name: reasoning-complex litellm_params: model: bedrock/amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 aws_region_name: us-east-1 max_tokens: 8192 tags: [provider:bedrock, private, local, paid] model_info: input_cost_per_token: 1.2e-06 output_cost_per_token: 4.8e-06 # New test model group -- same two deployments, tag filtering disabled per-group - model_name: reasoning-complex-notag litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY max_tokens: 8192 tags: [default, provider:anthropic, paid] model_info: id: reasoning-complex-notag-anthropic enable_tag_filtering: false input_cost_per_token: 3.0e-06 output_cost_per_token: 1.5e-05 - model_name: reasoning-complex-notag litellm_params: model: bedrock/amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 aws_region_name: us-east-1 max_tokens: 8192 tags: [provider:bedrock, private, local, paid] model_info: id: reasoning-complex-notag-nova enable_tag_filtering: false input_cost_per_token: 1.2e-06 output_cost_per_token: 4.8e-06 router_settings: routing_strategy: latency-based-routing enable_tag_filtering: true # proxy-wide defaul tag_filtering_match_any: false Proxy restarted after the config change; confirmed healthy before testing (/health showed 0 unhealthy endpoints across all model groups, a manual smoke-test call succeeded against Request sent (genuinely untagged) from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(api_key="...", base_url="http://localhost:4000/v1") client.chat.completions.create( model="reasoning-complex-notag", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "explain briefly"}], max_tokens=20, temperature=0, extra_body={"cache": {"no-cache": True}}, ) No tags field, no metadata field anywhere in the request. Expected behavior Per the described model_info.enable_tag_filtering: false semantics: the request should be routed via latency-based-routing across both deployments in reasoning-complex-notag, ignoreployments' own declared tags and any request-sidetags). Actual behavior openai.AuthenticationError: Error code: 401 - {'error': {'message': "Not allowed to access model due to tags configura model=reasoning-complex-notag and tags=['default', 'provider:anthropic', 'paid']", 'type': 'None', 'param': 'None', 'code': This is RouterErrors.no_deployments_with_tag_routi raised because zero deployments end up as validtag-matching candidates. Notably, the tags=[...] echoed in the error is the Sonnet deployment's own litellm_params.tags list (['default', 'provider:anthropic', 'paid']) — not anything the ugh, in this code path, a deployment's own declaredtags are being treated as the required request tags to satisfy, which the Nova Pro deployment in the same group (tags: ['provider:bedrock', 'private', 'local', 'paid'], ) can never match — resulting in animpossible-to-satisfy candidate set and a hard deny, even though the incoming request had no tags at all. We did not get to test a tagged request against this model group — it failed on the very first (untagged) call, before that could be tried. Source investigation We checked the installed package directly to under - litellm/router.py (Router.__init__): enable_tag_filtering is a constructor parameter stored as a single instance attribute (self.enable_tag_filtering = enable_tag_filtering)-deployment. - litellm/router_strategy/tag_based_routing.py (get_deployments_for_tag()): the very first check is if llm_router_instance.enable_tag_filtering is not Trs — reading the router-instance-level attribute, not anything from model_info. - We searched the entire installed package (grep -tering") and found zero references to aper-deployment/per-model_info tag-filtering override anywhere in the source of 1.93.0. Given that, we're not sure whether model_info.enable_tag_filtering is: (a) a real, newer feature not yet in 1.93.0, (b) a doc/support inaccuracy, or (c) real but implementeied (e.g. requires additional config we're missing), which would also explain the specific 401 we're hitting rather than a clean no-op. Why we were trying this in the first place (context, not required to reproduce the bug above) Separately, and probably relevant background: with router_settings.enable_tag_filtering: true (the global default) and no request tags at all, latency-based-routing consistently sends to 1 model group to one deployment (Anthropic, tagged default) and 0% to the other (Bedrock Nova Pro, no default tag) — even though we've directly measured Nova Pro as meaningfully faster per completion token on this eia matched back-to-back timing, ~2-5x faster, consistent across 6 pairs). Explicitly tagging requests works as expected and lets the faster deployment compete and win the majority of the time (confirmed: a shared tag both Pro selected 60% of the time; a Nova-exclusive taggets it selected 100% of the time). Setting router_settings.enable_tag_filtering: false globally also restores genuine latency-based competition for untagged traffic (coreached Nova Pro with this global flag off, versus0/10 with it on). We were trying model_info.enable_tag_filtering: false specifically to get this same effect for one model group without disabling tag filtering proxy-wide, since ng (e.g. private/local tags for data-residencyconstraints) elsewhere. Ask 1. Is model_info.enable_tag_filtering a real, supported config key in 1.93.0? If so, what are we missing that causes this specific 401 instead of the documented behavior? 2. If it's not supported in this version, is there a different documented way to get "tag filtering enabled globally, disabled for one specific model group" without hitting this error ### User Flow from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(api_key="...", base_url="http://localhost:4000/v1") client.chat.completions.create( model="reasoning-complex-notag", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "explain briefly"}], max_tokens=20, temperature=0, extra_body={"cache": {"no-cache": True}}, ) No tags field, no metadata field anywhere in the request. Expected behavior Per the described model_info.enable_tag_filtering: false semantics: the request should be routed via latency-based-routing across both deployments in reasoning-complex-notag, ignoreployments' own declared tags and any request-sidetags). signals.title: [Bug]: search router silently drops provider-specific litellm_params from yaml search_tools entries
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a `search_tools` entry in the proxy config carries provider-specific keys in its `litellm_params` (for example `tool_name` for the agentcore provider, or `aws_access_key_id` / `aws_secret_access_key` overrides), those keys are silently dropped. The search router forwards only `search_provider`, `api_key`, and `api_base` from the tool's `litellm_params` to the underlying search call (`SearchAPIRouter.async_search_with_fallbacks_helper` in `litellm/router_utils/search_api_router.py`), so every other key is ignored with no warning, no boot error, and no request-time error Expected: either every `litellm_params` key is forwarded to the provider (the way `model_list` entries forward their `litellm_params` to completion calls), or the proxy rejects unknown keys loudly at boot so an admin finds out their knob is dead The same keys do work when passed per request in the body or set via provider env vars (for agentcore, `AGENTCORE_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME`), which is how the guard behind `tool_name` stays reachable. Only the yaml path is dead. The agentcore example config was corrected in #36331 to stop advertising the yaml knobs; this issue tracks fixing the plumbing itself, which affects all search providers ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a proxy admin whose AgentCore gateway target has a custom name configures it in yaml and every search silently uses the wrong tool name 1. They add a `search_tools` entry with `search_provider: agentcore`, their gateway `api_base`, and `tool_name: MyTarget___WebSearch` in `litellm_params`, then start the proxy; boot succeeds with no warning 2. They send POST http://litellm-domain/v1/search/agentcore-search with `{"query": "latest AI developments", "max_results": 5}` 3. The request goes out with the default `web-search-tool___WebSearch` instead of their configured name; on a gateway whose target really has a custom name this comes back as an MCP tool-not-found error, and on a gateway that also has a default-named target it silently searches through the wrong one 4. Nothing in the response or the logs says their yaml `tool_name` was ignored After a (hypothetical) fix: the same config works, or fails loudly 1. They add the same `search_tools` entry and start the proxy 2. They send the same POST http://litellm-domain/v1/search/agentcore-search request 3. The request goes out with `MyTarget___WebSearch` and returns results from their target, or, if the key is deliberately unsupported, the proxy refuses to boot naming the unsupported key ### Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with (proxy booted from PR #36331 at commit `70a4f9a73aabd327b9c06e52bf5d47b437b76430`; the router file involved is untouched by that PR and identical on `litellm_internal_staging`): ```yaml search_tools: - search_tool_name: agentcore-badtool litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: https://litellm-qa-agentcore-tez4ymmxfc.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp tool_name: my-target___ListFiles ``` The agentcore provider rejects any `tool_name` not ending in `___WebSearch`, so this request must fail. Instead it returns HTTP 200 with real web results, against a real AgentCore gateway: ``` curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/v1/search/agentcore-badtool \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \ -d '{"query": "anything", "max_results": 2}' -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' {"results":[{"title":"Anything","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anything", ...}],"object":"search"} HTTP 200 ``` The proxy debug log shows the outgoing JSON-RPC call used the default tool name, not the configured one, proving the yaml value never reached the provider: ``` -d '{'jsonrpc': '2.0', 'id': 1, 'method': 'tools/call', 'params': {'name': 'web-search-tool___WebSearch', 'arguments': {'query': 'anything', 'maxResults': 2}}}' ``` Control showing the guard itself works when the value arrives via env var: rebooting the same proxy with `AGENTCORE_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME=my-target___ListFiles` exported makes the same request refuse with ``` Invalid AgentCore search tool_name 'my-target___ListFiles': must end with '___WebSearch' (a web-search connector tool). Other gateway tools cannot be invoked through this provider. ``` Fix sketch: forward the tool's full `litellm_params` (minus `search_provider`, which becomes the positional provider) as kwargs from `SearchAPIRouter.async_search_with_fallbacks_helper` into the search call, mirroring how `model_list` `litellm_params` flow into completion calls, with request-body params winning over yaml on key collisions. Needs a check across all search providers that previously-ignored yaml keys don't change behavior for existing configs ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? litellm_internal_staging at 2059033352de (also present at PR #36331 tip 70a4f9a7) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: generateContent bridge drops functionDeclarations.parameters, so tool schemas are silently lost for non-Gemini providers
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a Gemini-native `generateContent` request is served by a model whose deployment points at a non-Gemini provider, the tool parameter schema is dropped. The function name and description reach the upstream model; the arguments schema does not, so the model calls the function with empty or invented arguments. The request succeeds, nothing is logged as an error, and the caller gets a well-formed `functionCall` with the wrong `args`. The bridge that converts a `generateContent` body into a chat-completions body only reads `functionDeclarations[].parametersJsonSchema`. That is the field `gemini-cli` sends. The `google-genai` SDKs serialize tool schemas to `functionDeclarations[].parameters` instead, and there is no branch for it. I confirmed what the SDK puts on the wire by pointing `google-genai` 1.69.0 at a local HTTP listener. Both idiomatic ways of declaring a tool produce `parameters`: ```python fd = types.FunctionDeclaration( name="get_weather", description="Get weather", parameters=types.Schema(type="OBJECT", properties={"city": types.Schema(type="STRING", description="City name")}, required=["city"])) ``` ```json {"functionDeclarations":[{"name":"get_weather","description":"Get weather", "parameters":{"type":"OBJECT","properties":{"city":{"type":"STRING","description":"City name"}},"required":["city"]}}]} ``` Passing a plain Python callable as a tool produces `parameters` as well. I could not get the SDK to emit `parametersJsonSchema` through either path. Expected: a tool declared with `parameters` reaches the upstream model with its schema intact, exactly as one declared with `parametersJsonSchema` does today. ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer whose app uses the Google GenAI SDK against the proxy gets function calls back with empty arguments as soon as the model name is served by a non-Gemini deployment. 1. They point their app at the proxy and send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1beta/models/my-model:generateContent`, where `my-model` is served by an OpenAI-compatible deployment, with one tool declared: `get_weather`, taking a required string `city` 2. They get `200` back with `{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{}}}` — the right function, no arguments 3. Their app calls `get_weather()` with no city, and either raises a `KeyError` or looks up the weather for nowhere 4. On repeated runs the model sometimes returns `{"args":{"location":"Hanoi"}}` instead — a parameter name that appears nowhere in the tool they declared 5. They point the same app at `my-gemini-model`, served by a Gemini deployment, send the identical request, and get `{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{"city":"Hanoi"}}}` — so the same client code works on one model and silently misbehaves on another After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request returns the arguments the tool declared, whichever provider serves the model. 1. They point their app at the proxy and send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1beta/models/my-model:generateContent`, where `my-model` is served by an OpenAI-compatible deployment, with one tool declared: `get_weather`, taking a required string `city` 2. They get `200` back with `{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{"city":"Hanoi"}}}` 3. Their app calls `get_weather(city="Hanoi")` and returns the right weather 4. Repeated runs return the same `city` argument every time 5. Pointing the same app at `my-gemini-model` returns the identical result, so behaviour no longer depends on which provider backs the model name ### Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: my-model litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o api_base: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 # any OpenAI-compatible endpoint api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_COMPAT_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Version: `v1.97.0` (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.97.0`, `importlib.metadata.version("litellm")` reports `1.97.0`) Command — tool declared with `parameters`, which is what the SDK sends: ```bash for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1beta/models/my-model:generateContent" \ -H "x-goog-api-key: sk-1234" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "contents":[{"role":"user","parts":[{"text":"What is the weather in Hanoi? Use the tool."}]}], "tools":[{"functionDeclarations":[{"name":"get_weather","description":"Get the weather for a city", "parameters":{"type":"OBJECT","properties":{"city":{"type":"STRING","description":"City name"}},"required":["city"]}}]}]}' echo; done ``` Output — the model is called with no arguments on every run: ``` {"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{}}}],"role":"model"},"finishReason":"STOP","index":0,"safetyRatings":[]}],"usageMetadata":{"promptTokenCount":49,"candidatesTokenCount":11,"totalTokenCount":60}} {"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{}}}],"role":"model"},"finishReason":"STOP","index":0,"safetyRatings":[]}],"usageMetadata":{"promptTokenCount":49,"candidatesTokenCount":11,"totalTokenCount":60}} {"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{}}}],"role":"model"},"finishReason":"STOP","index":0,"safetyRatings":[]}],"usageMetadata":{"promptTokenCount":49,"candidatesTokenCount":11,"totalTokenCount":60}} ``` Control — the byte-identical schema under `parametersJsonSchema`, same proxy, same model, same prompt: ```bash for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1beta/models/my-model:generateContent" \ -H "x-goog-api-key: sk-1234" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "contents":[{"role":"user","parts":[{"text":"What is the weather in Hanoi? Use the tool."}]}], "tools":[{"functionDeclarations":[{"name":"get_weather","description":"Get the weather for a city", "parametersJsonSchema":{"type":"OBJECT","properties":{"city":{"type":"STRING","description":"City name"}},"required":["city"]}}]}]}' echo; done ``` Output — arguments arrive intact, so the upstream model and the provider are fine: ``` {"functionCall": {"name": "get_weather", "args": {"city": "Hanoi"}}} {"functionCall": {"name": "get_weather", "args": {"city": "Hanoi"}}} {"functionCall": {"name": "get_weather", "args": {"city": "Hanoi"}}} ``` Note on the prompt token counts: 49 in the failing case against 59 in the control — the schema is missing from what leaves the proxy, not merely ignored by the model. The same difference shows up against a Gemini-backed deployment, which takes the native path rather than the bridge and returns `{"city":"Hanoi"}` for both field spellings. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: fix(bedrock): Filter anthropic-beta header for Bedrock passthrough
signals.text: ## Summary - Filters out `anthropic-beta` header from requests before forwarding to AWS Bedrock - Prevents "invalid beta flag" errors when using Claude Code or other clients that send Anthropic beta headers through LiteLLM proxy to Bedrock ## Problem When using Claude Code with LiteLLM as a proxy to AWS Bedrock, requests fail with: ```json {"message":"invalid beta flag"} ``` This happens because Claude Code sends `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` (or other beta values) headers, which AWS Bedrock doesn't recognize or support. ## Solution Filter the `anthropic-beta` header (case-insensitively) in `BedrockPassthroughConfig.sign_request()` before the request is signed and forwarded to Bedrock. Key points: - Filtering happens before AWS SigV4 signing (critical for signature validity) - Case-insensitive matching handles `Anthropic-Beta`, `ANTHROPIC-BETA`, etc. - Other headers like `anthropic-version` are preserved ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests added covering: - Basic header filtering - Case-insensitive filtering - Multiple beta value types - Preservation of other headers - Edge cases (empty headers, only-beta-header) - [x] Manual testing with Claude Code + LiteLLM proxy + Bedrock Run tests: ```bash pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/bedrock/passthrough/test_bedrock_header_filtering.py -v ``` ## Related - Claude Code issue: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/2003 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

signals.title: fix(prompts): Prompt Studio fails to load prompts saved via UI
signals.text: ## Issue Prompt Studio fails to load any prompt that was saved via the Prompt Studio UI "Update" button or the PUT /prompts/{id} API using prompt_data. The editor opens blank with a generic "New prompt" placeholder instead of the actual prompt content. **Root cause:** The Prompt Studio save path writes prompt content to `litellm_params.prompt_data.content` (body only, no YAML frontmatter) and sets `litellm_params.dotprompt_content = null`. But the Prompt Studio load path only reads from `litellm_params.dotprompt_content`: ```javascript let t = e?.prompt_spec?.litellm_params?.dotprompt_content || ""; if (!t) throw Error("No dotprompt_content found in API response"); ``` When dotprompt_content is null, it throws and silently falls back to a blank editor. The prompt data is actually persisted correctly in prompt_data.content — it's just never read back. ## Fix Modified `parseExistingPrompt` to: 1. First try to parse `dotprompt_content` (existing behavior) 2. If not available, fall back to parsing `prompt_data` with both direct and nested formats 3. Updated error message to mention both data sources ## Changes - Modified `parseExistingPrompt` in utils.ts to check for prompt_data as fallback - Added `parsePromptData` helper function to handle both direct `{content, metadata}` and nested `{prompt_id: {content, metadata}}` formats - Added comprehensive tests for prompt_data parsing scenarios ## Testing All 37 tests pass, including 6 new tests for prompt_data fallback: - Parsing prompt_data with direct format - Parsing prompt_data with nested format - Preferring dotprompt_content over prompt_data - Parsing developer messages from prompt_data - Parsing tools from prompt_data - Default values for empty prompt_data Fixes #23935
