signals.title: fix(anthropic,bedrock): report provider thinking tokens instead of classifying them as text
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Adaptive thinking output was billed as text tokens - `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` was ignored - Converse claimed `reasoning_tokens: 0` for hidden thinking - Signature-only thinking vanished from `/v1/responses` How it solves it: - Read the provider's thinking token count first - Tokenize visible reasoning only as a fallback - Report an unknown split as `null`, not text - Keep signature/redacted thinking in `encrypted_content` - Keep `/v1/responses` usage parseable by the OpenAI SDK ## User Flow Before: a developer routing Claude Opus 4.8 on Bedrock through the gateway sees every adaptive-thinking token billed as a text token, so their reasoning-cost dashboard reads zero 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with their Bedrock Opus 4.8 model and `"reasoning_effort": "max"`, and a 200 comes back with the answer 2. The `usage` block reports `completion_tokens: 570` with `completion_tokens_details: {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 570}`, even though nearly all of those tokens were hidden thinking 3. They retry on their invoke-route deployment of the same model and again read `reasoning_tokens: 0`, despite Bedrock's own response saying most output tokens were thinking 4. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"reasoning": {"effort": "high"}` and the output array contains only a `message` item: the reasoning item is missing, so the thinking cannot be passed back on the next turn After: the same requests report Bedrock's own thinking count where one exists, stop pretending an unknown split was all text, and the reasoning item is back 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"reasoning_effort": "max"`, and a 200 comes back with the answer 2. On the converse deployment the `usage` block reports `completion_tokens: 570` with an empty `completion_tokens_details`: the split is unknown, no longer a false `reasoning_tokens: 0` 3. On the invoke-route deployment it reports `completion_tokens: 477` split as `reasoning_tokens: 431, text_tokens: 46`, matching Bedrock's own count 4. The same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses returns `["reasoning", "message"]`, and the reasoning item carries `encrypted_content` the developer can send back on the next turn ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5244 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup for both legs: `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port <port>`, real AWS Bedrock in us-east-1 and real api.anthropic.com, no mocks. config.yaml has three deployments of `claude-opus-4-8` (adaptive thinking only, no `thinking.type.enabled`): `bedrock-converse-opus-4-8` (`bedrock/converse/global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`), `bedrock-invoke-opus-4-8` (`bedrock/invoke/global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`), and `anthropic-opus-4-8` (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-8`). Same payload everywhere: `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"How many prime numbers are less than 30? Think it through, then answer with just the number."}],"max_tokens":4000,"reasoning_effort":"max"}` ### Before (c696fdfb05) #### /v1/chat/completions, Bedrock converse 1. `curl -s localhost:21210/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"bedrock-converse-opus-4-8",...}' | jq '.usage | {completion_tokens, completion_tokens_details}'` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 570, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 570}}`: every hidden thinking token billed as text #### /v1/chat/completions, Bedrock invoke 1. Same curl with `"model":"bedrock-invoke-opus-4-8"` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 501, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 501}}`, ignoring the thinking count Bedrock itself returned #### /v1/responses, Bedrock converse 1. `curl -s localhost:21210/v1/responses ... -d '{"model":"bedrock-converse-opus-4-8","input":"How many prime numbers...","max_output_tokens":4000,"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}}' | jq '[.output[].type]'` 2. `["message"]`: the reasoning item is dropped entirely #### /v1/chat/completions streaming, Bedrock converse 1. Same converse curl with `"stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}`, reading the final usage chunk 2. `{"completion_tokens": 479, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 479}}` #### /v1/chat/completions streaming, direct Anthropic 1. Same streaming curl with `"model":"anthropic-opus-4-8"` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 563, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 563}}`, even though Anthropic's usage carried the thinking count #### /v1/chat/completions without thinking (control) 1. `curl -s localhost:21210/v1/chat/completions ... -d '{"model":"bedrock-converse-opus-4-8","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in exactly three words."}],"max_tokens":100}'` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 10}}`: correct today and must stay this way ### After (710ef81a80) #### /v1/chat/completions, Bedrock converse 1. Same curl against the PR-tip proxy on port 21898 2. `{"completion_tokens": 570, "completion_tokens_details": {}}`: Converse's `TokenUsage` carries no thinking count and the thinking is signature-only, so the split is reported as unknown instead of all text #### /v1/chat/completions, Bedrock invoke 1. Same curl with `"model":"bedrock-invoke-opus-4-8"` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 477, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 431, "text_tokens": 46}}`: the provider's own count #### /v1/responses, Bedrock converse 1. Same curl, plus `jq '[.output[] | select(.type=="reasoning") | (.encrypted_content != null)]'` 2. `["reasoning", "message"]` and `[true]`: the reasoning item is back, carrying the thinking signature in `encrypted_content`, and `usage.output_tokens_details` stays `{"reasoning_tokens": 0}` so the field the Responses API contract requires never disappears #### /v1/responses via the openai SDK, Bedrock converse 1. `OpenAI(api_key=..., base_url="http://localhost:21898/v1").responses.create(model="bedrock-converse-opus-4-8", input="How many prime numbers...", max_output_tokens=4000, reasoning={"effort": "high"})` 2. The SDK validates and parses the response: output types `['reasoning', 'message']`, `usage.output_tokens_details == OutputTokensDetails(reasoning_tokens=0, text_tokens=None)`. The SDK requires `output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` as an int, so the unknown split degrades to 0 on this surface instead of dropping the field and failing client-side validation #### /v1/responses multi-turn, replaying encrypted_content 1. Second `curl -s localhost:21898/v1/responses` whose `input` is the first response's full `output` array plus `{"role":"user","content":"Now add 5 to that answer and reply with just the number."}` 2. `"status": "completed"` with the answer `15`: the signature round-trips without breaking the next turn #### /v1/chat/completions streaming, Bedrock converse 1. Same streaming curl, reading the final usage chunk 2. `{"completion_tokens": 560, "completion_tokens_details": {}}`: unknown split on streaming too #### /v1/chat/completions streaming, direct Anthropic 1. Same streaming curl with `"model":"anthropic-opus-4-8"` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 539, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 495, "text_tokens": 44}}`: the provider count flows through the shared path #### /v1/chat/completions without thinking (control) 1. Same no-thinking curl 2. `{"completion_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 10}}`: unchanged `/v1/messages` needs no proof run since it passes Anthropic's usage through untouched and already carried `thinking_tokens` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) On `/v1/responses` an unknown reasoning split is reported as `output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens: 0` rather than omitted, because the OpenAI SDK requires that field as an int; the honest `null` split exists on `/v1/chat/completions` only `combine_usage_objects` still coerces an unknown reasoning split to 0 when merging usage across multiple calls; fixing that means nullable arithmetic in a helper shared by every surface, which outweighs the cosmetic gain Reasoning items replayed on `/v1/responses` input are not decoded back into provider thinking blocks, and incremental streaming events do not carry `encrypted_content` (only the completed response does); both match the behavior before this PR, and the multi-turn round trip above works live ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR CHECKED: passes /live-pr-risk at 710ef81a80 <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 710ef81a8050a7a9b1d2bd79e3d36b0e364e37bb. signals.title: fix: map missing OpenAI credentials to 401 instead of 500
signals.text: ## Fixes #35860 ### Problem A missing API key is reported as `InternalServerError` (500). Because 500 is retryable under every standard retry policy, a permanently unfixable configuration error gets retried until attempts run out, and the useful `Missing credentials` message arrives last. ```python import litellm # with no OPENAI_API_KEY set litellm.completion(model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]) # -> InternalServerError: OpenAIException - Missing credentials... ``` ### Root cause The OpenAI SDK raises `openai.OpenAIError` at **client construction**, before any HTTP request. That exception carries no `status_code`. The broad handlers in `openai.py` do `getattr(e, "status_code", 500)`, and `exception_mapping_utils.py` then maps 500 to `InternalServerError`. A missing `status_code` means no HTTP exchange took place, so defaulting to 500 (server error) is wrong — this is a permanent client-side config problem. ### Fix Add `_get_openai_exception_status_code(e)`: - if the exception already has a `status_code` (a real HTTP response) → keep it - else if it is an `openai.OpenAIError` (pre-request, e.g. missing key) → **401** → non-retryable `AuthenticationError` - else → keep the `500` default Applied to the completion and streaming handlers. ### Verification ``` # after fix, with no OPENAI_API_KEY: AuthenticationError (isinstance AuthenticationError = True, InternalServerError = False) ``` Added unit tests in `test_openai_exception_status_code.py` (401 for credential error, preserved status codes incl. 0, 500 default for generic errors, real HTTP openai errors unchanged). Full local run: **32 passed** across the new tests + whisper transformation + openai common-utils suites. I chose `AuthenticationError` (401) since it reads as the credential problem it is; happy to switch to `BadRequestError` per the #35849 precedent if maintainers prefer.

signals.title: fix(realtime): honor explicit api_key/api_base in realtime calls
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Realtime calls dropped the api_key resolved from a named credential - `/v1/realtime` failed with "api_key is required for OpenAI realtime calls" How it solves it: - `_arealtime` now honors its explicit `api_key`/`api_base` arguments - Same precedence fix applied to the Azure branch ## Relevant issues Fixes #36066 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Credential resolution already worked: `load_credentials_from_list` hydrates `api_key` from `litellm_credential_name` into kwargs, which reaches `_arealtime` as its explicit `api_key` parameter. The provider branches then ignored that parameter and only looked at `dynamic_api_key`, the globals, and the env var, so with no `OPENAI_API_KEY` set the key ended up `None` and the handler raised Proxy run with a credential-only key, `OPENAI_API_KEY` unset. Note that this environment has no egress to api.openai.com, so the credential points at a local realtime websocket server that prints the Authorization header it receives; that is enough to show which key the proxy forwards upstream config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: my-rt litellm_params: model: gpt-4o-realtime-preview custom_llm_provider: openai litellm_credential_name: openai-secret credential_list: - credential_name: openai-secret credential_values: api_key: sk-credential-key-123 api_base: http://localhost:8799 general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` before, at 24dbd2b2db: ``` $ env -u OPENAI_API_KEY python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config rt_config.yaml --port 4002 $ python rt_client.py # websockets.connect("ws://localhost:4002/v1/realtime?model=my-rt") websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError: received 1011 (internal error) Internal server error # proxy log: raise ValueError("api_key is required for OpenAI realtime calls") ValueError: api_key is required for OpenAI realtime calls ``` after, at 63b2eca39b: ``` $ env -u OPENAI_API_KEY python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config rt_config.yaml --port 4001 $ python rt_client.py CLIENT RECEIVED: {"type": "session.created", "session": {"id": "sess_stub", "model": "gpt-4o-realtime-preview"}} # upstream log: UPSTREAM SAW Authorization: Bearer sk-credential-key-123 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `litellm/realtime_api/main.py` adds the explicit `api_key` and `api_base` arguments to the precedence chain in the openai and azure branches, right after the `dynamic_*` values from `get_llm_provider`, so an explicitly passed key wins over globals and env vars instead of being discarded `tests/test_litellm/realtime_api/test_main.py` gets two regression tests driving `_arealtime` with an explicit key and no globals or env vars, asserting the provider handler receives it. Both fail on the parent commit ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(proxy): keep the model-group alias through vector store credential merges
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #36103 ## What this does Since #24548, `get_deployment_credentials_with_provider` unconditionally injects the deployment's `litellm_params.model` into the returned credentials. The router-bound merge sites in the vector store files endpoints copied that dict over `data`, so requests left the endpoint carrying the underlying provider model instead of the alias the caller named. In `route_request` the underlying model matches `llm_router.deployment_names`, which dispatches with `specific_deployment=True` and skips access-group filtering entirely, so when several model groups share one `litellm_params.model` (different access groups, team scoping, per-group settings) the request can be served under the wrong group and spend/logs attribute to it. The fix adds a `routing_model` parameter to `prepare_data_with_credentials` and passes the resolved alias at the three router-bound merge sites in `litellm/proxy/vector_store_files_endpoints/endpoints.py` (unified vector store id path, model-hint path, single-OpenAI-team-deployment fallback). Direct-to-SDK call sites (batches, files) don't pass it and keep receiving the underlying model, so the #25104 fix from #24548 is preserved; a test pins each behavior. ## Test coverage - `TestPrepareDataWithCredentials::test_routing_model_keeps_alias_over_credentials_model` — alias survives the merge when two groups share one provider model - `TestPrepareDataWithCredentials::test_credentials_model_lands_in_data_without_routing_model` — direct-to-SDK sites still get the deployment model (#25104) - Updated the tenant-guard and vector store endpoint tests to assert the alias reaches dispatch instead of the underlying model `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/vector_store_endpoints/ tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_model_based_routing_files_batches.py tests/test_litellm/proxy/batches_endpoints/ tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_batch_x_litellm_model_encoding.py tests/test_litellm/proxy/openai_files_endpoint/` — 244 passed 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: ci: run the proxy search_endpoints tests in the endpoints shard
signals.text: ## What `tests/test_litellm/proxy/search_endpoints` is named by no job's test path. Adds it to the `proxy-endpoints` shard, alongside the 24 sibling `*_endpoints` directories it belongs with, and creates the directory as a package. ## Why `assert_ci_coverage` fails any PR that adds a test file under that directory — it is currently red on #36063 for exactly this reason: ``` ERROR: test files that no CI job invokes - tests/test_litellm/proxy/search_endpoints: 2 test file(s) invoked by no job ``` The gate is correct: without a shard entry those tests would be committed and then never run. Splitting the wiring out here so #36063 stays a behaviour change and this stays a CI change. ## Why the empty `__init__.py` The shard runs `pytest <paths...>`, and pytest exits 4 on a path that does not exist. `tests/test_litellm/proxy/search_endpoints` does not exist on `litellm_internal_staging` yet, so adding the path alone would turn `proxy-endpoints` red on this branch and make the two PRs merge-order dependent. Creating the directory as a package makes this PR green on its own and lets the two land in either order. It also closes a real gap: every other `*_endpoints` test directory carries an `__init__.py` and this one did not, so its `test_endpoints.py` would have been imported as a top-level `test_endpoints` module rather than a qualified one. ## Verification Run locally against this branch: - `python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py` → exit 0, `OK: 2363 test files and 10 Dockerfiles ...` - `pytest <the 26 shard paths> --collect-only` → exit 0, 6945 tests collected, every path resolves - With #36063's test files present, `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/search_endpoints` → 20 passed; run alongside `video_endpoints`, `google_endpoints` and `agent_endpoints` (which each also have a `test_endpoints.py`) → 263 passed, no import collision

signals.title: fix(proxy): read through to the DB on registry misses so just-created models, guardrails, and agents resolve on sibling replicas
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Objects created on one replica 400/404 on sibling replicas for seconds - Hits models, guardrails, A2A agents, and access group creation - Access group writes could falsely 500 during concurrent reloads - A failed refresh could silently drop a model a replica was serving How it solves it: - On a registry miss, the replica re-reads the object from the DB - It loads the object into its in-memory registry and retries once - A 2s negative cache and a 20-per-5s resync budget shield the DB - Access group verdicts read the reload's own atomic snapshot - A failed model refresh restores the previously served deployment - Resyncs honor `supported_db_objects` and take the reload's reconcile locks - An unknown A2A agent miss no longer consumes the model resync budget ## User Flow Before: an admin running two gateway replicas behind one URL creates an object, and the very next call that uses it fails whenever the load balancer picks the other replica; access group writes racing a reload can also return a false 500 and knock a serving model off a replica 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/model/new` with the admin key and `{"model_name": "team-gpt", "litellm_params": {"model": "openai/gpt-4o-mini", ...}}` and get 200 with the new deployment id 2. They immediately send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with `{"model": "team-gpt", ...}` and, when the other replica answers, get `400 "Invalid model name passed in model=team-gpt. Call /v1/models to view available models for your key."` (`/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages` fail the same way) 3. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/access_group/new` with `{"access_group": "prod-models", "model_names": ["team-gpt"]}` and get `400 {"error": "Model(s) not found: team-gpt"}` 4. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/guardrails` registering `pii-filter` and get 200 with a guardrail id 5. They immediately send `POST https://litellm-domain/guardrails/apply_guardrail` with `{"guardrail_name": "pii-filter", "text": "..."}` and get `404 "Guardrail 'pii-filter' not found. Please ensure the guardrail is configured in your LiteLLM proxy."` 6. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/agents` registering an agent and get 200 with an `agent_id` like `6d27a7e1-0aa6-...` 7. They immediately send `POST https://litellm-domain/a2a/{agent_id}` with JSON-RPC `message/send` and get `{"error": {"code": -32000, "message": "Agent '6d27a7e1-...' not found"}}` 8. Later, while routine model updates land in parallel, they send `POST https://litellm-domain/access_group/new` naming a model the answering replica already serves and occasionally get `500 {"error": "Access group 'prod-models' was saved to the database, but model id(s) [...] that this pod was serving are no longer live after the reload it triggered. ..."}` even though the write saved, and the named model can then stop serving on that replica (chat calls on it 400) until the next background reload 9. Retrying each failed call a few seconds later succeeds once the replicas catch up, so their provisioning scripts need sleeps and still flake After: the same admin runs the same sequence and every immediate follow-up call succeeds no matter which replica answers, and access group writes racing a reload stay 200 with no serving gap 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/model/new` with the admin key and `{"model_name": "team-gpt", "litellm_params": {"model": "openai/gpt-4o-mini", ...}}` and get 200 with the new deployment id 2. They immediately send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with `{"model": "team-gpt", ...}` and get 200 with a real completion from the new deployment, on whichever replica the call lands (`/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages` likewise) 3. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/access_group/new` with `{"access_group": "prod-models", "model_names": ["team-gpt"]}` and get `200 {"access_group": "prod-models", ..., "models_updated": 1}` 4. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/guardrails` registering `pii-filter` and get 200 with a guardrail id 5. They immediately send `POST https://litellm-domain/guardrails/apply_guardrail` and get `200 {"response_text": "..."}` 6. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/agents` registering an agent and get 200 with an `agent_id` 7. They immediately send `POST https://litellm-domain/a2a/{agent_id}` with JSON-RPC `message/send` and get a JSON-RPC result carrying the agent's real reply 8. The same access group writes racing parallel model updates return `200 {..., "models_updated": 1}` every time, and the models they name keep serving throughout 9. No sleeps or retry loops needed; provision-then-use flows pass deterministically ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5791 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Setup: two proxies booted from the same checkout sharing one fresh Postgres (`store_model_in_db: true`, no Redis), replica A and replica B on separate high ports. Every "create on A" is immediately followed by a "use on B" curl, which is exactly the cross-replica race from the 2-replica e2e suite. All LLM calls hit the real OpenAI API with `gpt-4o-mini` and cost real $ ```bash A=http://localhost:<portA>; B=http://localhost:<portB> K="Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY"; J="Content-Type: application/json" ``` ### Before (6d32d4081d) #### model created on A, immediate /v1/chat/completions on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/model/new -H "$K" -H "$J" -d '{"model_name": "lit5791-miss-2272", "litellm_params": {"model": "openai/gpt-4o-mini", "api_key": "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY"}}'` returns 200 with `"model_id": "a3d0f437-8e53-4bee-936b-0511f3c4732c"` 2. `curl -X POST $B/chat/completions -H "$K" -H "$J" -d '{"model": "lit5791-miss-2272", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "say hi"}]}'` returns HTTP 400: `/chat/completions: Invalid model name passed in model=lit5791-miss-2272. Call /v1/models to view available models for your key.` #### model created on A, immediate /v1/responses on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/model/new ...` (fresh name `lit5791-before-responses-971`) returns 200 2. `curl -X POST $B/v1/responses -H "$K" -H "$J" -d '{"model": "lit5791-before-responses-971", "input": "Reply with exactly: read-through works"}'` returns HTTP 400: `/responses: Invalid model name passed in model=lit5791-before-responses-971. ...` #### model created on A, immediate /v1/messages on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/model/new ...` (fresh name `lit5791-before-messages-591`) returns 200 2. `curl -X POST $B/v1/messages -H "$K" -H "$J" -d '{"model": "lit5791-before-messages-591", "max_tokens": 32, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: read-through works"}]}'` returns HTTP 400: `anthropic_messages: Invalid model name passed in model=lit5791-before-messages-591. ...` #### guardrail created on A, applied on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/guardrails -H "$K" -H "$J" -d '{"guardrail": {"guardrail_name": "lit5791-guard-7957", "litellm_params": {"guardrail": "litellm_content_filter", "mode": "pre_call", "default_on": false, "blocked_words": [{"keyword": "zebra", "action": "BLOCK"}]}}}'` returns 200 2. `curl -X POST $B/guardrails/apply_guardrail -H "$K" -H "$J" -d '{"guardrail_name": "lit5791-guard-7957", "text": "hello world"}'` returns HTTP 404: `Guardrail 'lit5791-guard-7957' not found. Please ensure the guardrail is configured in your LiteLLM proxy.` #### A2A agent created on A, message/send on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/v1/agents -H "$K" -H "$J" -d '{"agent_name": "lit5791-agent-13316", "agent_card_params": {...}, "litellm_params": {"custom_llm_provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-4o-mini"}}'` returns 200 with `"agent_id": "ff8a3a61-4c0c-4acd-b904-4928768e5dd1"` 2. `curl -X POST $B/a2a/lit5791-agent-13316 -H "$K" -H "$J" -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "1", "method": "message/send", "params": {"message": {"role": "user", "parts": [{"kind": "text", "text": "Reply with exactly: a2a works"}], "messageId": "m1"}}}'` returns HTTP 404: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32000,"message":"Agent 'lit5791-agent-13316' not found"}}` #### model created on A, access group naming it on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/model/new ...` (fresh name `lit5791-xag-14571`) returns 200 2. `curl -X POST $B/access_group/new -H "$K" -H "$J" -d '{"access_group": "lit5791-xg", "model_names": ["lit5791-xag-14571"]}'` returns HTTP 400: `{"detail":{"error":"Model(s) not found: lit5791-xag-14571"}}` #### unknown model on B keeps failing with 400 1. `curl -X POST $B/chat/completions -H "$K" -H "$J" -d '{"model": "lit5791-never-created", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}'` returns HTTP 400: `/chat/completions: Invalid model name passed in model=lit5791-never-created. ...` #### concurrent access-group writes during reload churn 1. Seed two models on A, then run 150 iterations of two concurrent `curl -X POST $A/access_group/new ...` writes, each naming its own model 2. All 300 writes return 200 locally: the false 500 from the 2-replica e2e run (signature `Access group '...' was saved to the database, but model id(s) [...] that this pod was serving are no longer live after the reload it triggered`) needs multi-pod reload timing and did not trigger on a single box ### After (afeed48a70, re-run green at 790d645d34 after the staging merge and at f8a23aab09 after the guardrail-review fixes) #### model created on A, immediate /v1/chat/completions on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/model/new ...` (fresh name `lit5791-after-miss-26853`) returns 200 2. `curl -X POST $B/chat/completions -H "$K" -H "$J" -d '{"model": "lit5791-after-miss-26853", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: read-through works"}]}'` returns HTTP 200: `"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"read-through works","role":"assistant",...}}]` #### model created on A, immediate /v1/responses on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/model/new ...` (fresh name `lit5791-after-responses-*`) returns 200 2. `curl -X POST $B/v1/responses ...` (same payload shape as Before) returns HTTP 200 with a real response object: `{"id":"resp_b6eh-WdsfbALI5MzCTklqw...` #### model created on A, immediate /v1/messages on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/model/new ...` (fresh name `lit5791-after-messages-6846`) returns 200 2. `curl -X POST $B/v1/messages ...` (same payload shape as Before) returns HTTP 200: `{"id":"resp_...","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"lit5791-after-messages-6846",...}` #### guardrail created on A, applied on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/guardrails ...` (same payload shape as Before, fresh name) returns 200 2. `curl -X POST $B/guardrails/apply_guardrail ...` returns HTTP 200: `{"response_text":"hello world"}` #### A2A agent created on A, message/send on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/v1/agents ...` (same payload shape as Before, fresh name) returns 200 2. `curl -X POST $B/a2a/<agent_name> ...` returns HTTP 200: `{"id":"1","jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"kind":"message","role":"agent","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"a2a works"}],...}}` #### model created on A, access group naming it on B 1. `curl -X POST $A/model/new ...` (fresh name `lit5791-after-xag-815`) returns 200 2. `curl -X POST $B/access_group/new ...` returns HTTP 200: `{"access_group":"lit5791-after-xg-32490","model_names":["lit5791-after-xag-815"],"model_ids":null,"models_updated":1}` #### unknown model on B keeps failing with 400 1. `curl -X POST $B/chat/completions ...` with `lit5791-never-created` returns HTTP 400 with the identical error text, still immediate (the 2s negative cache absorbs repeats) #### concurrent access-group writes during reload churn 1. Seed two models on A, then run 100 iterations of two concurrent `curl -X POST $A/access_group/new ...` writes, each naming its own model 2. All 200 writes return 200 (`non-200 access-group writes: 0/200`), and both replica logs contain zero `Error upserting deployment` lines, so no deployment was dropped by the churn #### cross-replica risk probes at the same tip 1. `curl -X PUT $B/access_group/lit5791-risk-ag-3229/update ...` naming a model just created on A returns HTTP 200: `{"access_group":"lit5791-risk-ag-3229","model_names":["lit5791-risk-new-2527"],...,"models_updated":1}` 2. `curl $B/a2a/<agent_name>/.well-known/agent-card.json` for an agent created on A returns HTTP 200 with the full agent card 3. `curl -X DELETE $B/access_group/lit5791-risk-ag-3229/delete` returns HTTP 200: `{"models_updated":1,"message":"Access group 'lit5791-risk-ag-3229' deleted successfully"}` 4. `curl -X POST $B/rerank ...` with an unknown model returns HTTP 400 with the clean invalid-model error, so the retry wrapper regressed nothing on other route types 5. `curl -X POST $B/a2a/lit5791-agent-nobody-created ...` returns HTTP 404 JSON-RPC `-32000` `Agent 'lit5791-agent-nobody-created' not found`, and the miss does not consume the model resync budget ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats - The access group false 500 reproduces only under multi-pod CI timing - Locally it is covered by unit tests plus the 200-write loop above - Resyncs are budgeted at 20 per 5s per replica; excess misses fail as today ## Changes New `litellm/proxy/common_utils/registry_read_through.py` holds one small `RegistryReadThrough` primitive: an asyncio-locked "re-read from the DB, load into the local registry, answer whether the key exists now" step with a 2 second negative-result TTL, plus a global budget of 20 resyncs per 5 second window that fails closed (the miss stands, nothing is negative-cached) so a flood of distinct unknown names can never turn into a DB hot loop. Three singletons wrap it for the three registries Each resync fetches only the missing object. The model resync selects just the rows matching the missing name (by `model_name`, then `model_id`) and upserts them through the additive deployment loader; it never runs the delete-reconciling full router rebuild with a partial list, which would evict healthy deployments. The agent resync does a unique lookup by `agent_id`, then `agent_name`, including the object permission, and registers the row as-is. The guardrail resync goes through the same DB loader the periodic config reload uses Four miss sites consult it before giving up. The LLM request router retries routing once after a model read-through (covers `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, and every other route the shared router serves). The A2A agent card and `message/send` lookups go through the agent read-through, as does A2A model routing. `POST /guardrails/apply_guardrail` re-checks after a guardrail read-through. Access group create and update re-validate their model names after a model read-through and only then 400 Two hardenings close the reload race the 2-replica e2e suite hit. The router reload now returns an atomic snapshot of which model ids were still desired and live when it finished, and the access group endpoints judge their "saved but no longer serving" 500 against that snapshot instead of re-reading router state that a concurrent reload may have mutated. And `Router.upsert_deployment` restores the previously served deployment when replacing it fails under `ignore_invalid_deployments`, so a bad refresh degrades to the old config instead of silently dropping the model A follow-up commit (afeed48a70) closes three gaps review found in the first cut. The model resync now mutates the router under `MODEL_RECONCILE_LOCK`, the same lock the full reconcile snapshots and reconciles under, so a read-through upsert can no longer interleave with a reload and get evicted by its stale snapshot. A new `AGENT_RECONCILE_LOCK` serializes the agent resync with `_init_agents_in_db`'s fetch-and-rebuild, with a re-check under the lock so an agent is never registered twice. Every resync first consults `should_load_db_object` (extracted to module level from `ProxyConfig._should_load_db_object`, which never used instance state), so a deployment that excludes an object type via `supported_db_objects` is honored by the read-through exactly as by the reload. And the A2A raise sites mark `ProxyModelNotFoundError` as not retryable with a model read-through, so an unknown agent no longer burns a model resync on the way out. Each fix carries a regression test: lock-held assertions on both resyncs and the reload, gating skips per object type, a duplicate-registration guard, and a budget-preservation test on the A2A miss path Unit tests cover the primitive (negative TTL expiry, no negative caching on resync exceptions or budget exhaustion, concurrent misses coalescing into one resync), one regression test per miss site driving the real recovery path against fake DB rows, and the upsert rollback Two review findings at the merged tip are fixed in f8a23aab09. The guardrail read-through now filters to `status: "active"` in the DB query itself, mirroring the reload's `get_all_guardrails_from_db`, so a team-submitted `pending_review` guardrail can no longer be activated by requesting it on a sibling pod. And a new `GUARDRAIL_RECONCILE_LOCK` serializes the guardrail resync with `_init_guardrails_in_db`'s snapshot-through-reconcile, closing the same eviction race models and agents were already locked against. Both carry regression tests: a status-filter assertion on the resync query, and lock-held assertions on the resync and the reload ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] f8a23aab09 passes /live-pr-risk (re-run at the tip; includes a live probe that a registered pending_review guardrail stays 404 on both pods) <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches core proxy routing, model router reconciliation, and multi-replica consistency; changes are guarded by locks, budgets, and extensive tests but affect hot request paths. > > **Overview** > Fixes **stale in-memory registries** on sibling proxy replicas: after a model, guardrail, or agent is created on one pod, requests on another no longer 400/404 until the periodic reload. > > Adds **`registry_read_through`**: on a miss it loads the row from Postgres into the local registry (with a 2s negative cache and a 20-per-5s resync cap), then retries once. Wired into **LLM routing**, **A2A** lookups, **`apply_guardrail`**, and **access-group** model validation. Resyncs run under **`MODEL_RECONCILE_LOCK`** / **`AGENT_RECONCILE_LOCK`** and honor **`supported_db_objects`**. Unknown **A2A** agent errors skip model read-through. > > **Access-group** reload checks use **`ReconcileOutcome`** from `clear_cache` instead of a fresh router read, avoiding false 500s when concurrent reloads race. **`Router.upsert_deployment`** restores the previous deployment when an update fails under `ignore_invalid_deployments`. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 790d645d3462a6017820b9a85fc5cd0240828ec0. signals.title: fix(proxy): preserve repeated multipart form fields in get_form_data
signals.text: Fixes #35937 ## Problem `get_form_data()` in `litellm/proxy/common_utils/http_parsing_utils.py` (used by `/v1/audio/transcriptions`) called `dict(form)` on Starlette's `FormData` object before iterating it. `FormData` is a multidict that can hold multiple values under the same key, but `dict()` collapses repeated keys and silently keeps only the last one. The OpenAI SDK encodes `timestamp_granularities=["word", "segment"]` as two separate `timestamp_granularities[]=...` multipart fields, so the collapse meant only the second value ever reached litellm — matching the exact "last one wins" behavior reported. ## Fix Replaced `dict(form).items()` with `form.multi_items()` in `get_form_data()`, which preserves every repeated key/value pair from the original multidict. ## Testing Updated `tests/test_litellm/proxy/common_utils/test_http_parsing_utils.py::test_get_form_data` to use a real `starlette.datastructures.FormData` (the previous mock was a plain dict literal, which can't represent a duplicate key and never actually exercised the bug) and assert both `"word"` and `"segment"` survive. Also fixed `TestGetRequestBody::test_form_post_routes_to_form_data`, whose mock likewise needed a real `FormData` object to support `.multi_items()`. Verified as a genuine regression guard: reverting the fix makes `test_get_form_data` fail with `AssertionError: assert ['segment'] == ['word', 'segment']`; restoring the fix passes it again. ``` ============================= 57 passed in 8.24s ============================== ```

signals.title: fix(xai): bill from the cost xAI reports instead of recomputing it
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - xAI reports what it charged, LiteLLM ignores it - LiteLLM re-derives the number from tokens and list rates - Only `web_search_calls` is priced, other tool calls cost nothing - Cached prompt discounts are missing from the estimate - Streamed requests skip the tool surcharge entirely How it solves it: - Bill the amount xAI reports, when it sends one - Fall back to today's token and per-call math otherwise - Skip the search surcharge that amount already covers - Carry it on `usage.cost`, the channel every route reads ## User Flow Before: a developer running Grok with server side web search sees spend that does not match their xAI invoice 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "xai/grok-4-latest"` and `"tools": [{"type": "web_search"}]` 2. The answer comes back with the citations they asked for 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request is logged at a cost worked out from token counts, with a flat $0.005 added for every search the model ran 4. Their xAI console shows a smaller amount for that same request, and the gap grows with every search 5. They resend the request with `"stream": true` and get a third number in the logs, because the streamed route adds nothing for the searches at all After: the same request is logged at the amount xAI says it charged 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "xai/grok-4-latest"` and `"tools": [{"type": "web_search"}]` 2. The answer is unchanged 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request at the figure xAI reported, tokens and every server side tool call together 4. That figure matches what the xAI console shows for the same request 5. Resending with `"stream": true` logs that same figure, and so does the same request sent to https://litellm-domain/v1/responses ## Relevant issues Relates to #35829, which reports that a provider-reported `usage.cost` is trusted verbatim as USD and records phantom spend when the upstream denominates that field in something else. This PR does not widen that path, and it is worth being explicit about why - xAI does not report a bare cost float. It reports `usage.cost_in_usd_ticks`, an integer denominated by a documented constant of 10,000,000,000 ticks to the dollar (https://docs.x.ai/developers/cost-tracking) - Both the conversion and the validation happen inside the xAI adapter, before anything reaches `usage.cost`. `xai_reported_cost_in_usd()` accepts only a non-negative integer, refusing bool as an int subclass, and returns USD. A malformed, negative or absent value yields None and the request falls back to the existing pricing with the search surcharge left intact - So what lands on `usage.cost` here is an already validated USD amount derived from a field with a defined unit, not an arbitrary number of unknown denomination. #35829's failure mode is the generic path accepting the latter, and nothing in this PR loosens that One consequence is worth stating rather than leaving to be discovered: on the streaming path `streaming_handler.py::_propagate_usage_cost_to_hidden_params()` copies `usage.cost` into `_hidden_params`, and `response_cost_calculator()` returns that before `completion_cost()` runs, so `llms/xai/cost_calculator.py` is not consulted for streamed requests. That is safe here precisely because the conversion and the validation already happened in the adapter. The guard in the cost calculator covers the non-streaming path, where usage reaches it directly Nothing in the tracker reports the remaining xAI mismatch itself. I searched issues for xai, grok, live search, web search cost and cost_in_usd_ticks, and the only other xAI cost bug on file is #15338, which is about tiered token pricing and is already closed. So there is no issue to close here ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix To be clear about what this is: not a live capture, but a documented xAI usage payload replayed through the transformations and then through the cost path spend tracking calls, at both commits. I do not have an xAI key with server side search billing enabled to capture a real invoice against. The curl commands a reviewer can run against a live proxy are at the end, and I am happy to add that run if you would rather have it ```python import httpx from unittest.mock import Mock import litellm from litellm.litellm_core_utils.streaming_handler import CustomStreamWrapper from litellm.llms.xai.chat.transformation import XAIChatCompletionStreamingHandler, XAIChatConfig from litellm.llms.xai.responses.transformation import XAIResponsesAPIConfig from litellm.responses.utils import ResponseAPILoggingUtils from litellm.types.utils import Choices, Message, ModelResponse TICKS = 137560000 TOOL_DETAILS = {"web_search_calls": 12, "x_search_calls": 0, "code_execution_calls": 0} CHAT_USAGE = {"prompt_tokens": 6153, "completion_tokens": 412, "total_tokens": 6565, "server_side_tool_usage_details": TOOL_DETAILS, "cost_in_usd_ticks": TICKS} def _chat_body(usage): return {"id": "chatcmpl-xai", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 0, "model": "grok-4-latest", "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "x"}, "finish_reason": "stop"}], "usage": usage} def _billed(usage): r = ModelResponse(id="p", model="grok-4-latest", object="chat.completion", created=0, choices=[Choices(index=0, message=Message(role="assistant", content="x"), finish_reason="stop")]) r.usage = usage return litellm.completion_cost(completion_response=r, model="xai/grok-4-latest", custom_llm_provider="xai", call_type="completion") chat = XAIChatConfig().transform_response( model="grok-4-latest", raw_response=httpx.Response(status_code=200, json=_chat_body(CHAT_USAGE)), model_response=ModelResponse(), logging_obj=Mock(), request_data={}, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "x"}], optional_params={}, litellm_params={}, encoding=None) parsed = XAIChatCompletionStreamingHandler(streaming_response=iter([]), sync_stream=True).chunk_parser( {"id": "chatcmpl-xai", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 0, "model": "grok-4-latest", "choices": [], "usage": CHAT_USAGE}) assembled = litellm.stream_chunk_builder(chunks=[parsed]) CustomStreamWrapper._propagate_usage_cost_to_hidden_params(assembled) streamed = litellm.cost_calculator.response_cost_calculator( response_object=assembled, model="grok-4-latest", custom_llm_provider="xai", call_type="completion", optional_params={}, cache_hit=None, base_model=None) responses = XAIResponsesAPIConfig().transform_response_api_response( model="grok-4-latest", raw_response=httpx.Response(status_code=200, json={ "id": "resp_xai", "object": "response", "created_at": 0, "model": "grok-4-latest", "status": "completed", "output": [], "parallel_tool_calls": False, "tool_choice": "auto", "tools": [], "usage": {"input_tokens": 6153, "output_tokens": 412, "total_tokens": 6565, "server_side_tool_usage_details": TOOL_DETAILS, "cost_in_usd_ticks": TICKS}}), logging_obj=Mock()) responses_usage = ResponseAPILoggingUtils._transform_response_api_usage_to_chat_usage(responses.usage) print(f"xAI reported for this request: ${TICKS / 1e10:.6f}") print(f" /v1/chat/completions billed: ${_billed(chat.usage):.6f}") print(f" /v1/chat/completions (stream) billed: ${streamed:.6f}") print(f" /v1/responses billed: ${_billed(responses_usage):.6f}") ``` Before, at base `55777d0e80`: ``` xAI reported for this request: $0.013756 /v1/chat/completions billed: $0.084639 /v1/chat/completions (stream) billed: $0.024639 /v1/responses billed: $0.084639 ``` After, at `78112c0b1d`: ``` xAI reported for this request: $0.013756 /v1/chat/completions billed: $0.013756 /v1/chat/completions (stream) billed: $0.013756 /v1/responses billed: $0.013756 ``` On the two non streamed routes the 12 searches were charged at $0.005 each, $0.06 on top of the $0.0246 token estimate, against the $0.0138 xAI actually charged. The streamed route dropped the searches entirely and priced from tokens alone, which is why it landed somewhere else again. All three now agree with the provider To run it against a live proxy with a real xAI key instead, with `XAI_API_KEY` set and the proxy started as in CLAUDE.md: ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"xai/grok-4-latest","tools":[{"type":"web_search"}], "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What did xAI ship this week? cite sources"}]}' \ | python -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print("ticks:", d["usage"].get("cost_in_usd_ticks"), "-> $", d["usage"].get("cost_in_usd_ticks",0)/1e10)' curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"xai/grok-4-latest","tools":[{"type":"web_search"}], "input":"What did xAI ship this week? cite sources"}' | python -m json.tool | grep -i cost ``` then open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs and compare the logged spend for those two requests against https://console.x.ai usage for the same minute ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Since #30817 the xAI cost calculator counts server side searches from `usage.server_side_tool_usage_details.web_search_calls` and prices them at xAI's published $5 per 1,000 calls, falling back to that list rate because no xai entry in the price map carries `search_context_cost_per_query`. That is the right rate for that one tool, and LiteLLM is still doing xAI's arithmetic for it Every xAI response already states the amount charged, in `usage.cost_in_usd_ticks`, at 10^10 ticks to the dollar. Per xAI's [cost tracking docs](https://docs.x.ai/developers/cost-tracking) that single figure is "the actual amount billed, after all applicable discounts (including prompt caching reductions) have been applied, and inclusive of all token costs and server-side tool invocation costs". This PR reads it and prices the request from it, which is the shape `llms/perplexity/cost_calculator.py` already uses for a provider that reports its own cost. `get_cost_for_web_search_request` needed no change, because the xAI calculator now returns 0 for the search surcharge once the reported total has been applied, the same way the perplexity branch two lines above it does Three things the re-derived number cannot reach, all of which the reported one already accounts for. xAI's [pricing page](https://docs.x.ai/developers/pricing) lists Web Search, X Search and Code Execution at $5 per 1,000 calls, Collections Search at $2.50 and File Attachments at $10, but only `web_search_calls` is priced today, so a request whose `server_side_tool_usage_details` reports `x_search_calls` or `code_execution_calls` is billed nothing for them. Prompt caching is the second: `xai/grok-4` and `xai/grok-4-latest` carry no `cache_read_input_token_cost`, so cached input is priced at the full $3 per 1M while xAI has already discounted it. The third is drift, since each of those rates needs a matching LiteLLM change every time xAI revises one The conversion lives in the xAI chat and responses transformations, which restate the ticks in USD on `usage.cost`. That is the field litellm already carries a provider stated cost in, and using it is what keeps this change inside the provider adapter: `ResponseAPILoggingUtils` already copies `usage.cost` onto the chat Usage for `/v1/responses`, and the streaming chunk assembler already carries `cost` through aggregation, so neither had to learn an xAI wire field. An earlier revision of this PR instead invented a parallel channel and taught `litellm/responses/utils.py` to preserve unmodelled provider fields, which changed `/v1/responses` for every provider to serve one. That is gone; the diff is now entirely under `litellm/llms/xai/` and its mirrored tests Without a reported figure nothing changes: the existing token math and the existing per-call search surcharge both run exactly as before Only the documented shape of that field is trusted, a non-negative integer, with bool refused since it is an int subclass. A caller who can set `api_base` controls the response body, so a negative amount would otherwise be billed as negative and subtracted from that caller's own recorded spend, slipping past a budget. Anything that is not a non-negative integer falls back to token pricing with the search surcharge still applied What that check cannot do is make a self-hosted `api_base` trustworthy, and neither can token pricing: the token counts come from the same response body, so an endpoint reporting `"prompt_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens": 0` already logs $0 today. Trusting a reported total hands such a caller nothing they did not already have, and it is the exposure the perplexity calculator has carried for a while On #35829, which reports a nano denominated `usage.cost` recorded verbatim as $3,144,000 of spend: this PR is the narrow per provider opt in that issue asks for as its first suggested fix, "only trust `usage.cost` for providers where the calling code explicitly opts in (e.g. Perplexity's own `cost_calculator.py` already does this narrowly and correctly)". The unit is converted from xAI's documented tick unit before it ever reaches `usage.cost` rather than guessed, so the confusion in that report cannot arise on this path. The blanket trust in `response_cost_calculator` that the issue is actually about is untouched and still wants a decision above this file On why not put the price in `model_info`, as #24372 did for gemini: that was right for gemini, since Google does not tell you what it charged and a configured price is the only option there. xAI does tell you. Going that way means adding tool prices to all 44 xai entries and keeping every one of them current through each xAI revision, and it still cannot express what xAI bills, since the server side tools are charged per invocation across several distinct tools at different rates and the model decides how many of each to call Not touched: the model price maps, and any provider neutral file ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(search): add Amazon Bedrock AgentCore web search provider
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - No AWS-native web search provider in LiteLLM - Bedrock users need a third-party search key today - Web Search on Bedrock AgentCore speaks MCP, unsupported How it solves it: - Adds `agentcore` search provider calling an AgentCore Gateway - SigV4 for AWS_IAM gateways, bearer token for CUSTOM_JWT - Works for `/search` and for `websearch_interception` ## User Flow Before: a developer on AWS wants Claude Code on Bedrock to search the web, but pointing the proxy at their AgentCore Gateway does nothing and every working option needs a non-AWS search key 1. They add a search tool with `search_provider: agentcore` pointing at their AgentCore Gateway MCP endpoint and start the proxy; boot succeeds with no warning 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/search with `{"query": "latest AI developments", "search_tool_name": "agentcore-search", "max_results": 5}` and get HTTP 500 `'agentcore' is not a valid SearchProviders` 3. GET https://litellm-domain/search_tools/ui/available_providers lists 18 providers, every one a third-party service (Tavily, Exa, Perplexity, Brave, ...), and `agentcore` is absent 4. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with a `web_search` tool and their Bedrock model; HTTP 200 comes back, but the web search result block is empty and the assistant apologizes about a search provider configuration error 5. In Claude Code pointed at the proxy, WebSearch errors on screen both times it runs, returning no links or content After: the same developer points the proxy at their AgentCore Gateway and search works, with the search traffic staying inside AWS 1. They create an AgentCore Gateway with a `web-search` connector target and set `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL` to its MCP endpoint 2. They add the same search tool entry with `search_provider: agentcore` (see `litellm/proxy/example_config_yaml/agentcore_websearch_config.yaml`) and no third-party key, then start the proxy 3. The same POST https://litellm-domain/search returns HTTP 200 with 5 real results carrying `title`, `url`, `snippet`, `date` 4. GET https://litellm-domain/search_tools/ui/available_providers now includes `agentcore` ("Web Search on Amazon Bedrock") 5. The same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages returns a filled web search result block (10 results) and an answer built from them; the search leg is a SigV4-signed call to their own gateway, billed by AWS 6. In Claude Code, Web Search returns real results and the answer cites them 7. Pointing `api_base` at a host that is not their gateway, or at a plain `http://` URL, returns an error instead of sending the server's `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_TOKEN` or a SigV4 signature, and a caller-supplied `tool_name` that is not a `___WebSearch` connector tool is rejected ## Relevant issues Fixes #31819 Supersedes #34098, which this builds on Docs live in the docs repo and are already merged: BerriAI/litellm-docs#834, plus BerriAI/litellm-docs#949 for the MCP protocol version env var Follow-up filed while QA'ing this PR: #37538 (the search router silently drops provider-specific yaml `litellm_params` for every search provider; pre-existing, untouched here) ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5375 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both runs hit a real AgentCore Gateway (`litellm-qa-agentcore-tez4ymmxfc`, us-east-1, `web-search` connector target, provisioned for this QA and deleted after) and real Bedrock Claude, no mocks or stubs anywhere. Shared setup, identical for both sides except the commit the proxy was booted from: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-sonnet litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 aws_region_name: us-east-1 search_tools: - search_tool_name: agentcore-search litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: https://litellm-qa-agentcore-tez4ymmxfc.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp - search_tool_name: agentcore-untrusted litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: https://untrusted-host.example.com/mcp - search_tool_name: agentcore-badtool litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: https://litellm-qa-agentcore-tez4ymmxfc.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp tool_name: my-target___ListFiles - search_tool_name: agentcore-plaintext litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: http://gw.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp litellm_settings: callbacks: ["websearch_interception"] websearch_interception_params: enabled_providers: ["bedrock"] search_tool_name: agentcore-search ``` Env for both proxies: `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL` (the real gateway), SigV4 credentials, `AWS_REGION=us-east-1`, and `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` for the Bedrock model call. Before proxy booted from the merge base on port 46526, After proxy from the PR tip on port 26793. Claude Code runs are the real TUI (v2.1.236) driven interactively under tmux with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointed at the proxy ### Before (2059033352de) #### POST /search through the configured agentcore search tool 1. `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:46526/search -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-before-7731' -d '{"query": "latest AI developments", "search_tool_name": "agentcore-search", "max_results": 5}'` 2. ```json {"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: 'agentcore' is not a valid SearchProviders
Traceback (most recent call last):

...ValueError: 'agentcore' is not a valid SearchProviders
. Received Model Group=agentcore-search
Available Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}} ``` HTTP 500. The proxy had booted cleanly with all four agentcore search tools configured, so the failure only surfaces at request time #### Provider discovery 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:46526/search_tools/ui/available_providers -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-before-7731'` 2. 18 providers returned (`perplexity, tavily, parallel_ai, exa_ai, brave, google_pse, dataforseo, firecrawl, fastcrw, searxng, linkup, duckduckgo, searchapi, serper, you_com, apiserpent, tinyfish, nimble`), `agentcore` absent #### /v1/messages with the Anthropic web_search tool on real Bedrock Claude 1. `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:46526/v1/messages -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-before-7731' -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":1024,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Use the web_search tool to look up the latest LiteLLM release, then list the result titles you got."}],"tools":[{"type":"web_search_20250305","name":"web_search","max_uses":2}]}'` 2. HTTP 200, but the `web_search_tool_result` block came back empty (`"content":[]`) and the assistant text was: `The web search tool encountered an error on my end (a configuration issue with the search provider — "'agentcore' is not a valid SearchProviders") and was unable to return any results.` 3. Proxy log: `WebSearchInterception: Search failed for 'latest LiteLLM release': litellm.APIConnectionError: 'agentcore' is not a valid SearchProviders` #### Interactive Claude Code under tmux 1. Asked Claude Code (real TUI under tmux, proxy as `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) to look up the latest LiteLLM release with web search; its WebFetch fallback was denied so the search path stayed the thing under test 2. It ran WebSearch twice, both erroring. On-screen output: ``` ⏺ That search attempt returned an internal error rather than real results ... ⏺ The search tool itself is erroring out (backend misconfiguration, not fixable from my end). ⏺ Here's what happened: I ran WebSearch twice ... Both times, the tool returned no actual search results — instead it came back with an error saying an invalid search provider ("agentcore") was configured on the backend. No links or content were retrieved either time. ``` #### Credential and tool-name guards 1. Not reachable at this commit: every agentcore search tool already fails with the provider error above, so no credentialed request to a gateway can be produced at all ### After (70a4f9a7) The PR tip 7744b9100e differs from 70a4f9a7 only by a comment edit in the example config (nothing loads that file at runtime or in tests), so this run stands for the tip #### POST /search through the configured agentcore search tool 1. `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/search -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-after-9917' -d '{"query": "latest AI developments", "search_tool_name": "agentcore-search", "max_results": 5}'` 2. Now includes `{"provider_name": "agentcore", "ui_friendly_name": "Web Search on Amazon Bedrock"}` #### /v1/messages with the Anthropic web_search tool on real Bedrock Claude 1. `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/v1/messages -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-after-9917' -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":1024,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Use the web_search tool to look up the latest LiteLLM release, then list the result titles you got."}],"tools":[{"type":"web_search_20250305","name":"web_search","max_uses":2}]}'` 2. Proxy log attributes that exact query to a `tools/call` against the real gateway; no other search backend existed in the environment #### Credential and tool-name guards 1. Untrusted host: `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/v1/search/agentcore-untrusted ...` returned HTTP 500 with no request sent: `Refusing to send SigV4-signed AgentCore requests to 'https://untrusted-host.example.com/mcp': it is neither an AgentCore gateway hostname nor the host in AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL. Set AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL to authorize a custom gateway hostname.` 2. Plaintext transport: `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/v1/search/agentcore-plaintext ...` returned HTTP 500 with no request sent: `Refusing to send AgentCore credentials over plaintext HTTP to 'http://gw.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp': a bearer token or SigV4 signature would be readable in transit. Use an https gateway URL (plain http is allowed only for localhost).` 3. Tool-name guard, exercised via env var: with `AGENTCORE_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME=my-target___ListFiles` exported, `/v1/search/agentcore-search` refused with `Invalid AgentCore search tool_name 'my-target___ListFiles': must end with '___WebSearch' (a web-search connector tool). Other gateway tools cannot be invoked through this provider.` 4. The `agentcore-badtool` yaml entry did NOT trigger that guard: it returned HTTP 200 because the search router forwards only `search_provider`/`api_key`/`api_base` from yaml `litellm_params` and dropped the `tool_name`, so the request went out with the default tool name. That plumbing predates this PR and hits every search provider; filed as #37538, and the example config here no longer advertises yaml knobs the router drops. The guard itself stays load-bearing for the reachable paths: request-body `tool_name`, the env var, and SDK calls Observations from the runs, for the reviewer: - Provider-only /search body 500s; pre-existing validation; PR leaves alone - Interception search failure still answers HTTP 200; pre-existing; PR leaves alone - Unknown search_provider passes proxy boot silently; pre-existing; PR leaves alone - Router drops extra yaml litellm_params (#37538); pre-existing; PR leaves alone - Guard refusals surface as HTTP 500 with tracebacks; pre-existing error shape; PR leaves alone - Gateway result dates occasionally nonsense ("April 12 2000"); upstream data; PR leaves alone ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Admin UI search-tool form has no `api_base` field, so UI setup needs `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL` - Cost map entry is $0 per query, AWS bills the gateway directly - `tool_name` and aws credential overrides work per request or via env vars, not yaml (#37538) ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR ## Changes `AgentCoreSearchConfig` (`litellm/llms/bedrock/search/transformation.py`) is a `BaseSearchConfig` that speaks MCP instead of a bespoke REST API: `transform_search_request` builds a JSON-RPC `tools/call` body, and `transform_search_response` accepts both a plain JSON reply and the Streamable HTTP SSE framing, picking the event that carries `result` or `error` so a progress notification can't shadow the response. ```python {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "web-search-tool___WebSearch", "arguments": {"query": query[:200], "maxResults": max_results}}} ``` Results are parsed from the tool result's text blocks first, falling back to `result.structuredContent` (the web-search connector 1.1.0+ can return machine-readable results there while the text blocks carry prose). Requests go out with `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-03-26`, the version a gateway with a default `protocolConfiguration` accepts, overridable via `AGENTCORE_MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION` for gateways pinning `supportedVersions`. Signing needed a new optional hook, because a SigV4 signature covers the exact bytes on the wire: ```python class BaseSearchConfig: def sign_request(self, headers, optional_params, request_data, api_base, api_key=None) -> tuple[dict, bytes | None]: return headers, None # default no-op ``` `BaseLLMHTTPHandler.search` / `async_search` call it and, when a signed body comes back, send it verbatim as `data=` rather than re-serializing it through `json=`. Three things the gateway makes easy to get wrong, all covered by tests: a caller-supplied `tool_name` must end in `___WebSearch`, so this provider can't be used to invoke unrelated tools on the same gateway with the proxy's credentials; server-managed credentials, both `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_TOKEN` and a SigV4 signature, only go to a trusted host (a real `*.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.<region>.amazonaws.com` hostname or the host in `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL`, which is how a custom or private gateway hostname gets authorized); and credentials only ride https, with plain http refused unless the host is localhost, so neither token nor signature is readable in transit. A `tools/call` that fails in-band, HTTP 200 with `result.isError`, raises instead of looking like a search with no results. The signing region comes from the gateway hostname, falling back to the AWS config chain and erroring out rather than guessing a region the gateway would reject. `api_key=""` is passed down to `BaseAWSLLM._sign_request` so the Bedrock Runtime `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` never leaks to an AgentCore endpoint. Also adds `agentcore/search` to the cost map (AWS bills the gateway directly) and an example proxy config wiring it into `websearch_interception` for Bedrock Claude Code. Search `pre_call` logs the headers as they were before signing, so a configured `logger_fn` never sees the SigV4 or bearer `Authorization` value; only the outbound request carries it Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/902d85f7efbc4becb45d3340ad7c6782 Requested by: @yassin-berriai - [x] 7744b9100ef68f43ab87ca8eb5b1b8d8b117ddc3 passes /live-pr-risk

signals.title: fix(responses-bridge): preserve reasoning input items as reasoning_content
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Responses `/v1/responses` requests that replay `type: "reasoning"` input items are mishandled by the chat-completions bridge - Plaintext reasoning leaks into ordinary message content or is silently dropped - DeepSeek V4 and Kimi K2.6 reject or lose context when prior `reasoning_content` is not passed back How it solves it: - Reasoning input items are converted to assistant `reasoning_content` - Standalone reasoning merges into the following assistant turn, or is preserved before a user turn - Opaque encrypted-only items are skipped instead of polluting the prompt - Guardrail text extraction and redaction now cover reasoning content and summary blocks ## User Flow Before: a developer reuses a prior response's reasoning item in a new stateless `/v1/responses` request and the model loses its chain of thought 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with an `input` array containing a `type: "reasoning"` item followed by a user message 2. LiteLLM forwards the reasoning text as ordinary message content, or drops it 3. The model answers without the prior reasoning, and DeepSeek V4 can return HTTP 400 with `reasoning_content must be passed back` After: the same request preserves the reasoning as `reasoning_content` 1. They send the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` body 2. LiteLLM emits the reasoning on an assistant `reasoning_content` field, merging it with the following assistant turn when one exists 3. The model receives the prior chain-of-thought and answers correctly ## Relevant issues - #36197 — reasoning items (including `encrypted_content`) are silently dropped for non-native Responses providers - Related PR: #27630 (drop-based alternative handling of the same input item) ## Linear ticket <!-- leave blank if no Linear ticket --> ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (lint/format/unit passed locally; CI re-running on the rebased head) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 (5/5 on the latest head) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live smoke after the fix (original capture at commit `f6c0cbb49a`; same code rebased onto `litellm_internal_staging` as `2d4e6afe1c` with the guardrail coverage fix): ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "BLSC/DeepSeek-V4-Flash", "input": [ {"type": "reasoning", "id": "rs_1", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "The secret word is BLUEBERRY."}]}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is the secret word? Answer with one word."} ], "store": true, "max_output_tokens": 256, "stream": false }' ``` Result: HTTP 200, `status: "completed"`, no provider rejection. Guardrail regression coverage: `iter_message_text`, `walk_user_text`, and `build_inspection_messages` now see reasoning `content` and `summary` text; the new tests assert both inspection and in-place redaction. Full local suite: `54 passed` for the targeted guardrail + reasoning bridge tests; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on the changed files; all three repo gates pass locally. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `_transform_responses_api_input_item_to_chat_completion_message` handles `type: "reasoning"` explicitly - `_extract_reasoning_text_from_input_item` extracts plaintext from `content` or `summary` blocks - `_merge_reasoning_only_assistant_messages` merges standalone reasoning into the following assistant turn, preserving chronology when that turn already has `reasoning_content` - `litellm/proxy/guardrails/_content_utils.py` inspects and rewrites reasoning content/summary text so guardrails see every plaintext shape the bridge forwards - New unit tests cover item shapes, merging, preservation, non-reasoning regressions, and guardrail coverage ## QA runbook N/A — this PR adds mocked unit tests, not e2e tests. The live proof above was captured manually. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
