signals.title: fix(shadow_eval): read completed once the turn budget is spent, not stopped
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A budget-exhausted shadow eval keeps showing "running" forever - Starting the next eval flips it to "stopped", looking like a termination - Timestamp inference could misreport an explicit stop as completion, in ever-smaller corners each review round How it solves it: - Expose each job's attempt count on list and detail reads - Status derives "completed" once attempts reach max_turns, matching the sampler - stopped_at was doing two jobs: index slot marker and stop marker - A new internal released_at column takes over slot bookkeeping - Sweeps write only released_at, so any stopped_at now means stopped, always - stopped_by records who; the migration backfills legacy rows that displayed stopped - Counts are only consulted for unstamped jobs; no stamp-vs-count reasoning remains - All raw-SQL stamps and comparisons use UTC like every other writer ## User Flow Before: an admin's finished eval looks alive until they start another one, which then appears to kill it 1. They start a shadow eval from http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=cost-optimization with a 200 turn budget 2. The eval judges its 200th turn and stops sampling on its own 3. The page keeps showing the eval as "running" indefinitely, days later included 4. They start a second eval on another key via the same form, which returns 201 5. The first eval's card instantly flips to "stopped", as if starting the new eval terminated it After: a finished eval reports itself finished, and later evals leave it alone 1. They start a shadow eval from http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=cost-optimization with a 200 turn budget 2. The eval judges its 200th turn and stops sampling on its own 3. On the next refresh the card reads "completed", with no admin action 4. They start a second eval on another key via the same form, which returns 201 5. The first eval's card still reads "completed"; "stopped" now only ever means someone pressed Stop ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Setup: proxy from this repo against a Postgres DB, config with `auto_router1` (complexity router over gpt-5 family deployments) and a deterministic OpenAI-compatible upstream. Same commands both sides; only the checked-out commit differs. `max_turns: 1` with 100% sampling so two chat turns exhaust the budget immediately ```bash curl -sX POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -d '{"key_alias": "shadowstatus-qa"}' curl -sX POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -d '{"api_key_id": "<token_id from key/generate>", "router_name": "auto_router1", "shadow_percentage": 100.0, "judge_model": "gpt-5-nano", "duration_days": 7, "max_turns": 1}' for i in 0 1; do curl -sX POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer <generated key>" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-5-mini", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi"}]}'; done curl -s http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" ``` ### Before (e75b4b1c2a) #### Budget exhaustion keeps reading running, then a new start flips it to stopped 1. Start returns 201, job `cmsz94j3m0000mgiu4ceug3h8`, status `running` 2. Both chat completions return 200; the sampler judges turn 1 of 1, exhausting the budget 3. GET /auto_router/shadow_eval polled 6 times over 30s: status stays `"running"`, `stopped_at: null`, every single poll 4. Start a second eval on the same key: 201, job `cmsz958wv0005mgiu71x7lv4n` 5. GET /auto_router/shadow_eval now shows the first job as `"stopped"` with `stopped_at` set: the new start is what visibly "terminated" it #### Attempts racing an explicit stop 1. No completed-by-budget state exists at this commit, so the case does not apply; it guards the review findings on this PR's earlier commits, where an attempt landing around the stop could flip a stopped job to `"completed"` ### After (2043578171; tip e43e3bdfd1 only moves a lint suppression, no runtime change) #### Budget exhaustion reads completed on its own, and a new start leaves it alone 1. Start returns 201 with a 1 turn budget, status `running` 2. Both chat completions return 200; the sampler judges turn 1 of 1, exhausting the budget 3. GET /auto_router/shadow_eval on the next poll: status `"completed"`, `attempt_count: 2`, `stopped_at: null`, `stopped_by: null`; no sweep or admin action needed 4. Start a second eval on the same key: 201 5. GET /auto_router/shadow_eval keeps the first job `"completed"` and its `stopped_at` stays null; the sweep freed the slot through the internal released_at column #### Attempts racing an explicit stop never reclassify it as completed 1. POST /auto_router/shadow_eval/{job}/stop on a running 5-turn job returns 200, status `"stopped"`, `stopped_by` recording the operator 2. Simulate the in-flight race at its worst: insert 6 attempt rows timestamped one second before `stopped_at`, taking the count to 6, over the 5 turn budget 3. GET list keeps status `"stopped"` with `attempt_count: 6`; the recorded stop outranks budget arithmetic, so no attempt timing can turn a stop into completion #### A rolling-deploy stop written without stopped_by still reads stopped 1. Insert a job shaped like an old pod's stop mid-deploy: bare `stopped_at`, no `stopped_by`, 5 attempts against a 5 turn budget 2. GET detail reads `"stopped"`: a stamp means a stop, unconditionally, because budget and window completion no longer write `stopped_at` at all #### A legacy stop with overshoot is closed by the migration backfill 1. Insert a pre-column shaped job: `stopped_at` set a day ago, `stopped_by` null, 6 attempts against a 5 turn budget, window still open 2. GET detail reads `"completed"`: the exact misread the review flagged 3. Run the migration's backfill (`SET stopped_by = 'unknown' WHERE stopped_at IS NOT NULL AND ends_at > now-utc`) 4. GET detail now reads `"stopped"` with `stopped_by: "unknown"`, permanently ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Adds two nullable columns: stopped_by (who stopped it) and released_at (internal slot bookkeeping); the unique index moves to released_at and the migration backfills both for existing rows - The only mixed-version residue left: a job swept by a pre-column pod during the deploy minutes reads stopped instead of completed, the safe direction - attempt_count includes errored attempts, matching the sampler's budget arithmetic - The multi-key shadow eval PR needs this derivation ported after merge ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit e43e3bdfd1fa0e9b07ebd5ed17f3ede8aeb5b024. signals.title: refactor(ui): migrate the key edit form off Ant Design onto react-hook-form
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Key editing was the last antd Form in the key flow - antd's store made the saved payload implicit, not stated - A control could silently stop feeding the payload undetected How it solves it: - Ports the form to react-hook-form and the shadcn primitives - Projects the payload explicitly, so every saved key is written out - Keeps the existing suite as the contract, unedited apart from query mechanics - A payload net written against the antd version passes unchanged ## User Flow This is a refactor, so the two flows are step-for-step identical and the saved key is byte-identical. What changes is the rendered control set Before: a proxy admin edits a virtual key and the form is drawn with Ant Design controls 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click a key, then Settings 2. The editor shows the antd controls: an antd multi-select for Models, antd selects for Key Type and Reset Budget, antd inputs for the limits 3. They change Key Alias, add a model, set Reset Budget, then click Save Changes 4. The key is saved and the row reflects the new alias and models After: the same admin edits the same key and the form is drawn with the dashboard's own controls 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click a key, then Settings 2. The editor shows the shadcn controls: a chips combobox for Models, dashboard selects for Key Type and Reset Budget, dashboard inputs for the limits 3. They change Key Alias, add a model, set Reset Budget, then click Save Changes 4. The key is saved and the row reflects the new alias and models, exactly as before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, run once in two terminals from the repo root: ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log ``` ```bash cd ui/litellm-dashboard && npm run dev ``` Then create the key both sides edit, so the starting record is the same: ```bash curl -sX POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"parity-probe","models":["gpt-4o"],"max_budget":10,"tpm_limit":100,"rpm_limit":10,"metadata":{"tags":["blue"]}}' ``` The capture is the same on both sides: open http://localhost:3000/?page=api-keys, click the `parity-probe` key, open Settings, open DevTools Network and filter on `key/update`, make exactly these edits, click Save Changes, then copy the request payload of the `POST /key/update` that fires. The edits, in order: set Key Alias to `parity-probe-edited`, add `gpt-4o-mini` to Models, set Reset Budget to `monthly`, set TPM Limit to `250`, tick Never Expire ### Before (MERGE_BASE_SHA) #### /key/update request payload, antd form 1. `git checkout MERGE_BASE_SHA` and restart the dev server 2. Run the capture above 3. Paste the request payload here #### the saved record 1. `curl -s "http://localhost:4000/key/info?key=<the generated key>" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` 2. Paste the response here ### After (TIP_SHA) #### /key/update request payload, react-hook-form 1. `git checkout TIP_SHA` and restart the dev server 2. Run the capture above against a freshly generated `parity-probe` key 3. Paste the request payload here, it should match the Before payload key for key #### the saved record 1. `curl -s "http://localhost:4000/key/info?key=<the generated key>" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` 2. Paste the response here Screenshots of the editor on both sides go under the matching case, so the control change is visible next to the identical payload ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - Seven tests had queries rewritten; antd selectors cannot match shadcn - Those seven are proven by mutation, not by passing both ways - MCP and Agent selectors are stubbed here, they remain antd - `TagsInput` still lives under the guardrails route folder - Several selector labels resolve to nothing, pre-existing, not fixed here - `TagsInput` and `MultiSelect` gained an optional `disabled` prop ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: test(ui): pin the MCP server edit save payload before the form migration
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Nothing asserts the MCP server edit save payload - No `toStrictEqual` anywhere, so key changes stay invisible - Upcoming form migration would change it silently How it solves it: - 19 cases pin the exact object sent to the server - Values captured from live behaviour, not read off the source - Six-mutant battery proves the net actually bites ## User Flow There is no user-visible change here, by design. This PR adds tests only, and the point of it is that the flow below stays byte-identical before and after. Both lists are therefore the same list Before: an admin edits an MCP server and saves 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and click an existing server 2. They change a field, say the auth type or the alias, and press Save Changes 3. The server updates and the row reflects the change After: unchanged 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and click an existing server 2. They change a field, say the auth type or the alias, and press Save Changes 3. The server updates and the row reflects the change ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This PR changes no runtime behaviour, so there is no live-proxy before and after to show. Stating that plainly rather than staging a run that would look identical on both sides The evidence that matters for a characterization net is whether it fails when the thing it pins changes. That is the mutation battery below, run at `9df4cafcfb`, six mutants applied one at a time to the payload builder in `mcp_server_edit.tsx`, each reverted before the next Every anchor was asserted unique before substitution, and every run was checked to have executed all 19 tests, so a mutant that silently failed to apply or broke the file would report as a harness fault instead of a kill. Two earlier mutants did exactly that and were caught by those guards | mutant | payload change | tests red | | --- | --- | --- | | M1 | leaks `created_by` into the body | 19 / 19 | | M2 | drops `logo_url` from `mcp_info` | 18 / 18 strict cases | | M3 | emits `allowed_tools` with the gate removed | 17 | | M4 | turns a flat key into a lodash path | 18 / 18 strict cases | | M5 | sends `null` where today it sends `undefined` | 18 / 18 strict cases | | M6 | sends `null` where today it sends `[]` | 18 / 18 strict cases | Kill rate 6/6. M3 spares the two allowlist cases because `allowed_tools` is present either way in one and the gate is the subject of the other. M1 is the only mutant the leak-guard case catches, which is what it exists for M5 is the one worth reading twice. It is caught only because the file uses `toStrictEqual`; `toEqual` treats a key holding `undefined` as absent, and that is precisely the distinction that separates a gated-off field from a mounted-but-empty one in this form today ## Type ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Records current behaviour, including anything currently wrong - `alias` assignment is dead, shadowed by `...restValues` - `mcp_access_groups` mapping is a no-op only while antd yields strings - Do not delete either during the migration; the second can revive - Integration tier, so roughly two seconds per case ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: test(ui): characterize the create key form payload contract
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The create-key suite mocked antd wholesale - Its fake form store submitted every value ever typed - Real antd submits only currently mounted fields - So the suite passed whatever the form actually sent - A form-library port could regress it undetected How it solves it: - Renders the real tree, stubs only the network boundary - Pins the exact submitted body with `toStrictEqual` - Covers each collapsible section closed, alone, and open - Splits the genuinely unit-level logic into a unit test ## User Flow This PR changes no runtime behaviour, so the two lists below walk the same admin through the same task with a plausible form regression applied, showing what reaches the proxy today versus what CI would let ship Before: a regression in the create-key form silently wipes a setting the admin never touched, and the suite stays green 1. An admin opens https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys and clicks Create New Key 2. They type a Key Name, expand Advanced Settings to read the options, change nothing there, and click Create Key 3. The key comes back created, but its soft budget has been explicitly cleared rather than left at whatever the team or default policy would have given it 4. CI is green, so nothing stops the change from shipping After: the same regression turns CI red before it can reach an admin 1. An admin opens https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys and clicks Create New Key 2. They type a Key Name, expand Advanced Settings to read the options, change nothing there, and click Create Key 3. The key comes back created with its soft budget untouched, exactly as before this PR 4. Had the regression been introduced, CI would fail naming the extra key in the submitted body ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This PR only touches tests, so there is no runtime behaviour to curl. The equivalent proof is that the same injected regression survives the suite at the merge base and is caught here, run at both hashes with no other difference Two regressions, each applied identically at both hashes and reverted afterwards. Snippet A makes the form send an explicit null for a field the admin left empty inside a section they merely opened, which is what a form library that emits its whole registered set would do: ``` if ("soft_budget" in formValues && formValues.soft_budget === undefined) { formValues.soft_budget = null; } ``` Snippet B sends an explicit null for a budget the admin never reached at all, because its section stayed collapsed: ``` if (formValues.max_budget === undefined) { formValues.max_budget = null; } ``` On the wire the difference matters: an omitted key leaves the setting alone, an explicit null wipes it Run at both hashes: ``` cd ui/litellm-dashboard && npx vitest run src/components/organisms/create_key_button.integration.test.tsx src/components/organisms/create_key_button.test.tsx ``` ### Before (704cc41f28) #### an empty field in a section the admin opened 1. Ran the command above with snippet A inserted into `handleCreate` 2. Output: ` ✓ src/components/organisms/create_key_button.test.tsx (26 tests) 527ms`, ` ✓ src/components/organisms/create_key_button.integration.test.tsx (5 tests) 19601ms`, ` Test Files 2 passed (2)`, exit 0 3. All 31 tests pass while the form sends a soft budget the admin never set #### a budget field in a section the admin never opened 1. Ran the command above with snippet B inserted into `handleCreate` 2. Output: ` ✓ src/components/organisms/create_key_button.test.tsx (26 tests) 448ms`, ` ❯ src/components/organisms/create_key_button.integration.test.tsx (5 tests | 2 failed) 18989ms`, ` Test Files 1 failed | 1 passed (2)`, exit 1 3. The antd-mocked file passes all 26 of its tests; the two reds come entirely from the small real-tree file that landed in #37348 ### After (7980164841) #### an empty field in a section the admin opened 1. Ran the same command with snippet A inserted into `handleCreate` 2. Output: ` ✓ src/components/organisms/create_key_button.test.tsx (7 tests) 4ms`, ` ❯ src/components/organisms/create_key_button.integration.test.tsx (60 tests | 2 failed) 308322ms`, ` Test Files 1 failed | 1 passed (2)`, exit 1 3. Red: `sends the full mounted field set when every section is open` and `adds exactly the advanced section's own keys when it is the only nested section open`, both reporting a `soft_budget` of null where the admin left the field alone #### a budget field in a section the admin never opened 1. Ran the same command with snippet B inserted into `handleCreate` 2. Output: ` ✓ src/components/organisms/create_key_button.test.tsx (7 tests) 4ms`, ` ❯ src/components/organisms/create_key_button.integration.test.tsx (60 tests | 14 failed) 322370ms`, ` Test Files 1 failed | 1 passed (2)`, exit 1 3. Fourteen cases go red, including every section-opened-alone case and both serialised-wire-key cases, because the extra null shows up in each of them ## Type ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Integration cases are slow, roughly five minutes for the file - Advanced Settings fields come from the proxy's OpenAPI schema - That schema is stubbed through global fetch, not the networking module - Nine collapsible sections exist, but only eight mount at once - The two Logging Settings panels are one ternary's premium branches ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(cost): stop double-billing cached tokens that overlap a modality
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Providers report cached and image tokens as overlapping counts - Billing treats them as separate slices of the prompt - Cached image tokens are therefore charged twice - Synthetic case in the issue bills 109e-6 instead of 39e-6 How it solves it: - Cap each modality at what the cache did not cover - Billed components sum back to prompt_tokens again - Uncached tokens keep their own modality rate ## User Flow Before: a team sending image prompts with prompt caching turned on sees spend far above what the provider invoices, so their dashboard cannot be trusted for chargeback 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with an image prompt, to a provider that reports `cached_tokens` and `image_tokens` as overlapping subsets of `prompt_tokens` 2. The provider serves most of that prompt from cache and reports it in `usage` 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see the request logged at roughly 2.8x the price the provider actually charged 4. Sending the same prompt again makes the gap worse, because a warmer cache means more overlap After: the same request is logged at the price the provider charges, so cached image prompts get cheaper instead of more expensive 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same image prompt 2. The provider serves most of it from cache and reports the same `usage` 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows the cached portion at the cache-read rate and the rest once at the ordinary rate 4. Sending it again lowers the logged spend, matching what caching is supposed to do ## Relevant issues Fixes #37281 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Reproducing the issue's synthetic case at cd7cdb3e3a, using a model with no explicit image rate so image tokens fall back to the ordinary input rate: ```python usage = Usage( prompt_tokens=100, completion_tokens=10, total_tokens=110, prompt_tokens_details=PromptTokensDetailsWrapper( text_tokens=None, cached_tokens=90, image_tokens=80, ), ) generic_cost_per_token(model=model, usage=usage, custom_llm_provider="openai") ``` Before: ``` prompt=89.0e-6 completion=20.0e-6 total=109.0e-6 ``` After: ``` prompt=19.0e-6 completion=20.0e-6 total=39.0e-6 ``` The 70 tokens counted as both cached and image were previously billed at the cache rate and again at the input rate. Now the 90 cached tokens bill at 1e-7 and the 10 uncached tokens bill once at 1e-6 ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Overlap is assumed maximal, since providers do not report it - Only applies when a cached or cache-creation count is present

signals.title: feat(proxy): add POST /auto_router/validate_config to dry-run the complexity-router write gate
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The only way to check a complexity-router config is a real save - A bad config fails as a raw 400 on the write - Forms and scripts cannot show the validator's verdict beforehand How it solves it: - POST /auto_router/validate_config dry-runs the exact write-gate validator - Returns valid plus the verdict text, saves and routes nothing - Same auth as the other auto-router management endpoints ## User Flow Before: an operator drafting a custom-tier router config can only test it by attempting a save 1. They POST https://litellm-domain/model/new with their drafted complexity router config 2. The save fails 400 with the validator's message buried in an error wrapper 3. They fix one field and repeat, each attempt being a real write that could half-succeed After: the same operator checks the draft without writing anything 1. They POST https://litellm-domain/auto_router/validate_config with the same drafted config 2. A 200 comes back with valid true, or valid false plus the exact message the save would give 3. They iterate until valid true, then POST https://litellm-domain/model/new once and it succeeds ## Relevant issues Extracted from #37246 so the validation contract lands before its UI consumers ## Linear ticket Part of LIT-5214 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Run from this branch against a live proxy on port 4471 ### Valid config ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/auto_router/validate_config -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"complexity_router_config": {"tiers": {"CASUAL": "tier-simple", "AUDIT": "tier-security"}, "tier_definitions": [{"name": "CASUAL", "description": "casual chat"}, {"name": "AUDIT", "description": "security audits"}], "fallback_tier": "AUDIT", "classifier_type": "llm", "classifier_llm_config": {"model": "classifier-model"}}}' ``` ``` {"valid":true,"error":null} ``` ### Config the write gate rejects ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/auto_router/validate_config -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"complexity_router_config": {"tiers": {"CASUAL": "tier-simple", "AUDIT": "tier-security"}, "tier_definitions": [{"name": "CASUAL", "description": "casual chat"}, {"name": "AUDIT", "description": "security audits"}], "fallback_tier": "AUDIT", "session_affinity": true, "classifier_type": "llm", "classifier_llm_config": {"model": "classifier-model"}}}' ``` ``` {"valid":false,"error":"complexity_router_config is invalid at complexity_router_config: Value error, session_affinity cannot be combined with tier_definitions: these features rely on the built-in tier severity order, which a custom tier set does not define. The router would drop this deployment at load time, so the write is rejected instead."} ``` ### Unauthenticated ``` curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:4471/auto_router/validate_config -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"complexity_router_config": {}}' ``` ``` 401 ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - The endpoint validates config shape only; it does not check that tier model names resolve to deployments, matching the write gate it mirrors <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 7451ad9f3163f47762e79a3c96b780194fed1193. signals.title: fix(mcp): forward the per-server auth header on OpenAPI tool calls
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `x-mcp-{alias}-authorization` is dropped on OpenAPI-backed MCP servers - The internal API receives no Authorization header at all - The managed MCP path resolves that header correctly, so the two drifted How it solves it: - One owner resolves the credential for both OpenAPI dispatch arms - Per-server values forward verbatim, BYOK values keep their prefix - The credential now reaches the passthrough resolver, not just a ContextVar ## User Flow Before: a developer whose internal REST API is exposed through the gateway as an MCP server sends their own API token per server, and every call comes back unauthorized 1. Their admin registers the internal API as an MCP server from its OpenAPI spec, in a token forwarding mode 2. The developer calls a tool through POST https://litellm-domain/mcp/ with `x-litellm-api-key` for admission and `x-mcp-{alias}-authorization: Bearer <their API token>` 3. The call returns HTTP 200 and the tool output is the internal API's own rejection, `{"error":"invalid_token"}` 4. The internal API's access log shows the request arrived with no Authorization header at all, so the token never left the gateway 5. Sending the token as a top-level `Authorization` does work, but that is one token for the whole request, so it cannot address two forwarding servers in one scope After: the same call reaches the internal API carrying the developer's own token 1. Same registration 2. The developer sends the same call with the same `x-mcp-{alias}-authorization` header 3. The tool returns the real payload from the internal API 4. The internal API's access log shows the request arrived with exactly the token the developer bound to that server, unchanged 5. A wrong token still fails at the internal API, and several forwarding servers can now be addressed in one request, one token each ## Relevant issues - Per-server `x-mcp-{alias}-authorization` now reaches the upstream on `spec_path` MCP servers - Both OpenAPI dispatch arms are fixed, and one owner replaces the logic each carried separately - Top-level `Authorization` and BYOK credentials behave exactly as before Closes #33344 Supersedes #33349, whose analysis and approach this borrows from, credit to its author. That PR predates `resolve_openapi_upstream_auth` so it no longer applies, and it fixes only the `_request_auth_header` ContextVar. That is not enough on current staging: `_merge_openapi_tool_request_headers` lets `_request_resolved_auth_headers` outrank the ContextVar, so for the client-forwarded modes the credential also has to reach the resolver's passthrough arm. `_passthrough_token_from_mcp_auth_header` already accepts the `str | dict` shape and documents itself as sourced from `x-mcp-{alias}-authorization`; that dict branch was simply dead because no OpenAPI caller passed it Worth knowing for review: OpenAPI tools register into the local tool registry, so `execute_mcp_tool` serves MCP-protocol and REST tool calls while `MCPServerManager.call_tool` serves the responses-API handler. The proof below records which arm ran and it is the local-registry one; the other arm is covered by a parametrized symmetry test rather than by assumption The two kinds of credential are deliberately kept apart. A per-server header is already a complete header value and is forwarded unchanged, while a BYOK credential is a raw secret that takes the server's auth-type prefix, so conflating them would ship `Bearer Bearer <token>`. A test pins that ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical on both legs. One proxy on `:4612` against real Postgres, plus a real internal REST API on `:9201` that publishes an OpenAPI spec, requires `Authorization: Bearer upstream-ok`, and logs the auth header of every request it receives. Like a real internal API it publishes no OAuth metadata ```yaml mcp_servers: api_spec: url: http://127.0.0.1:9201 spec_path: http://127.0.0.1:9201/openapi.json auth_type: oauth_delegate authorization_url: http://127.0.0.1:9299/authorize token_url: http://127.0.0.1:9299/token extra_headers: ["Authorization"] ``` Both legs run the same script. Every call carries `x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-1234` for admission and `x-mcp-servers: api_spec` for scope; only the credential header differs across the three cases ### Before (41de13aa0c) ``` 1. tools/call against the OpenAPI-backed server, by header shape top-level Authorization {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"workspace\":\"finance\",\"reports\":[\"Sales\",\"Ops\"]}"}],"isError":false}} [HTTP 200] x-mcp-api_spec-authorization {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"error\":\"invalid_token\"}"}],"isError":false}} [HTTP 200] per-server, WRONG token {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"error\":\"invalid_token\"}"}],"isError":false}} [HTTP 200] 2. what the internal API actually received, in order {"path": "/reports", "method": "GET", "got_authorization": "Bearer upstream-ok"} {"path": "/reports", "method": "GET", "got_authorization": null} {"path": "/reports", "method": "GET", "got_authorization": null} 3. which dispatch arm served the calls execute_mcp_tool local-registry arm: 3 MCPServerManager.call_tool arm: 0 ``` ### After (1e54ddce28) ``` 1. tools/call against the OpenAPI-backed server, by header shape top-level Authorization {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"workspace\":\"finance\",\"reports\":[\"Sales\",\"Ops\"]}"}],"isError":false}} [HTTP 200] x-mcp-api_spec-authorization {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"workspace\":\"finance\",\"reports\":[\"Sales\",\"Ops\"]}"}],"isError":false}} [HTTP 200] per-server, WRONG token {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"error\":\"invalid_token\"}"}],"isError":false}} [HTTP 200] 2. what the internal API actually received, in order {"path": "/reports", "method": "GET", "got_authorization": "Bearer upstream-ok"} {"path": "/reports", "method": "GET", "got_authorization": "Bearer upstream-ok"} {"path": "/reports", "method": "GET", "got_authorization": "Bearer wrong-token"} 3. which dispatch arm served the calls execute_mcp_tool local-registry arm: 3 MCPServerManager.call_tool arm: 0 ``` The After leg was captured at 37cf5a8927; 1e54ddce28 amends it with one extra test assertion and leaves the production diff byte identical, so the run above still describes the tip Step 2 is the whole change: the second request went from no Authorization header to the caller's own token, forwarded unchanged. The third case shows a wrong token still reaching the API and still being rejected, which also proves the value is not re-prefixed. Step 3 records which dispatch arm served the calls, identical on both legs ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - An upstream 401 still surfaces as `isError: false` on OpenAPI tools - Only the OpenAPI arms change; managed MCP servers already resolved this header ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 1e54ddce280dfcd729f1b1a4156f2d9942fcb7f2. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: chore(ui): upgrade the dashboard to React 19
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Dashboard ran React 18 while Next 16 wants a React 19 peer - Base UI and shadcn upstream both assume the React 19 ref model - Test setup enforced an 18-only rule that 19 deliberately removed How it solves it: - Bumps react and react-dom 18.3.1 to 19.2.8, plus matching @types - Widens one ref prop that useRef now types as nullable - Rewrites the ref assertions to the React 19 contract - Waits for a select popup to open before clicking its option - Stops the MCP edit form flashing a false no-OAuth-flow warning ## User Flow Before: nothing is broken for the end user, the dashboard just runs a React major behind the framework serving it 1. An admin opens http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and the page renders normally 2. Every other dashboard page renders normally too 3. The gap is invisible from the browser, it only shows up as a peer mismatch at install time and as upstream components the dashboard cannot adopt After: the same pages render the same way on React 19 1. An admin opens http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and sees the same key table, filters, and modals 2. Navigating to Models, Usage, Logs, Teams, and Playground shows the same content and the same interactions 3. Nothing on screen changes, which is the point: the runtime moved forward with no visible behavior shift 4. signals.title: fix(pass_through): don't override client-forwarded Anthropic OAuth with server x-api-key
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `/anthropic` passthrough always sent the server's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as `x-api-key` - Anthropic authenticates off `x-api-key` when both it and `Authorization` are present - A client forwarding its own OAuth token (e.g. Claude Code Max) got silently ignored How it solves it: - Skip injecting the server `x-api-key` when the request already carries a client OAuth token - The client's own `Authorization` header then reaches Anthropic unmodified ## User Flow Before: a developer routing a Claude Code Max subscription through the `/anthropic` passthrough gets authenticated as the proxy's own configured key instead of their subscription 1. They set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000/anthropic` and run Claude Code with their Max subscription OAuth token 2. Claude Code sends `POST http://localhost:4000/anthropic/v1/messages` with `Authorization: Bearer sk-ant-oat...` 3. The proxy also attaches `x-api-key: <the operator's configured ANTHROPIC_API_KEY>` to the upstream request 4. Anthropic authenticates off `x-api-key`, so every request runs as the proxy's own key, not the developer's Max subscription (probing with a deliberately invalid client token still returns "API key is invalid" instead of an OAuth-token error, proving the client's identity never reached Anthropic) After: the same flow authenticates as the developer's own subscription 1. They set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000/anthropic` and run Claude Code with their Max subscription OAuth token 2. Claude Code sends `POST http://localhost:4000/anthropic/v1/messages` with `Authorization: Bearer sk-ant-oat...` 3. The proxy forwards only that `Authorization` header; it no longer attaches its own `x-api-key` 4. Anthropic authenticates the request as the developer's own Max subscription ## Relevant issues Relates to #37344 (the `/anthropic` passthrough auth-substitution finding in that report; the report's separate 429 rate-limit observation on the router/provider path is not reproduced or explained by this change and remains open) ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Ran the real proxy (`litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py`) with `ANTHROPIC_API_BASE` pointed at a local echo listener standing in for `api.anthropic.com`, so the actual outbound headers can be inspected directly, the same technique the issue reporter used to diagnose this. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-server-configured-fakekey` simulates the operator's configured key; the request carries a fake Claude Code Max OAuth token (`sk-ant-oat01-...`) as the client's own `Authorization` header. ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4111/anthropic/v1/messages \ -H "x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-test-master-key-1234" \ -H "authorization: Bearer sk-ant-oat01-fake-claude-code-max-oauth-token" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-4-5","max_tokens":10,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' ``` ### Before (41de13aa0c) 1. Ran the command above against the proxy on the merge-base commit 2. The echo listener recorded both headers on the outbound request: ```json { "authorization": "Bearer sk-ant-oat01-fake-claude-code-max-oauth-token", "x-api-key": "sk-ant-server-configured-fakekey" } ``` 3. Anthropic would authenticate this request off `x-api-key`, i.e. as the proxy operator, not the client ### After (abf911ec19) 1. Ran the identical command against the proxy rebuilt from this branch's tip 2. The echo listener recorded only the client's own header: ```json { "authorization": "Bearer sk-ant-oat01-fake-claude-code-max-oauth-token" } ``` 3. `x-api-key` is no longer sent, so Anthropic has only the client's own credential to authenticate with ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Does not address the report's separate 429 rate-limit observation on the router/provider `/v1/messages` path; that needs reproduction against a real Claude Max subscription, which wasn't available here - Testing used a local echo listener instead of the live Anthropic API since no Anthropic OAuth subscription or API key was available in this environment ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(router): keep acreate_file fallbacks inside the requested model group
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Files uploaded for one model group could silently land on another provider via router fallbacks - The returned unified file id then fails every batch create with a permanent 429 How it solves it: - File creation now reuses the fallback pin that already protects batch and fine-tuning calls - Cross-group fallbacks are skipped for uploads, so the real provider error surfaces instead ## User Flow Before: a developer uploading a batch file for their azure model group gets HTTP 200, but every batch create against the returned id fails forever 1. During transient Azure trouble they send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with form fields `purpose=batch`, `target_model_names=azure-gpt`, and their JSONL file 2. They get HTTP 200 with `"status": "uploaded"` and a scrambled file id, so they believe the file is ready for azure-gpt 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with that file id and get HTTP 429 "No deployments available for selected model, Try again in 5 seconds" 4. They wait and retry the batch create, and it returns the same 429 every time, because the file actually landed under the account of the fallback group's provider After: the upload fails loudly while Azure is down, and a retried upload once Azure is back produces a working batch 1. During the same transient Azure trouble they send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with `purpose=batch` and `target_model_names=azure-gpt` 2. They get HTTP 500 carrying the real connection error, so they know the upload did not go through and nothing was stored anywhere 3. Once Azure is reachable they retry the upload, get HTTP 200, and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with the returned id succeeds ## Relevant issues Related to #35371 and #36181, which pinned the batch and fine-tuning side of the same fallback walk ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5788 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) - [x] b7f4f531b3f88f58ffbed3d3adbcafa4614d5fa0 passes /live-pr-risk ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: proxy booted from the worktree with a fresh Postgres DB and the master key from .env, on random free ports: 30362 for the before leg, then 45817 and (after OpenAI finished the batch) 38571 for the after leg, both boots of the same tip commit. Config has an unreachable azure group, a healthy openai group, and a fallback between them: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: azure-gpt litellm_params: model: azure/my-azure-deployment api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9 api_key: dummy-key api_version: "2024-06-01" - model_name: openai-gpt litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4.1-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY router_settings: fallbacks: - azure-gpt: - openai-gpt num_retries: 1 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/LIT5788_DATABASE_URL ``` `batch_input.jsonl`: ```json {"custom_id": "req-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/chat/completions", "body": {"model": "azure-gpt", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "say hi"}], "max_tokens": 5}} ``` ### Before (ec6f1c1a56345350f669377f14ec8586bd43329e) #### Upload for azure-gpt during the outage, then batch create 1. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:30362/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" -F purpose=batch -F target_model_names="azure-gpt" -F file=@batch_input.jsonl` 2. HTTP 200 with `"status":"uploaded"` and a unified id, even though azure-gpt is unreachable: ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK {"id":"","bytes":176,"created_at":1787106179,"filename":"modified_file.jsonl","object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"uploaded",...} ``` 3. The id base64-decodes to `target_model_names,azure-gpt` next to an OpenAI-format `llm_output_file_id,file-9LPo6PjRrhgCtkhQ3M1Ryc`, and the file physically exists on the provider the caller never named: `curl -sS https://api.openai.com/v1/files/file-9LPo6PjRrhgCtkhQ3M1Ryc -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY"` returns `"status": "processed"` 4. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:30362/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"input_file_id\": \"$UF\", \"endpoint\": \"/v1/chat/completions\", \"completion_window\": \"24h\", \"model\": \"azure-gpt\"}"` 5. Permanent failure inviting infinite retries (a retry 8 seconds later returned the same thing): ``` HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests {"error":{"message":"No deployments available for selected model, Try again in 5 seconds. Passed model=azure-gpt. pre-call-checks=False, cooldown_list=[]","type":"internal_server_error","param":"None","code":"429"}} ``` #### Control: upload and batch on the healthy openai-gpt group 1. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:30362/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" -F purpose=batch -F target_model_names="openai-gpt" -F file=@batch_input.jsonl` 2. HTTP 200 and the decoded id consistently pairs `target_model_names,openai-gpt` with the openai deployment, so the harness itself is sound ### After (b7f4f531b3f88f58ffbed3d3adbcafa4614d5fa0) #### Upload for azure-gpt during the outage 1. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:38571/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" -F purpose=batch -F target_model_names="azure-gpt" -F file=@batch_input.jsonl` 2. The upload now surfaces the real provider error instead of silently succeeding, and there is no unified id to orphan: ``` HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error {"error":{"message":"Connection error.. Received Model Group=azure-gpt\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=['openai-gpt']\nError doing the fallback: Connection error.","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}} ``` 3. Proxy log shows the pin doing its job: `LiteLLM Router:INFO: fallback_event_handlers.py:354 - Skipping fallback to model_group = openai-gpt: request is pinned to model_group = azure-gpt by its uploaded file` 4. Nothing landed cross-provider: the managed file table holds 5 rows and `select count(*) from "LiteLLM_ManagedFileTable" where model_mappings::text like '%6e195556%'` (the azure deployment id) returns 0 #### Control: upload and batch on the healthy openai-gpt group 1. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:45817/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" -F purpose=batch -F target_model_names="openai-gpt" -F file=@batch_input.jsonl` returns HTTP 200 with `"status":"uploaded"` and a unified id decoding to `litellm_proxy:application/octet-stream;unified_id,aac1a6f4-48f5-45b3-a4cc-ac3ce98ee7f4;target_model_names,openai-gpt;llm_output_file_id,file-U2CAp3DGvD2ACLjahMxQNd;...` 2. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:45817/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"input_file_id\": \"$UF\", \"endpoint\": \"/v1/chat/completions\", \"completion_window\": \"24h\", \"model\": \"openai-gpt\"}"` is accepted with `"object":"batch","status":"validating"`, creating real OpenAI batch `batch_6a851bc251c08190add73205b555055c` 3. Once OpenAI finished processing, `curl -sS "http://localhost:38571/v1/batches/$UB?provider=openai" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY"` returns `"status": "completed"` with `"request_counts": {"completed": 1, "failed": 0, "total": 1}` and an output file id decoding to `llm_output_file_id,file-GsDJ474EBaYsHEyRzJqRuT`, a real gpt-4.1-mini batch run costing real money ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Cross-group fallbacks are now skipped for every router file upload, managed or not ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(proxy): log spend for OpenAI passthrough embeddings with unmapped models
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - OpenAI passthrough embeddings with unmapped models return 200 but never get billed - Cost lookup failure crashed the logging task, dropping the spend log row How it solves it: - Embeddings cost failures now log spend at cost 0 instead of crashing - Errors on non-chat bodies no longer hit the chat-shaped fallback ## User Flow Before: a developer calls embeddings through the OpenAI passthrough with their Azure deployment name, gets a normal 200, and the proxy admin never sees the request billed 1. The proxy admin exposes the OpenAI passthrough by setting the upstream base URL and key, then hands the developer a virtual key 2. The developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/openai_passthrough/v1/embeddings` with `{"model": "my-embeddings-deployment", "input": ["hello"]}`, a deployment name LiteLLM has no pricing for 3. They get back 200 with a normal embeddings body: `object: "list"`, the vector in `data`, and real token usage 4. The admin opens https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request is nowhere in the list; `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs` shows no row for it either 5. The key's spend at `GET https://litellm-domain/key/info` never moves, so the request is served but invisible and unbilled forever After: the same request shows up in the spend logs with its token counts, priced at $0 until a mapped price exists 1. The proxy admin exposes the OpenAI passthrough by setting the upstream base URL and key, then hands the developer a virtual key 2. The developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/openai_passthrough/v1/embeddings` with `{"model": "my-embeddings-deployment", "input": ["hello"]}`, a deployment name LiteLLM has no pricing for 3. They get back 200 with a normal embeddings body: `object: "list"`, the vector in `data`, and real token usage 4. The admin opens https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request is there; `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id=<id>` returns the row with the deployment name, its real prompt token count, and `"spend": 0.0` 5. Requests with models LiteLLM does have pricing for keep billing at their real cost, exactly as before ## Relevant issues Embeddings residual of #36646 (the chat completions side was fixed in #36660) ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5787 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: live proxy from the worktree against a real Azure OpenAI upstream (real API calls, real $) ```bash export OPENAI_API_BASE="https://e2e-claude-foundry.openai.azure.com/openai" export OPENAI_API_KEY="<azure key>" .venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --port <port> ``` `lit5787-embed-qa2` is an Azure deployment name with no entry in the pricing map; `text-embedding-3-small` is mapped ### Before (ec6f1c1a56) #### Unmapped deployment name 1. Request served fine: ```bash curl -sS http://localhost:43217/openai_passthrough/v1/embeddings \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "lit5787-embed-qa2", "input": ["spend attribution probe LIT-5787"]}' ``` Returns 200 with a normal embeddings body (`object: "list"`, vector in `data`, real `usage`), and the proxy log shows `"POST /openai_passthrough/v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1" 200 OK` 2. The logging task dies before writing anything: ```text 19:27:50 - LiteLLM:ERROR: logging_worker.py:104 - LoggingWorker error: litellm.APIError: LiteLLM: provider returned a response with no 'choices'. Raw keys: ['id', 'object', 'data', 'model', 'usage'] ... ValueError: This model isn't mapped yet. Add it here - https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json ``` 3. The next spend flush has nothing for the request, and no spend log row is ever written: ```text 19:27:51 - spend_update_queue.py:37 - Aggregating updates by entity type: [] 19:27:51 - db_spend_update_writer.py:1225 - User Spend transactions: {} 19:27:51 - db_spend_update_writer.py:1267 - KEY Spend transactions: {} ``` #### Mapped model (control) 1. Same curl with `{"model": "text-embedding-3-small", "input": "spend attribution probe LIT-5787 control"}` returns 200 2. Spend row written as expected: `SpendTable: created payload - request_id: d0d17210-..., model: text-embedding-3-small, spend: 2e-07` ### After (81914ebc31) #### Unmapped deployment name 1. Same request against the fixed tip: ```bash curl -sS http://localhost:24886/openai_passthrough/v1/embeddings \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "lit5787-embed-qa2", "input": ["spend attribution probe LIT-5787 tip"]}' ``` Returns the same 200 embeddings body 2. The logging task now survives and writes the spend row (zero LoggingWorker errors in the whole run): ```text 19:48:32 - openai_passthrough_logging_handler.py:246 - Error calculating embeddings cost for model lit5787-embed-qa2, logging spend with cost 0: This model isn't mapped yet. ... 19:48:32 - spend_tracking_utils.py:441 - SpendTable: created payload - request_id: cacdffd2-40ed-4baa-9fda-4e2fc2686324, model: lit5787-embed-qa2, spend: 0.0 19:48:32 - db_spend_update_writer.py:816 - Writing spend log to db - request_id: cacdffd2-40ed-4baa-9fda-4e2fc2686324, spend: 0.0 ``` 3. The row is visible where the admin looks: ```bash curl -sS "http://localhost:24886/spend/logs?request_id=cacdffd2-40ed-4baa-9fda-4e2fc2686324" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" ``` Returns the row: `request_id: cacdffd2-40ed-4baa-9fda-4e2fc2686324`, `model: lit5787-embed-qa2`, `custom_llm_provider: openai`, `spend: 0.0`, `prompt_tokens: 11`, `completion_tokens: 0`, `call_type: pass_through_endpoint` #### Mapped model (control) 1. Same curl with `{"model": "text-embedding-3-small", "input": "spend attribution probe LIT-5787 control tip"}` returns 200 2. Real cost still billed: `SpendTable: created payload - request_id: be84855d-014b-4e2f-b972-ea6ed18e627d, model: text-embedding-3-small, spend: 2.2e-07` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Unmapped models bill at $0 until pricing is added to the map ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR live-pr-risk CHECKED at 81914ebc31: PASS. Only dispatch site (success_handler) A/B verified on a live proxy at base and tip with real Azure calls; no subclasses, no wire/config/DB/UI surface. Error paths on image and responses routes previously always crashed the chat-shaped fallback (body has no choices), so returning the pre-existing result-None contract removes no working behavior

signals.title: fix(model_prices): set prompt_cache_min_tokens=4096 for Gemini 3.5/3.6/3.7 Flash and 3.1 Pro Preview
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Gemini 3.5/3.6/3.7 Flash entries lack `prompt_cache_min_tokens` - LiteLLM assumes the default 1024-token caching minimum for them - Google requires 4,096 tokens minimum, so small prompts hit a 400 How it solves it: - Adds `prompt_cache_min_tokens: 4096` to those models (all provider variants) - Also adds it to `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, listed at 4,096 in the same Google table ## User Flow Before: a developer using prompt caching with a small prompt gets a hard 400 from Vertex 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to model group `gemini-3.5-flash` with `cache_control` on a ~3,300-token prompt 2. The request fails with `400: The cached content is of 3334 tokens. The minimum token count to start explicit caching is 4096.` After: the same request is handled knowing the real 4,096-token minimum 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to `gemini-3.5-flash` 2. LiteLLM's prompt-caching checks resolve the model's minimum as 4,096, so sub-minimum prompts are no longer treated as cacheable and routed into the failing explicit-caching path ## Relevant issues Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/caching#implicit-caching — "Gemini 3.7 Flash 4,096 / Gemini 3.6 Flash 4,096 / Gemini 3.5 Flash 4,096 / Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview 4,096" (verified against the raw page HTML on 2026-08-19). These minimums were introduced in #33637. ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [ ] I have added meaningful tests (metadata-only JSON change; behavior covered by existing `prompt_cache_min_tokens` tests from #33637) - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### Before (bc6e7df05b) 1. `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run python -c "from litellm.utils import get_prompt_cache_min_tokens; [print(m, '->', get_prompt_cache_min_tokens(m)) for m in ['gemini/gemini-3.5-flash','gemini/gemini-3.6-flash','gemini/gemini-3.7-flash','vertex_ai/gemini-3.5-flash']]"` 2. Output: ``` gemini/gemini-3.5-flash -> 1024 gemini/gemini-3.6-flash -> 1024 gemini/gemini-3.7-flash -> 1024 vertex_ai/gemini-3.5-flash -> 1024 ``` ### After (5bc7fe574e) 1. Same command 2. Output: ``` gemini/gemini-3.5-flash -> 4096 gemini/gemini-3.6-flash -> 4096 gemini/gemini-3.7-flash -> 4096 vertex_ai/gemini-3.5-flash -> 4096 ``` Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/68133c6e441e49d7955c0712f01c6a9b

signals.text: ## Title fix(user_update): stop premium metadata fields reaching the user table as columns ## Relevant issues None filed. Found by comparing `/user/update` against its two siblings, `/key/update` and `/team/update`. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the `tests/litellm/` directory: `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_internal_user_endpoints.py` - [x] I have added the test output below - [x] My PR passes the touched test file with no new failures (control run below) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible: one added condition plus one new test ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `POST /user/update` (and the bulk variant, which shares the same helper) with `guardrails` or `prompts` in the body builds a prisma payload carrying them as **top-level keys**. Neither is a column on `LiteLLM_UserTable`, so `prisma_client.update_data(..., table_name="user")` hands them to the upsert and the write fails instead of storing the value. `_update_internal_user_params` filters the payload against only one of the two management-metadata name lists: ```python elif ( v is not None and v not in ([], {}) and k not in LiteLLM_ManagementEndpoint_MetadataFields ): non_default_values[k] = v ``` `LiteLLM_ManagementEndpoint_MetadataFields_Premium` (which holds `guardrails`, `policies`, `prompts`, `tags`, `logging`, ...) is never consulted, so those keys survive. `prepare_metadata_fields()` runs afterwards and **does** copy them into `non_default_values["metadata"]`, but it never pops the top-level key, so each one is written twice: once correctly into metadata, once as a phantom column. The two sibling routes get this right. `prepare_key_update_data` skips both lists: ```python if k in LiteLLM_ManagementEndpoint_MetadataFields or k in LiteLLM_ManagementEndpoint_MetadataFields_Premium: continue ``` `/team/update` does the same, and `/user/new` is unaffected because `generate_key_helper_fn` puts these into metadata and never into `user_data`. Only `/user/update` leaks them. What makes this an omission of one list rather than a deliberate design: the **non**-premium fields reachable on this request model (`model_rpm_limit`, `model_tpm_limit`, `mcp_rpm_limit`, `tag_rpm_limit`) are already dropped correctly today. Same class of field, same destination, opposite handling. The fix mirrors the sibling key path by filtering the premium list too. `LiteLLM_ManagementEndpoint_MetadataFields_Premium` is already in scope through the module's `from litellm.proxy._types import *`, so there is no new import. Nothing is lost: `prepare_metadata_fields` already persists all of these into metadata, which is where the request path reads them from (`litellm_pre_call_utils.py` reads `policies` and `guardrails` out of key / team / project **metadata**, never out of a user column). ### One nuance worth a maintainer's call `policies` **is** a real column on `LiteLLM_UserTable`, so today `/user/update` writes it to both the column and metadata. After this change it goes to metadata only, which matches `/user/new`, `/key/update` and `/team/update`. I checked for readers of the column before including it: a repo-wide search finds no code that reads `policies` off a user row (the one nearby hit is `team_repository.py`, a different table). If you would rather keep that vestigial column write, say so and I will drop `policies` from the exclusion; the `guardrails` / `prompts` half is the part that actually errors. ## Testing New test in the existing file, next to the other `_update_internal_user_params` tests. No database needed. ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_internal_user_endpoints.py \ -k keeps_premium_metadata_out_of_columns # before the fix E AssertionError: guardrails must not be sent as a user column E assert 'guardrails' not in {'user_id': 'test_user_id', 'guardrails': ['my-guardrail'], E 'policies': ['my-policy'], 'prompts': ['my-prompt']} 1 failed # after the fix 1 passed ``` The test also asserts the values still arrive in `metadata` after `prepare_metadata_fields`, so it pins that the fix drops the phantom column without dropping the value. Direct before/after on the helper: ``` before: _update_internal_user_params(...) -> ['guardrails', 'policies', 'prompts', 'user_id'] after: _update_internal_user_params(...) -> ['user_id'] metadata -> {'model_rpm_limit': {'gpt-4': 5}, 'guardrails': ['my-guardrail'], 'policies': ['my-policy'], 'prompts': ['my-prompt']} ``` Control on the whole touched test file, same environment, with and without the change: ``` before: 8 failed, 29 passed, 61 errors after: 8 failed, 30 passed, 61 errors ``` Exactly +1 test and +1 pass; the failing set is byte-identical (diffed, not just counted). Those pre-existing failures and errors are environment gaps in my local install, not related to this change. `ruff check` reports the same 91 pre-existing findings before and after, none on a touched line. `ruff format --check --config ruff.toml` reports the source file already formatted; the test file reports the same single pre-existing reformat (an unrelated assert) both before and after. Note on the proxy checklist: I do not have a live proxy with paid LLM credentials, so I have not exercised this through a running server. This is a management-endpoint payload-shaping change with no LLM call in the path, and the function-level before/after above is the direct evidence.

signals.title: fix(zai): add provider and current model catalog
signals.text: ## TLDR Fixes the Z.AI dashboard onboarding path and brings the bundled Z.AI catalog up to the current documented models. - Adds Z.AI to the Add Model provider catalog. - Lets provider search match the LiteLLM slug `zai` as well as the display name. - Adds the six current Z.AI models missing from the model cost map: `glm-5.3`, `glm-5.2`, `glm-5-turbo`, `glm-5v-turbo`, `glm-4.7-flashx`, and `glm-4.6v`. - Keeps `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and the bundled backup map in sync. The Z.AI provider uses the OpenAI-compatible base URL `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4`. ## User Flow Before: 1. A proxy admin opens Add Model and searches for `zai` or `z.ai`. 2. The provider dropdown returns no result, so no Z.AI credentials or model choices can be configured. After: 1. The same admin searches for `zai` or `z.ai` and selects Z.AI. 2. The form shows the API key field and default Z.AI API base. 3. The model selector includes the current Z.AI models, including GLM-5.3, GLM-5.2, GLM-5-Turbo, GLM-5V-Turbo, GLM-4.7-FlashX, and GLM-4.6V. ## Root Cause LiteLLM supported the `zai` provider in the SDK and had existing Z.AI metadata, but the dashboard provider-creation catalog omitted it. The catalog also lagged the current Z.AI model list. ## Relevant Issues Fixes #25482 Supersedes the stale unmerged implementation in #25485. The existing provider-name mapping from #26419 is retained. ## Validation - `python3 -m json.tool model_prices_and_context_window.json` - Verified the canonical and bundled backup maps are byte-identical. - Added `tests/test_litellm/test_zai_model_metadata.py`, which asserts the documented 15-model Z.AI subset and exact metadata for the six newly catalogued models. - `npm run test -- --run src/components/add_model/AddModelForm.test.tsx` passes: 13 tests. - In a local Admin UI running against the proposed bundled catalog, `GET /public/litellm_model_cost_map` exposes all six new model IDs and the Add Model selector shows all six, including search results for `zai/glm-4.7-flashx` and `zai/glm-4.6v`. ## CI Note The earlier `misc` failure in run 32214763016 is unrelated to this PR's original changes. It failed `tests/test_litellm/batches/test_batch_utils.py::test_handle_completed_vertex_batch_computes_cost_usage_and_models`, where a Vertex batch cost expectation was double the observed value. This PR did not change batch code, Vertex code, or the model cost map in that run. The new push should receive a fresh CI result. ## Pre-Submission Checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests. - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks. - [x] My PR's scope is isolated to Z.AI dashboard onboarding and catalog metadata. - [x] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting maintainer review. ## Type Bug Fix ## Caveats - The focused Python test requires the full LiteLLM Python dependency set, which is unavailable in this local worktree. The JSON, bundled-map consistency, runtime API, and UI flows were verified locally; GitHub CI will run the Python test. - A full local Docker image build requires the Docker buildx plugin. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including edge cases and real-world customer regressions.

signals.title: fix(ui): gate the pass-through guardrail field inputs when the section is disabled
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Disabling the guardrails section left two inputs fully typeable - Every prop crossed to those inputs except the enforcing one - `TagsInput`'s own `disabled` prop had no test at all How it solves it: - Pass `disabled` to both field-targeting `TagsInput` controls - Add a test that types into the control, not one asserting an attribute - Enabled cases act as the liveness gate for the disabled ones ## User Flow This gate is latent today. Neither call site passes `disabled`, so no end user can currently reach either flow. Both lists below describe the flow a caller gets the moment it passes the prop, which is what this PR changes. Before: an admin viewing a read-only pass-through endpoint sees a greyed-out guardrails section and can still edit the parts of it that matter 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints, click the "Pass-Through Endpoints" tab and open an endpoint whose guardrails section is rendered disabled 2. The guardrail picker is greyed out and the "+ query", "+ documents[*]" and "+ results[*]" buttons are all unclickable, so the section reads as locked 3. They click into the "Request Fields (pre_call)" box, type `query` and press comma 4. The tag is accepted and appears as a chip, and the same works in "Response Fields (post_call)" 5. The section reports itself as locked while still taking edits, so what is on screen no longer matches what is enforced After: the same section refuses every edit, matching what it says about itself 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints, click the "Pass-Through Endpoints" tab and open the same endpoint 2. The guardrail picker is greyed out and the three quick-add buttons are unclickable, exactly as before 3. They click into the "Request Fields (pre_call)" box and type `query` followed by a comma 4. Nothing is entered, no chip appears, and the same holds for "Response Fields (post_call)" 5. Typing, pressing Enter and clicking away all leave the field untouched, so the section is locked in the way it already looked ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Reaching this needs a one-line local edit, because no call site passes `disabled` yet, so there is no route that shows it today. Steps for both sides: ### Before (c94d692864) #### Request and response field targeting accept input while the section is disabled 1. Check out the merge base and start the dashboard dev server against a running proxy: `git checkout c94d692864`, then `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard` 2. In `src/components/add_pass_through.tsx` at the `PassThroughGuardrailsSection` usage, add `disabled` to the props 3. Open http://localhost:3000/models-and-endpoints, click the "Pass-Through Endpoints" tab, then "+ Add Pass-Through Endpoint" 4. Pick any guardrail so the "Field Targeting (Optional)" card appears 5. Observe the guardrail picker and the "+ query", "+ documents[*]" and "+ results[*]" buttons are all greyed out 6. Click into "Request Fields (pre_call)", type `query` then a comma, and observe the chip is accepted 7. Repeat in "Response Fields (post_call)" and observe the same ### After (5b92500127) #### Request and response field targeting accept input while the section is disabled 1. Check out this PR's tip and repeat the same one-line edit from step 2 above 2. Open http://localhost:3000/models-and-endpoints, click the "Pass-Through Endpoints" tab, then "+ Add Pass-Through Endpoint" 3. Pick any guardrail so the "Field Targeting (Optional)" card appears 4. Observe the picker and all three quick-add buttons are greyed out, unchanged 5. Click into "Request Fields (pre_call)", type `query` then a comma, and observe nothing is entered 6. Repeat in "Response Fields (post_call)" and observe the same 7. Revert the one-line edit from step 1 ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Latent, not live: no call site passes `disabled` today - `TagsInput` needed no change; measured that it already gates typing - Test drives the control because Base UI can paint state without enforcing ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Two field hints vanished from Cache Control Injection Points - The Index hint was the only "optional" signal users had - No test covered the add-model payload, so nothing caught it How it solves it: - Restore both hints as tooltips beside their labels - Make each hint trigger a real, keyboard-reachable button - Add a payload net over the real add-model panel - Pin exact submit bodies so silent key drift fails loudly ## User Flow Before: an admin adding a cache-aware deployment cannot tell what Role does, or that Index is optional, so they fill in a value they did not need 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=llm-models and click Add Model 2. They pick Anthropic, fill in the model and key, and expand Advanced Settings 3. They switch on Cache Control Injection Points and see a row with Type, Role and Index 4. Role and Index carry bare labels with no hint icon and nothing on hover, so neither field explains itself 5. Tabbing through the row skips straight from one control to the next, so there is no guidance to reach by keyboard either 6. Reading Index as required, they type an index they did not want, and every request now marks that one message cacheable After: the same admin sees a hint on each field and leaves Index alone 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=llm-models and click Add Model 2. They pick Anthropic, fill in the model and key, and expand Advanced Settings 3. They switch on Cache Control Injection Points and see a row with Type, Role and Index 4. Role and Index each show a hint icon. Hovering Role reads "LiteLLM will mark all messages of this role as cacheable" and hovering Index reads "(Optional) If set litellm will mark the message at this index as cacheable" 5. Tabbing through the row stops on each hint icon and shows the same text, so a keyboard or screen-reader user gets the guidance too 6. Knowing Index is optional, they leave it blank and pick a role instead, so caching applies where they meant it to ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge?
