signals.title: fix(proxy/mcp): pass through client-native tool_use turns in auto-execute loop (#37031)
signals.text: Fixes #37031 ## Problem When `require_approval: "never"` is configured for server-side MCP tools, the proxy auto-executes tools emitted by models during `/v1/messages` calls. When an agentic client (e.g. Claude Code) sends its own client-side tools (`Read`, `Bash`, `Edit`) in the same turn, the auto-execute loop attempts to look up every requested tool in `tool_server_map`. Missing client tools cause a `KeyError` that is caught and converted into `Error executing tool: '<tool>'`, breaking all client-native tools. ## Fix Updated `anthropic_messages_with_mcp` in `mcp_handler.py` to check whether any emitted `tool_use` block is missing from `tool_server_map`. If client-native tools are detected in the turn, server-side auto-execution breaks and returns the response directly to the client. This allows agentic clients to handle their local tools while preserving valid Anthropic tool/result message ordering. ## Checklist - [x] Verified fix via unit test (`pytest tests/test_mcp_client_tool_passthrough.py` passes). - [x] Handled mixed client/server tool turns without invalidating message sequence.

signals.title: feat(ui): add mounted-field projections for the MCP server form graph
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - antd submits only mounted fields; react-hook-form submits the whole store - The MCP server form graph gates 89 bindings behind 22 conditions - Four of those gates are invisible when reading the roots' JSX - Porting the graph without them written down silently changes the payload How it solves it: - Adds pure mounted-field projections for both MCP server roots - Covers all 22 gates with unit tests, one case per gate - Pins three antd behaviours measured by probe, not assumed - Touches no JSX; nothing imports the module yet ## User Flow No user-visible change, so the two flows below are identical by construction. The new module is not imported anywhere; it is groundwork the form port will consume. Before: an admin edits an MCP server and saves 1. They open the MCP Servers page and edit a server 2. They change a field and click Save Changes 3. The server updates After: unchanged, step for step 1. They open the MCP Servers page and edit a server 2. They change a field and click Save Changes 3. The server updates ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix There is no runtime behaviour to demonstrate. The module is not imported by any component, so no request an end user can make reaches it and a live proxy would show nothing either way. Recording that plainly rather than presenting a test run as a proof of fix. What the change is verified by instead is a per-field deletion battery over the projections, which is the instrument that decides whether each of the 89 bindings is load-bearing. Each of the 80 emitted field-name sites is deleted one at a time and the suite must go red for it. The harness gates every entry on the mutation applying, the file still compiling, and the suite running the expected test count, and reports INVALID rather than a verdict when any gate fails. Result, at the tip of this branch: ``` RED 80 GREEN 0 INVALID 0 tree restored byte-identical: true ``` The first run of that battery was 46 RED / 32 GREEN / 9 INVALID. Every survivor was investigated individually rather than banked. Thirty-two were real coverage holes, closed by pinning the exact mounted set per auth configuration instead of spot-checking membership. The nine INVALID were the harness correctly refusing to score a mutation of a gate's comparison value, plus one output-parsing bug in the harness itself that mislabelled a genuine red. That one is worth naming: it failed safe, but it means the first run's greens were the finding and its invalids were not. A kill rate of 80 out of 80 is only worth something if the battery can also let something live, so it is checked against a mutation that provably cannot matter: swapping two names inside one credential array. The projected object holds the same keys, and key order is not observable in the payload, so that mutation has to survive. It did not. It went red, and the two assertions it tripped turned out to compare the returned array against a source-order literal, pinning order rather than membership. Those two now sort both sides like the other fifteen already did. Deleting any of the eighty names still fails the suite, reordering two of them no longer does. The last survivor to fall was `token_exchange_endpoint` on the Entra OBO branch. Deleting it left the suite green because the Entra case asserted the two fields that drop and never asserted the endpoint that stays. That would have dropped the token exchange endpoint from the payload for Entra OBO servers. ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Nothing imports the projections yet; the port consumes them - antd `useWatch` returns undefined for an unmounted field, RHF `watch` does not - That divergence moves mount gates, so it changes the payload, and it is not fixed here - `Form.List` child names are generated at runtime, so no static scan rules out duplicates ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

Both lists below are the same list, deliberately Before: an admin edits an MCP server and saves 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and click an existing server 2. They change the auth type, the transport, or a credential, and press Save Changes 3. The server updates, and an invalid stdio config or tool display name still surfaces the same error toast After: unchanged 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and click an existing server 2. They change the auth type, the transport, or a credential, and press Save Changes 3. The server updates, and an invalid stdio config or tool display name still surfaces the same error toast ## Relevant issues Builds on #37404 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Nothing user-facing changes, so a live-proxy before and after would be two identical screenshots. The honest evidence for a refactor is that the characterization net written against the old code still passes against the new code unmodified, plus a mutation battery showing the new tests are not vacuous. Both are below, captured at `770a4feb8d` Since this does touch the edit form, here is what to exercise by hand if you want a screenshot on the PR. Start the proxy and the dashboard, then on http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers 1. Open any existing server, change nothing, and press Save Changes; expect the success toast and no field changes on the row 2. Switch a server from `http` to `stdio`, paste `{"mcpServers": {"fs": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "x"]}}}` into the config box, and save; expect success and the command persisted 3. Repeat with `{not json` in that box; expect the toast "Invalid JSON in stdio configuration" 4. Clear the command field on the dedicated-fields path and save; expect "Stdio transport requires a command" 5. Switch a server from `oauth2` to `api_key` and save; expect the oauth endpoints cleared rather than left stale ### Regression net, unmodified from #37404 1. `npx vitest run "src/app/(dashboard)/mcp-servers/_components/mcp_server_edit.integration.test.tsx"` 2. `Tests 20 passed (20)`, with no change to any expected payload in that file ### Mutation battery on the extracted module Ten mutants applied one at a time to `editServerPayload.ts`, each reverted before the next, every run checked to have executed all 40 tests | mutant | removed behaviour | result | | --- | --- | --- | | U1 | stdio json missing-command check | 1 test red | | U2 | dedicated-path blank-command check | 1 test red | | U3 | admin-config explicit-null clearing | 1 test red | | U4 | openapi mapped to http | 1 test red | | U5 | removeStoredApp override | 1 test red | | U6 | dcr_bridge gate | 1 test red | | U7 | empty-scopes guard | 1 test red | | U8 | access-group name normalisation | 1 test red | | U9 | delegate_auth_to_upstream oauth2 gate | 1 test red | | U10 | oauth_passthrough Authorization gate | 1 test red | Kill rate 10/10. signals.title: refactor(ui): port the create key form off antd Form onto react-hook-form
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Create Key was the last big antd `Form` in the dashboard - antd `Form.Item` submits only mounted fields; nothing else reproduces that - Blocks removing antd, and the payload shape is easy to break silently How it solves it: - Moves the form onto react-hook-form with a mount registry - Registry records mounted field names and projects the store at submit - Submit payload is unchanged in both directions, key for key ## User Flow The contract here is zero functional change, so the two lists are identical on purpose. That identity is the deliverable, not a shortcut. Anything that differs between them is a bug in this PR. Before: a proxy admin creates a virtual key and the request carries exactly the fields that were on screen 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click "+ Create New Key" 2. They type a key name, leave every collapsible section closed, and click "Create Key" 3. The browser sends POST /key/generate carrying only the always-visible fields: team, key name, models, key type, user, duration, metadata 4. They repeat with "Optional Settings" expanded, and the same POST now also carries the budget, rate limit, guardrail, tag and access-group fields, each empty 5. They type a max budget, collapse "Optional Settings", and submit; the budget is not on the request at all, rather than being sent as an empty value 6. They expand "Optional Settings" again and the budget they typed is still in the box After: the same admin sees the same screens and the proxy receives the same requests 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click "+ Create New Key" 2. They type a key name, leave every collapsible section closed, and click "Create Key" 3. The browser sends POST /key/generate carrying only the always-visible fields: team, key name, models, key type, user, duration, metadata 4. They repeat with "Optional Settings" expanded, and the same POST now also carries the budget, rate limit, guardrail, tag and access-group fields, each empty 5. They type a max budget, collapse "Optional Settings", and submit; the budget is not on the request at all, rather than being sent as an empty value 6. They expand "Optional Settings" again and the budget they typed is still in the box ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, done once and left running for both sides: 1. Start the proxy: `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log` 2. Start the dashboard dev server: `cd ui/litellm-dashboard && npm run dev` 3. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=api-keys, open DevTools, go to the Network tab and filter on `key/generate` ### Before (8941f2a622) #### Every section closed 1. Click "+ Create New Key", type `proof-key` into Key Name, leave every section collapsed, click "Create Key" 2. In Network, open the `/key/generate` request and record its full Request Payload #### Optional Settings open 1. Click "+ Create New Key", type `proof-key-2` into Key Name, expand "Optional Settings", click "Create Key" 2. Record the full Request Payload #### Budget typed then collapsed 1. Click "+ Create New Key", type `proof-key-3` into Key Name, expand "Optional Settings", type `150.75` into Max Budget (USD) 2. Collapse "Optional Settings", expand it again, and confirm `150.75` is still in the box 3. Collapse "Optional Settings" once more, click "Create Key", record the full Request Payload ### After (4748856403) #### Every section closed 1. Same steps as Before 2. Record the full Request Payload and compare it key for key against the Before capture #### Optional Settings open 1. Same steps as Before 2. Record the full Request Payload and compare it key for key against the Before capture #### Budget typed then collapsed 1. Same steps as Before 2. Confirm `150.75` still survives the collapse and re-expand 3. Record the full Request Payload and compare it key for key against the Before capture The three After payloads should match the three Before payloads exactly, including which keys are absent rather than sent empty ## How the mounted set is reproduced antd hands `onFinish` exactly the fields mounted at submit time, and it keeps the values of unmounted ones so re-expanding a section restores what was typed. react-hook-form reaches only one of those per `shouldUnregister` setting: true reproduces the payload and destroys re-expansion, false reproduces re-expansion and ships keys the antd form omitted. Neither flag reaches both, so the store is kept whole and projected down to the mounted set through a registry that records which fields are currently mounted. Validation needs no equivalent, because RHF already skips unmounted fields, which is the same rule antd applies. Two smaller pieces of the `Form.Item` contract mattered to the payload. Defaults come from each field's own declaration rather than a blanket empty value, so a key that antd sent as `undefined` is not turned into `null` or `""`. And antd's `help` prop replaces the rule's message rather than sitting beside it, including when it is the empty string, so a field carrying help never shows a validation message even while `aria-invalid` is set. The shared `FormField` in this repo always renders `FieldError`, which is why it could not be reused here. The registry counts by name and the projection emits flat keys, so it holds only static literal names. A `Form.List` row, and the per-row sub-fields under it, generates its name at runtime, never lands in the mounted set, and would go missing from the payload without a sound. No such field exists in this form, so nothing here is broken today, but the next form to adopt this needs the registry taught about generated names first. That constraint used to sit in a comment at the export and is recorded here instead, so there is only one place to keep in sync with the code. ## What the tests prove The 60-case submit differential from #37405 runs unedited, and the port passed it on the first run with no gesture repair. Five cases were added for the classes a payload net misses by construction: a writer that lives outside the submit path, validation following the mounted set, Enter to submit, switch coercion, and a required message on a field carrying no help. Every binding was then checked individually by dropping it from the mounted projection, leaving the field rendered, bound and validating, so the key vanishes from the payload the way a real porting defect would. 29 mutants, each suite running all 65 cases, 28 killed on payload assertions with no crashes, and one survivor predicted in advance: `mcp_tool_permissions`, which the payload builder drops unconditionally, so removing it cannot change the request. Five bindings turned out to be held by exactly one case each, which is worth recording because it is a general trap rather than a quirk of this form. A payload builder that defaults, coalesces or unconditionally stamps a key hides that key's binding from every fixture that does not defeat the default. `duration` is coalesced to `null`, `metadata` defaults to `"{}"`, `disable_global_guardrails` is dropped when falsy, and `user_id` is stamped from the signed-in user for one owner type. That last one had no coverage at all before this PR: all sixty inherited cases pass whether or not the form's own `user_id` binding reaches the payload. ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats - antd widgets stay; only `Form` and `Form.Item` were replaced - `MountedFormField` is new and reusable for the remaining antd forms - Advanced Settings fields still come from the live `/openapi.json` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

They push a branch and open a PR at https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/37432 2. That is the point of the first case: the gateway was already billing Vertex batches at half price, and only the test had missed it. Each side runs a proxy booted from its own tree, both serving the same config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gemini-batch litellm_params: model: vertex_ai/gemini-3.6-flash vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEX_PROJECT vertex_location: us-central1 general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ### Before (8941f2a622) #### What a customer is billed for a Vertex batch 1. Boot the proxy from the base tree and ask it what the model costs: ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config vbc_config.yaml --port 55117 curl -s http://localhost:55117/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin)['data'][0]['model_info']; print(json.dumps({k: d[k] for k in ('input_cost_per_token','output_cost_per_token','input_cost_per_token_batches','output_cost_per_token_batches')}, indent=2))" ``` 2. It fails on the stale expectation, exactly as CI reports it: ``` assert cost > 0 > assert cost == pytest.approx(30 * 7.5e-07 + 15 * 3.75e-06) E assert 3.9375e-05 == 7.875e-05 ± 7.9e-11 E E comparison failed E Obtained: 3.9375e-05 E Expected: 7.875e-05 ± 7.9e-11 tests/test_litellm/batches/test_batch_utils.py:894: AssertionError =========================== short test summary info ============================ FAILED tests/test_litellm/batches/test_batch_utils.py::test_handle_completed_vertex_batch_computes_cost_usage_and_models 1 failed, 94 passed in 0.35s ``` ### After (df0d8ff15e) #### What a customer is billed for a Vertex batch 1. Boot the proxy from this branch and ask it the same question: ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config vbc_config.yaml --port 49395 curl -s http://localhost:49395/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin)['data'][0]['model_info']; print(json.dumps({k: d[k] for k in ('input_cost_per_token','output_cost_per_token','input_cost_per_token_batches','output_cost_per_token_batches')}, indent=2))" ``` 2. Same answer, since no runtime code changed: ```json { "input_cost_per_token": 7.5e-07, "output_cost_per_token": 3.75e-06, "input_cost_per_token_batches": 3.75e-07, "output_cost_per_token_batches": 1.875e-06 } ``` #### The batch-cost suite CI actually runs 1. It passes, now expecting the same `3.9375e-05` the live proxy prices: ``` ........................................................................ [ 75%] ....................... [100%] 95 passed in 0.32s ``` ## Type ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Reads the cost map, so promo pricing changes no longer break it - Dropping the batch-rate keys would raise KeyError, not an assertion ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] df0d8ff15ea2f65e9f1ba90209239f241cf16d91 passes /live-pr-risk

signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Vertex batch cost test hardcoded gemini-3.6-flash's published batch rates - Halving those rates left the required misc unit-test job red on staging How it solves it: - The test registers its own vertex model with fixed rates - Batch rates are not half the standard ones, so the assertion still bites - A future price refresh can no longer make it stale ## User Flow No runtime code changes here, so nothing an API caller does or sees moves. The person this reaches is the contributor whose PR is blocked by a red required check Before: a contributor opens any PR and the required misc unit-test job fails on a batch pricing assertion they never touched 1. They open a pull request against litellm_internal_staging 2. They watch the checks on their pull request, and "Unit Tests: MCP, Secrets, Containers & Misc / misc / Run tests" reports failure after about 10 minutes 3. They open the job and read `assert 3.9375e-05 == 7.875e-05`, pointing at a vertex batch cost case with no connection to their change 4. The same job is failing on pushes straight to litellm_internal_staging, so there is nothing they can fix on their own branch and the required check stays red After: the same contributor opens the same PR and the job goes green 1. They open a pull request against litellm_internal_staging 2. They watch the checks on their pull request, and "Unit Tests: MCP, Secrets, Containers & Misc / misc / Run tests" reports success 3. There is no unrelated pricing failure to read past, so the only check results left are the ones their own change produced ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5799 https://linear.app/litellm-ai/issue/LIT-5799 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This PR edits one test file and no runtime code, so there is no request whose response changes and nothing to curl against a live proxy. The observable thing that changes is the required check, so the proof below is that check's own failing case, captured on both sides, plus a mutation run showing the repaired assertion still catches the bug it exists to catch ### Before (559310f077) #### the failing assertion 1. `uv run --no-sync pytest "tests/test_litellm/batches/test_batch_utils.py::test_handle_completed_vertex_batch_computes_cost_usage_and_models" -q --no-header` 2. Output: ``` assert cost > 0 > assert cost == pytest.approx(30 * 7.5e-07 + 15 * 3.75e-06) E assert 3.9375e-05 == 7.875e-05 +- 7.9e-11 E comparison failed E Obtained: 3.9375e-05 E Expected: 7.875e-05 +- 7.9e-11 1 failed in 0.61s ``` #### the assertion still catches standard-vs-batch pricing 1. Swap the batch call type for the plain completion one so the cost map hands back standard rates instead of batch rates, then re-run the same case: ``` sed -i '140s/CallTypes.aretrieve_batch.value/CallTypes.completion.value/' litellm/batches/batch_utils.py uv run --no-sync pytest "tests/test_litellm/batches/test_batch_utils.py::test_handle_completed_vertex_batch_computes_cost_usage_and_models" -q --no-header ``` 2. Output: it passes. Halving the model's rates left the stale literals sitting exactly on the new standard rates, so the case was demanding standard pricing, and deleting the batch call type is what turns it green ``` 1 passed in 0.45s ``` ### After (983ab0f24e) #### the failing assertion 1. `uv run --no-sync pytest "tests/test_litellm/batches/test_batch_utils.py::test_handle_completed_vertex_batch_computes_cost_usage_and_models" -q --no-header` 2. Output: ``` . [100%] 1 passed in 0.44s ``` #### the assertion still catches standard-vs-batch pricing 1. Swap the batch call type for the plain completion one so the cost map hands back standard rates instead of batch rates, then re-run the same case: ``` sed -i '140s/CallTypes.aretrieve_batch.value/CallTypes.completion.value/' litellm/batches/batch_utils.py uv run --no-sync pytest "tests/test_litellm/batches/test_batch_utils.py::test_handle_completed_vertex_batch_computes_cost_usage_and_models" -q --no-header ``` 2. Output: the case fails under the mutation and passes once it is reverted, so the repaired assertion is still load-bearing ``` 1 failed in 0.52s ``` #### the whole file 1. `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_litellm/batches/test_batch_utils.py -q --no-header` 2. Output: ``` 95 passed in 0.75s ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes The test asserted `30 * 7.5e-07 + 15 * 3.75e-06`, which were gemini-3.6-flash's batch rates when it was written. Commit 94a29e0708 repriced that model at Google's introductory rates and halved every tier, batch included, so the code kept pricing the batch correctly at the new rates while the test kept demanding the old ones, and the failure read as exactly double Because every tier halved by the same factor, those old batch literals landed precisely on the model's new standard rates, so the case had quietly inverted into an assertion that batches get billed at standard prices. That is what the second Before case above shows: taking the batch call type out of the cost lookup is what makes the old case pass Rather than copy the new numbers in and wait for the next refresh to break it again, the case now registers a vertex model of its own with rates it owns. Its batch rates are deliberately not half its standard rates, so the assertion pins the specific fields the batch path is supposed to read instead of any across-the-board discount, and swapping the batch call type for the completion one still fails the case ## Caveats (if any) - The pinned gemini prices in the cost-calc tests can still go stale ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: refactor(ui): host KeyLifecycleSettings tests in react-hook-form instead of antd Form
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - This suite hosted the component in a real antd `Form` - Its suppression claimed that hosting was required - The create key form stopped driving it that way How it solves it: - Harness moves to react-hook-form with an explicit `Controller` - `value`, `onChange` and `id` now arrive as visible props - The `no-restricted-imports` suppression goes away with the import ## User Flow This is a test-only change, so there is no behavior for a user to observe on either side, and the two lists are identical by construction. The flow below is the one the suite covers, and it reads the same before and after because the component itself is untouched. Before: a proxy admin sets an expiry and a rotation schedule on a new key 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click "+ Create New Key" 2. They expand "Key Lifecycle" and pick an expiry from the duration control 3. They tick "Never expire" and the duration control stops accepting input 4. They untick it, turn on auto rotation, and pick a rotation interval 5. They click "Create Key" and the key comes back with the expiry and interval they chose After: the same admin sees the same screens and gets the same key back 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click "+ Create New Key" 2. They expand "Key Lifecycle" and pick an expiry from the duration control 3. They tick "Never expire" and the duration control stops accepting input 4. They untick it, turn on auto rotation, and pick a rotation interval 5. They click "Create Key" and the key comes back with the expiry and interval they chose ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix No shipped code changes here, so there is nothing for a live proxy to show differently. The component under test is byte-identical on both sides, and the check that matters is that it still behaves the same in the product. Setup, done once and left running for both captures: 1. Start the proxy: `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log` 2. Start the dashboard dev server: `cd ui/litellm-dashboard && npm run dev` 3. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=api-keys, open DevTools, and filter the Network tab on `key/generate` ### Before (8941f2a622) #### Expiry, never-expire, and rotation 1. Click "+ Create New Key", type `lifecycle-proof` into Key Name, expand "Key Lifecycle" 2. Set the duration to `30d`, tick "Never expire", and confirm the duration control is disabled 3. Untick "Never expire", turn on auto rotation, set the rotation interval to `7d` 4. Click "Create Key" and record the `/key/generate` Request Payload ### After (91cf27aa0a) #### Expiry, never-expire, and rotation 1. Same steps as Before 2. Record the `/key/generate` Request Payload and compare it key for key against the Before capture ## Type ✅ Test ## Caveats - Test-only: the component and every shipped file are untouched - `value`, `onChange` and `id` are the component's own declared props - Two auto-rotation cases were racing the select popup already `KeyLifecycleSettings` has always taken `value`, `onChange` and `id` as its own props; antd's `Form.Item` was supplying them invisibly rather than adding an API of its own. So the harness drives the same contract either way, and the component file is untouched by this PR. What changed is which host supplies the props, and #37442 moved the create key form onto supplying them directly, which is the integration this suite now mirrors. ## A latent race this surfaced Two of the auto-rotation cases were racing the Base UI select popup before this PR, and the antd harness was hiding it rather than avoiding it. `findByText` resolves the moment the option text lands in the DOM, but the popup still carries `pointer-events: none` until its open transition settles, so a click that arrives in that window is rejected. Every extra render is another chance to land in it, which is why the failure rate tracks the harness rather than the component: 0 failures in 6 runs under antd, 1 in 6 under plain React state, 5 in 6 under a react-hook-form `Controller`. The component is identical in all three. Both cases now take the same `PointerEventsCheckLevel.Never` that their sibling case in this file already used for this exact interaction, which stops user-event asserting on a CSS property jsdom never animates. That is the only thing it relaxes, and the assertions were checked to still bite: removing the click turns the first case red, and stubbing the propagation callback turns the second red along with two others. Ten consecutive runs pass. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(ui): rebuild nested and list paths in the mounted-field projection
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The mounted-field projection emitted one flat key per registered name - Credential paths and field-array rows both flattened, so the payload lost them - Splitting every name on `.` fixed that but diverged from antd - antd nests only for an array name, never for a dotted string How it solves it: - `name` accepts `string | readonly string[]` - An array nests, with a numeric segment as an array index - A string stays one literal key, dots included - 8 unit tests, including the flat-string case that pins the divergence ## User Flow Before: an admin saves an MCP server that authenticates with AWS SigV4, and the credentials never arrive 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and edit a server 2. They set Auth Type to AWS SigV4 and fill in region, access key and secret 3. They click Save Changes and the request returns 200 4. They reopen the same server and every credential field is empty again After: the same edit round-trips 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and edit a server 2. They set Auth Type to AWS SigV4 and fill in region, access key and secret 3. They click Save Changes and the request returns 200 4. They reopen the same server and the credentials they entered are still there ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The user flow above is the reproduction. The projection is a pure function, so behaviour is pinned by unit tests and the round-trip is what an admin would see once the MCP form graph consumes it. ``` MountedFormField.test.ts 8 passed create_key_button.integration.test.ts 65 passed ``` The second number is the one that matters. The create key form is the existing consumer of this projection, so it is the regression surface for a change to shared form plumbing. A passing count on a behaviour-preserving change cannot tell two trees apart, so that green was liveness-gated rather than trusted. With the projection gutted to return `undefined` for every value, the consumer suite goes red on a payload diff, `models` from `[]` to `undefined` and `team_id` from `null` to `undefined`, which is an assertion failure rather than a crash. The tree was restored byte-identical afterwards. That converts "their suite passed" into "their suite can detect this". ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) Behaviour that is not visible in the diff and that the next change here can undo silently. A numeric path segment is an array index, so `["env_vars","0","name"]` rebuilds an array holding one row rather than an object keyed `"0"`. A sparse index keeps its position instead of shifting later rows down. A mounted-but-unset field is emitted as a key holding `undefined` rather than omitted, which is what antd's own submit does, and the payload builder distinguishes an absent key from an explicitly undefined one. Nesting is opt-in because antd's `getNamePath` is `toArray`. `check_openapi_schema` registers names taken from a live `/openapi.json`, so its field set is a runtime input rather than source, and a spec property containing a dot would silently nest under an unconditional split. ## HANDOVER: the MCP form graph port is NOT in this PR This PR is the primitive only. The 92-field port of the MCP server form graph is not started beyond two fields, and this section exists so the next person does not rediscover any of it. **Measured surface.** 92 `<Form.Item` opens, 89 named, 3 unnamed, 57 distinct name literals, across 14 files under `mcp-servers/_components/`. Counting raw `Form.Item` occurrences gives 187 because it counts closing tags too. Use a brace-aware scan, not a regex: a `name=` on a continuation line and a `name={expr}` both defeat the obvious pattern. **Do the roots first.** This is the ordering constraint and it is not negotiable. `OpenAPIFormSection` takes an antd `FormInstance` and calls `setFieldsValue` and `resetFields` imperatively, and siblings thread the same instance, so children cannot move before their root provides react-hook-form equivalents. The two roots, `mcp_server_edit.tsx` and `CreateMCPServer.tsx`, are also the two largest files. **The graph is one atomic unit.** A half-ported form is two stores that do not merge: fields still on antd submit through `onFinish`, fields moved to react-hook-form submit through the projection, and the payload silently carries one set or the other. Two fields, `DcrBridgeToggle` and `TokenEndpointAuthMethodField`, are ported but deliberately NOT committed for this reason. Redo them with their root. **The port pattern.** `MountedFormField` is not a drop-in. Its children are a render prop receiving `{id, name, value, onChange, onBlur, aria-*}`, so every call site has its JSX children rewritten rather than its tag swapped. Every antd `Form.Item` child was receiving `value` and `onChange` it never declared, so a child that reads them without declaring them compiles fine and silently receives `undefined`. Nested names become arrays, not dotted strings. **Eight inversions need individual attention.** Six `valuePropName` and two `getValueProps`/`getValueFromEvent`. A reversed boolean does not fail to compile. `available_on_public_internet` is both an inversion and a coalesced key, which makes it the single most dangerous field in the graph. **Five keys cannot be proven by any payload assertion in the obvious way.** `allow_all_keys`, `available_on_public_internet`, `delegate_auth_to_upstream`, `oauth_passthrough` and `dcr_bridge` all resolve as `Boolean(raw ?? mcpServer.x)`. The `??` falls back to the stored server value when a binding is absent, so on a fixture where submitted equals stored, a deleted binding is invisible and a payload test passes either way. Any test covering the first two must set the stored value to the OPPOSITE of what the form submits; an equal-valued run is INVALID, not GREEN. Three of those five are forced to a constant by the payload builder and are therefore usable as harness controls rather than as coverage. `delegate_auth_to_upstream` is forced false when `auth_type` is not `oauth2`, `dcr_bridge` unless `isClientForwardedTokenMode`, and `oauth_passthrough` unless the server is none-auth with an `Authorization` extra header. On an `api_key` scenario all three are forced regardless of the submitted value, so deleting those bindings cannot move the payload and a red on them localises the defect to the harness. **The verification instrument changes when the code does.** Against antd, delete the `name` attribute: antd tolerates it by not registering the field, so the payload loses the key and the battery measures bindings. After the port that operator is degenerate, because `Controller` throws and the battery becomes a crash detector that reads as a clean sweep. Post-port, drop the binding from the mounted projection while the field still renders and validates. **Cost model, measured under contention so treat as upper bounds.** The edit suite is 19 tests at 43s, the create suite 71 tests at 214s. A per-binding battery rerunning a full suite is about 6.35 hours. `--bail=1` collapses a red mutation from 214s to 5s because only the first failure is needed for the verdict, so cost is dominated by survivors rather than by sweep size. Root scoping by import closure saves a further 18%: 19 edit-only fields, 21 create-only, 52 reachable from both. **One trap that cost real time.** The edit root binds all seven AWS credentials inline at `mcp_server_edit.tsx`, while `AwsSigV4Fields.tsx` is the create root's separate copy of the same seven. Same logical fields bound twice in two places, so a component-level import closure is blind to the edit root's copy. Port both and keep them consistent. **There are two field-array sites, not one.** `env_vars` in `EnvVarsSection` and `static_headers` in `MCPPermissionManagement`. The second feeds `reduceStaticHeaders`, so missing it is the same silent loss. **A port can turn a latent test defect into an intermittent one without touching it.** Measured by another lane on a byte-identical component, 6 runs per harness on the same machine and base: the antd `Form` harness failed 0 of 6, a native form with plain `useState` failed 1 of 6, and a native form with a react-hook-form `Controller` failed 5 of 6. The cause is not the port. Two cases were already racing the Base UI select popup, because `findByText` resolves as soon as the option text is in the DOM while the popup still carries `pointer-events: none` until its open transition settles, so a click landing in that window is rejected by user-event. The antd harness was hiding the race rather than avoiding it, and what moves the failure rate is render count, which a `Controller` raises. Any suite in this graph that drives a Base UI popup, select, dropdown, combobox or tooltip and asserts with `findBy*` before clicking carries the same latent race. The port will make it intermittent, it will present as "the port broke these tests", and the diff will look innocent. So: measure a popup-driving suite with REPEATED runs before concluding anything, because neither a single green nor a single red is evidence. Measure the pre-port harness too, which is how the component was shown not to have changed. The fix is `PointerEventsCheckLevel.Never` on the offending interaction, which relaxes only user-event's assertion about a CSS property jsdom never animates; look for a sibling case in the same file already using it for the same interaction, which is corroboration rather than invention. Then gate the fix: removing the click must turn the case red, and stubbing the callback must turn it red. A fix that makes a case vacuous leaves both gates green and tells you so. ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(tests): keep a host PROXY_BASE_URL out of request-derived URL tests
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The proxy reads its public origin from `PROXY_BASE_URL` first - A developer who sets it locally fails 65 OAuth URL tests How it solves it: - An autouse fixture clears it for every unit test - Sits beside the host AWS config isolation already in that conftest - Tests needing a configured origin still set it themselves ## User Flow No runtime code changes here, so nothing an API caller does or sees moves. The person this reaches is the developer running the unit suite on a machine that also has a proxy deployment configured Before: a developer with `PROXY_BASE_URL` exported for their own proxy runs the MCP OAuth suites and watches dozens of unrelated cases fail 1. They set `PROXY_BASE_URL` to their gateway's public origin so their local proxy hands out correct OAuth discovery URLs 2. They run the MCP OAuth and URL helper suites and get 65 failures across five files they never touched 3. They read one and see `redirect_uri` came back as their own gateway origin plus `/callback` where the case expected the origin the request carried 4. Nothing in the diff explains it, so they either chase a phantom regression or clear their environment and rerun to find out the code was fine all along After: the same developer, with the same variable still exported, runs the same suites and they all pass 1. They set `PROXY_BASE_URL` to their gateway's public origin so their local proxy hands out correct OAuth discovery URLs 2. They run the MCP OAuth and URL helper suites and all 676 cases pass 3. Their proxy still resolves its public origin from that variable when they actually start it, so the local deployment is unaffected ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5798 https://linear.app/litellm-ai/issue/LIT-5798 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This PR touches test scaffolding and no runtime code, so there is no request whose response changes and nothing to curl against a live proxy. What changes is whether the suite still passes on a machine that has a proxy configured, so both sides below run with `PROXY_BASE_URL=https://litellm.mycorp.example.com` exported, which is what a developer running a local gateway has ``` FILES="tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_mcp_management_endpoints.py \ tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/test_byok_oauth_endpoints.py \ tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/test_discoverable_endpoints.py \ tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/test_mcp_env_vars.py \ tests/test_litellm/proxy/utils/helpers/test_url_helpers.py" ``` ### Before (559310f077) #### the suites a configured origin breaks 1. `PROXY_BASE_URL=https://litellm.mycorp.example.com uv run --no-sync pytest $FILES -q --no-header -n 4` 2. Output: ``` FAILED tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/test_discoverable_endpoints.py::test_xff_misconfig_warning_emitted_once 65 failed, 611 passed, 34 warnings in 31.68s ``` #### the regression test that pins it 1. With the conftest fixture backed out: `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_litellm/test_conftest.py -q --no-header` 2. Output, with the leaked origin standing in for the one the request carried: ``` > assert exchange_mock.await_args.kwargs["redirect_uri"] == "https://litellm.example.com/callback" E AssertionError: assert 'https://leak....com/callback' == 'https://lite....com/callback' E - https://litellm.example.com/callback E + https://leaked-host-origin.example.com/callback 1 failed in 34.26s ``` ### After (69133f6baa) The only commit since, 9ef6a8826d, trims two docstrings and changes no behavior, so this run still stands #### the suites a configured origin breaks 1. `PROXY_BASE_URL=https://litellm.mycorp.example.com uv run --no-sync pytest $FILES -q --no-header -n 4` 2. Output: ``` 676 passed, 33 warnings in 28.43s ``` #### the regression test that pins it 1. `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_litellm/test_conftest.py -q --no-header` 2. Output: ``` . [100%] 1 passed in 30.11s ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `get_request_base_url` consults `PROXY_BASE_URL` before it looks at the request at all, which is right for a deployment sitting behind an ingress and wrong for a unit test, because every OAuth discovery, `redirect_uri`, and dynamic client registration case builds a request with a known `base_url` and asserts on what comes back out. A value in the developer's shell or `.env` replaces that origin everywhere, so 65 cases across five files fail on an origin no test supplied The conftest for `tests/test_litellm` already isolates host AWS configuration for exactly this reason, so the new fixture is one `delenv` sitting next to it. Every test that genuinely wants a configured public origin sets the variable inside its own body, and an autouse conftest fixture is ordered ahead of those, so they keep the value they set The regression test runs one of the sensitive cases in a subprocess with the variable deliberately poisoned. That is the only way to check what a test's starting environment looks like from inside the same session, and it means deleting the fixture turns the test red rather than leaving a check that passes either way on a clean CI runner It drops the coverage subprocess variables on the way into that child. Inheriting them makes the nested run measure coverage a second time, which took the case from 63 seconds to 282 in a CI-shaped run and buys nothing the parent's own measurement does not already have ## Caveats (if any) - A host `SERVER_ROOT_PATH` still breaks two discovery cases and six A2A agent card cases, and a host `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` still breaks the empty-database SSO settings case. Same class of leak, different variables, each wants its own probe, so they stay out of this PR - The regression only bites while its probe test keeps asserting on a request-derived URL; if that case changes, the check passes without proving anything ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] 9ef6a8826d passes /live-pr-risk

signals.title: fix(fireworks): strip pattern, title, default:null from tool param schemas
signals.text: ## Summary Fireworks AI rejects tool parameter schemas containing `pattern`, `title`, or `default: null`, returning 400 errors: - **`pattern`**: `"Conflict in schema definitions for key 'pattern'"` — occurs when LiteLLM's Anthropic→OpenAI translation injects a second `pattern` on a field that already has one from the client (e.g. Claude Code sends `^[^\n\r]*$`, LiteLLM adds `^[\s\S]{0,300}$`). Fireworks' grammar compiler sees two conflicting patterns and rejects the request. Reported by a Fireworks customer using Claude Code + LiteLLM + `kimi-k3`. - **`title` / `default: null`**: `"JSON Schema not supported: could not understand the instance {'default': None, 'title': 'Page Size'}"` — auto-emitted by Pydantic models from MCP servers. See #27821 and #28149. The existing `_transform_tools` only popped `strict` and inlined legacy `$ref` defs. The Anthropic path already strips these keywords (`filter_anthropic_output_schema` in #22447 / #21045 / #34319), but the Fireworks path had no equivalent recursive sanitizer. ## Changes **`litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/chat/transformation.py`**: - Added `_FIREWORKS_TOOL_SCHEMA_STRIP_KEYS` class constant (`pattern`, `title`) - Added `_sanitize_tool_schema` static method that recursively walks `properties`, `items`, `anyOf`/`allOf`/`oneOf`, and `$defs` to strip: - `pattern` (always removed — Fireworks compiles it into a constrained-decoding grammar; conflicts arise when multiple patterns land on the same field) - `title` (always removed) - `default` (only when value is `None`; non-null defaults preserved) - Wired into `_transform_tools` after the existing `unpack_legacy_defs` call **`tests/test_litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/chat/test_fireworks_schema_sanitize.py`**: - 20 new unit + integration tests covering: top-level removal, nested properties, array items, anyOf/allOf/oneOf, $defs, deeply nested schemas, field preservation, non-null default preservation (including falsy `False`), no-op on clean schemas, non-function tools, tools without parameters, and combined strict+pattern stripping ## Design decisions - **Fireworks-only**: The sanitizer lives on `FireworksAIConfig`, not in shared utils, so no other provider's tool schemas are affected. - **Preserves non-null defaults**: Only `default: null` is stripped. `{"default": 10}` and `{"default": False}` survive (Fireworks specifically chokes on null defaults). - **Recursive**: Handles arbitrarily nested schemas (MCP tools and Claude Code often produce complex schemas). - **Consistent with Anthropic path**: The Anthropic sanitizer already strips `pattern`, `title`-adjacent keywords, and other constrained-decoding constraints. This brings the Fireworks path to parity. ## Related issues - Closes #27821 - Closes #28149 - Related: #26692 (legacy `$ref` defs — already fixed), #22447 / #21045 / #34319 (Anthropic path schema filtering) ## Test plan - [x] `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/chat/test_fireworks_schema_sanitize.py` — 20 passed - [x] `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/chat/` — 108 passed (16 pre-existing caplog failures deselected, unrelated to this change) - [x] Black formatted Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signals.title: fix(logging): serialize mixed-type sets safely
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Mixed-type metadata sets break JSON log serialization - A TypeError prevents the log record from being emitted How it solves it: - Sort serialized set values by their JSON representation - Preserve deterministic output across heterogeneous values ## User Flow Before: a Python developer using JSON logs loses a record when metadata contains mixed set values 1. They enable JSON logging in their Python application 2. They emit an INFO record with label metadata containing `"beta"`, `7`, and `None` 3. Logging raises `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'NoneType'` After: the same record is emitted as valid JSON with every label preserved 1. They enable JSON logging in their Python application 2. They emit the same INFO record with label metadata containing `"beta"`, `7`, and `None` 3. Logging emits a JSON record whose labels are `["beta", 7, null]` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The same Python 3.12 environment and logging script were used for both runs ### Before (`c696fdfb05c2b11d9f7f4d06b23f4e783c85ef54`) 1. Run this logging script: ```bash python - <<'PY' import logging from litellm._logging import JsonFormatter record = logging.LogRecord("litellm", logging.INFO, __file__, 1, "request", (), None) record.metadata = {"labels": {"beta", 7, None}} print(JsonFormatter().format(record)) PY ``` 2. Observe `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'NoneType'` ### After (`b0689f99a472f128e7a7e3e4b32d69c9bc14f6d9`) 1. Run the same logging script: ```bash python - <<'PY' import logging from litellm._logging import JsonFormatter record = logging.LogRecord("litellm", logging.INFO, __file__, 1, "request", (), None) record.metadata = {"labels": {"beta", 7, None}} print(JsonFormatter().format(record)) PY ``` 2. Observe `{"metadata": {"labels": ["beta", 7, null]}}` in the emitted JSON record ## Type Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(batches): stop one bad output line from zeroing an entire batch's spend
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - One status-200 batch output line with an empty `body` raised inside batch costing - That error zeroed the whole batch's spend and made the cost poller re-error every cycle - A malformed or undecodable (invalid UTF-8) JSONL line in the output file had the same effect How it solves it: - Each output line is costed on its own; a line that cannot be costed is billed at $0 and warned - Malformed, undecodable, or non-object output lines are skipped with a warning instead of raising - The rest of the batch is billed normally and the poller marks the job done ## User Flow Before: a developer whose completed batch output carries one status-200 line with an empty body never sees that batch billed 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with `purpose=batch`, `target_model_names=gpt-4.1-mini`, and a two-line JSONL of chat requests; 200 back with a long scrambled file id 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with that `input_file_id`, `endpoint: /v1/chat/completions`, `completion_window: 24h`; 200 back, `status: validating`, a long scrambled batch id 3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it reads `status: completed`, `request_counts: 2/2`, `usage.total_tokens: 31` 4. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and see their two answers plus a third line whose `response.body` is `{}` 5. They check GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id}_batch_cost (or the Logs page) minutes later and still get `[]`: the batch sits at $0 spend indefinitely and the key, team, and daily spend totals never move for it After: the same batch is billed for its two healthy lines within a minute of completing 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with `purpose=batch`, `target_model_names=gpt-4.1-mini`, and a two-line JSONL of chat requests; 200 back with a long scrambled file id 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with that `input_file_id`, `endpoint: /v1/chat/completions`, `completion_window: 24h`; 200 back, `status: validating`, a long scrambled batch id 3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it reads `status: completed`, `request_counts: 2/2`, `usage.total_tokens: 31` 4. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and see their two answers plus a third line whose `response.body` is `{}` 5. Within a minute, GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id}_batch_cost returns one `aretrieve_batch` row for `gpt-4.1-mini` with 28 prompt and 3 completion tokens and `spend: 0.000008`; the empty-body line counts as $0 and the key, team, and daily spend totals move by the same amount ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5789 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, both legs: the proxy runs on port 35383 with Postgres, `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_INTERVAL=45`, master key `sk-1234`, and this deployment: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4.1-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4.1-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY api_base: http://127.0.0.1:45105 ``` Port 45105 is a tiny passthrough in front of `https://api.openai.com` that forwards every call unchanged except `GET /v1/files/{id}/content`, where it appends one extra line to the real output file: `{"custom_id": "request-poison-empty", "response": {"status_code": 200, "request_id": "inject-empty-body-1185", "body": {}}}`. That reproduces the customer's output file (one status-200 line with an empty body) on top of a real OpenAI batch. The batch is a real OpenAI batch, `batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189`, 2 chat requests on `gpt-4.1-mini`, completed 2/2: ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:35383/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -F purpose=batch -F target_model_names=gpt-4.1-mini -F file=@batch_input.jsonl {"id":"bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9vY3RldC1zdHJlYW07dW5pZmllZF9pZCwzZTljMDE0Ni0yNjJhLTQ3ZTItYjg5ZC0xNmNkNmU2ZjM2MjI7...","bytes":417,"created_at":1787129282,"filename":"modified_file.jsonl","object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"uploaded",...} $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:35383/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input_file_id": "<that file id>", "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions", "completion_window": "24h"}' {"id":"bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTttb2RlbF9pZDo1Nzg5YTExYjJjM2Q0ZTVmNjA3MTgyOTNhNGI1YzZkN2U4ZjkwYTFiMmMzZDRlNWY2MDcxODI5M2E0YjVjNmQ3O2xsbV9iYXRjaF9pZDpiYXRjaF82YTg1NmRjOWI0NWM4MTkwOTU2OGJiOTE5MGJmMTE4OQ","completion_window":"24h","created_at":1787129289,"endpoint":"/v1/chat/completions",...,"status":"validating",...} $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:35383/v1/batches/<batch id> -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" # ~3 minutes later {"status": "completed", "request_counts": {"completed": 2, "failed": 0, "total": 2}, "usage": {"total_tokens": 31, "input_tokens": 28, "output_tokens": 3, ...}, "output_file_id": "bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9qc29uO3VuaWZpZWRfaWQsODY0ODcwNjAtOWM5NS01ZmZlLTkzZDgtMDU5MGE1ZDIyNWM1O..."} $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:35383/v1/files/<output file id>/content -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"id": "batch_req_6a856e4862ac819093f9278db3ebb658", "custom_id": "req-1", "response": {"status_code": 200, ..., "body": {"id": "chatcmpl-EEWGweQMfHyv4lVQklDf116jkDUgE", "object": "chat.completion", "model": "gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14", "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hello!", ... {"id": "batch_req_6a856e486b0881909a103ac8f05144e2", "custom_id": "req-2", "response": {"status_code": 200, ..., "body": {"id": "chatcmpl-EEWHtka04uPUWZWaHOMz2mD1IUOwJ", "object": "chat.completion", "model": "gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14", "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Blue", ... {"custom_id": "request-poison-empty", "response": {"status_code": 200, "request_id": "inject-empty-body-1185", "body": {}}} ``` ### Before (ec6f1c1a56) 1. The cost poller picks the completed batch up and errors on the empty-body line, then keeps re-erroring on every 45s cycle (proxy log, three consecutive cycles): ``` 01:51:54 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: check_batch_cost.py:591 - Batch ID: batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 is complete, tracking cost and usage 01:51:55 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: check_batch_cost.py:881 - CheckBatchCost: failed to track cost for batch batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 (job 35332d3a-c1ad-4c82-954f-f4a9234f9755); leaving it unprocessed so the next poll retries: Model is None and does not exist in passed completion_response. Passed completion_response={} 01:53:08 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: check_batch_cost.py:591 - Batch ID: batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 is complete, tracking cost and usage 01:53:08 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: check_batch_cost.py:881 - CheckBatchCost: failed to track cost for batch batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 (job 35332d3a-c1ad-4c82-954f-f4a9234f9755); leaving it unprocessed so the next poll retries: Model is None and does not exist in passed completion_response. Passed completion_response={} 01:54:21 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: check_batch_cost.py:591 - Batch ID: batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 is complete, tracking cost and usage 01:54:22 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: check_batch_cost.py:881 - CheckBatchCost: failed to track cost for batch batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 (job 35332d3a-c1ad-4c82-954f-f4a9234f9755); leaving it unprocessed so the next poll retries: Model is None and does not exist in passed completion_response. Passed completion_response={} ``` 2. Three minutes after completion the only spend row tied to the batch is the $0 creation row; no cost row exists and the whole database still sums to $0: ``` $ curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:35383/spend/logs?request_id=<batch id>" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" [{"call_type": "acreate_batch", "model": "openai/gpt-4.1-mini", "spend": 0.0, "total_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens": 0, "startTime": "2026-08-19T08:48:09.332000Z"}] $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select call_type, model, spend, total_tokens from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" where request_id = '<batch id>' or metadata::text like '%batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189%';" call_type | model | spend | total_tokens ---------------+---------------------+-------+-------------- acreate_batch | openai/gpt-4.1-mini | 0 | 0 $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select count(*) as spend_rows, coalesce(sum(spend),0) as total_spend from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\";" spend_rows | total_spend ------------+------------- 18 | 0 $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select status, batch_processed from \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" where model_object_id='batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189';" status | batch_processed -----------+----------------- completed | f ``` ### After (608d749983) 1. Same DB, same batch, same passthrough still appending the empty-body line. The poller costs the batch on its first pass, warns about the one bad line, bills the rest, and later cycles do not touch it again: ``` 01:56:50 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: check_batch_cost.py:591 - Batch ID: batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 is complete, tracking cost and usage 01:56:50 - LiteLLM:WARNING: batch_utils.py:135 - batch output line could not be costed, so it is billed at $0 and the rest of the batch is still billed. custom_id=request-poison-empty error=Model is None and does not exist in passed completion_response. Passed completion_response={}, model=None 01:56:50 - LiteLLM:DEBUG: batch_utils.py:227 - batch output aggregate: cost=8e-06 usage=Usage(completion_tokens=3, prompt_tokens=28, total_tokens=31, ...) models=['gpt-4.1-mini'] 01:58:02 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: scheduled_job_stagger.py:341 - Scheduled job check_batch_cost_job started ... (no further "failed to track cost" lines on this or any later cycle) ``` 2. The batch now has a spend row and the job is marked done: ``` $ curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:35383/spend/logs?request_id=<batch id>_batch_cost" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" [{"call_type": "aretrieve_batch", "model": "gpt-4.1-mini", "spend": 8e-06, "total_tokens": 31, "prompt_tokens": 28, "completion_tokens": 3, "startTime": "2026-08-19T08:56:50.332000Z"}] $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select status, batch_processed from \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" where model_object_id='batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189';" status | batch_processed ----------+----------------- complete | t $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select model, spend, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens from \"LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend\" where model = 'gpt-4.1-mini';" model | spend | prompt_tokens | completion_tokens --------------+-------+---------------+------------------- gpt-4.1-mini | 8e-06 | 28 | 3 ``` ### Re-run at the tip (5eeccf69b6) After merging `litellm_internal_staging` into the branch (51cafe4365), both scenarios were re-driven at the tip on fresh DBs with the same rig: the inline retrieve and the cost poller each warn on the injected lines and bill `8e-06 / 31 tokens`, the managed object reads `complete | t`, and `LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend` reads `gpt-4.1-mini | 8e-06 | 28 | 3` Cursor Bugbot then flagged that a batch output line that is not valid UTF-8 still aborted billing, since `json.loads` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` there, which `except json.JSONDecodeError` does not catch. 5eeccf69b6 catches `ValueError` instead and was A/B'd on the same rig with the passthrough also appending `{"custom_id": "request-bad-utf8", "note": "\xff"}` (a raw `0xff` byte). Before the fix the retrieve leaves no spend row and the proxy log shows the abort; at the tip the line is skipped and the batch still bills: ``` # before the fix (51cafe4365) UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 43: invalid start byte $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select request_id, spend, total_tokens from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\";" # no rows # at the tip (5eeccf69b6) 14:37:23 - LiteLLM:WARNING: batch_utils.py:430 - skipping malformed batch output line: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 43: invalid start byte $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select request_id, spend, total_tokens from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\";" batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189_batch_cost | 8e-06 | 31 ``` A control retrieve at the tip with the passthrough disarmed bills the same `8e-06 / 31` with zero warnings ## Live PR risk (base vs head A/B) live-pr-risk: CHECKED at 5eeccf69b6. No breaking dependent path. One backward-incompatible contract change (intended, see below). Not verified: the Vertex `disable_vertex_batch_output_transformation` path. Changed surface: `_iter_batch_input_entries` renamed to `_iter_batch_output_entries` and it now skips malformed or non-object lines (raises change); `_get_file_content_as_dictionary` inherits that; `_iter_successful_output_line_stats` now isolates per-line costing failures (raises change); `dict` parameter annotations widened to `Mapping[str, Any]` (no runtime effect); `_parse_batch_output_line` catches `ValueError` rather than only `json.JSONDecodeError`, so an undecodable (invalid UTF-8) line is skipped like a malformed one instead of aborting the pass. Dependents reached from outside the module, ranked by reachability: (1) `GET /v1/batches/{raw_id}` and `litellm.aretrieve_batch` through `litellm_logging.async_success_handler` -> `_handle_completed_batch` (tests mock `_handle_completed_batch`, so untested live); (2) the enterprise cost poller `check_batch_cost._track_completed_batch_cost` -> `_get_file_content_as_dictionary` -> `calculate_batch_cost_and_usage` (tests mock `_get_file_content_as_dictionary`); (3) `_handle_completed_batch`'s Vertex branch -> `calculate_vertex_ai_batch_cost_and_usage(_get_file_content_as_dictionary(...))` (only the malformed-line skip reaches it; unit-tested at the helper level, not driven live). `batch_rate_limiter` uses the unchanged `_iter_batch_input_lines`, so it is not a dependent. No string dispatch, registry, config key, DB column, dashboard, SDK client, or docs reference to any changed symbol (grepped `litellm/`, `enterprise/`, `ui/`, `litellm/proxy/client/`, `~/Development/litellm-docs`). Rig: base ec6f1c1a56 (the merge base when the A/B first ran) and head on separate ports with separate fresh Postgres DBs, same config, `litellm.__file__` asserted per side. Real OpenAI upstream behind a passthrough that appends one empty-body line, one non-JSON line, and (since the 5eeccf69b6 leg) one invalid-UTF-8 line to every `GET /v1/files/*/content`. `origin/litellm_internal_staging` was later merged into the branch at 51cafe4365 (merge base now e126975468); the drift touches none of `batch_utils.py`, `check_batch_cost.py`, or `litellm_logging.py` and is annotation-only in `cost_calculator.py`, so the base legs stand, and the head legs were re-run at 51cafe4365 (both scenarios) and at 5eeccf69b6 (undecodable-line A/B plus a clean control), all passing. Scenario 1, inline retrieve of a completed raw batch id (path 1), poisoned file. Base: `LoggingWorker error: Model is None ... completion_response={}` from `_handle_completed_batch`, no `aretrieve_batch` spend row at all. Head: `WARNING batch_utils.py:135 ... custom_id=request-poison-empty`, `WARNING batch_utils.py:430 - skipping malformed batch output line`, `batch output aggregate: cost=8e-06 ... total_tokens=31`, spend row `aretrieve_batch | 8e-06 | 31`. Control with the passthrough disarmed: both sides aggregate `cost=8e-06`, identical response bodies, identical spend rows. Scenario 2, managed batch through the enterprise poller (path 2), one new gpt-4.1-mini batch per side, poisoned output. Base: `CheckBatchCost: failed to track cost for batch batch_6a857319a6a08190b360862029606fd1 ... leaving it unprocessed so the next poll retries: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` at 02:18:55 and again at 02:20:01, managed object `validating | batch_processed f`, no `aretrieve_batch` row. Head: both warnings, `batch output aggregate: cost=8e-06 ... models=['gpt-4.1-mini']`, spend row `aretrieve_batch | gpt-4.1-mini | 8e-06 | 31`, managed object `complete | t`, `LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend` `gpt-4.1-mini | 8e-06 | 28 | 3`, no error on later cycles. Backward incompatible: the poller's "leave unprocessed and retry" contract no longer covers a bad output line. Before, one uncostable or malformed line kept the job unprocessed forever (and bumped `litellm_check_batch_cost_errors_total{cost_tracking_error}` every cycle); now the healthy lines are billed once, the bad line is $0 with a WARNING, and the job is marked processed. Fetch failures and aggregate-level failures still retry. An unmapped model was already billed at $0 without raising on both sides, so the per-line try/except does not change that case. Not verified: Vertex batches with `disable_vertex_batch_output_transformation` (needs a Vertex batch job plus GCS output; the only behavior change on that path is the malformed-line skip, covered by `test_parse_jsonl_malformed_lines_skipped` and `test_iter_output_entries_skips_malformed_and_non_object_lines`). ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - A line that cannot be costed is billed at $0 with a warning, not retried; the cost poller no longer leaves such a batch unprocessed for a later retry (see Live PR risk) ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(llms): add Token Kiosk provider integration
signals.text: ## Summary Adds **Token Kiosk** (`https://agent-router.gaib.ai/v1`) as a supported LLM provider in LiteLLM. - Adds `TOKEN_KIOSK = "token_kiosk"` in `LlmProviders` (`litellm/types/utils.py`) - Adds `token_kiosk` to `openai_compatible_providers` in `litellm/constants.py` - Creates `TokenKioskConfig` (`litellm/llms/token_kiosk/chat/transformation.py`) with default base URL `https://agent-router.gaib.ai/v1` - Registers `TokenKioskConfig` in `ProviderConfigManager` and `_lazy_imports_registry.py` - Adds unit tests in `tests/test_litellm/test_token_kiosk.py`

signals.title: test(ui): give the Member Role Select more time to open in CI
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - UI Unit Tests fail intermittently on `litellm_internal_staging` - One case in `user_search_modal.test.tsx` times out looking for the admin option - The Select mounts via a portal and the default 1000ms window runs out under 14-fork parallelism How it solves it: - Raise the option lookup timeout to 5000ms, matching the 3000ms pattern already in the file - No product code change; the case still asserts the same submit payload ## User Flow Not applicable, this is a test-only change to a flaky case; no user-visible behaviour differs. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### Before (parent 0700b1e54e, tip c696fdfb05) 1. Push lands on `litellm_internal_staging`, workflow UI Unit Tests runs `npm run test -- --run --pool forks --poolOptions.forks.maxForks=14` on a 16-core runner 2. The `UserSearchModal submit payload > carries a role changed off its default into the payload` case fails after 1630ms with `Unable to find role="option" and name /^admin/` and no listbox in the ignored-body dump ([run 32225855539](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/32225855539/job/95985296306)) 3. Same failure has repeated on 5 of the last 8 pushes to staging: runs 32212443909, 32212447968, 32220389183, 32221449993, 32222734805, 32225855539 ### After (this branch) 1. `cd ui/litellm-dashboard && CI=true npx vitest run --pool forks --poolOptions.forks.maxForks=14 src/components/common_components/user_search_modal.test.tsx`, repeated 8 times, all report `Tests 9 passed (9)` 2. The bumped 5000ms window absorbs the base-ui Select's portal mount even when other fork workers are competing for CPU ## Type Test ## Caveats (if any) - Only patches this one case; a similar guardrail info characterization test has also been observed flaky and is out of scope here ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
