signals.title: feat(cli): add `lite login --config-claude` to wire Claude Code at login
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Claude Code users re-wire `~/.claude/settings.json` by hand after every login - `lite up` does it, but only while it runs, and reverts on exit - The apiKeyHelper `lite up` writes is malformed and returns nothing How it solves it: - `lite login --config-claude` writes that config persistently - Unrelated Claude Code settings preserved; plain `lite login` unchanged - Credential reached via apiKeyHelper, so re-login refreshes it - Fixes the helper's option order so it actually parses ## User Flow Before: a developer proxying Claude Code through LiteLLM has to re-point Claude Code at the proxy by hand every time their login expires 1. They run `lite --base-url https://litellm-domain login` and complete the browser sign-in 2. They open `~/.claude/settings.json` in an editor and paste the proxy URL and a token in themselves, or they keep a `lite up` process alive in a spare terminal for as long as they want Claude Code proxied 3. If they instead try `lite --base-url https://litellm-domain login --config-claude`, the CLI answers `Error: No such option: --config-claude` and exits 2 4. If they took the `lite up` route, closing that terminal restores the old settings and Claude Code goes straight back to Anthropic 5. Either way, tomorrow's login means doing it all again After: the same developer wires Claude Code up once, at login, and re-login keeps it working 1. They run `lite --base-url https://litellm-domain login --config-claude` and complete the same browser sign-in 2. The CLI prints `Login successful!` and then `Configured Claude Code: ~/.claude/settings.json now routes through https://litellm-domain.` 3. They open `~/.claude/settings.json` and see their theme, permissions and other env vars exactly as they left them, with the proxy URL added alongside 4. They run `claude` in any terminal, with no wrapper, and it answers through the proxy 5. When the login expires they run the same command again and Claude Code keeps working, with nothing to copy and no process to keep alive ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5817 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical for both sides: a live proxy on `:4817` backed by real Postgres and Redis, serving real Anthropic through `anthropic/*`, and a sandboxed `HOME` seeded with a pre-existing `~/.claude/settings.json` carrying a theme, permissions and an unrelated env var. `lite` is on `PATH` in both legs. The browser leg of the CLI SSO flow is stood in for by writing the completed session to the same Redis key `/sso/callback` writes; every other step is a real HTTP call against the running proxy. ```bash $ cat ~/.claude/settings.json { "theme": "dark", "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(git status)", "Read"], "deny": ["Bash(rm -rf *)"] }, "env": { "MY_TEAM_FLAG": "keep-me" } } ``` ### Before (133e72c8fd) #### The flag does not exist 1. Confirm the tree really lacks it, so the leg cannot pass for the wrong reason ``` $ grep -c "config-claude" litellm/proxy/client/cli/commands/auth.py 0 $ ls litellm/proxy/client/cli/commands/claude_settings.py absent ``` 2. Run the command ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 login --config-claude Usage: lite login [OPTIONS] Try 'lite login --help' for help. Error: No such option: --config-claude exit=2 ``` 3. The nearest thing that does exist offers nothing either ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 login --help Usage: lite login [OPTIONS] Login to LiteLLM proxy using SSO authentication Options: --help Show this message and exit. ``` #### The apiKeyHelper `lite up` writes is rejected by its own CLI 1. Run the exact command `lite up` puts in `~/.claude/settings.json` ``` $ lite auth print-token --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 Try 'lite auth print-token --help' for help. Error: No such option: --base-url exit=2 ``` 2. Claude Code gets an empty token from it, so the request is refused ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4817/v1/messages -H "x-api-key: " ... {"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, No api key passed in.","type":"auth_error","code":"401"}} ``` ### After (210ea7fe4d) #### Login writes the config and preserves everything else 1. Run the login ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 login --config-claude Opening browser to: http://127.0.0.1:4817/sso/key/generate?source=litellm-cli&key=cli-<login-id> Please complete the SSO authentication in your browser... Verification code: <code> Waiting for authentication... ``` 2. Complete the browser sign-in, then watch the CLI finish ``` Login successful! JWT Token: _somTPYtyB9DYmSKESqX... You can now use the CLI without specifying --api-key Configured Claude Code: ~/.claude/settings.json now routes through http://127.0.0.1:4817. Your other Claude Code settings were left untouched. Restart Claude Code to pick this up. ``` 3. Read the file back: theme, permissions and `MY_TEAM_FLAG` are untouched, the two proxy settings are added, and the mode tightened from `0644` to `0600` ``` $ cat ~/.claude/settings.json { "theme": "dark", "permissions": { "allow": [ "Bash(git status)", "Read" ], "deny": [ "Bash(rm -rf *)" ] }, "env": { "MY_TEAM_FLAG": "keep-me", "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:4817" }, "apiKeyHelper": "/.../bin/lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 auth print-token" } $ stat -f '%Sp' ~/.claude/settings.json -rw------- ``` #### The apiKeyHelper it wrote actually runs 1. Execute the helper string on its own, exactly as Claude Code does ``` $ /.../bin/lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 auth print-token _somTPYtyB9DYmSKESqXpzqd... (784 chars) ``` #### It refuses while another command owns the file 1. Simulate a running `lite autoroute up` session, which backs up to a different path than `lite up` does ``` $HOME/.litellm/autorouter/claude_settings_backup.json present $HOME/.litellm/claude_settings_backup.json absent ``` 2. Run the login and watch it refuse the settings write while still completing the login ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 login --config-claude Login successful! JWT Token: tAELCbEebUGE-NDxfAIq... You can now use the CLI without specifying --api-key Error: Logged in, but could not configure Claude Code: `lite autoroute up` is currently managing ~/.claude/settings.json (backup at ~/.litellm/autorouter/claude_settings_backup.json) and will restore it when it stops. Run `lite autoroute down` first, then retry. ``` 3. Confirm the file was left alone ``` $ grep -c ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL ~/.claude/settings.json 0 $ grep -c apiKeyHelper ~/.claude/settings.json 0 ``` #### Real Claude Code reaches real Anthropic through the proxy 1. Launch Claude Code bare, with no wrapper and no env vars, so its only configuration is the file the login wrote ``` $ claude -p "Reply with exactly: LIT-5817 end to end" LIT-5817 end to end exit: 0 ``` 2. Confirm it went through the proxy rather than to Anthropic directly ``` $ grep -oE '"POST /v1/messages[^"]*" [0-9]{3}' proxy.log | sort | uniq -c 1 "POST /v1/messages HTTP/1.1" 401 <- the Before leg, with the malformed helper 5 "POST /v1/messages?beta=true HTTP/1.1" 200 ``` 3. Confirm the proxy booked real spend for it ``` $ psql -d litellm -c 'select model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, spend from "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" ...' anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 1180 | 18 | 0.00635000 anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 31116 | 12 | 0.19477250 anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 1180 | 1 | 0.00592500 anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 31116 | 12 | 0.19477250 anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 1180 | 1 | 0.00592500 anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 31116 | 12 | 0.19477250 $ psql -d litellm -c 'select count(*), sum(spend) from "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"' 7 | 0.60251750 ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix ## Review notes Greptile's P1 was real and is fixed. Its placement was better than mine: normalizing the read-side `OSError` inside `load_json_or_empty` rather than at my call site fixes `lite up` and `lite autoroute` at the same time, so I took its version. A regression test drives it by pointing the loader at a directory, and the mutation that narrows the catch back to `FileNotFoundError` fails that test. Round four was a CI red, not a review finding: the `lint` job's basedpyright gate rejected `owner: Final` bound inside the guard's loop (`A "Final" variable cannot be assigned within a loop`, `reportGeneralTypeIssues`, ceiling 0). Rather than drop the annotation, the registry now carries explicit `SettingsFileOwner(backup_path, start_command, stop_command)` records. That removes the loop-local binding, and with it a `== AUTOROUTE_BACKUP_PATH` identity check and a `.replace(' up', ' down')` string surgery that derived one command name from another. Same messages, no behaviour change, and the test for the autoroute case no longer has to patch a module constant to reach it. Round three came from a second reviewer and found the sharpest issue in the PR, which neither I nor Greptile had caught: the "another command owns this file" guard checked only `lite up`'s backup path, while `lite autoroute up` backs up to `~/.litellm/autorouter/claude_settings_backup.json`. So the exact hazard the guard existed for was still open through autoroute, which would have restored over this write with a success message. `claude_settings.py` now owns the registry of both owners and the guard iterates it, with a test that pins the registry against the path `autoroute` actually uses so the two definitions cannot drift. Two more from the same round, both specific to this write being persistent where `lite up`'s is backed up and reverted. `write_private_json` ends in `os.replace`, which swaps a symlinked `settings.json` for a regular file, silently detaching a dotfiles repo with nothing to restore from; the write now resolves a symlink and updates its target instead. And `merge_claude_settings` coerces a non-object `env` to `{}`, which is recoverable under `lite up` and permanent data loss here, so the persistent path refuses instead. That strictness is deliberately scoped to this path so `lite up` keeps its existing tolerance. Round two: Greptile then found that `UnicodeDecodeError` is a `ValueError`, not an `OSError`, so a settings file containing invalid UTF-8 still escaped the boundary the round-one fix had just built. Real, and confirmed by driving it. Rather than add a second `except`, the loader now reads bytes and hands them straight to the JSON validator, which removes the decode step altogether; a file that is not valid UTF-8 is not valid JSON, and it now reports as such. Mutating the read back to text fails the new test. Separately, while checking that round, I found a coverage gap the suite could not see: `lite up` calls `ctx.invoke(login)` on the real command object, but every `_ensure_fresh_login` test monkeypatches `up_module.login` with a fake, so no test would have noticed a login parameter `ctx.invoke` cannot supply. Adding `--config-claude` is exactly that kind of change. Two tests now drive the real command through `ctx.invoke` and assert both that it binds and that it leaves `~/.claude/settings.json` alone without the flag. Its P2 on the merge mutation is taken too; `env` is now built declaratively with no `pop`. That also removed the one LIT002 violation this PR added, so the `lint` budget gate goes from `total 26899 over limit 26886` to `OK: every LIT rule is within its codebase ceiling`. I have not taken the P2 asking for the docs to move to the `litellm-docs` repository. The section I added sits directly under the existing `lite up` section in the CLI's own README, and `lite up` is documented nowhere in `litellm-docs` (`grep -rn "lite up" litellm-docs/docs/` returns nothing), so that file is where this surface already lives rather than a customer-facing docs page I am bypassing. Happy to open a companion docs PR if the whole `lite up` / `lite autoroute` surface should be published there, but moving only the new subsection would split one section across two repositories. ## Caveats (if any) - Claude CLI only; VS Code and JetBrains are follow-ups - Shared settings handling moved out of `up.py` to break a cycle - Refuses while `lite up` or `lite autoroute up` holds the file - Forces the settings file to 0600; `lite up` leaves umask default - Proxy base URL disables Claude Code's MCP tool search by default ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix: omit thinking.type=disabled for always-on thinking Claude models
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` forwarded verbatim to Fable/Mythos models - those models 400: "thinking.type.disabled is not supported for this model" - routers retargeting requests across model generations hit this constantly How it solves it: - new cost map flag `thinking_always_on` on Fable/Mythos entries - Anthropic, /v1/messages, and Bedrock Converse transforms omit the param when flagged - omission is the API documented remedy; model thinks adaptively by default ## User Flow Before: a caller whose request was valid on Claude Sonnet 4.5 gets a 400 when a router sends the same request to Claude Fable 5 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model": "claude-fable-5"`, `"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}` 2. The response is a 400 with `"thinking.type.disabled" is not supported for this model. Thinking defaults to adaptive mode when not specified` 3. The same body against a router model group fails the whole request whenever the router picks a Fable 5 deployment, even though the request was valid on the model the caller originally targeted After: the same request succeeds; the model thinks adaptively as the API prescribes 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model": "claude-fable-5"`, `"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}` 2. The response is a 200 with the model's normal content; the gateway omitted the unsupported param and logged a warning 3. Requests carrying `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` to models that accept it (Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Sonnet 5) are forwarded byte for byte, unchanged ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Setup: local proxy on :4620 from this branch, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`, real Postgres, models `claude-fable-5` and `claude-sonnet-4-5` served through a live Anthropic-compatible upstream (real provider account for this repo is out of credit; the upstream is the team's live gateway hitting the real Anthropic API, so requests, money, and the 400 are real). Config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-fable-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-fable-5 api_base: https://<gateway-host> api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN - model_name: claude-sonnet-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 api_base: https://<gateway-host> api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ### Before (4bb3152cc5) #### /v1/messages, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. `curl -s -w "HTTP %{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4620/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"claude-fable-5","max_tokens":64,"thinking":{"type":"disabled"},"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi repro leg 1"}]}'` 2. `HTTP 400` with `"\"thinking.type.disabled\" is not supported for this model. Thinking defaults to adaptive mode when not specified; use \"thinking.type.enabled\" with \"budget_tokens\" for extended thinking"` #### /v1/chat/completions, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. Same body against http://127.0.0.1:4620/v1/chat/completions 2. `HTTP 400`, `litellm.BadRequestError: AnthropicException` wrapping the same provider error #### /v1/messages, claude-sonnet-4-5, thinking disabled (negative control) 1. Same body with `"model": "claude-sonnet-4-5"` 2. `HTTP 200`, normal text content (this model accepts disabled) ### After (63f1f11eaf) #### /v1/messages, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. Same curl as Before 2. `HTTP 200`, content starts with an adaptive thinking block then text; proxy log shows `Dropping thinking={'type': 'disabled'} for model=claude-fable-5: thinking is always on for this model and cannot be disabled. The model thinks adaptively when the param is omitted.` #### /v1/chat/completions, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. Same curl as Before (max_tokens 2048 so text survives the thinking budget) 2. `HTTP 200`, `content: "Hi! ..."`, `model: claude-fable-5` #### /v1/messages, claude-sonnet-4-5, thinking disabled (negative control) 1. Same curl as Before 2. `HTTP 200`, normal text content, request body forwarded unchanged (no warning logged) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Bedrock Converse arm covered by unit tests only; no AWS credentials in this rig - /v1/responses already converts `thinking` to `reasoning`, never forwards disabled - Opus 5 `disabled` plus `output_config.effort xhigh/max` is a caller contradiction, untouched - unmapped future Fable/Mythos ids covered by a `fallback_generalizations` rule ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 63f1f11eafc92ee42b30b8e9e25b151ede9edb2e. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY --> - [x] 63f1f11eaf passes /live-pr-risk

signals.title: fix(anthropic): handle Authorization header case-insensitively
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Capitalized `Authorization` headers bypass Anthropic OAuth detection. - Standard HTTP header casing can therefore break OAuth requests. How it solves it: - Looks up `Authorization` header names case-insensitively. - Adds a regression test for capitalized header casing. ## User Flow Before: a developer sends an Anthropic OAuth token using the standard `Authorization` header casing, but LiteLLM does not recognize it as OAuth. 1. They send an Anthropic request with `Authorization: Bearer sk-ant-oat...`. 2. LiteLLM fails to recognize that capitalized header as the OAuth credential. 3. The request does not receive the expected Anthropic OAuth authentication handling. After: the same request is recognized regardless of HTTP header-name casing. 1. They send the same Anthropic request with `Authorization: Bearer sk-ant-oat...`. 2. LiteLLM recognizes the OAuth credential case-insensitively. 3. The request receives the expected Anthropic OAuth authentication handling. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix No live E2E proof attached yet. This draft currently includes regression-test coverage for the header-casing behavior. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `make lint` passes locally. - Anthropic common-utils tests pass: 152/152. - LLM suite: 9003 passed, 83 skipped, 1 unrelated Vertex AI failure. - Repository-wide `make test-unit` hit an unrelated pytest collection collision. ### Final Attestation - [x] The regression test covers the capitalized `Authorization` edge case.

signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Fireworks serverless models like kimi-k3 report $0 cost - Cost map lags behind the Fireworks serverless pricing page How it solves it: - Adds 10 missing serverless models to the cost map - Prices and context windows taken from Fireworks pricing docs ## User Flow Before: a platform team routing traffic to Fireworks serverless models sees zero spend for kimi-k3 and deepseek-v4-flash-0731, so budgets and chargeback reports undercount 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "kimi-k3"` (backed by `fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k3`) 2. The response arrives with header `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0` 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request shows $0 spend 4. GET https://litellm-domain/model_group/info shows `"input_cost_per_token": 0.0, "output_cost_per_token": 0.0` for kimi-k3 After: the same request is billed at the published Fireworks serverless rates 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "kimi-k3"` 3. The response header `x-litellm-response-cost` now carries a non-zero amount at $3/1M input and $15/1M output 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request at non-zero spend, and https://litellm-domain/model_group/info reports the real prices and 1M context window ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? signals.title: fix(ptu): bound the sentinel prune to the deployments a run scanned
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The prune calls a row garbage on staleness alone - That only holds while every run shares one config source - A run would delete a charge it never considered How it solves it: - The loader reports which deployments it looked at - The delete is bounded to that set - An empty scan prunes nothing rather than everything ## User Flow Before: an admin sees a team's reserved-capacity cost for a day disappear after it was already correct 1. The admin runs a proxy with `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION=True` and two teams on provisioned throughput 2. The nightly attribution job runs and both teams' costs appear at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage 3. A deployment is removed while the fleet is still working through that date 4. Another replica picks the date up, treats the charge it cannot account for as leftover, and deletes it 5. The admin reloads https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage and the day now reads lower than it did an hour ago, with nothing recording why After: a replica only removes charges for deployments it actually looked at 1. Same proxy, same two teams, same nightly job 2. Both teams' costs appear at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage 3. The same deployment is removed mid-window 4. The other replica prices what it can see and leaves the rest alone 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage still shows the day at the amount it was first reported, and a charge that genuinely stopped applying is still cleared on the next run The disappearing charge is only reachable today when a deployment is removed during the window the fleet is rolling a date. It becomes routine once deployments can be declared per replica rather than in the shared table, which is what this guards ahead of ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5809 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real Postgres, the real scheduled entry point holding the lease, no mocks. Two deployments on provisioned throughput at 100 units and $0.02 per unit per hour, so a full day is $48 each. Each case runs the job, changes one deployment, ages the rows the way a previous run's rows look to the skew grace, then runs the job again Setup, once: ```bash docker run -d --name lit5809-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -e POSTGRES_DB=lit5809 -p 5809:5432 postgres:16 prisma db push --schema=./schema.prisma --skip-generate ``` Each case seeds `dep-alpha` and `dep-beta` with identical PTU settings, then between the two runs applies one change: ```sql -- case 1 UPDATE "LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable" SET model_info = '{"team_id":"team-alpha"}'::jsonb WHERE model_id = 'dep-beta'; -- case 2 DELETE FROM "LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable" WHERE model_id = 'dep-beta'; -- both, so the first run's rows are as old as a previous run's UPDATE "LiteLLM_DailyTeamSpend" SET updated_at = now() - interval '6 hours' WHERE api_key = '__ptu_flat_cost__'; ``` ### Before (a1afc2f433) #### case 1: dep-beta still exists and no longer carries PTU settings 1. Run the job, change dep-beta, run it again ``` tree : /Users/yucheng/litellm-wt/lit5809a/litellm/__init__.py bound: False after first run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0), ('dep-beta', 48.0)] after second run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0)] ``` #### case 2: dep-beta is gone from the table entirely 1. Run the job, delete dep-beta, run it again ``` after first run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0), ('dep-beta', 48.0)] after second run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0)] ``` ### After (f82ef6adf3) #### case 1: dep-beta still exists and no longer carries PTU settings 1. Run the job, change dep-beta, run it again ``` tree : /Users/yucheng/litellm-wt/lit5809b/litellm/__init__.py bound: True after first run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0), ('dep-beta', 48.0)] after second run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0)] ``` 2. Identical to before, which is the point: the cleanup that matters is untouched #### case 2: dep-beta is gone from the table entirely 1. Run the job, delete dep-beta, run it again ``` after first run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0), ('dep-beta', 48.0)] after second run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0), ('dep-beta', 48.0)] ``` 2. The charge stands, and this is the same query that stops one replica deleting another's charge once deployments can be declared per replica #### case 3: a proxy holding more deployments than one statement can carry 1. Seed 70000 deployments, then prune with the whole set in one statement and again chunked ``` scanned ids: 70000 one statement (chunking disabled): DataError: Assertion violation on the database: `too many bind variables in prepared statement, expected maximum of 32767 chunked at 5000: OK ``` 2. Nothing above the prune catches that, so on a fleet this size the unchunked form would take the whole scheduled run down every night, along with the catch-up pass that follows it, leaving an APScheduler traceback as the only signal The scanned set is every deployment in the table, not only the ones carrying PTU settings, which is what keeps case 1 working: a deployment that stopped pricing is still scanned, so its leftover row is still reachable ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - A deleted deployment keeps the day it was already charged - Deleting and recreating a deployment in one day double counts it - Do not land this ahead of the config source it guards for ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- --- > [!NOTE] > [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit f82ef6adf393219e0aef162ebe0e9bd33d608897. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "bedrock/us.xai.grok-4.6"` 2. The call errors with "This model isn't mapped yet. model=bedrock/us.xai.grok-4.6" 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows no priced spend for the model After: the same request resolves with correct pricing and capabilities 1. The request routes normally and the response is priced at $2.20/$6.60 per 1M input/output tokens 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request with non-zero spend ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? signals.title: feat(proxy)!: default audit logs on for enterprise licenses
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Enterprise admins record nothing until they add a setting - Audit logging is already premium-only, so off-by-default is friction - `LITELLM_STORE_AUDIT_LOGS` was ignored by the key hooks How it solves it: - `store_audit_logs` is now tri-state, unset means auto - Unset plus a premium license resolves to enabled - One resolver replaces ~15 scattered gate checks - Explicit `store_audit_logs: false` stays a hard opt-out ## User Flow Before: an admin running an enterprise license creates a virtual key, then finds the audit trail empty because a setting they never knew about was missing 1. They start the proxy with their enterprise license and no `store_audit_logs` in the config 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate with the master key and a `key_alias`, and get back 200 with a new `sk-` key 3. They send GET http://localhost:4000/audit to review who created that key, and get `{"audit_logs": [], "total": 0}` 4. Nothing they did through the admin API is recoverable for a compliance review until they find `store_audit_logs: true`, add it, and restart After: the same admin gets the audit trail without configuring anything, and can still turn it off 1. They start the proxy with their enterprise license and no `store_audit_logs` in the config 2. They send the same POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate and get back 200 with a new `sk-` key 3. They send GET http://localhost:4000/audit and see an entry with `"action": "created"`, the key id, and the admin who created it, with the key value itself masked 4. If they do not want it, they set `store_audit_logs: false` under `litellm_settings` and restart, and keys created after that are recorded nowhere Admins without an enterprise license see no change, since audit entries were already refused for them and unset still means off. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5847 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: one proxy on localhost:4000 against postgres, started the same way for every case with a real enterprise license in `LITELLM_LICENSE`, using `litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml`, which carries no `store_audit_logs` and no `audit_log_callbacks`. The opt-out case uses a copy of that config with `litellm_settings.store_audit_logs: false` added. API responses below are trimmed to the fields that matter, and the UI screenshots come from a separate run with the audit table truncated first, where the `Updated` / `Users` row is written by the Admin UI login itself, not by the key creations ```bash LITELLM_LICENSE="$LITELLM_LICENSE" uv run --no-sync litellm --config <config> --detailed_debug --port 4000 ``` The two totals in the After section count rows left in the same postgres by earlier runs, so the signal is which `object_id` values are present, not the count itself ### Before (a1afc2f433edf0d4961512713cec94761d112c54) #### Default, no store_audit_logs 1. Create a key on the enterprise license ```bash $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias": "audit-default-demo-before"}' {"key_alias": "audit-default-demo-before", ..., "token_id": "eec838aa078bca75...", "created_by": "default_user_id"} ``` 2. Read the audit trail, nothing was recorded ```bash $ curl -s "http://localhost:4000/audit?page=1&page_size=5" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"audit_logs": [], "total": 0, "page": 1, "page_size": 5, "total_pages": 0} ``` #### Explicit store_audit_logs false 1. Not run at the merge base, where off was already the only behavior ### After (25de920930c6e0444878d73ceb9fabb1b0de9679) #### Default, no store_audit_logs 1. Create a key with the same call and the same config ```bash $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias": "audit-default-demo-after-default-25de920930"}' {"key_alias": "audit-default-demo-after-default-25de920930", ..., "token_id": "b7be25eba8f3b299...", "created_by": "default_user_id"} ``` 2. The creation is now recorded, attributed to the admin, pointing at the new key, with the key value masked ```bash $ curl -s "http://localhost:4000/audit?page=1&page_size=5" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"audit_logs": [{"changed_by": "default_user_id", "changed_by_api_key": "litellm_proxy_master_key", "action": "created", "table_name": "LiteLLM_VerificationToken", "object_id": "b7be25eba8f3b29914227ce3d7511200744546c9afef3fc26ddcdb37cb39cf5", "before_value": null, "updated_values": {"key": "sk-…*****S1lg", "key_alias": "audi****0930", "created_by": "default_user_id", ...}}, ...], "total": 2, "page": 1, "page_size": 5, "total_pages": 1} ``` 3. Creating a key named `ui-audit-default-on` in the Admin UI puts a `Created` / `Keys` row on http://localhost:4000/ui/logs/audit ![Audit Logs tab showing the Created Keys row](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..BWd2K3ThY3MNTjshjJLWgz6Mxz7I5LZZe2r9c7YMdeg) 4. Its detail drawer shows the acting admin and the after-values, with `key` and `key_name` masked ![Audit log drawer with masked key values](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..k67Pwl_5eaDNJtkOY9wdEYvGwuhp-UsB2EB2zvAPKDM) 5. Scrolling the same drawer shows `key_alias` masked too ![Audit log drawer scrolled to key_alias](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..NvN_BGtPl4EdYj_8QhZEtYLFXK1lFaXGpK6ddov9mZ4) #### Explicit store_audit_logs false 1. Restart with `store_audit_logs: false` and create another key on the same enterprise license ```bash $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias": "audit-default-demo-after-opt-out-25de920930"}' {"key_alias": "audit-default-demo-after-opt-out-25de920930", ..., "created_by": "default_user_id"} ``` 2. The trail is unchanged, still the two rows from the default runs and nothing for the opt-out key ```bash $ curl -s "http://localhost:4000/audit?page=1&page_size=5" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"audit_logs": [{"object_id": "b7be25eba8f3b29914227ce3d7511200744546c9afef3fc26ddcdb37cb39cf5", "action": "created", ...}, {"object_id": "05ad32b5d72f55f1ea58ca6f4186b12fa52e0524c3b0b210a9edf82c090e965a", "action": "created", ...}], "total": 2, "page": 1, "page_size": 5, "total_pages": 1} ``` 3. Same in the UI: creating `ui-audit-optout-should-not-log` adds no row ![Audit Logs tab unchanged after the opt-out key](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..2Z4cI9LGmSMiOJsawVasI3zPdkyBcWwWCgF0DUPFeOc) #### No license 1. Running with the license unset and the default config, creating `ui-audit-no-license` adds no row either ![Audit Logs tab unchanged without a license](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..H7mrqjUtPVnJOHKcZKCbe7jmzNQMMCDBBZGxl6be1_A) ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Nothing on the LLM request path writes audit entries, so inference latency is untouched. Default-on adds one JSON serialization plus one insert per admin mutation, and most call sites already dispatch that write in the background, so the worst case is high-rate programmatic key provisioning - `LiteLLM_AuditLog` has no index beyond its primary key and no retention job, and GET /audit sorts by `updated_at` with a full count, so turning this on by default makes that growth common. Tracked in LIT-5848 rather than here - Several team and key-rotation tests mock Prisma rows that cannot serialize into an audit payload, so they now opt out of audit logging explicitly instead of relying on the old off-by-default - MCP management endpoints keep their existing empty audit stubs, this PR does not fill them in ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e80aa2b7e845458f8a7a5c09bf013abe Requested by: @yucheng-berri - [x] 25de920930 passes /live-pr-risk

signals.title: fix(proxy): run pre-call guardrails on batch input file uploads
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Guardrails never ran on batch input file uploads - Batch records reached providers completely unscanned - The gap was silent: nothing in the response said so How it solves it: - Scan each JSONL record through the existing guardrail dispatch - Reject the upload when any record trips a guardrail - Skipped entirely when no pre-call guardrail is configured ## User Flow Before: a platform team with a PII guardrail turned on for every request finds that batch jobs bypass it entirely 1. They upload a batch file with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files, `purpose=batch`, where one row's prompt contains a customer email address 2. The upload returns 200 with an id like `file-LHBKaMQriJAMc5ErcabLTx` 3. They fetch https://litellm-domain/v1/files/file-LHBKaMQriJAMc5ErcabLTx/content and see the email address stored verbatim at the provider 4. Nothing in the response, the headers, or the logs says a guardrail was skipped 5. Any team member with a key on that proxy can move data past the guardrail simply by putting it in a batch file instead of a chat request After: the same upload is refused, and the response names the row that tripped 1. They upload the same file with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files, `purpose=batch` 2. The upload returns 400 saying `A guardrail changed batch input line 2 (custom_id row-2)` 3. Nothing is stored at the provider, so there is no file id to fetch 4. They remove or clean row 2, re-upload, and get a normal 200 with a file id 5. A team member can no longer move data past the guardrail by putting it in a batch file ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-2026 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical on both sides. `config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY guardrails: - guardrail_name: "custom-pre-guard" litellm_params: guardrail: custom_guardrail.myCustomGuardrail mode: "pre_call" default_on: true files_settings: - custom_llm_provider: openai api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY ``` `custom_guardrail.myCustomGuardrail` is the example guardrail shipped in `litellm/proxy/example_config_yaml/custom_guardrail.py`, which masks the literal `litellm` in any message. Uploads go to the real OpenAI files API. `batch_input.jsonl`, whose line 2 trips the guardrail: ``` {"custom_id": "row-1", ... "content": "hello clean row"} {"custom_id": "row-2", ... "content": "this row mentions litellm and should be redacted"} {"custom_id": "row-3", ... "content": "another clean row"} ``` `clean.jsonl` holds two rows the guardrail does not touch. `mixed_malformed.jsonl` holds a valid row, then the line `{this is not valid json at all`, then a valid row. ### Before (da7a10ebbd) #### 1. clean batch file 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@clean.jsonl` 2. `{"id":"file-QmbpifMXHYtCWqMsv2WUmF","bytes":372,"object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"processed"}` #### 2. batch file whose line 2 trips the guardrail 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@batch_input.jsonl` 2. `HTTP 200` and `{"id":"file-LHBKaMQriJAMc5ErcabLTx","bytes":590,"object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"processed"}` 3. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files/file-LHBKaMQriJAMc5ErcabLTx/content` 4. Line 2 comes back verbatim, unscanned: `{"custom_id": "row-2", ... "content": "this row mentions litellm and should be redacted"}` #### 3. batch file with a malformed line 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@mixed_malformed.jsonl` 2. `HTTP 200` and `{"id":"file-MsQpeK8YHLYapSDmbFS1tC","bytes":373,"object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"processed"}` ### After (45b549c522) #### 1. clean batch file 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@clean.jsonl` 2. `{"id":"file-DsEyrC5NxqKxsQzMpcRRQz","bytes":372,"object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"processed"}` #### 2. batch file whose line 2 trips the guardrail 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@batch_input.jsonl` 2. `HTTP 400` and `{"error":{"message":"{'error': 'A guardrail changed batch input line 2 (custom_id row-2). Per-record redaction is not enabled, so the file was rejected rather than modified'}","code":"400"}}` 3. No file id is returned, so nothing was stored at the provider #### 3. batch file with a malformed line 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@mixed_malformed.jsonl` 2. `HTTP 400` and `{"error":{"message":"{'error': \"Batch input line 2 is not a JSON object with a 'body' field, so guardrails cannot be applied to it\"}","code":"400"}}` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Records are rejected, not redacted; redaction is the follow-up - A guardrail that only runs post_call does not trigger scanning - Model-level guardrails still run post-routing, so batch misses them - A record whose body has no readable content is refused - Large files scan serially in windows of 32; no cap yet - Only `purpose=batch` is scanned; see the note below A batch record is scanned under the call type its `url` names, and when the url is unfamiliar the body shape decides instead, so a record carrying `messages`, `prompt` or `input` is still scanned rather than refused. Only a body with none of those is refused, since there is nothing a guardrail could read. This matters because the provider transformers are permissive here: bedrock treats any non-empty url as chat, and vertex strips query strings and trailing slashes. Two consequences of scanning a record outside a real request, both worth knowing. A record referencing a LiteLLM unified file id is handed to guardrails with that id un-translated, because managed-file resolution rides the per-request hook chain that a scan deliberately skips. And `sensitive_data_routing` cannot reroute during a scan for the same reason, so only guardrails and guardrail pipelines inspect batch content, not that handler. Only `purpose=batch` uploads are scanned, and `purpose` comes from the caller, so in principle a caller could upload the same JSONL under another purpose and then pass that file id to `POST /v1/batches`. Against OpenAI this does not work: the provider rejects a `.jsonl` upload under `purpose=assistants` with `Invalid extension jsonl`, verified live. It is unverified for the managed files, Bedrock and Vertex paths, where LiteLLM stores the file itself rather than the provider, and nothing revalidates `purpose` at batch creation. Worth closing on those paths as follow-up work. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: refactor(ui): migrate shared primitives and common components off antd
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - antd is still the widget library under shared UI primitives - Shared components block every page-level antd removal - Alert and Badge lack the variants antd call sites need How it solves it: - Adds success to shared Alert, plus success, warning, info to Badge - Replaces antd DatePicker with a native UtcDateTimeInput - Converts common components and key/team helpers to shadcn ## User Flow One of four PRs taking the Admin UI off Ant Design, each independent and targeting internal staging. It is a refactor, so the flows below are identical in outcome and differ only in the widgets the user touches. Before: an admin editing a key's budget windows or picking an access group works against Ant Design controls, and any date field is an antd picker with its own calendar popup 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click a key, then Edit 2. They open the access group picker and choose a group 3. They open a budget window row and set a reset time in the antd date picker 4. They save and the key detail view shows the new values After: the same admin does the same task on the shadcn controls, with a native date and time field 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click a key, then Edit 2. They open the access group picker, now a shadcn combobox, and choose a group 3. They open a budget window row and set a reset time in a native date and time field that still submits UTC 4. They save and the key detail view shows the same values as before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### Before (7675ba8717) 1. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys, click any key, then Edit, and screenshot the access group picker open 2. Open a budget window row and screenshot the date picker open ### After (5dd5dd55bd) 1. Same steps, screenshot the combobox open 2. Same steps, screenshot the native date and time field ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - The other three antd PRs build on these primitives - Modal call sites still import antd, landing separately ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: refactor(ui): migrate the MCP servers pages off antd
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The MCP servers pages are the densest remaining antd surface - Their test helpers drive antd DOM, so conversions break them - Permission switches there have no accessible name, and the Authentication select has no label How it solves it: - Converts the create, edit, connect and permission screens to shadcn - Rewrites the select and collapse test helpers onto the new DOM - Adds aria-labels so switches are reachable by role and name - Labels the Authentication select and the auth settings panel it sits in ## User Flow One of four independent PRs taking the Admin UI off Ant Design. Behavior is unchanged; one accessibility gap is closed. signals.title: feat(e2e): canonical content-based match keys for record-and-replay
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Replay matched verb + path in recorded order only - A changed request body silently replayed the stale recorded response - Reordering two independent calls broke replay entirely - Credential body/form fields landed in bundles verbatim How it solves it: - Canonical match keys: method, path, and a content hash - Volatile headers, credentials, markers, generated ids, and timestamps canonicalize out - A miss hard-fails naming the computed key, closest recorded key, and diff - Matching is order-independent across keys, FIFO within one key - Recording now redacts credential body and form fields on write - Replay pools build once at load; consumption is one atomic pop ## User Flow Before: an engineer replaying a recorded e2e run gets a stale response silently served for a request the suite no longer makes, and a harmless reorder of independent calls kills the replay with no hint of what was expected 1. They start a proxy on http://localhost:37526 and run the streaming chat suite with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record`; the test passes, hitting POST http://localhost:37526/model/new, GET /v1/models, POST /key/generate, POST /chat/completions (SSE), POST /key/delete, and POST /model/delete, and one JSON file per call lands in the bundle 2. They change the test's prompt and temperature, stop the proxy, blank `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and rerun with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay`: the run passes anyway, asserting against the old recording's streamed response as if the new request had been served 3. They restore the test and instead move the key-generate call before model-create; replay fails with "replay mismatch ... recorded post /model/new, test made post /key/generate", naming only positions, with no key for what the test sent and no closest recorded request After: the same replay matches by request content wherever the call sits and fails loudly with both keys on any real drift, never touching the network 1. They start a proxy on http://localhost:37526 and run the streaming chat suite with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record`; the test passes, hitting POST http://localhost:37526/model/new, GET /v1/models, POST /key/generate, POST /chat/completions (SSE), POST /key/delete, and POST /model/delete, and one JSON file per call lands in the bundle 2. The changed-prompt rerun now fails with `ReplayMiss` printing the computed key `stream /chat/completions #e7ded1b5e0795c01`, the closest recorded key `stream /chat/completions #76ff084d9d1dd427 (0003-stream-chat-completions.json)`, and a diff pinpointing exactly the prompt and temperature drift; with the proxy down and no provider key, no network call is made 3. The reordered run passes, since matching is by content key, not recorded position 4. Recording the suite twice yields identical match key sets, so a bundle recorded on one machine replays on another with no misses ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5741 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: proxy config with `gpt-4o-mini -> openai/gpt-4o-mini` (`api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY`), master key sk-1234, `store_model_in_db: true`, booted with `DATABASE_URL=... uv run python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config <config> --port 37526 --use_v2_migration_resolver`. The vehicle suite is `tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py`, recorded against the live proxy with real OpenAI spend, then replayed with the proxy stopped and `OPENAI_API_KEY=` blank ### Before (6bf535bb8f) #### Content drift on replay is a silent pass 1. `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:37526 uv run pytest tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py -v` -> `1 passed in 20.30s`, bundle written with `0000-post-model-new.json` ... `0005-post-model-delete.json` 2. Kill the proxy; mutate the test's prompt ("Reply with the single word ok." -> "Reply with the single word HELLO in French.") and temperature (0.0 -> 1.0) 3. `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:37526 OPENAI_API_KEY= uv run pytest tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py -v` -> `1 passed in 15.17s`: the mutated request silently consumed the stale recorded response #### Reordering independent calls breaks replay without naming keys 1. Restore the test; move `resources.key()` before `proxy.create_model(...)` 2. Same replay command -> `FAILED` with `fixture_transport.ReplayMiss: replay mismatch for ...test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done at call #1: recorded post /model/new, test made post /key/generate; re-record with E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record`: position-only matching, no computed key, no closest recorded request #### Match keys across separate recordings 1. Inspect the recorded bundle: the only identity an interaction has is its filename ordinal (`0000-post-model-new.json`), so nothing defines, computes, or compares a match key between two recordings of the same suite ### After (975e79dcef) #### Content drift on replay is a silent pass 1. `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:37526 uv run pytest tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py -v` -> `1 passed in 17.51s`, same six interaction files 2. Kill the proxy; apply the same prompt + temperature mutation 3. Same replay command -> `1 failed in 15.14s` with `fixture_transport.ReplayMiss: replay miss for ...test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done: no recorded interaction matches key stream /chat/completions #e7ded1b5e0795c01; closest recorded key is stream /chat/completions #76ff084d9d1dd427 (0003-stream-chat-completions.json)` followed by a unified diff whose only hunks are `-"content": "Reply with the single word ok. <marker>"` / `+"content": "Reply with the single word HELLO in French. <marker>"` and `-"temperature": 0.0` / `+"temperature": 1.0`, and a re-record hint; proxy down and provider key blank, so no network call was possible #### Reordering independent calls breaks replay without naming keys 1. Restore the test; move `resources.key()` before `proxy.create_model(...)` 2. Same replay command -> `1 passed in 15.08s`: content-keyed matching is order-independent across distinct keys 3. Restore the test; same replay command untouched -> `1 passed in 15.15s` with the proxy still down (clean replay needs no proxy and no provider key) #### Match keys across separate recordings 1. Record the same suite a second time into a separate bundle dir (`E2E_FIXTURE_DIR=<run2>`) -> `1 passed in 15.71s`, fresh OpenAI spend 2. Canonicalize every recorded request in both bundles and compare: both runs produce the same six keys (`get /v1/models #b582c5a565697d4d`, `post /key/delete #5e6c7d6ab75728c2`, `post /key/generate #1c98fef54321506b`, `post /model/delete #750972c5895baecc`, `post /model/new #d7d220d80dbafcc2`, `stream /chat/completions #76ff084d9d1dd427`) -> `IDENTICAL KEY SETS` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - No bundle format bump: keys are recomputed at load, existing bundles replay unchanged - Streaming chunk fidelity (LIT-5742) and provider scoping (LIT-5745) are follow-ups ## QA runbook - tests/e2e/test_fixture_canonical.py::TestKeyStability::test_volatile_material_does_not_change_the_key - two requests differing only in auth headers, request ids, dates, markers, and credential values share one key - [ ] Record any e2e test twice on two different days or machines (fresh virtual keys, new markers) - [ ] Canonicalize both bundles' requests (`fixture_canonical.canonicalize(...).key`) and expect identical key sets - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/test_fixture_transport.py::TestReplayTransport::test_content_drift_on_the_same_route_misses_with_no_live_call - drifted request content on a recorded route is a hard miss, not a stale replay - [ ] Record `tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_chat_stream_contract_e2e.py` against a live proxy with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record` - [ ] Stop the proxy, blank `OPENAI_API_KEY`, change the test's prompt, rerun with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay` - [ ] Expect `ReplayMiss` naming the computed key, the closest recorded key with its file, and a diff showing exactly the prompt drift, with no network call - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/test_fixture_transport.py::TestReplayTransport::test_replays_out_of_recorded_order_across_distinct_keys - independent calls replay in any order; duplicates of one request stay FIFO - [ ] With the same recording, swap two independent setup calls in the test and replay - [ ] Expect a pass, and expect teardown to still fail a test that leaves recorded interactions unconsumed, naming a leftover key - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/test_fixture_transport.py::TestRecordingTransport::test_redacts_credential_body_fields_in_the_recorded_request - provider keys in request bodies never land in bundles - [ ] Record a test that creates a deployment whose body carries a literal provider key (`/model/new` with `litellm_params.api_key`) - [ ] Open the bundle's `0000-post-model-new.json` and expect `"<redacted>"` where the key was, with `null` fields left `null` - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] 125587d286ed2a681bdb80e4e3bd661afa19fede passes /live-pr-risk - [x] 975e79dcefb599f7efd5cc6f1d83d77eff9f5959 passes /live-pr-risk <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Changes are confined to the e2e harness under tests/e2e with no production proxy or auth paths touched; behavior is heavily covered by new and updated harness unit tests. > > **Overview** > E2e **record/replay** no longer matches interactions by **call order and verb+path**. Replay now uses **canonical content keys** from new **`fixture_canonical.py`**: method, path, and a hash of headers, params, body, form, and file identity after stripping volatile auth/trace headers, redacting credential field names, and normalizing markers, UUIDs, timestamps, and provider ids. > > **`ReplaySource`** builds per-test **pools** keyed by that hash: distinct keys can replay **out of recorded order**; duplicate keys stay **FIFO** (poll loops). Misses raise **`ReplayMiss`** with the computed key, closest recorded key, file name, and a **content diff**—no silent stale responses and no live fallback. **Recording** also redacts credential fields in JSON bodies and form data on write (aligned with canonical secret rules). Docs mark **LIT-5741** done; harness tests cover canonicalization, drift misses, reordering, concurrency, and cross-run key stability. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 975e79dcefb599f7efd5cc6f1d83d77eff9f5959. signals.title: fix(bedrock): enable tool search for Opus 4.8 and gen 5 Claude on Invoke
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock Opus 4.8, Opus 5, and Sonnet 5 lack `supports_tool_search` metadata - Invoke tool-search allowlist stops at Opus 4.7, missing newer families - Chat Invoke path sent the tool-search beta for unsupported Opus 4/4.1 How it solves it: - Sets `supports_tool_search: true` on Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Sonnet 5 entries - Shares one `supports_tool_search_on_bedrock` helper across both Invoke paths - Helper reads the model map first, name patterns cover unmapped ids ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin checking model capabilities sees no tool-search support on the newest Bedrock Claude models even though live Bedrock InvokeModel accepts tool search for them, verified 2026-08-19 1. They add `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` to their config and start the proxy 2. They GET http://localhost:4000/v1/model/info and the entry shows no `supports_tool_search` field 3. Their capability-based routing treats the model as unable to do tool search, and requests routed by that signal skip a model that Bedrock itself serves tool search on After: the same models advertise tool search and requests work end to end 1. They add `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` to their config and start the proxy 2. They GET http://localhost:4000/v1/model/info and the entry shows `supports_tool_search: true` 3. They POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages with a `tool_search_tool_regex_20251119` tool and a deferred tool, and get 200 with `server_tool_use` and `tool_search_tool_result` blocks ## Relevant issues Follow-up to #36502, which added the tool-search beta for Haiku 4.5 on Invoke /v1/messages ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: proxy on localhost:41411 with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`, real AWS Bedrock credentials, config mapping `claude-{opus-4-8,opus-5,sonnet-5}-bedrock-invoke` to `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-{opus-4-8,opus-5,sonnet-5}` in us-east-1. Request body used for every /v1/messages call: ```json { "model": "<alias>", "max_tokens": 128, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Use tool discovery to find a tool that can add 2 and 3, then call it."}], "tools": [ {"type": "tool_search_tool_regex_20251119", "name": "tool_search_tool_regex"}, {"name": "add_numbers", "description": "Add two integers", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"a": {"type": "integer"}, "b": {"type": "integer"}}, "required": ["a", "b"]}, "defer_loading": true} ] } ``` ### Before (0de60a2ff2) #### /v1/model/info capability flag 1. `curl -s http://localhost:41412/v1/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` then print `model_info.supports_tool_search` per model 2. Output: ``` claude-opus-4-8-bedrock-invoke supports_tool_search= None claude-opus-5-bedrock-invoke supports_tool_search= None claude-sonnet-5-bedrock-invoke supports_tool_search= None ``` #### /v1/messages tool search against real Bedrock 1. `curl -s http://localhost:41412/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @body.json` for the sonnet-5 alias 2. Output (Bedrock currently accepts the versioned tool type even without the beta, so the request itself does not fail at base; the gap is the missing capability signal and the inconsistent beta header): ``` claude-sonnet-5-bedrock-invoke HTTP 200 types=['server_tool_use', 'tool_search_tool_result', 'text', 'tool_use'] ``` ### After (caf9c1890e) #### /v1/model/info capability flag 1. `curl -s http://localhost:41411/v1/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` then print `model_info.supports_tool_search` per model 2. Output: ``` claude-opus-4-8-bedrock-invoke supports_tool_search= True claude-opus-5-bedrock-invoke supports_tool_search= True claude-sonnet-5-bedrock-invoke supports_tool_search= True ``` #### /v1/messages tool search against real Bedrock 1. `for m in claude-opus-4-8-bedrock-invoke claude-opus-5-bedrock-invoke claude-sonnet-5-bedrock-invoke; do curl -s http://localhost:41411/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @body.json; done` 2. Output: ``` claude-opus-4-8-bedrock-invoke HTTP 200 types=['text', 'server_tool_use', 'tool_search_tool_result', 'text', 'tool_use'] claude-opus-5-bedrock-invoke HTTP 200 types=['text', 'server_tool_use', 'tool_search_tool_result', 'text', 'tool_use'] claude-sonnet-5-bedrock-invoke HTTP 200 types=['thinking', 'server_tool_use', 'tool_search_tool_result', 'text', 'tool_use'] ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Fable 5 left unflagged: probe blocked by an account data-retention setting - Converse still skips tool-search tools, Anthropic documents Invoke-only support - Chat Invoke no longer sends the beta for Opus 4/4.1, per Anthropic docs ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/87676b2806ad445d902372e77191d5be

signals.title: feat(proxy): fast-fail validation for batch input files at /v1/files
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bad batch input files stream fully to the provider before failing - Failures surface minutes later, degraded, without naming the bad field - No knob caps batch file size; `max_request_size_mb` caps every route How it solves it: - New `general_settings.max_batch_file_size_mb` rejects oversized batch uploads with 413 - Settable in config.yaml or from the admin dashboard; dashboard edits apply on the next periodic config reload, no restart - `purpose=batch` uploads validated locally: `.jsonl` extension, JSON lines, required keys - Errors are OpenAI-shaped, naming the offending param and line number ## User Flow Before: a developer running a batch job through the gateway only learns their input file is bad after it has fully streamed to the provider, and the size cap their admin configured does nothing 1. The proxy admin sets `max_batch_file_size_mb: 10` under `general_settings` and restarts; the proxy boots clean and silently ignores the knob 2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with `purpose=batch` and a 210 MB `batch.jsonl`; the request streams for minutes, the whole file crosses the wire, and only then the provider's own error comes back 3. They retry with `batch.csv`; it returns 200 OK and a `file-...` id as if the file were fine 4. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with that id; it returns a `batch_...` id, and about a minute later GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} shows status `failed` with `Missing required parameter: 'method'`, the first hint anything was wrong After: the same developer gets an immediate 4xx at upload time that names the offending field, and nothing invalid ever reaches the provider 1. The proxy admin sets `max_batch_file_size_mb: 10` under `general_settings` in config.yaml, or saves it from the admin dashboard (POST https://litellm-domain/config/field/update), where it takes effect on the next periodic config reload without a restart 2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with `purpose=batch` and a 210 MB `batch.jsonl`; it returns 413 instantly with `"param": "file"` and a message naming `max_batch_file_size_mb` and saying the file was not forwarded 3. They retry with `batch.csv`; it returns 400 instantly with `"param": "file"` saying batch input files must be `.jsonl` 4. signals.title: docs: run only the tests covering your change, leave suites to CI
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `make test-unit` runs all of `tests/test_litellm`, an hour plus locally - Checklists pushed contributors and agents into full-suite local runs How it solves it: - CONTRIBUTING and the PR template ask for the covering test files only - Both point the suites at CI, which finishes in ~15 minutes ## User Flow Before: a contributor about to open a PR 1. The CONTRIBUTING checklist lists "Unit Tests - `make test-unit`" as a required check, so they run `pytest tests/test_litellm -x -vv -n 4` and wait an hour on tests unrelated to their change 2. The Running Unit Tests section leads with "Run all unit tests", making that full run the documented default 3. The PR template's pre-submission checklist only mentions passing CI checks, giving no hint about how much to run locally After: the same contributor runs only what their change touches 1. The CONTRIBUTING checklist asks for the tests covering the change, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`, noting CI runs the full unit test matrix 2. The Running Unit Tests section leads with that scoped run and says to lean on CI when the whole suite really is needed 3. The PR template checklist repeats only the essentials: the covering test files pass locally, suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) belong to CI at ~15 minutes versus an hour or more on a laptop, with a link to CONTRIBUTING for the rest ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review Docs-only change, so no tests apply ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Docs-only change with no runtime behavior, so there is nothing to run against a live proxy. The rendered result is the diff itself ## Type 📖 Documentation ## Caveats (if any) - None ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ccaba15ac1e54379a25919909f6aa7d7 Requested by: @mateo-berri

signals.title: fix(ci): stop Agent Shin reconsider from triggering on bot comments
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Agent Shin's own comments re-trigger the reconsider workflow - Every sweep close comment spawned a doomed unauthorized run How it solves it: - Job now skips comments authored by bots - Human authors and collaborators are unaffected ## User Flow Before: a maintainer watching the Agent Shin triage sweep gets a burst of pointless workflow runs, one per PR the sweep touched 1. The sweep posts its close comment on a PR, e.g. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/28399, and that comment tells the contributor to reply `@agent-shin reconsider` to bring the PR back 2. Because the comment body contains that phrase, the reconsider workflow triggers on the bot's own comment 3. The maintainer opens https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/workflows/triage_reconsider.yml and sees a run per closed PR, each one green but doing nothing except logging that `devin-ai-integration[bot]` is not authorized 4. The noise repeats on every sweep, so a real contributor reconsider is hard to spot in the run list After: the same sweep leaves the reconsider run list clean, so the only runs there are real contributor requests 1. The sweep posts the same close comment on the same PR, with the same `@agent-shin reconsider` instructions 2. No reconsider run is created at all, since the comment came from a bot 3. The maintainer opens the same Actions page and sees only runs triggered by humans 4. A contributor who actually comments `@agent-shin reconsider` still gets the 👀 reaction and a verdict, exactly as before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review No tests: the change is a GitHub Actions `if:` expression, which has no test harness in this repo. The trigger data below is from the real events ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix `issue_comment` workflows always run from the default branch, so the new gate cannot execute from a PR branch. Before is the live behavior on `litellm_internal_staging`, After is the same real event payload evaluated against the new condition ### Before (f4b46c81da) 1. List the reconsider runs from today's sweep ``` $ gh run list --workflow triage_reconsider.yml -L 200 --json conclusion,createdAt,displayTitle \ | jq -r '[.[] | select(.conclusion != "skipped")] | .[] | "\(.createdAt) \(.displayTitle)"' 2026-08-19T21:36:09Z proto(mcp): per-user env-var fields demo flow (UI mockup) 2026-08-19T21:36:06Z prototype(ui): per-user fields for MCP servers (mock/throwaway) 2026-08-19T21:36:03Z feat(mcp): per-server env vars with global + per-user scopes 2026-08-19T21:36:01Z feat(mcp): add admin-declared per-user fields for MCP servers 2026-08-19T21:35:58Z fix(proxy): make pass-through auth checks method-aware 2026-08-19T21:35:55Z fix(bedrock): forward clear_tool_uses context_management on Invoke route 2026-08-19T21:35:54Z fix(azure): preserve AD token refresh in v1 OpenAI client path 2026-08-19T21:35:52Z fix(proxy): keep the model-group alias through vector store credential merges ``` Eight runs in 17 seconds, all of them from the sweep's own comments rather than from any contributor 2. Read what one of those runs actually did ``` $ gh run view 32304710883 --log | grep -E "COMMENTER: |not authorized" COMMENTER: devin-ai-integration[bot] ##[notice]Commenter 'devin-ai-integration[bot]' (CONTRIBUTOR) is not authorized to trigger reconsider; skipping subsequent steps. ``` Every later step (reaction, checkout, Python setup, the LLM judge) was skipped, so the run could never have produced a verdict ### After (fe97a9d719) 1. Pull the triggering comment from the same run and check it against the new condition ``` $ gh api repos/BerriAI/litellm/issues/comments/5348285161 \ -q '{login: .user.login, type: .user.type, has_phrase: (.body | contains("@agent-shin reconsider"))}' {"has_phrase":true,"login":"devin-ai-integration[bot]","type":"Bot"} ``` `github.event.comment.user.type != 'Bot'` is false and `!endsWith(github.event.comment.user.login, '[bot]')` is false, so the job condition is false and no run is created for any of those eight comments 2. Confirm a human reconsider still passes the gate ``` $ gh api repos/BerriAI/litellm/issues/comments/5348285161 -q .author_association CONTRIBUTOR ``` The added clauses only look at the commenter's account type, so the existing author / OWNER / MEMBER / COLLABORATOR authorization step is what still decides human comments ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats (if any) - Takes effect once merged to the default branch - A bot-authored PR can no longer self-reconsider Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2e6fbd7ba56d4655b42601c88868a654

signals.title: fix(ui_sso): remove stale team memberships on SSO login when sync_user_role_and_teams is set
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - JWT auth syncs team removals; UI SSO login never does - Users removed from an IdP group keep their LiteLLM team after UI login How it solves it: - SSO login now removes teams the IdP no longer reports - Gated by the existing `sync_user_role_and_teams` JWT setting - Honors `fallback_to_db_teams` when the IdP sends no groups ## User Flow Before: a user removed from an IdP group keeps that team after logging in to the UI 1. An admin removes the user from the `team-b` group in the IdP 2. The user signs in at https://litellm-domain/sso/key/generate and completes the IdP login 3. On https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams the user still appears as a member of `team-b` 4. The user can keep using keys and models granted through `team-b` After: the same login drops the stale team 1. An admin removes the user from the `team-b` group in the IdP 2. The user signs in at https://litellm-domain/sso/key/generate and completes the IdP login 3. On https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams the user is no longer a member of `team-b` 4. Access granted through `team-b` is gone; teams still present in the IdP are untouched ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge?
