signals.title: fix(spend-logs): backfill created_at/updated_at from row endTime instead of migration time
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - #37361 stamps every pre-existing spend log row with migration time - Export checkpoints then see all history as freshly written How it solves it: - Follow-up migration backfills `created_at`/`updated_at` from each row's `endTime` - Guard only rewrites rows stamped over an hour past `endTime` - Same guard makes re-runs no-ops and spares genuine rows ## User Flow Before: a data engineer upgrades the gateway and every historical spend log row comes back stamped with the upgrade moment, so their incremental export treats months of history as written just now 1. For months their app has been sending POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions, and GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id=<id> shows each logged row with `startTime` and `endTime` but no `created_at` 2. They upgrade the gateway and it boots normally 3. They send GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?start_date=<months back>&end_date=<today>&summarize=false with the master key 4. Every pre-upgrade row carries identical `created_at` and `updated_at` equal to the moment the upgrade ran, so a request that finished on 2026-07-20 claims it was written on 2026-08-19 5. Their export job checkpoints on `created_at`, so the entire history collapses into one checkpoint window and write-time ordering is meaningless for everything before the upgrade After: the same upgrade backfills each historical row's write timestamps from the row's own completion time, so the export sees honest values 1. For months their app has been sending POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions, and GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id=<id> shows each logged row with `startTime` and `endTime` but no `created_at` 2. They upgrade the gateway and it boots normally 3. They send GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?start_date=<months back>&end_date=<today>&summarize=false with the master key 4. Every pre-upgrade row carries `created_at` and `updated_at` equal to that row's own `endTime`, so the request that finished on 2026-07-20 says it was written on 2026-07-20 5. A fresh POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions logs a row whose `created_at` is its real write time, so the checkpoint job works across old and new rows alike ## Relevant issues Follow-up to #37361 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5854 ## Why a follow-up migration instead of editing the merged one `prisma migrate deploy` (both the default resolver and `--use_v2_migration_resolver` front with it) skips migrations already recorded by name in `_prisma_migrations` without re-reading their SQL. Verified live on a scratch database: after applying the merged `20260818000000_add_spend_log_timestamps`, appending the backfill UPDATE to that same file and re-running deploy prints "No pending migrations to apply", the edited SQL never executes, and the recorded checksum stays the original. The default resolver's post-deploy sanity check diffs the live schema against schema.prisma, and a data-only edit produces no schema diff, so it never re-runs there either. Editing in place would therefore silently skip every database that already applied the original migration, which is exactly the population holding the bad stamps. A follow-up migration runs exactly once on every migrate-managed database, old or fresh The WHERE guard doubles as the idempotence story: after one pass `created_at` equals `endTime`, so a second execution matches zero rows (verified, `UPDATE 0`). That matters beyond re-deploys because the default resolver's pooler-URL fallback executes every migration file directly via `prisma db execute` instead of consulting the ledger The guard boundary is deliberate. Rows written in the final hour before the upgrade keep their stamp, which is at most an hour off. Genuine rows are written within seconds of their `endTime`, so an hour of headroom also absorbs realistic app-to-database clock skew, and `endTime` is NOT NULL so no row can be nulled or skipped on that account. Even a pathological genuine row that trips the guard (a spend write delayed by over an hour) just gets set to its own `endTime`, which is the more honest value anyway schema.prisma is untouched in all three copies: #37361 already added the columns there, and this PR only corrects the data, so there is no schema change to sync. No unit test is added because the change is a single raw SQL migration and the repo has no harness that executes migration SQL against a database; the proof of fix below is the live upgrade run instead ## Deploy-time cost on large tables The UPDATE seq-scans the table once and rewrites every row the guard matches, which on first upgrade is essentially every pre-existing row. Untouched TOASTed columns (`messages`, `response`, `proxy_server_request`) are not rewritten, only the main heap tuples, so a hundred-million-row table rewrites tens of GB of heap and emits a comparable WAL volume, with dead tuples up to doubling heap size until autovacuum reclaims them. The lock is ROW EXCLUSIVE, so concurrent reads and the append-only spend log inserts from still-running replicas proceed throughout; prior migrations built indexes on this same table non-concurrently, a stricter lock than this takes. Prisma applies the migration in one transaction, so an interrupted run rolls back whole rather than half-stamping the table, and the ledger guarantees the scan happens once per database ever The honest worst case is time, not locking: prisma commands run under `LITELLM_PRISMA_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` (default 60s), and a table where this UPDATE needs longer will time out, roll back, and fail the boot until the operator raises that variable for the one deploy that performs the backfill. Since #37361 is in no tag yet, only internal staging and dev databases hold the bad stamps today, and shipping the backfill in the same rc keeps the affected population that small permanently ## Replacement heads-up for #37361 The earlier contributor guidance, only trust `created_at` for rows written after the rollout, is obsolete once this lands. Replacement wording: `created_at`/`updated_at` are trustworthy across the whole table; rows that predate the upgrade carry their `endTime` as both values, and rows written within the hour before the upgrade may keep the upgrade-time stamp ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests (migration-only PR, no harness executes migration SQL; proven via the live upgrade run below) - [ ] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live before/after upgrade run with a real proxy, a real Postgres, and real OpenAI calls. The before leg is the control and upgrades to the litellm_internal_staging tip 629d7683f2, which has #37361 but not this PR. The after leg upgrades to this PR's head 096263db15 Seed, shown for the before leg (the after leg is identical with database `lit5854_qa_after` and port 47731): ```bash createdb lit5854_qa_before .venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --port 49662 # boots and applies the 152 migrations at this commit for i in 1 2 3; do curl -sS http://localhost:49662/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4-nano","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' done psql lit5854_qa_before -c "UPDATE \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" SET \"startTime\" = \"startTime\" - interval '30 days', \"endTime\" = \"endTime\" - interval '30 days' WHERE request_id IN ('chatcmpl-EEkZoBblFxkEfhUfaP9koccOTyxeV', 'chatcmpl-EEkZoGyqnACjMnWuNGJCxDVfLgkGy');" ``` Upgrade: check out the target commit in place and reboot the proxy, which runs `prisma migrate deploy` at boot. signals.title: feat(shadow_eval)!: gate the per-key budget on dollar spend instead of turns
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Shadow eval budgets are turn counts, but the thing operators care about is dollars - A turn's cost varies wildly by model and prompt, so max_turns bounds spend only loosely - The job's own judge_spend read $0.00 for deployment-priced judges How it solves it: - start_shadow_eval takes `max_budget` (USD per key) instead of `max_turns` - Each attempt records the shadow arm's and judge's billed cost on its row - Sampler, sweep, stop guard, and derived status all gate on recorded spend - Costs come from the billed figure, so deployment pricing is respected - Billed cost is recorded on every exit, even empty replies and pipeline errors - A request still sending max_turns gets a 422 naming the replacement - A 10,000-sample internal valve terminates zero-cost error loops - Pre-migration jobs keep their configured turn budget (max_budget stays NULL) ## User Flow Before: an operator wants to cap a shadow eval at 20 cents of eval overhead, and there is no way to say that 1. They send POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start with `{"router_name": "my-router", "api_key_ids": ["<hash>"], "judge_model": "judge", "shadow_percentage": 100, "max_budget": 0.20}` 2. The job is created anyway: the `max_budget` field is silently ignored and the response shows only `"max_turns": 200` 3. Their key's traffic gets sampled until 200 turns are judged, whatever that costs; the detail response shows `"judge_spend": 0.0` even though the spend logs bill real dollars for every shadow and judge call After: the same request caps the eval at 20 cents per key 1. They send the same POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start with `"max_budget": 0.20` 2. The response shows `"max_budget": 0.2` on their key, and sampling stops as soon as the key's recorded shadow plus judge spend reaches it 3. The detail response shows `"spend": 0.24, "status": "completed"` with real dollar figures per key, matching what the spend logs billed ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Rig: local proxy from this branch on :4321 with real Postgres (all 148 migrations plus this PR's), stub OpenAI upstream with explicit `input_cost_per_token`/`output_cost_per_token` on every deployment so each call has a real, deterministic billed cost ($0.04 per call at the stub's fixed 20 in / 10 out usage). Every local provider credential is dead, so the upstream is stubbed; the owed real-provider re-run is the same script against live models. Config: `cheap`/`strong`/`judge` deployments plus auto-router `my-router` ### Before (3f2e0badb4) #### A dollar budget cannot be expressed and spend figures lie 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4321/auto_router/shadow_eval/start -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"router_name": "my-router", "api_key_ids": ["<hash>"], "judge_model": "judge", "shadow_percentage": 100, "max_turns": 3, "max_spend": 0.05, "max_budget": 0.05}'` creates the job; both dollar fields are silently ignored, the response carries only `"max_turns": 3` 2. 5 chat turns through the shadowed key: `for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4321/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model": "cheap", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "direct spend repro turn '$i' unique probe"}]}'; done` 3. Detail reads `"attempt_count": 3, "judge_spend": 0.0, "status": "completed"`: the count gated it, and judge_spend reads zero because the public price map cannot see deployment pricing 4. Meanwhile `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` shows the eval's own legs billing real money: `shadow_eval_router` $0.04 and `shadow_eval_judge` $0.04 per attempt, $0.24 of unaccounted, uncappable eval overhead ### After (82a488b3c5) #### The dollar budget bounds the job 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4321/auto_router/shadow_eval/start -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"router_name": "my-router", "api_key_ids": ["<hash>"], "judge_model": "judge", "shadow_percentage": 100, "max_budget": 0.20}'` returns `"max_budget": 0.2, "max_turns": 10000, "status": "running"` 2. The same 5 chat turns through the shadowed key 3. Exactly 3 are sampled (3 x $0.08 = $0.24 >= $0.20) and the detail reads `"attempt_count": 3, "spend": 0.24, "judge_spend": 0.12, "status": "completed"` 4. `SELECT outcome, shadow_cost, judge_cost FROM "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalAttempt" ...` shows every row carrying both legs' billed cost: `tie | 0.04 | 0.04` x3 5. `curl -s -X POST .../auto_router/shadow_eval/<job>/stop` answers 400 `"Job <job> is already completed"` #### A caller still sending the retired max_turns is told, not silently defaulted 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4321/auto_router/shadow_eval/start ... -d '{"router_name": "my-router", "api_key_ids": ["<hash>"], "judge_model": "judge", "shadow_percentage": 100, "max_turns": 200}'` 2. Answers 422 with `"max_turns was replaced by max_budget, the per-key USD cap on the eval's own spend"` #### A pre-migration job keeps its turn budget 1. Create a job, then reshape its row into the legacy form with psql: `UPDATE "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalJob" SET max_budget = NULL, max_turns = 2 WHERE group_id = '<job>'` 2. 3 chat turns through the shadowed key 3. Detail reads `"attempt_count": 2, "max_budget": null, "spend": 0.16, "status": "completed"`: the turn budget gated it, the recorded spend is display only ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Breaking: start_shadow_eval replaces `max_turns` with `max_budget` - Admission checks recorded spend, so in-flight samples overshoot by one cache window - During a rolling deploy old pods gate new jobs by the valve only - Attempt rows written by old pods mid-deploy price as judge-only - Stub-backed proof; real-provider re-run owed (precedent #30277, #34029) - UI PR #37389 touches the same component and will need a rebase ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 82a488b3c5ec29cec1e56f7ab99c33140e5faaee. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: feat(ptu): accrue flat cost for PTU deployments declared in config.yaml
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A PTU deployment in config.yaml accrues no flat cost - The rollup only reads the database model table - Its traffic is billed per token instead How it solves it: - The rollup also reads config-declared deployments off the router - Registering one zeroes its pricing, since capacity is prepaid - Both halves apply the same rules from one module ## User Flow Before: a team on reserved capacity is billed for its tokens and never for the capacity 1. An admin declares a provisioned-throughput deployment in `config.yaml` with `team_id`, `ptu_count`, `cost_per_ptu_per_hour` and `ptu_effective_from`, then starts the proxy with `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION=True` 2. Someone on that team sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and gets a normal answer 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request charged at the provider's per-token rate 4. The nightly attribution job runs at 00:15 UTC and writes nothing for that deployment 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage shows the team's token spend and no reserved-capacity cost, so the hourly charge the provider is invoicing appears nowhere After: the same team is billed for the capacity it reserved, and not again for the traffic that capacity serves 1. The admin declares the same deployment and starts the same proxy 2. Someone on that team sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and gets the same answer 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request at $0, because the reservation already paid for it 4. The nightly job runs and attributes the reservation to the team 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage shows the team's reserved-capacity cost for the day, charted separately from request cost An admin who wants the deployment billed per token instead removes `ptu_count` and `cost_per_ptu_per_hour`, exactly as on the API path ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5809 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real Postgres, real Gemini traffic, a proxy booted from the config below on each side, no mocks. Gemini stands in for Azure because PTU capacity cannot be provisioned here; the fields the feature reads are provider-agnostic, and what is being proven is the cost path. The only thing not exercised is the cron trigger itself, since the job has no on-demand entry point, so each side calls the same scheduled function directly against its own database. ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-ptu litellm_params: model: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY input_cost_per_token: 0.000005 output_cost_per_token: 0.000015 model_info: team_id: ptu-team-0001 ptu_count: 100 cost_per_ptu_per_hour: 0.02 ptu_effective_from: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" general_settings: master_key: sk-lit5809 ``` ```bash export LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION=True python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config ptu.yaml --port KEY=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5809" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_id":"ptu-team-0001","models":["gpt-4o-ptu"]}' | jq -r .key) ``` ### Before (eecb226762) #### a real request through the config.yaml PTU deployment 1. Send it ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4811/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-ptu","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi."}],"max_tokens":25}' ``` ``` tokens: 4 / 21 ``` 2. The deployment is priced at what the operator declared ``` router pricing: input=5e-06 output=1.5e-05 ``` #### the nightly attribution job 1. Run it for that day ``` rollup: RollupResult(day=2026-08-18, models_processed=0, rows_written=0, rows_failed=0, lapsed=()) flat-cost rows: [] ``` 2. Read the team's day back out of Postgres ``` api_key | model_group | spend | prompt_tokens | completion_tokens | ptu_flat_cost ------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------+----------+---------------+-------------------+--------------- 291e0dcf9ff6ecfbb84b5306a9cd6fb2575ca8a2fa992d859ad81593d58ba670 | gpt-4o-ptu | 0.000335 | 4 | 21 | 0 ``` The tokens are billed at 4 x 5e-06 plus 21 x 1.5e-05, and the reservation the provider is invoicing hourly is recorded nowhere ### After (286bbc97b8) #### a real request through the config.yaml PTU deployment 1. Send the same request ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4812/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-ptu","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi."}],"max_tokens":25}' ``` ``` tokens: 4 / 21 ``` 2. The deployment carries no per-token rate ``` router pricing: input=0.0 output=0.0 ``` #### the nightly attribution job 1. Run it for that day ``` rollup: RollupResult(day=2026-08-18, models_processed=1, rows_written=1, rows_failed=0, lapsed=()) flat-cost rows: [('ptu-team-0001', 'gpt-4o-ptu', 48.0)] ``` 2. Read the team's day back out of Postgres ``` api_key | model_group | spend | prompt_tokens | completion_tokens | ptu_flat_cost ------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------+-------+---------------+-------------------+--------------- 8d808bffd673ab86d6f0e3a2addf8f5933ed7f26fd5a6b9d2666ed5aa52c0864 | gpt-4o-ptu | 0 | 4 | 21 | 0 __ptu_flat_cost__ | gpt-4o-ptu | 0 | 0 | 0 | 48 ``` 100 units at $0.02 an hour over a full day is $48, the same request records 4 and 21 real tokens at no per-token charge, and the deployment id is unchanged from the before run, so cooldowns, deployment budgets and existing spend rows all still key on it Re-run at the current tip, exit code checked and the log grepped for a traceback, after an earlier capture turned out to be a partially completed run ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes The rollup reads the router's deployments alongside the table, keeping the ones no database row owns and dropping the per-request credential clones, which carry `original_model_id` and would otherwise bill one reservation once per distinct caller key. Registering such a deployment zeroes its pricing. The rules for what accrues and what that zeroes live in `litellm/litellm_core_utils/ptu_pricing.py`, which the write endpoints now import as well, because a deployment the rollup declines to charge and the router prices at zero would serve its traffic for free. `tiered_pricing` is emptied rather than zeroed, since its tiers outrank the rates beside them; the search context table is written zeroed because an absent one means the provider's default rather than free; and any further rate the deployment declares is zeroed alongside the standing set. The prune is bounded to the deployments a run scanned, but only for a run that priced a config-declared deployment, so a database-only proxy sweeps exactly as it does today. The nightly catch-up shares that loader, so a config-declared reservation is priced for its elapsed days too. Verified live: a reservation started five days ago writes five days at $240, one started two hundred days ago writes 91 days at $4,368, and a second run of either writes nothing further. ## QA runbook ## Caveats (if any) - A zeroed deployment wins QualityRouter's cost tiebreak where an unset rate lost it - Attribution needs every replica booted from the same config.yaml - Outside its window a PTU deployment bills nothing, matching the database path - Enabling this prices up to 91 elapsed days on the first nightly run ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR ---

signals.title: fix(proxy): log call IDs for request failures
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Failed proxy logs cannot be linked to a request How it solves it: - Logs `litellm_call_id` for error and disconnect paths - Preserves the existing format when the ID is absent ## User Flow Before: a developer receives a failed chat completion but cannot connect its error log to that request 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions while other requests are in flight 2. One request fails and the client receives an error response with `x-litellm-call-id` 3. They inspect the proxy error log but cannot identify the matching request After: the same failure can be correlated from the proxy error log 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions while other requests are in flight 2. One request fails and the client receives an error response with `x-litellm-call-id` 3. They inspect the proxy error log and match its `litellm_call_id` to the response header ## Relevant issues Closes #37532 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] Focused regression tests pass locally - [ ] Full lint and CI checks are pending - [x] My PR scope is isolated to one problem ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix No live-provider run was performed because this local environment has no configured provider credential. The draft includes provider-free regression coverage for the error, client-disconnect, absent-ID, distinct-ID, and request-body boundaries ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Draft pending CI and a live-provider verification ### Final Attestation - [x] The regression tests cover the affected logging branches and preserve no-ID behavior

signals.title: fix(anthropic): log partial stream spend when a /v1/messages client disconnects mid-stream
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Canceled Bedrock `/v1/messages` streams recorded zero spend - Partial output tokens Bedrock already billed vanished from budgets How it solves it: - Client disconnects now dispatch the stream's spend logging on teardown - Output tokens are recovered from the chunks already streamed ## User Flow Before: a developer streams a Bedrock-backed answer through `/v1/messages`, their end user cancels mid-answer, and the request never shows up in spend tracking 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model": "bedrock-claude-opus-5"`, `"stream": true`, and `"max_tokens": 4000` 2. SSE events start arriving; mid-answer their end user hits stop, so the client closes the connection 3. They query GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id=<x-litellm-call-id> and get `[]` back no matter how long they wait 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs has no row for the request, so the tokens Bedrock generated and billed are invisible to budgets and chargeback After: the same canceled stream lands in spend logs within seconds, with the partial output tokens counted 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model": "bedrock-claude-opus-5"`, `"stream": true`, and `"max_tokens": 4000` 2. SSE events start arriving; mid-answer their end user hits stop, so the client closes the connection 3. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id=<x-litellm-call-id> returns one `success` row seconds later, with the prompt tokens plus the output tokens generated before the cancel and their real cost 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request with that partial spend, and a stream left to finish normally is logged exactly as before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5839 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? Same POST as Before, `x-litellm-call-id: 23c11e3c-09f9-47dd-88fd-94b7a40b9b8c` 2. Full SSE stream ends in `message_stop` with `"usage": {"input_tokens": 25, "output_tokens": 600}` 3. `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:44545/spend/logs?request_id=23c11e3c-09f9-47dd-88fd-94b7a40b9b8c" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"` returns one row identical in shape to Before: `status success, call_type anthropic_messages, prompt_tokens 25, completion_tokens 600, total_tokens 625, spend 0.0166375` #### Client disconnect mid-stream 1. signals.title: perf(ci): gate the lint, MCP and dashboard jobs on the pull request's file list
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Four required jobs never got the change gate from #37550 - UI-only PRs still paid ~17 runner-minutes of Python work - Backend-only PRs still installed and built the dashboard - Skipped shards still spent 12 seconds setting up uv How it solves it: - Lint and the MCP suite take the existing backend decision - Dashboard build and unit tests take a new ui decision - CI config counts as ui-relevant, so those workflows self-test - Setup steps that leaked past the gate now carry it ## User Flow Before: a contributor opens a dashboard-only pull request and waits on Python jobs that cannot see their change 1. They push a branch touching only `ui/litellm-dashboard/**` and open a PR against `litellm_internal_staging` 2. The backend shards go green in seconds, because #37550 already gates them 3. `lint` still runs for 6 to 7 minutes: it installs uv, generates a Prisma client and runs ruff and basedpyright over `litellm/` 4. `test` still runs the MCP suite for about 4 minutes, `code-quality` and `validate-model-prices-json` add 6 more 5. Their checks tab stays busy for roughly 7 minutes on work no dashboard file can affect After: the same pull request settles as soon as the dashboard jobs finish 1. They push the same branch and open the same PR 2. `lint` and `test` report success in under a minute, having installed nothing 3. `build-ui`, `ui-unit-tests` and `frontend-lint` still run in full, because the change is theirs to check 4. The reverse also holds: a backend-only PR now skips `build-ui` and `ui-unit-tests` instead of running `npm ci` and a full Next build ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both sides run the gate against three real pull requests through the live GitHub API, with the file counts the API reports for them: #37553 touches 45 files, all under `ui/`; #37545 touches 1 file, `.gitignore`; #37528 touches 2 markdown files. `backend` is the decision `lint`, `test` and the shards consume, `ui` is the one `build-ui` and `ui-unit-tests` consume ### Before (a6163e01466303bc522b408ac5b1d9efd0e3248c) #### Dashboard-only pull request (#37553) 1. Ask for both decisions at the merge base: ```bash git worktree add --detach /tmp/gate-before a6163e01466303bc522b408ac5b1d9efd0e3248c cd /tmp/gate-before REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37553 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=45 \ bash .github/scripts/detect_backend_changes.sh | tail -1 REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37553 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=45 CATEGORY=ui \ bash .github/scripts/detect_backend_changes.sh | tail -1 ``` 2. There is only one decision, and asking for `ui` returns the backend answer because the category does not exist: ``` detect-backend-changes: decision=skip detect-backend-changes: decision=skip ``` 3. `lint` and `test` never read that decision at all, so both ran in full. On this pull request `lint` took 6 minutes 6 seconds and `test` took 4 minutes 24 seconds 4. A skipped shard still did setup work. `misc / Run tests` on this pull request, 23 seconds end to end: ``` 1s success Set up job 5s success Run actions/checkout 0s success Detect backend-relevant changes 1s success Set up Python 5s success Set up uv 7s success Cache uv dependencies 0s skipped Install dependencies 0s skipped Run tests ``` #### Backend-only pull request (#37545, `.gitignore`) 1. Ask for both decisions: ```bash cd /tmp/gate-before REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37545 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=1 \ bash .github/scripts/detect_backend_changes.sh | tail -1 REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37545 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=1 CATEGORY=ui \ bash .github/scripts/detect_backend_changes.sh | tail -1 ``` 2. Both say run, so the dashboard jobs had nothing to skip on: ``` detect-backend-changes: decision=run detect-backend-changes: decision=run ``` #### Documentation-only pull request (#37528) 1. Ask for both decisions: ```bash cd /tmp/gate-before REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37528 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=2 \ bash .github/scripts/detect_backend_changes.sh | tail -1 REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37528 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=2 CATEGORY=ui \ bash .github/scripts/detect_backend_changes.sh | tail -1 ``` 2. Both skip, which is already correct: ``` detect-backend-changes: decision=skip detect-backend-changes: decision=skip ``` ### After (fb2dab19b80325b6ff71416e75e9291f688ca35a) #### Dashboard-only pull request (#37553) 1. Ask for both decisions at this branch's tip: ```bash REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37553 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=45 \ bash .github/scripts/detect_changes.sh | tail -1 REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37553 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=45 CATEGORY=ui \ bash .github/scripts/detect_changes.sh | tail -1 ``` 2. The two decisions now differ, and `lint` and `test` consume the first one: ``` detect-changes[backend]: decision=skip detect-changes[ui]: decision=run ``` 3. The dashboard jobs still run in full, which is what this pull request is for #### Backend-only pull request (#37545, `.gitignore`) 1. Ask for both decisions: ```bash REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37545 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=1 \ bash .github/scripts/detect_changes.sh | tail -1 REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37545 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=1 CATEGORY=ui \ bash .github/scripts/detect_changes.sh | tail -1 ``` 2. The dashboard build and unit tests now skip, so `npm ci` and the Next build stop running for a one-line gitignore change: ``` detect-changes[backend]: decision=run detect-changes[ui]: decision=skip ``` #### Documentation-only pull request (#37528) 1. Ask for both decisions: ```bash REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37528 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=2 \ bash .github/scripts/detect_changes.sh | tail -1 REPO=BerriAI/litellm PR_NUMBER=37528 CHANGED_FILE_COUNT=2 CATEGORY=ui \ bash .github/scripts/detect_changes.sh | tail -1 ``` 2. Still both skip, so nothing regressed for markdown: ``` detect-changes[backend]: decision=skip detect-changes[ui]: decision=skip ``` #### This pull request's own checks 1. It edits `.github/` and `.circleci/`, so both categories say run and every gated job here runs in full. That is the gate refusing to skip the change that rewrites it ## Type 🧹 Refactoring 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats (if any) - The gate stays in-job: `on.paths` would never report a required check - A skipped caller job publishes its own name, not the nested one - `ui` deliberately runs on any `.github` or `.circleci` change - `code-quality` and `validate-model-prices-json` are still ungated ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(proxy): include litellm_call_id in LLM API exception logs
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Proxy error logs had no request id - Concurrent failures can't be traced to a request How it solves it: - Log `litellm_call_id` alongside the exception - Also emit it as a JSON log field ## User Flow Before: a developer running the proxy hits a provider timeout and can't tell which of their concurrent requests failed 1. Their app sends many concurrent `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions`, each response carrying an `x-litellm-call-id` header 2. One request times out and comes back `408` with a `litellm.Timeout` message 3. They open the proxy's application logs and find an ERROR line with the exception text and traceback, a timestamp, and nothing tying it to a request 4. They cannot match that line to the `x-litellm-call-id` their app received, or to the row on `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs`, so they can't tell which call failed After: the same failure logs the id the client already has, so the request is identifiable 1. Their app sends many concurrent `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions`, each response carrying an `x-litellm-call-id` header 2. One request times out and comes back `408` with a `litellm.Timeout` message 3. The ERROR line now reads `Exception occured - litellm_call_id=<id> - litellm.Timeout: ...` and, with `JSON_LOGS=1`, carries a top level `litellm_call_id` field 4. They match that id to the `x-litellm-call-id` their app received and to the row on `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs`, and investigate the exact failed request ## Relevant issues Fixes #37532 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5856 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, a deployment whose upstream never answers within the timeout, so every call fails the way the reporter's did. The proxy is run with `JSON_LOGS=1 LITELLM_LOG=INFO litellm --config config.yaml --port 4000` ```yaml model_list: - model_name: slow-model litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o api_key: fake-key api_base: http://127.0.0.1:8899 # server that accepts the request and never replies timeout: 5 litellm_settings: num_retries: 0 ``` ### Before (a6163e0146) 1. Send the request that will time out ``` $ curl -sS -i -m 30 http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @body.json HTTP/1.1 408 Request Timeout x-litellm-call-id: 8e99b19e-1634-4415-affd-bf76bc2334d9 {"error":{"message":"litellm.Timeout: APITimeoutError - Request timed out. Error_str: Request timed out. - timeout value=5.0, time taken=5.3 seconds ..."}} ``` 2. Look at the ERROR line the proxy logged for it, no call id anywhere (stacktrace elided) ``` {"message": "litellm.proxy.proxy_server._handle_llm_api_exception(): Exception occured - litellm.Timeout: APITimeoutError - Request timed out. Error_str: Request timed out. - timeout value=5.0, time taken=5.3 seconds

Deployment Info: request_timeout: None
timeout: 5.0. Received Model Group=slow-model
Available Model Group Fallbacks=None", "level": "ERROR", "timestamp": "2026-08-20T01:06:18.206077", "component": "LiteLLM Proxy", "logger": "common_request_processing.py:1331", "stacktrace": "..."} ``` 3. Grep the log for the id the client received, nothing matches ``` $ grep -c 8e99b19e proxy.log 0 ``` ### After (c44e3598dd) 1. Send the same request ``` $ curl -sS -i -m 30 http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @body.json HTTP/1.1 408 Request Timeout x-litellm-call-id: 64e235a8-9fec-450e-8b37-c6a6f1abfaad x-litellm-timeout: 5.0 {"error":{"message":"litellm.Timeout: APITimeoutError - Request timed out. Error_str: Request timed out. - timeout value=5.0, time taken=5.0 seconds ..."}} ``` 2. The ERROR line now names that exact call id, both in the message and as a JSON field (stacktrace elided) ``` {"message": "litellm.proxy.proxy_server._handle_llm_api_exception(): Exception occured - litellm_call_id=64e235a8-9fec-450e-8b37-c6a6f1abfaad - litellm.Timeout: APITimeoutError - Request timed out. Error_str: Request timed out. - timeout value=5.0, time taken=5.0 seconds

Deployment Info: request_timeout: None
timeout: 5.0. Received Model Group=slow-model
Available Model Group Fallbacks=None", "level": "ERROR", "timestamp": "2026-08-20T01:15:01.753171", "litellm_call_id": "64e235a8-9fec-450e-8b37-c6a6f1abfaad", "component": "LiteLLM Proxy", "logger": "common_request_processing.py:1332", "stacktrace": "..."} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - The upstream here is a local never-answering server, no provider spend applies to a timeout - Only the proxy's LLM exception funnel is covered, other log lines unchanged ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/9c16527a525743449636d1f8b6b8aad3

signals.title: feat(proxy): redact or drop individual batch records instead of rejecting the file
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - One bad record rejected an entire batch upload - Unusable for a file holding thousands of rows - No way to see which records a guardrail touched How it solves it: - Rewritten records are submitted in their rewritten form - Blocked records are left out, the rest go - The response reports every changed record ## User Flow Before: a platform team with a PII guardrail cannot use batch at all, because one row with a customer email rejects the whole job 1. They upload a 4 row file with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files, `purpose=batch`, where row 2 contains an email address and row 3 asks for something the guardrail blocks 2. The upload returns 400 naming row 3 3. They have no way to submit the other three rows without hand-editing the file first 4. Scaled to a real job of thousands of rows, they would have to find and fix every offending row before any of it runs After: the same upload is accepted, the offending rows are handled per record, and the response says what happened to each 1. They upload the same file with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files, `purpose=batch` 2. The upload returns 200 with a normal file id, plus `litellm_batch_guardrail` reporting `submitted_records: 3` and naming row 2 as `redacted` and row 3 as `dropped` 3. They fetch https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{id}/content and see three rows, with row 2's email replaced by the guardrail's mask and rows 1 and 4 exactly as written 4. They create the batch against that file id as normal 5. A proxy admin sees the same per-record outcome in the proxy logs, so the change is not visible only to the caller ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5276 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Stacked on #37519, which makes guardrails run on batch uploads at all. Base for this QA is that PR's head, `45b549c522` Shared setup. `config.yaml` configures two guardrails, one that masks and one that blocks, using the example guardrail shipped in `litellm/proxy/example_config_yaml/custom_guardrail.py`: ```yaml guardrails: - guardrail_name: "mask-guard" litellm_params: guardrail: custom_guardrail.myCustomGuardrail # masks the literal "litellm" mode: "pre_call" default_on: true - guardrail_name: "block-guard" litellm_params: guardrail: custom_guardrail.myBlockingGuardrail # raises 400 on "blockme" mode: "pre_call" default_on: true files_settings: - custom_llm_provider: openai api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY ``` `pr2_mixed.jsonl` holds four records: a clean row, a row containing `litellm`, a row containing `blockme`, and another clean row. Uploads go to the real OpenAI files API. ### Before (45b549c522) #### 1. mixed file 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@pr2_mixed.jsonl` 2. `HTTP 400` and `{"error":{"message":"{'error': 'Violated guardrail policy', 'guardrail': 'block-guard', 'guardrail_name': 'block-guard', 'guardrail_mode': 'pre_call'}","code":"400"}}` 3. No file id is returned, so none of the four records can be submitted ### After (b61af8d0a8) Full run, recorded live against real OpenAI: ![batch guardrail redaction, recorded live against real OpenAI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr37561/.assets/batch-guardrail-demo.gif) #### 1. mixed file 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@pr2_mixed.jsonl` 2. `HTTP 200` and ```json { "id": "file-...", "object": "file", "purpose": "batch", "bytes": 594, "status": "processed", "litellm_batch_guardrail": { "submitted_records": 3, "modified_records": [ {"line": 2, "custom_id": "row-2", "action": "redacted"}, {"line": 3, "custom_id": "row-3", "action": "dropped"} ] } } ``` 3. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files/file-.../content -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..."` 4. Three records reached OpenAI, with row 2 masked and rows 1 and 4 unchanged: ``` row-1 -> a perfectly clean row row-2 -> this row mentions ******** and should be masked row-4 -> another clean row ``` 5. The proxy log carries the same outcome, so it is not visible only to the caller: ``` batch guardrails changed 2 of 4 records in pr2_mixed.jsonl: line 2 (custom_id row-2) redacted, line 3 (custom_id row-3) dropped ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Only guardrails that run pre_call see batch records - Model-level guardrails still run post-routing, so batch misses them - The report is on create, not on file retrieve - A guardrail that cannot be reached aborts the upload ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit b61af8d0a80dcf8666efc89b812423cfb6c36b69. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: fix(ci): run the full dashboard suite when a change reaches outside src/
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `vitest related` selects no tests for non-`src/` files - `--passWithNoTests` then turns that empty selection green - dashboard dependency bumps merge having run zero unit tests - the breakage only surfaces later, on staging's full run How it solves it: - one changed file outside `src/` now runs the full suite - `related` still covers the common `src/`-only pull request - the decision is a script, so it is testable ## User Flow Before: a maintainer bumping a dashboard dependency gets a green UI Unit Tests check that ran nothing, and finds out on staging 1. They open a pull request that changes only `ui/litellm-dashboard/package.json` and `package-lock.json` 2. The UI Unit Tests check reports success in about a minute 3. Opening the check's "Run UI unit tests (Vitest)" step shows `No test files found, exiting with code 0` 4. They merge, and the full run on the push to `litellm_internal_staging` fails on components the bumped package broke 5. Staging is now red for everyone until someone bisects the merge queue back to that bump After: the same pull request runs every dashboard test before anyone can merge it 1. They open the same pull request changing only `ui/litellm-dashboard/package.json` and `package-lock.json` 2. The UI Unit Tests check now reports `1 changed UI files reach outside src/, so related would miss their dependents; running the full suite` 3. The step runs the whole dashboard suite and fails on the pull request itself if the bump broke anything 4. They see the breakage on their own check instead of on staging 5. A pull request that only touches files under `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/` keeps the fast `related` path and its short runtime ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. signals.title: fix(otel v2): honor per-key and per-team langfuse_host in dynamic tracer routing
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A key's own Langfuse host was ignored under `LITELLM_OTEL_V2` - Its spans went to the operator's Langfuse with the key's credentials - Two keys sharing credentials on different hosts shared one exporter How it solves it: - Credentials and their host now travel as one `TenantRoute` - The per-tenant provider cache keys on that route, endpoint included - Reuses the V1 host resolution, so the two paths cannot drift ## User Flow Before: a developer whose virtual key logs to their own team's Langfuse sees nothing arrive there, while the company-wide Langfuse receives their calls under credentials it does not recognize 1. The proxy admin runs the gateway with `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=1` and `LANGFUSE_HOST` set to the company-wide Langfuse 2. They create a key with `POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate`, giving its logging settings the team's own Langfuse host plus that host's public and secret keys 3. The developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with that key and gets a normal 200 and a completion 4. They open their team's Langfuse and find no trace for the call 5. The company-wide Langfuse receives it instead, presented with the team's public key, which that host does not know, so a real deployment answers 401 and the trace is lost 6. A second key holding the same credentials but a different host fares no better: both keys' calls leave in a single export to the one host After: the same key's traces arrive in the team's own Langfuse, and the company-wide one no longer sees them 1. The proxy admin runs the gateway with `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=1` and `LANGFUSE_HOST` set to the company-wide Langfuse 2. They create a key with `POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate`, giving its logging settings the team's own Langfuse host plus that host's public and secret keys 3. The developer sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with that key and gets a normal 200 and a completion 4. They open their team's Langfuse and find the trace, with the observation for the call 5. The company-wide Langfuse receives only the traces its own credentials cover, so the team's prompts no longer land in an instance the team never named 6. A second key holding the same credentials on a different host reaches its own host, and neither key can read the other's traces ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5857 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real Gemini calls against a real self-hosted Langfuse v3, no mocks. Two Langfuse destinations stand in for two tenants: - host B is the real Langfuse at `http://localhost:3100`, project credentials `pk-lf-85750ac8...` - host C is a capture endpoint at `http://127.0.0.1:3857` that logs the OTLP POST it receives and the public key it was signed with - the proxy's own env host is a third capture endpoint at `http://127.0.0.1:3856`, holding the unrelated operator credentials `pk-lf-global-0000` Shared setup, identical on both sides: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o litellm_params: model: gemini/gemini-3.6-flash api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY litellm_settings: callbacks: ["langfuse_otel"] general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY store_model_in_db: true ``` ```bash export LITELLM_OTEL_V2=1 export LANGFUSE_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:3856 # the operator's host export LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-global-0000 # the operator's credentials export OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=span_and_event ``` Two keys, the same Langfuse credentials, different hosts: ```bash # key B -> the real Langfuse curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4856/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"same-creds-hostB","models":["gpt-4o"], "metadata":{"logging":[{"callback_name":"langfuse_otel","callback_type":"success","callback_vars": {"langfuse_public_key":"pk-lf-85750ac8...","langfuse_secret_key":"sk-lf-...","langfuse_host":"http://localhost:3100"}}]}}' # key C -> the same credentials, a different host curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4856/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"same-creds-hostC","models":["gpt-4o"], "metadata":{"logging":[{"callback_name":"langfuse_otel","callback_type":"success","callback_vars": {"langfuse_public_key":"pk-lf-85750ac8...","langfuse_secret_key":"sk-lf-...","langfuse_host":"http://127.0.0.1:3857"}}]}}' ``` ### Before (3a048601220606f3b0c123c155684bbdb5dd2cf4) 1. Fire both keys at once, each asking the model to echo a unique marker ```bash ( curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4856/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_C" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say only: LIT5857-BEFORE-185212-C"}],"max_tokens":2000}' ) & ( curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4856/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_B" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say only: LIT5857-BEFORE-185212-B"}],"max_tokens":2000}' ) & wait ``` ``` reply key C: LIT5857-BEFORE-185212-C reply key B: LIT5857-BEFORE-185212-B ``` 2. Count the traces in the real Langfuse that key B names ```bash curl -s -u "$PK:$SK" "http://localhost:3100/api/public/traces?limit=1" | jq .meta.totalItems ``` ``` 31 (unchanged from 31 before the calls) ``` 3. Read what the capture endpoint for host C received ```bash cat hostc.jsonl ``` ``` (nothing) ``` 4. Read what the operator's env host received ```bash cat envhost.jsonl ``` ``` {"path": "/api/public/otel/v1/traces", "method": "POST", "public_key": "pk-lf-global-0000", "bytes": 5923} {"path": "/api/public/otel/v1/traces", "method": "POST", "public_key": "pk-lf-85750ac8-240b-485e-9be4-5e8b4ad0af54", "bytes": 7542} ``` Neither key reached the host it names. Both keys' spans left in one 7542 byte POST to the operator's host, signed with the tenant's public key, which is the shared-exporter collision as well as the wrong destination ### After (8494dc0a930ae042d713183ba9279d023a1aab87) 1. Fire both keys at once, same order, new markers ```bash ( curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4856/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_C" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say only: LIT5857-AFTER-185255-C"}],"max_tokens":2000}' ) & ( curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4856/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_B" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say only: LIT5857-AFTER-185255-B"}],"max_tokens":2000}' ) & wait ``` ``` reply key C: LIT5857-AFTER-185255-C reply key B: LIT5857-AFTER-185255-B ``` 2. Count the traces in the real Langfuse that key B names ```bash curl -s -u "$PK:$SK" "http://localhost:3100/api/public/traces?limit=1" | jq .meta.totalItems ``` ``` 32 (was 31 before the calls) ``` 3. Read what the capture endpoint for host C received ```bash cat hostc.jsonl ``` ``` {"path": "/api/public/otel/v1/traces", "method": "POST", "public_key": "pk-lf-85750ac8-240b-485e-9be4-5e8b4ad0af54", "bytes": 4087} ``` 4. Read what the operator's env host received ```bash cat envhost.jsonl ``` ``` {"path": "/api/public/otel/v1/traces", "method": "POST", "public_key": "pk-lf-global-0000", "bytes": 5923} ``` 5. Open the new trace in the real Langfuse and check which marker it carries ```bash TID=$(curl -s -u "$PK:$SK" "http://localhost:3100/api/public/traces?limit=1" | jq -r .data[0].id) curl -s -u "$PK:$SK" "http://localhost:3100/api/public/traces/$TID" | grep -c LIT5857-AFTER-185255-B curl -s -u "$PK:$SK" "http://localhost:3100/api/public/traces/$TID" | grep -c LIT5857-AFTER-185255-C ``` ``` 1 key B's marker is in the trace on the host key B names 0 key C's marker is not, so the two keys did not share an exporter ``` Each key reached its own host, the operator's host saw only its own credentials, and neither key's content appeared on the other's destination Confirming the V1 path is untouched, the same key with `LITELLM_OTEL_V2` unset also delivered to the host it names, and the env host received nothing ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Applies to trace export; events and metrics still use the env destination - `TenantTracerCache` builds providers without a lock, unchanged here - A key naming the env host explicitly gets its own cache entry - Provider count is unchanged for one-host-per-key setups, measured ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(e2e): move record/replay to the provider edge (LIT-5745)
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - e2e replay stubbed the whole proxy, not just the providers - a replay pass proved nothing about auth, routing, cost, or spend - replay even passed with the proxy process fully stopped How it solves it: - record/replay now scopes to the proxy's provider-bound traffic only - an in-process provider edge server fronts the real providers - edge-wired tests register deployments whose api_base points at the edge - record forwards to the real provider and stores each exchange - replay answers provider calls from the bundle, zero provider spend - proxy and database stay live, so proxy regressions turn replay red - drift fails loudly with HTTP 599 instead of silently going live ## User Flow Before: a contributor replays an e2e suite and gets a green run that never touched the proxy, so it certifies nothing the proxy does 1. They start the proxy and confirm GET http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness returns "I'm alive!" 2. They record a spend test with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record uv run pytest tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/ -v`; it passes against the real provider and writes a fixture bundle 3. They rerun it with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay`; it passes, but the proxy saw zero requests during the run: every response, key mint included, came from the bundle 4. They stop the proxy entirely and replay again; still green, so a replay pass says nothing about key auth, routing, cost calculation, or spend-log writes After: the same replay drives the live proxy end to end and only the provider is answered from the recording 1. They start the proxy and confirm GET http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness returns "I'm alive!" 2. They record with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record uv run pytest tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py -v`; the test registers its model via POST http://localhost:4000/model/new with an api_base pointing at a local edge address, and the real provider's answer lands in the bundle 3. They replay with `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake` on both the proxy and the run; POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate mints a real key, POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions returns the recorded completion, GET http://localhost:4000/spend/logs shows a non-zero spend row, and the run passes with zero provider calls 4. They stop the proxy and replay again; the run now goes red at setup with "No live proxy", because replay needs the proxy 5. They break the proxy instead (disable spend logging, or corrupt key generation); replay goes red with "no SpendLogs row" or a 401, catching the regression ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5745 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a scratch database `lit5745_qa`, and this proxy config ```yaml model_list: - model_name: bootstrap-noop litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.5 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY store_model_in_db: true proxy_batch_write_at: 5 ``` Proxy boot (per checkout, port checked free first with `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN`): ```bash set -a && source .env && set +a export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://...:.../lit5745_qa" uv run python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config lit5745_qa_config.yaml --port <port> --use_v2_migration_resolver curl -fs http://localhost:<port>/health/liveliness # "I'm alive!" ``` ### Before (629d7683f2) #### record 1. Boot the merge-base proxy on port 28353 and record one spend test against the real provider: ```bash E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record E2E_RESET_SPEND_LOGS=1 LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:28353 \ uv run pytest "tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_spend_tracking_e2e.py::test_chat_completion_writes_nonzero_spend_row" -v ``` ``` tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_spend_tracking_e2e.py::test_chat_completion_writes_nonzero_spend_row PASSED [100%] ========================= 1 passed in 66.49s (0:01:06) ========================= ``` #### replay with zero provider calls 1. Stop the proxy and confirm nothing listens: ```bash kill <proxy pid>; lsof -nP -iTCP:28353 -sTCP:LISTEN # proxy DOWN ``` 2. Replay the same test with the proxy down and a fake provider key: ```bash E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:28353 OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake \ uv run pytest "tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_spend_tracking_e2e.py::test_chat_completion_writes_nonzero_spend_row" -v ``` ``` tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_spend_tracking_e2e.py::test_chat_completion_writes_nonzero_spend_row PASSED [100%] ========================= 1 passed in 65.06s (0:01:05) ========================= ``` Green with no proxy process running at all: the run certified key auth, cost calculation, and spend writes that never executed #### replay against a broken proxy 1. No separate run can go red: the replay above already passed with the proxy stopped, the most broken proxy possible, so no proxy regression can ever turn a Before replay red ### After (367dd537b9) #### record 1. Boot the PR-tip proxy on port 28141 with real keys and record the edge-wired spend test (one real OpenAI call): ```bash E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record E2E_RESET_SPEND_LOGS=1 LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:28141 \ uv run pytest tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py -v ``` ``` tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py::test_edge_wired_chat_writes_nonzero_spend_row PASSED [100%] ========================= 1 passed in 83.98s (0:01:23) ========================= ``` #### replay with zero provider calls 1. Reboot the proxy with `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-fake` in its env, then replay with the same fake keys on the pytest side: ```bash E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay E2E_RESET_SPEND_LOGS=1 LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:28141 \ OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-fake \ uv run pytest tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py -v ``` ``` tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py::test_edge_wired_chat_writes_nonzero_spend_row PASSED [100%] ========================= 1 passed in 80.88s (0:01:20) ========================= ``` Neither side holds a real provider key, so a single leaked provider call would 401 and fail the run; the key mint, chat routing, cost calculation, and the non-zero spend row all executed against the live proxy and database #### replay against a broken proxy 1. Break spend writes: add `disable_spend_logs: true` to the config, reboot, replay again: ``` > assert matching, f"no SpendLogs row for request_id {chat.id}; saw {len(rows)} row(s)" E AssertionError: no SpendLogs row for request_id chatcmpl-EEmBI8wmtyO8weuLkSiCiobRa30zC; saw 0 row(s) ======================== 1 failed in 197.13s (0:03:17) ========================= ``` 2. Revert that, then break key generation with a temporary one-line patch that persists the hash of a corrupted token (`{**key_data, "token": f"{key_data['token']}-broken"}` at the DB insert), reboot, replay again: ``` E AssertionError: kind='unauthorized' body='{"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Invalid proxy server token passed. Received API Key = sk-...8xKQ, Key Hash (Token) =db63ec69e77741b877decb60ed70824cc9b1d0c3f0cf21f1f9be524686cd9e56. Unable to find token in cache or `LiteLLM_VerificationTokenTable`","type":"token_not_found_in_db","param":"key","code":"401"}}' ======================== 1 failed in 75.69s (0:01:15) ========================= ``` 3. Revert the patch (`git checkout -- litellm/`), reboot clean, and replay goes green again: ``` tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py::test_edge_wired_chat_writes_nonzero_spend_row PASSED [100%] ========================= 1 passed in 80.76s (0:01:20) ========================= ``` ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - streaming records as one buffered body for now (LIT-5742) - CI wiring for record/replay is LIT-5748 - Bedrock cannot be edge-mounted: SigV4 signs the Host header - multipart bodies miss on replay: per-run random boundaries - only `/model/new` deployments can be edge-wired, not config-baked ones - replaying over a record run's DB rows dedupes spend writes (same response id is the SpendLogs primary key); run both modes with `E2E_RESET_SPEND_LOGS=1` or replay against a fresh DB ## QA runbook - tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py::test_edge_wired_chat_writes_nonzero_spend_row - an edge-wired chat billed through the live proxy writes a non-zero spend row, in live, record, and replay modes alike (needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` for live/record, `store_model_in_db: true`, and `DATABASE_URL` plus `E2E_RESET_SPEND_LOGS=1` in the pytest env so consecutive record/replay sessions do not dedupe each other's spend rows) - [ ] Run it once with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record`; it registers a model via POST /model/new whose api_base points at the local provider edge, sends one real chat, and writes `tests/e2e/.fixtures` - [ ] Restart the proxy with `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake` and rerun with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay`; expect green with zero provider calls - [ ] To reproduce by hand against the same proxy: POST /key/generate with the master key, POST /v1/chat/completions with that key and the registered model, then GET /spend/logs?api_key=<hashed key> and expect a row whose request_id matches the completion id with spend > 0 - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR CHECKED: live-pr-risk at 367dd537b9. Harness-only change: no references to the reworked modules outside tests/e2e (repo and docs greps), full e2e suite collects clean on the head (685 tests, 0 errors), basedpyright over tests/e2e reports 0 errors, and record/replay plus three broken-proxy red runs were driven live on a real proxy, database, and provider

signals.title: fix(google_genai): read functionDeclarations.parameters in the generateContent bridge
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Gemini tool schemas vanish when the model is not Gemini - Models get a function with no arguments, invent their own - Fails silently: 200 OK, wrong `args`, no log How it solves it: - Read `functionDeclarations[].parameters` when `parametersJsonSchema` is absent - `parametersJsonSchema` still wins when both are present ## User Flow Before: a developer whose app uses the Google GenAI SDK against the proxy gets function calls back with empty arguments as soon as the model name is served by a non-Gemini deployment. 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1beta/models/my-model:generateContent`, where `my-model` is served by an OpenAI-compatible deployment, declaring one tool `get_weather` that takes a required string `city` 2. They get `200` back with `{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{}}}` — right function, no arguments 3. Their app calls `get_weather()` with no city and raises a `KeyError` 4. On repeated runs the model sometimes answers `{"args":{"location":"Hanoi"}}`, a parameter name that appears nowhere in the tool they declared 5. They get `200` back with `{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{"city":"Hanoi"}}}` 3. Their app calls `get_weather(city="Hanoi")` and returns the right weather 4. Repeated runs return the same `city` argument every time 5. signals.title: refactor(ui): migrate the last antd components off antd onto shadcn
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - 18 dashboard components were still rendering antd - Two UI kits on one page, inconsistent controls - antd Select popups sit above shadcn ones - Blocks the React 19 and antd-removal work How it solves it: - Ports the last 18 components onto shadcn primitives - Zero `from "antd"` imports left in `src` - Prunes 63 stale `no-restricted-imports` suppressions - Fixes a router settings race the speedup exposed ## User Flow Before: an admin creating a key sees the modal in two visual languages, and a router setting they just typed can be dropped from the request 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys and click Create New Key 2. The dialog mixes antd and shadcn controls: the Models picker, Key Type picker and Router Settings inputs do not match the surrounding fields, and their dropdown popups render on a separate stacking layer 3. They expand Router Settings, change a value, and click Create within about a tenth of a second 4. The key is created without the router settings they just entered, silently After: the same modal renders as one consistent kit, and the value they typed is always the value that is sent 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys and click Create New Key 2. Every control in the dialog is the same shadcn kit as the rest of the page, and the dropdowns open in the same layer as everything else 3. They expand Router Settings, change a value, and click Create immediately 4. The key is created with exactly the router settings shown on screen ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### Before (7b6e16cfd315d940d8b34cebd39ef16f3d2f0c26) ### After (776069b777) ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats - Switches lose antd's inline Yes/No labels - The "New" tag is a primary badge, not purple - `tests/e2e/ui` still holds dead `.ant-*` selectors - The `antd` dependency stays installed, removed separately

signals.text: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0). **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: ```bash cosign verify \ --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \ ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-dev.1 ``` **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: ```bash cosign verify \ --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.99.0-dev.1/cosign.pub \ ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-dev.1 ``` Expected output: ``` The following checks were performed on each of these signatures: - The cosign claims were validated - The signatures were verified against the specified public key ``` --- ## What's Changed * chore(typing): drop 1.3k basedpyright errors across 30 Any hotspot files by @mateo-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/37073 * signal.title: fix(proxy): preserve repeated multipart form fields in get_form_data
signal.text: Fixes #35937 ## Problem `get_form_data()` in `litellm/proxy/common_utils/http_parsing_utils.py` (used by `/v1/audio/transcriptions`) called `dict(form)` on Starlette's `FormData` object before iterating it. `FormData` is a multidict that can hold multiple values under the same key, but `dict()` collapses repeated keys and silently keeps only the last one. The OpenAI SDK encodes `timestamp_granularities=["word", "segment"]` as two separate `timestamp_granularities[]=...` multipart fields, so the collapse meant only the second value ever reached litellm — matching the exact "last one wins" behavior reported. ## Fix Replaced `dict(form).items()` with `form.multi_items()` in `get_form_data()`, which preserves every repeated key/value pair from the original multidict. ## Testing Updated `tests/test_litellm/proxy/common_utils/test_http_parsing_utils.py::test_get_form_data` to use a real `starlette.datastructures.FormData` (the previous mock was a plain dict literal, which can't represent a duplicate key and never actually exercised the bug) and assert both `"word"` and `"segment"` survive. Also fixed `TestGetRequestBody::test_form_post_routes_to_form_data`, whose mock likewise needed a real `FormData` object to support `.multi_items()`. Verified as a genuine regression guard: reverting the fix makes `test_get_form_data` fail with `AssertionError: assert ['segment'] == ['word', 'segment']`; restoring the fix passes it again. ``` ============================= 57 passed in 8.24s ============================== ```
