signal.title: fix(xai): bill from the cost xAI reports instead of recomputing it
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - xAI reports what it charged, LiteLLM ignores it - LiteLLM re-derives the number from tokens and list rates - Only `web_search_calls` is priced, other tool calls cost nothing - Cached prompt discounts are missing from the estimate - Streamed requests skip the tool surcharge entirely How it solves it: - Bill the amount xAI reports, when it sends one - Fall back to today's token and per-call math otherwise - Skip the search surcharge that amount already covers - Carry it on `usage.cost`, the channel every route reads ## User Flow Before: a developer running Grok with server side web search sees spend that does not match their xAI invoice 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "xai/grok-4-latest"` and `"tools": [{"type": "web_search"}]` 2. The answer comes back with the citations they asked for 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request is logged at a cost worked out from token counts, with a flat $0.005 added for every search the model ran 4. Their xAI console shows a smaller amount for that same request, and the gap grows with every search 5. They resend the request with `"stream": true` and get a third number in the logs, because the streamed route adds nothing for the searches at all After: the same request is logged at the amount xAI says it charged 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "xai/grok-4-latest"` and `"tools": [{"type": "web_search"}]` 2. The answer is unchanged 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request at the figure xAI reported, tokens and every server side tool call together 4. That figure matches what the xAI console shows for the same request 5. Resending with `"stream": true` logs that same figure, and so does the same request sent to https://litellm-domain/v1/responses ## Relevant issues Relates to #35829, which reports that a provider-reported `usage.cost` is trusted verbatim as USD and records phantom spend when the upstream denominates that field in something else. This PR does not widen that path, and it is worth being explicit about why - xAI does not report a bare cost float. It reports `usage.cost_in_usd_ticks`, an integer denominated by a documented constant of 10,000,000,000 ticks to the dollar (https://docs.x.ai/developers/cost-tracking) - Both the conversion and the validation happen inside the xAI adapter, before anything reaches `usage.cost`. `xai_reported_cost_in_usd()` accepts only a non-negative integer, refusing bool as an int subclass, and returns USD. A malformed, negative or absent value yields None and the request falls back to the existing pricing with the search surcharge left intact - So what lands on `usage.cost` here is an already validated USD amount derived from a field with a defined unit, not an arbitrary number of unknown denomination. #35829's failure mode is the generic path accepting the latter, and nothing in this PR loosens that One consequence is worth stating rather than leaving to be discovered: on the streaming path `streaming_handler.py::_propagate_usage_cost_to_hidden_params()` copies `usage.cost` into `_hidden_params`, and `response_cost_calculator()` returns that before `completion_cost()` runs, so `llms/xai/cost_calculator.py` is not consulted for streamed requests. That is safe here precisely because the conversion and the validation already happened in the adapter. The guard in the cost calculator covers the non-streaming path, where usage reaches it directly Nothing in the tracker reports the remaining xAI mismatch itself. I searched issues for xai, grok, live search, web search cost and cost_in_usd_ticks, and the only other xAI cost bug on file is #15338, which is about tiered token pricing and is already closed. So there is no issue to close here ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix To be clear about what this is: not a live capture, but a documented xAI usage payload replayed through the transformations and then through the cost path spend tracking calls, at both commits. I do not have an xAI key with server side search billing enabled to capture a real invoice against. The curl commands a reviewer can run against a live proxy are at the end, and I am happy to add that run if you would rather have it ```python import httpx from unittest.mock import Mock import litellm from litellm.litellm_core_utils.streaming_handler import CustomStreamWrapper from litellm.llms.xai.chat.transformation import XAIChatCompletionStreamingHandler, XAIChatConfig from litellm.llms.xai.responses.transformation import XAIResponsesAPIConfig from litellm.responses.utils import ResponseAPILoggingUtils from litellm.types.utils import Choices, Message, ModelResponse TICKS = 137560000 TOOL_DETAILS = {"web_search_calls": 12, "x_search_calls": 0, "code_execution_calls": 0} CHAT_USAGE = {"prompt_tokens": 6153, "completion_tokens": 412, "total_tokens": 6565, "server_side_tool_usage_details": TOOL_DETAILS, "cost_in_usd_ticks": TICKS} def _chat_body(usage): return {"id": "chatcmpl-xai", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 0, "model": "grok-4-latest", "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "x"}, "finish_reason": "stop"}], "usage": usage} def _billed(usage): r = ModelResponse(id="p", model="grok-4-latest", object="chat.completion", created=0, choices=[Choices(index=0, message=Message(role="assistant", content="x"), finish_reason="stop")]) r.usage = usage return litellm.completion_cost(completion_response=r, model="xai/grok-4-latest", custom_llm_provider="xai", call_type="completion") chat = XAIChatConfig().transform_response( model="grok-4-latest", raw_response=httpx.Response(status_code=200, json=_chat_body(CHAT_USAGE)), model_response=ModelResponse(), logging_obj=Mock(), request_data={}, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "x"}], optional_params={}, litellm_params={}, encoding=None) parsed = XAIChatCompletionStreamingHandler(streaming_response=iter([]), sync_stream=True).chunk_parser( {"id": "chatcmpl-xai", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 0, "model": "grok-4-latest", "choices": [], "usage": CHAT_USAGE}) assembled = litellm.stream_chunk_builder(chunks=[parsed]) CustomStreamWrapper._propagate_usage_cost_to_hidden_params(assembled) streamed = litellm.cost_calculator.response_cost_calculator( response_object=assembled, model="grok-4-latest", custom_llm_provider="xai", call_type="completion", optional_params={}, cache_hit=None, base_model=None) responses = XAIResponsesAPIConfig().transform_response_api_response( model="grok-4-latest", raw_response=httpx.Response(status_code=200, json={ "id": "resp_xai", "object": "response", "created_at": 0, "model": "grok-4-latest", "status": "completed", "output": [], "parallel_tool_calls": False, "tool_choice": "auto", "tools": [], "usage": {"input_tokens": 6153, "output_tokens": 412, "total_tokens": 6565, "server_side_tool_usage_details": TOOL_DETAILS, "cost_in_usd_ticks": TICKS}}), logging_obj=Mock()) responses_usage = ResponseAPILoggingUtils._transform_response_api_usage_to_chat_usage(responses.usage) print(f"xAI reported for this request: ${TICKS / 1e10:.6f}") print(f" /v1/chat/completions billed: ${_billed(chat.usage):.6f}") print(f" /v1/chat/completions (stream) billed: ${streamed:.6f}") print(f" /v1/responses billed: ${_billed(responses_usage):.6f}") ``` Before, at base `55777d0e80`: ``` xAI reported for this request: $0.013756 /v1/chat/completions billed: $0.084639 /v1/chat/completions (stream) billed: $0.024639 /v1/responses billed: $0.084639 ``` After, at `78112c0b1d`: ``` xAI reported for this request: $0.013756 /v1/chat/completions billed: $0.013756 /v1/chat/completions (stream) billed: $0.013756 /v1/responses billed: $0.013756 ``` On the two non streamed routes the 12 searches were charged at $0.005 each, $0.06 on top of the $0.0246 token estimate, against the $0.0138 xAI actually charged. The streamed route dropped the searches entirely and priced from tokens alone, which is why it landed somewhere else again. All three now agree with the provider To run it against a live proxy with a real xAI key instead, with `XAI_API_KEY` set and the proxy started as in CLAUDE.md: ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"xai/grok-4-latest","tools":[{"type":"web_search"}], "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What did xAI ship this week? cite sources"}]}' \ | python -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print("ticks:", d["usage"].get("cost_in_usd_ticks"), "-> $", d["usage"].get("cost_in_usd_ticks",0)/1e10)' curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"xai/grok-4-latest","tools":[{"type":"web_search"}], "input":"What did xAI ship this week? cite sources"}' | python -m json.tool | grep -i cost ``` then open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs and compare the logged spend for those two requests against https://console.x.ai usage for the same minute ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Since #30817 the xAI cost calculator counts server side searches from `usage.server_side_tool_usage_details.web_search_calls` and prices them at xAI's published $5 per 1,000 calls, falling back to that list rate because no xai entry in the price map carries `search_context_cost_per_query`. That is the right rate for that one tool, and LiteLLM is still doing xAI's arithmetic for it Every xAI response already states the amount charged, in `usage.cost_in_usd_ticks`, at 10^10 ticks to the dollar. Per xAI's [cost tracking docs](https://docs.x.ai/developers/cost-tracking) that single figure is "the actual amount billed, after all applicable discounts (including prompt caching reductions) have been applied, and inclusive of all token costs and server-side tool invocation costs". This PR reads it and prices the request from it, which is the shape `llms/perplexity/cost_calculator.py` already uses for a provider that reports its own cost. `get_cost_for_web_search_request` needed no change, because the xAI calculator now returns 0 for the search surcharge once the reported total has been applied, the same way the perplexity branch two lines above it does Three things the re-derived number cannot reach, all of which the reported one already accounts for. xAI's [pricing page](https://docs.x.ai/developers/pricing) lists Web Search, X Search and Code Execution at $5 per 1,000 calls, Collections Search at $2.50 and File Attachments at $10, but only `web_search_calls` is priced today, so a request whose `server_side_tool_usage_details` reports `x_search_calls` or `code_execution_calls` is billed nothing for them. Prompt caching is the second: `xai/grok-4` and `xai/grok-4-latest` carry no `cache_read_input_token_cost`, so cached input is priced at the full $3 per 1M while xAI has already discounted it. The third is drift, since each of those rates needs a matching LiteLLM change every time xAI revises one The conversion lives in the xAI chat and responses transformations, which restate the ticks in USD on `usage.cost`. That is the field litellm already carries a provider stated cost in, and using it is what keeps this change inside the provider adapter: `ResponseAPILoggingUtils` already copies `usage.cost` onto the chat Usage for `/v1/responses`, and the streaming chunk assembler already carries `cost` through aggregation, so neither had to learn an xAI wire field. An earlier revision of this PR instead invented a parallel channel and taught `litellm/responses/utils.py` to preserve unmodelled provider fields, which changed `/v1/responses` for every provider to serve one. That is gone; the diff is now entirely under `litellm/llms/xai/` and its mirrored tests Without a reported figure nothing changes: the existing token math and the existing per-call search surcharge both run exactly as before Only the documented shape of that field is trusted, a non-negative integer, with bool refused since it is an int subclass. A caller who can set `api_base` controls the response body, so a negative amount would otherwise be billed as negative and subtracted from that caller's own recorded spend, slipping past a budget. Anything that is not a non-negative integer falls back to token pricing with the search surcharge still applied What that check cannot do is make a self-hosted `api_base` trustworthy, and neither can token pricing: the token counts come from the same response body, so an endpoint reporting `"prompt_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens": 0` already logs $0 today. Trusting a reported total hands such a caller nothing they did not already have, and it is the exposure the perplexity calculator has carried for a while On #35829, which reports a nano denominated `usage.cost` recorded verbatim as $3,144,000 of spend: this PR is the narrow per provider opt in that issue asks for as its first suggested fix, "only trust `usage.cost` for providers where the calling code explicitly opts in (e.g. Perplexity's own `cost_calculator.py` already does this narrowly and correctly)". The unit is converted from xAI's documented tick unit before it ever reaches `usage.cost` rather than guessed, so the confusion in that report cannot arise on this path. The blanket trust in `response_cost_calculator` that the issue is actually about is untouched and still wants a decision above this file On why not put the price in `model_info`, as #24372 did for gemini: that was right for gemini, since Google does not tell you what it charged and a configured price is the only option there. xAI does tell you. Going that way means adding tool prices to all 44 xai entries and keeping every one of them current through each xAI revision, and it still cannot express what xAI bills, since the server side tools are charged per invocation across several distinct tools at different rates and the model decides how many of each to call Not touched: the model price maps, and any provider neutral file ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: refactor(ui): migrate antd Modal onto the shared shadcn Dialog
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - antd Modal was the largest remaining blocker to dropping antd - 52 files and 65 call sites still rendered it - Two of those modals had no test that could catch a regression - One form only appeared to reset because antd re-rendered it How it solves it: - Moves 51 files onto the in-repo shadcn Dialog - Adds real coverage to the two blind spots first - Fixes the reset bug antd was hiding - Clears 31 no-restricted-imports suppressions ## User Flow Before: an admin working through the dashboard's dialogs meets a handful of rough edges, one of which loses their work 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams and click a team, then Edit Member on a row 2. They change the member's role and save. The dialog stays open with the previous member's ID and email still filled in, so the next edit starts from stale data 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=guardrails and click Create guardrail. The dialog has no accessible name, so a screen reader announces it as an unlabelled dialog 4. On https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=guardrails they open Submit for Review from a team's guardrails tab. The page's own Status filter behind the dialog is still reachable by a screen reader and by tabbing, even though it is visually covered 5. Every one of these dialogs is antd's, so the dashboard ships two dialog implementations with different focus, escape and backdrop behaviour After: the same admin gets one consistent dialog everywhere, and the edit form starts clean 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams and click a team, then Edit Member on a row 2. They change the member's role and save. The fields clear, so the next edit starts empty 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=guardrails and click Create guardrail. The dialog announces itself as "Create guardrail" 4. signal.title: feat(providers): add SCX.ai as a JSON-configured OpenAI-compatible provider
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - SCX.ai is not a supported provider, so callers have to route through `openai/` with a custom `api_base` - SCX.ai takes `max_tokens` rather than `max_completion_tokens`, and caps `temperature` How it solves it: - Registers `scx-ai` in `litellm/llms/openai_like/providers.json` with the parameter mapping and the ceiling as a constraint, so no Python module is needed - Adds GLM-5.2 and Qwen3.8 Max to the cost map, and registers the provider in the endpoint matrix and the dashboard ## Relevant issues Docs live in the other repo, so the provider page goes up separately in [BerriAI/litellm-docs#808](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/808). That one is a prerequisite here: `documentation` and `code-quality` both run `tests/documentation_tests/test_env_keys.py`, which checks out `BerriAI/litellm-docs` and fails while `SCX_API_KEY` is read under `./litellm` but mentioned nowhere in the docs. Both jobs go green once it merges ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All captured at `1e24f93d3` against the real SCX.ai API, with the proxy started as `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config scx_config.yaml --port 4000` on a config with both models pointed at `os.environ/SCX_API_KEY` Chat completions, with the cost header showing the new rates being applied ```bash $ for m in scx-glm-5.2 scx-qwen3.8-max; do curl -sS -D /tmp/h_$m.txt http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Reply with exactly: hello from SCX\"}],\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c "{m:\"$m\", content: .choices[0].message.content}" grep -i "^x-litellm-response-cost:" /tmp/h_$m.txt done {"m":"scx-glm-5.2","content":"hello from SCX"} x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0002285815 {"m":"scx-qwen3.8-max","content":"hello from SCX"} x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0004901237 ``` Tool calling and `json_schema` structured output on both ```bash $ for m in scx-glm-5.2 scx-qwen3.8-max; do curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"What is the weather in Sydney? Use the tool.\"}],\"tools\":[{\"type\":\"function\",\"function\":{\"name\":\"get_weather\",\"description\":\"Get the weather for a city\",\"parameters\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"city\":{\"type\":\"string\"}},\"required\":[\"city\"]}}}],\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c "{m:\"$m\", tool: .choices[0].message.tool_calls[0].function}" done {"m":"scx-glm-5.2","tool":{"arguments":"{\"city\": \"Sydney\"}","name":"get_weather"}} {"m":"scx-qwen3.8-max","tool":{"arguments":"{\"city\": \"Sydney\"}","name":"get_weather"}} $ for m in scx-glm-5.2 scx-qwen3.8-max; do curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"City is Sydney\"}],\"response_format\":{\"type\":\"json_schema\",\"json_schema\":{\"name\":\"c\",\"schema\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"city\":{\"type\":\"string\"}},\"required\":[\"city\"],\"additionalProperties\":false}}},\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c "{m:\"$m\", content: .choices[0].message.content}" done {"m":"scx-glm-5.2","content":"{\n \"city\": \"Sydney\"\n}"} {"m":"scx-qwen3.8-max","content":"{\"city\":\"Sydney\"}"} ``` Image input on Qwen3.8 Max, which is the one of the two that declares `supports_vision`, sending a 64x64 solid red PNG as a data URI ```bash $ IMG=$(base64 -i red64.png) $ curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"scx-qwen3.8-max\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"What colour fills this image? One word.\"},{\"type\":\"image_url\",\"image_url\":{\"url\":\"data:image/png;base64,$IMG\"}}]}],\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c '{content: .choices[0].message.content, image_tokens: .usage.prompt_tokens_details.image_tokens}' {"content":"Red","image_tokens":66} ``` The Add Model form reads `/public/providers/fields`, which now returns the provider ```bash $ curl -sS http://localhost:4000/public/providers/fields | jq -c '.[] | select(.litellm_provider=="scx-ai") | {provider, provider_display_name, default_model_placeholder}' {"provider":"SCX_AI","provider_display_name":"SCX.ai","default_model_placeholder":"scx-ai/GLM-5.2"} ``` With that proxy running and `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard`, Models and Endpoints then Add Model lists SCX.ai in the Provider dropdown with its logo ## Type New Feature ## Changes `providers.json` carries the base URL, `SCX_API_KEY`, the `SCX_API_BASE` override, the `max_completion_tokens` to `max_tokens` mapping and a `temperature_max` of 1.99. SCX accepts `temperature` in `[0.0, 2.0)` and returns a 400 on 2.0 exactly, and the clamp is an inclusive `min()`, so 2.0 would let through a value the endpoint rejects. The slug is registered in `LlmProviders`, the OpenAI-compatible provider and endpoint lists, the api base autodetection branch, and the endpoint support matrix Two chat models go into the cost map. GLM-5.2 has a 1M context window and is text only; Qwen3.8 Max has a 1M window and takes image input. Both cap output at 131072, which is what the endpoint's own validator enforces rather than what the catalogue advertises, and both do implicit prompt caching, so each carries a cache read rate The dashboard needs both the display metadata in `provider_info_helpers.tsx` and an entry in `provider_create_fields.json`, since the Add Model form renders from the latter Tests cover registration, config values, model resolution, api base override and autodetection, the temperature clamp, the parameter mapping, router config, cost map and backup sync, the create-fields entry and the dashboard helpers I work at SCX.ai ## QA runbook Export `SCX_API_KEY`, start the proxy on the config above and run the curl commands in the proof section ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(proxy): retry spend updates on Postgres deadlock instead of dropping them
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Postgres deadlocks silently drop spend increments under concurrency - Only httpx.ConnectError was retried; deadlocks re-raised immediately - The end-user spend flush was still fully unprotected How it solves it: - Classify prisma deadlocks (P2034 / 40P01) as retry-safe - Route every spend path through one jittered-retry helper - End-user spend flush now uses that helper too - Each retry logs a warning instead of recovering silently ## User Flow Before: a gateway admin metering per-end-user spend loses increments whenever the periodic spend flush deadlocks with another spend writer 1. An end user's app sends POST http://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"user": "end-user-a"` (or Claude Code pointed at the gateway sends POST /v1/messages); the call returns 200 with the completion 2. Seconds later the background spend flush collides with a concurrent writer touching the same end-user rows and the admin's log shows a `prisma.errors.DataError ... 40P01 "deadlock detected"` traceback, with the alert text `[Non-Blocking]LiteLLM Prisma Client Exception - update spend logs` 3. GET http://litellm-domain/customer/info?end_user_id=end-user-a still shows the old spend, and every end-user increment carried by that flush cycle is gone for good After: the same collision is retried with jittered backoff and the spend lands 1. The end user's app sends the same POST http://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"user": "end-user-a"`; the call returns 200 2. The flush hits the same deadlock, but the log now shows one warning, `Retrying spend update after retryable DB error (attempt 1/3): ... deadlock detected`, and no failure traceback 3. GET http://litellm-domain/customer/info?end_user_id=end-user-a shows spend increased by exactly the new requests' cost; nothing is dropped ## Relevant issues Fixes #27989 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-3449 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy, fresh Postgres DB, real Anthropic calls. Config: `claude-haiku-4-5` -> `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` plus a `claude-*` wildcard, `proxy_batch_write_at: 20`. Traffic comes from curl with a `user` field and from a real Claude Code TUI session pointed at the gateway (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:53817`). The concurrent opposing-order writer (at 1K+ RPS this is another pod's unsorted or scan-order EndUserTable write) is stood in for deterministically by one psql transaction, `inducer.sql`, which locks the highest-sorting end-user row, waits until the flush blocks on it, then updates the lowest-sorting row to complete the lock cycle: ```sql BEGIN; SELECT user_id, spend FROM "LiteLLM_EndUserTable" WHERE user_id = 'zzz-mat2-user' FOR UPDATE; DO $$ DECLARE n int; i int := 0; BEGIN LOOP SELECT count(*) INTO n FROM pg_locks l JOIN pg_stat_activity a ON a.pid = l.pid WHERE NOT l.granted AND a.pid <> pg_backend_pid() AND a.datname = current_database(); EXIT WHEN n > 0 OR i > 2400; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.05); i := i + 1; END LOOP; END $$; UPDATE "LiteLLM_EndUserTable" SET blocked = blocked WHERE user_id = 'aaa-mat2-user'; COMMIT; ``` ### Before (a613773fca) 1. Seed two end users with real completions: `for u in aaa-mat2-user zzz-mat2-user; do curl -s http://localhost:53817/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"model\":\"claude-haiku-4-5\",\"user\":\"$u\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Reply with exactly: ok\"}],\"max_tokens\":10}"; done` -> both 200, and after the flush `SELECT user_id, spend FROM "LiteLLM_EndUserTable"` shows `3.2e-05` each 2. Start the opposing transaction: `psql -d litellm_mat2_repro -f inducer.sql` 3. Send the same two curls again plus one Claude Code prompt through the gateway; all return 200 4. Proxy log shows the flush job failing: `prisma.errors.DataError: ... PostgresError { code: "40P01", message: "deadlock detected" ... }` with a full traceback through the update-spend job, and no retry 5. `SELECT user_id, spend FROM "LiteLLM_EndUserTable"` still shows `3.2e-05` for both users two flush cycles later (expected `6.4e-05`): the increments are permanently dropped; `SELECT deadlocks FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname='litellm_mat2_repro'` incremented to 1 ### After (708ff0b910) 1. Same seed state; spends carried over from earlier cycles 2. Start the same `psql -d litellm_mat2_repro -f inducer.sql` 3. Send the same two curls plus one Claude Code prompt; all return 200 4. Proxy log now shows `LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING ... Retrying spend update after retryable DB error (attempt 1/3): ... deadlock detected` and no failure traceback (`grep -c "raised an exception"` -> 0) 5. `SELECT user_id, spend FROM "LiteLLM_EndUserTable"` shows both users up by exactly one increment (`1.28e-04` -> `1.60e-04`) and the Claude Code end-user row grew by its request's cost (`4.302231` -> `5.634576`); `pg_stat_database.deadlocks` incremented `4 -> 5` (the deadlock really happened) yet nothing was dropped ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `PrismaDBExceptionHandler.is_deadlock_error` recognizes a Postgres deadlock surfaced through prisma, matching transaction-conflict code `P2034` first and falling back to `40P01` / "deadlock detected" in the message for raw statements. prisma-client-py has no dedicated deadlock class, so this is the only reliable signal. `DBSpendUpdateWriter._handle_spend_update_failure` centralizes the retry decision: it retries when the error is in `DB_RETRY_SAFE_ERROR_TYPES` or is a deadlock, logs a warning naming the attempt, sleeps a randomized jitter backoff, and otherwise (or once `n_retry_times` is spent) re-raises through the existing `_raise_failed_update_spend_exception` contract. All the inline loops in `_commit_spend_updates_to_db` (user, key, team, team_member, org, and the shared `_update_entity_spend_in_db` used by tag/agent) call it, and `ProxyUpdateSpend.update_end_user_spend`, the path GH #27989 actually reported (the `LiteLLM_EndUserTable` batch upsert), now delegates its failure handling to the same helper instead of retrying only `httpx.ConnectError` and dropping everything else. The daily-spend upsert path (`_update_daily_spend`) gets the same classification inline while preserving its outer cleanup that pops processed keys on a fatal error, so a non-retryable failure still behaves exactly as before. Retrying a deadlock is safe despite the increment being non-idempotent because Postgres aborts and fully rolls back the victim transaction; nothing is partially committed, so replaying starts from clean state. This is the key difference from the ambiguous post-send errors (for example ReadTimeout) deliberately excluded from `DB_RETRY_SAFE_ERROR_TYPES`, which could double-apply. Tests cover the classifier on both P2034 and the 40P01 / "deadlock detected" text plus non-deadlock exclusions, the retry-then-commit, retry-exhaustion, and non-retryable paths on both the writer loops and the end-user flush, and a parametrized case that drives a deadlock through every entity path (user, key, team, team_member, org, tag, agent) so no spend surface is left unretried. ## Caveats (if any) - Sorted flushes can still deadlock against scan-order writers (budget reset cascade); they now recover by retry - A permanent prisma error whose message happens to contain "deadlock detected" would be retried 3 times (~14s worst case) before raising exactly as today; failure semantics are preserved, only delayed - An extreme multi-entity deadlock storm could stack jittered sleeps toward the 60s pod-lock TTL; observed holds under a real deadlock were 2-4s, and the overlap consequence is the same one the existing 60s transaction timeout already carries ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] 708ff0b910 passes /live-pr-risk
signal.author: RayJueWang

signal.title: fix(helm): default litellm-helm to the ghcr.io/berriai/litellm image
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Chart default image is the legacy `litellm-database` repository - That image no longer differs from `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm` - Chart README, release notes and cosign docs all say `litellm` How it solves it: - Point `image.repository` at `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm` - Update the chart's tests and README to match - Bump chart version to 1.1.2 ## User Flow Before: a platform engineer installing the chart gets an image the project's own release notes never mention, so they cannot verify what they are running 1. They run `helm install litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm` with a Postgres endpoint and no `image.repository` override 2. The proxy pod and the migrations Job both come up on `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:v1.85.1` 3. They open the chart's own README, which documents the `image.repository` default as `berriai/litellm`, and it disagrees with what is running 4. They follow the release notes to verify the image signature, and the published `cosign verify` command names `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm`, which is not the image they pulled After: the same install runs the image the docs describe, so verification and the README line up 1. They run the same `helm install` with no `image.repository` override 2. The proxy pod and the migrations Job both come up on `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.85.1` 3. The chart README's documented default now matches what is running 4. The `cosign verify` command from the release notes names the image they pulled 5. Anyone who had pinned `image.repository` to `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database` keeps working, since that repository is still published ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5814 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Why the two images are interchangeable `Dockerfile` and `docker/Dockerfile.database` differ only in comment text and one builder-stage `apk` package: ``` $ diff Dockerfile docker/Dockerfile.database 31d30 < # Builder stage 45d43 < rust \ 98d95 < # Runtime stage 127,130c124,129 < # runtime uid can read and that no cache volume mount shadows. The paths are < # pinned via PRISMA_BINARY_CACHE_DIR / PRISMA_CLI_PATH and recorded into the < # generated client at build time, so `prisma migrate deploy` on a fresh < # database needs no npm and no network access (#33650, #24554). --- > # runtime uid can read and that no cache volume mount shadows (unlike > # /app/.cache or $HOME/.cache in readOnlyRootFilesystem + emptyDir setups). > # The paths are pinned via PRISMA_BINARY_CACHE_DIR / PRISMA_CLI_PATH and > # recorded into the generated client at build time, so `prisma migrate > # deploy` on a fresh database needs no npm and no network access > # (#33650, #24554). ``` `rust` is a builder-stage compile dependency and does not reach the runtime layer. Both images bake the prisma CLI and engines, `schema.prisma`, and `litellm/proxy/prisma_migration.py`, which is the file the migrations Job executes. Reading both manifests and config blobs straight off GHCR at `v1.97.0`, `linux/amd64`, they agree on entrypoint, working dir, prisma configuration and layer count, and the first 11 layer digests are byte-identical: ``` ===== litellm:v1.97.0 ===== Entrypoint: ['docker/prod_entrypoint.sh'] Cmd: ['--port', '4000'] WorkingDir: /app PRISMA env: ['PRISMA_BINARY_CACHE_DIR=/opt/prisma/binaries', 'PRISMA_CLI_PATH=/opt/prisma/binaries/node_modules/.bin/prisma', 'PRISMA_CLI_QUERY_ENGINE_TYPE=binary', 'PRISMA_OFFLINE_MODE=true'] layers: 21 ===== litellm-database:v1.97.0 ===== Entrypoint: ['docker/prod_entrypoint.sh'] Cmd: ['--port', '4000'] WorkingDir: /app PRISMA env: ['PRISMA_BINARY_CACHE_DIR=/opt/prisma/binaries', 'PRISMA_CLI_PATH=/opt/prisma/binaries/node_modules/.bin/prisma', 'PRISMA_CLI_QUERY_ENGINE_TYPE=binary', 'PRISMA_OFFLINE_MODE=true'] layers: 21 ``` Three other things already point at the plain image. The chart README documents the `image.repository` default as `berriai/litellm`, so `values.yaml` contradicted the table published beside it. `.github/workflows/create-release.yml` publishes `cosign verify` instructions for `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm` only. And the Grype image scan builds `Dockerfile` and `docker/Dockerfile.non_root`, while `docker/Dockerfile.database` is built only by CircleCI's `build_docker_database_image` for the bad-`DATABASE_URL` test, and `grep -c grype .circleci/config.yml` returns 0. ## Review notes Greptile filed two P2s on `78fe47a34f`'s predecessor. One taken, one rebutted **Taken, "avoid maintenance-sensitive image commentary" on `values.yaml`.** The second half of my comment asserted that `litellm-database` "is still published", which is a claim about an external registry's state that rots the day that stops being true, and the bot is right that it does not belong in a values file. Trimmed to one line covering only why this image can run the migrations Job, which is the non-obvious bit a future maintainer needs and cannot drift. Not deleted outright, because comments in `values.yaml` are this file's documentation convention and render into the chart's values table **Rebutted, "keep product docs centralized" on `README.md`.** `helm/litellm-helm/README.md` is chart metadata rather than product documentation: it ships inside the chart package, is rendered by Artifact Hub from the packaged chart, and has always lived beside `Chart.yaml`. Nothing was added here; one existing table cell that already disagreed with `values.yaml` was corrected, and it would still be wrong after this change if left alone. The real product-docs drift this PR creates is in the `litellm-docs` repo, where the monolithic `values.yaml` sample pinned the legacy repository, and that is fixed in BerriAI/litellm-docs#946 ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, a real kind cluster with the chart's own bundled Postgres, one namespace per side, both installed from the same values file: ```bash kind create cluster --name lit5814 kind get kubeconfig --name lit5814 > "$SC/kubeconfig"; export KUBECONFIG="$SC/kubeconfig" # the Before side is the chart exactly as it ships on the base branch git archive origin/litellm_internal_staging helm/litellm-helm | tar -x -C "$SC/basechart" cat > "$SC/vals.yaml" <<'EOF' db: deployStandalone: true migrationJob: enabled: true masterkey: sk-lit5814 proxy_config: model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6 litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.6 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: os.environ/PROXY_MASTER_KEY EOF ``` ### Before (133e72c8fd) #### The chart renders and runs the legacy image 1. Confirm the Before tree genuinely lacks the fix ``` $ grep -n "repository:" $SC/basechart/helm/litellm-helm/values.yaml | head -1 10: repository: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database $ grep -c "repository: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm$" $SC/basechart/helm/litellm-helm/values.yaml 0 ``` 2. Render the chart at its defaults ``` $ helm template lit $SC/basechart/helm/litellm-helm --set migrationJob.enabled=true | grep -n berriai 231: image: "ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:v1.85.1" 540: image: "ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:v1.85.1" ``` 3. Install it on the cluster and read back what is running ``` $ helm install lit $SC/basechart/helm/litellm-helm -n before -f $SC/vals.yaml \ --set environmentSecrets[0]=openai-key --wait --timeout 15m $ kubectl -n before get job,deploy -o custom-columns='KIND:.kind,NAME:.metadata.name,IMAGE:.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image,SUCCEEDED:.status.succeeded,READY:.status.readyReplicas' --no-headers Job lit-litellm-migrations ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:v1.85.1 1 <none> Deployment lit-litellm ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:v1.85.1 <none> 1 ``` #### Both images migrate a fresh Postgres identically 1. Run the exact command the migrations Job runs, once per image, each against its own empty Postgres ``` $ docker run --rm --network container:lit5814-pg-database \ -e DATABASE_URL="postgresql://postgres:pw@127.0.0.1:5432/litellm" -e DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=false \ -w /app --entrypoint python ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:v1.85.1 litellm/proxy/prisma_migration.py ... 2026-08-19 18:07:35,960 - litellm_proxy_extras - INFO - Migration diff applied successfully 2026-08-19 18:07:35,960 - litellm_proxy_extras - INFO - Post-migration sanity check completed LiteLLM: Setup complete. Skipping server startup as requested. --- exit: 0 --- --- tables created --- 65 $ docker run --rm --network container:lit5814-pg-plain \ -e DATABASE_URL="postgresql://postgres:pw@127.0.0.1:5432/litellm" -e DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=false \ -w /app --entrypoint python ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.85.1 litellm/proxy/prisma_migration.py ... 2026-08-19 18:08:22,304 - litellm_proxy_extras - INFO - Migration diff applied successfully 2026-08-19 18:08:22,304 - litellm_proxy_extras - INFO - Post-migration sanity check completed LiteLLM: Setup complete. Skipping server startup as requested. --- exit: 0 --- --- tables created --- 65 ``` 2. Compare the two resulting schemas ``` $ diff /tmp/lit5814-database.tables /tmp/lit5814-plain.tables && echo "IDENTICAL TABLE SET" IDENTICAL TABLE SET ``` ### After (78fe47a34f) #### The chart renders and runs the canonical image 1. Render the chart at its defaults ``` $ helm template lit helm/litellm-helm --set migrationJob.enabled=true | grep -n berriai 231: image: "ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.85.1" 540: image: "ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.85.1" ``` The full rendered diff against Before is those two lines, the chart version label, and the per-render random master key and Postgres password. Nothing else moves 2. Install it on the cluster and read back what is running ``` $ helm install lit helm/litellm-helm -n after -f $SC/vals.yaml \ --set environmentSecrets[0]=openai-key --wait --timeout 15m $ kubectl -n after get job,deploy -o custom-columns='KIND:.kind,NAME:.metadata.name,IMAGE:.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image,SUCCEEDED:.status.succeeded,READY:.status.readyReplicas' --no-headers Job lit-litellm-migrations ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.85.1 1 <none> Deployment lit-litellm ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.85.1 <none> 1 ``` 3. Serve a real request through it, against the chart's bundled Postgres ``` $ kubectl -n after get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=litellm -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.containers[0].image}' ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.85.1 $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:45814/health/readiness {"status":"healthy","db":"connected"} $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:45814/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5814" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: helm default image works"}]}' {"id":"chatcmpl-EEfEFgL6RSeoMzDQautTGT4NZwbBR","created":1787163783,"model":"gpt-5.6","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"helm default image works","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":7,"prompt_tokens":14,"total_tokens":21}} ``` 4. Confirm the spend row landed in the Postgres the migrations Job set up ``` $ kubectl -n after exec lit-postgresql-0 -- psql -U postgres -d litellm \ -c 'select model, spend, total_tokens, api_base from "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" order by "startTime" desc limit 3;' model | spend | total_tokens | api_base ----------------+---------+--------------+---------------------------- openai/gpt-5.6 | 0.00028 | 21 | https://api.openai.com/v1/ (1 row) ``` #### The chart's own tests 1. Run what the `Helm unit test` workflow runs, with the plugin version CI pins (v0.8.2, checksum-verified) and its declared-vs-executed suite guard ``` $ helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm-helm Charts: 1 passed, 1 total Test Suites: 14 passed, 14 total Tests: 97 passed, 97 total helm/litellm-helm: all 14 declared test suites ran $ helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm Charts: 1 passed, 1 total Test Suites: 8 passed, 8 total Tests: 79 passed, 79 total helm/litellm: all 8 declared test suites ran ``` 2. Mutation check, restore the old default and require the updated assertion to fail ``` $ python3 -c '...' # revert values.yaml to ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database MUTATED values.yaml back to litellm-database $ helm unittest -f 'tests/deployment_tests.yaml' helm/litellm-helm Path: spec.template.spec.containers[0].image Expected to equal: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:test Actual: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:test Test Suites: 1 failed, 0 passed, 1 total Tests: 1 failed, 19 passed, 20 total ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats - `docker/Dockerfile.database` and its published image stay - Installs pinning `image.repository` explicitly are unaffected - `ci_cd/security_scans_readme.md` claims a Grype scan on `Dockerfile.database`; stale, left alone ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(search): add Amazon Bedrock AgentCore web search provider
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - No AWS-native web search provider in LiteLLM - Bedrock users need a third-party search key today - Web Search on Bedrock AgentCore speaks MCP, unsupported How it solves it: - Adds `agentcore` search provider calling an AgentCore Gateway - SigV4 for AWS_IAM gateways, bearer token for CUSTOM_JWT - Works for `/search` and for `websearch_interception` ## User Flow Before: a developer on AWS wants Claude Code on Bedrock to search the web, but pointing the proxy at their AgentCore Gateway does nothing and every working option needs a non-AWS search key 1. They add a search tool with `search_provider: agentcore` pointing at their AgentCore Gateway MCP endpoint and start the proxy; boot succeeds with no warning 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/search with `{"query": "latest AI developments", "search_tool_name": "agentcore-search", "max_results": 5}` and get HTTP 500 `'agentcore' is not a valid SearchProviders` 3. GET https://litellm-domain/search_tools/ui/available_providers lists 18 providers, every one a third-party service (Tavily, Exa, Perplexity, Brave, ...), and `agentcore` is absent 4. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with a `web_search` tool and their Bedrock model; HTTP 200 comes back, but the web search result block is empty and the assistant apologizes about a search provider configuration error 5. In Claude Code pointed at the proxy, WebSearch errors on screen both times it runs, returning no links or content After: the same developer points the proxy at their AgentCore Gateway and search works, with the search traffic staying inside AWS 1. They create an AgentCore Gateway with a `web-search` connector target and set `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL` to its MCP endpoint 2. They add the same search tool entry with `search_provider: agentcore` (see `litellm/proxy/example_config_yaml/agentcore_websearch_config.yaml`) and no third-party key, then start the proxy 3. The same POST https://litellm-domain/search returns HTTP 200 with 5 real results carrying `title`, `url`, `snippet`, `date` 4. GET https://litellm-domain/search_tools/ui/available_providers now includes `agentcore` ("Web Search on Amazon Bedrock") 5. The same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages returns a filled web search result block (10 results) and an answer built from them; the search leg is a SigV4-signed call to their own gateway, billed by AWS 6. In Claude Code, Web Search returns real results and the answer cites them 7. Pointing `api_base` at a host that is not their gateway, or at a plain `http://` URL, returns an error instead of sending the server's `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_TOKEN` or a SigV4 signature, and a caller-supplied `tool_name` that is not a `___WebSearch` connector tool is rejected ## Relevant issues Fixes #31819 Supersedes #34098, which this builds on Docs live in the docs repo and are already merged: BerriAI/litellm-docs#834, plus BerriAI/litellm-docs#949 for the MCP protocol version env var Follow-up filed while QA'ing this PR: #37538 (the search router silently drops provider-specific yaml `litellm_params` for every search provider; pre-existing, untouched here) ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5375 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both runs hit a real AgentCore Gateway (`litellm-qa-agentcore-tez4ymmxfc`, us-east-1, `web-search` connector target, provisioned for this QA and deleted after) and real Bedrock Claude, no mocks or stubs anywhere. Shared setup, identical for both sides except the commit the proxy was booted from: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-sonnet litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 aws_region_name: us-east-1 search_tools: - search_tool_name: agentcore-search litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: https://litellm-qa-agentcore-tez4ymmxfc.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp - search_tool_name: agentcore-untrusted litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: https://untrusted-host.example.com/mcp - search_tool_name: agentcore-badtool litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: https://litellm-qa-agentcore-tez4ymmxfc.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp tool_name: my-target___ListFiles - search_tool_name: agentcore-plaintext litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: http://gw.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp litellm_settings: callbacks: ["websearch_interception"] websearch_interception_params: enabled_providers: ["bedrock"] search_tool_name: agentcore-search ``` Env for both proxies: `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL` (the real gateway), SigV4 credentials, `AWS_REGION=us-east-1`, and `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` for the Bedrock model call. Before proxy booted from the merge base on port 46526, After proxy from the PR tip on port 26793. Claude Code runs are the real TUI (v2.1.236) driven interactively under tmux with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointed at the proxy ### Before (2059033352de) #### POST /search through the configured agentcore search tool 1. `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:46526/search -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-before-7731' -d '{"query": "latest AI developments", "search_tool_name": "agentcore-search", "max_results": 5}'` 2. ```json {"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: 'agentcore' is not a valid SearchProviders
Traceback (most recent call last):
 File ".../litellm/search/main.py", line 244, in search
 provider=SearchProviders(search_provider),
...ValueError: 'agentcore' is not a valid SearchProviders
. Received Model Group=agentcore-search
Available Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}} ``` HTTP 500. The proxy had booted cleanly with all four agentcore search tools configured, so the failure only surfaces at request time #### Provider discovery 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:46526/search_tools/ui/available_providers -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-before-7731'` 2. 18 providers returned (`perplexity, tavily, parallel_ai, exa_ai, brave, google_pse, dataforseo, firecrawl, fastcrw, searxng, linkup, duckduckgo, searchapi, serper, you_com, apiserpent, tinyfish, nimble`), `agentcore` absent #### /v1/messages with the Anthropic web_search tool on real Bedrock Claude 1. `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:46526/v1/messages -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-before-7731' -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":1024,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Use the web_search tool to look up the latest LiteLLM release, then list the result titles you got."}],"tools":[{"type":"web_search_20250305","name":"web_search","max_uses":2}]}'` 2. HTTP 200, but the `web_search_tool_result` block came back empty (`"content":[]`) and the assistant text was: `The web search tool encountered an error on my end (a configuration issue with the search provider — "'agentcore' is not a valid SearchProviders") and was unable to return any results.` 3. Proxy log: `WebSearchInterception: Search failed for 'latest LiteLLM release': litellm.APIConnectionError: 'agentcore' is not a valid SearchProviders` #### Interactive Claude Code under tmux 1. Asked Claude Code (real TUI under tmux, proxy as `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) to look up the latest LiteLLM release with web search; its WebFetch fallback was denied so the search path stayed the thing under test 2. It ran WebSearch twice, both erroring. On-screen output: ``` ⏺ That search attempt returned an internal error rather than real results ... ⏺ The search tool itself is erroring out (backend misconfiguration, not fixable from my end). ⏺ Here's what happened: I ran WebSearch twice ... Both times, the tool returned no actual search results — instead it came back with an error saying an invalid search provider ("agentcore") was configured on the backend. No links or content were retrieved either time. ``` #### Credential and tool-name guards 1. Not reachable at this commit: every agentcore search tool already fails with the provider error above, so no credentialed request to a gateway can be produced at all ### After (70a4f9a7) The PR tip 7744b9100e differs from 70a4f9a7 only by a comment edit in the example config (nothing loads that file at runtime or in tests), so this run stands for the tip #### POST /search through the configured agentcore search tool 1. `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/search -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-after-9917' -d '{"query": "latest AI developments", "search_tool_name": "agentcore-search", "max_results": 5}'` 2. HTTP 200 with 5 real live-web results, e.g.: ```json {"title": "AI News & Artificial Intelligence", "url": "https://techcrunch.com/category/artificial-intelligence/", "date": "08:44AM, Wednesday, August 19 2026, PDT"} {"title": "The trends that will shape AI and tech in 2026", "url": "https://www.ibm.com/think/news/ai-tech-trends-predictions-2026", "date": "02:42PM, Friday, July 24 2026, PDT"} ``` (others: openai.com announcement, aiweekly.co, a forbes.com article dated the day of the run) #### Provider discovery 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:26793/search_tools/ui/available_providers -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-after-9917'` 2. Now includes `{"provider_name": "agentcore", "ui_friendly_name": "Web Search on Amazon Bedrock"}` #### /v1/messages with the Anthropic web_search tool on real Bedrock Claude 1. `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/v1/messages -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-after-9917' -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet","max_tokens":1024,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Use the web_search tool to look up the latest LiteLLM release, then list the result titles you got."}],"tools":[{"type":"web_search_20250305","name":"web_search","max_uses":2}]}'` 2. HTTP 200 with content blocks `['server_tool_use', 'web_search_tool_result', 'text']`: `{"name": "web_search", "input": {"query": "latest LiteLLM release"}}`, then 10 real results (`docs.litellm.ai/release_notes/...`, `github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases`, ...), then a real answer listing the titles; `stop_reason: end_turn`, usage 10770 in / 581 out 3. Proxy log shows the search leaving as a SigV4-signed `tools/call` of `web-search-tool___WebSearch` to the gateway #### Interactive Claude Code under tmux 1. Same TUI flow as Before: typed the prompt, approved the Web Search permission prompt on screen 2. On-screen output, real results this time: ``` ⏺ Web Search("LiteLLM latest stable release version 2026") ⎿ Did 1 search in 30s ⏺ Fetch(https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases) ⎿ Received 757.4KB (200 OK) ⏺ The latest stable LiteLLM release is v1.97.0 (released Aug 16, 2026), per GitHub's "Latest" tag ... ``` 3. Proxy log attributes that exact query to a `tools/call` against the real gateway; no other search backend existed in the environment #### Credential and tool-name guards 1. Untrusted host: `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/v1/search/agentcore-untrusted ...` returned HTTP 500 with no request sent: `Refusing to send SigV4-signed AgentCore requests to 'https://untrusted-host.example.com/mcp': it is neither an AgentCore gateway hostname nor the host in AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL. Set AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL to authorize a custom gateway hostname.` 2. Plaintext transport: `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/v1/search/agentcore-plaintext ...` returned HTTP 500 with no request sent: `Refusing to send AgentCore credentials over plaintext HTTP to 'http://gw.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp': a bearer token or SigV4 signature would be readable in transit. Use an https gateway URL (plain http is allowed only for localhost).` 3. Tool-name guard, exercised via env var: with `AGENTCORE_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME=my-target___ListFiles` exported, `/v1/search/agentcore-search` refused with `Invalid AgentCore search tool_name 'my-target___ListFiles': must end with '___WebSearch' (a web-search connector tool). Other gateway tools cannot be invoked through this provider.` 4. The `agentcore-badtool` yaml entry did NOT trigger that guard: it returned HTTP 200 because the search router forwards only `search_provider`/`api_key`/`api_base` from yaml `litellm_params` and dropped the `tool_name`, so the request went out with the default tool name. That plumbing predates this PR and hits every search provider; filed as #37538, and the example config here no longer advertises yaml knobs the router drops. The guard itself stays load-bearing for the reachable paths: request-body `tool_name`, the env var, and SDK calls Observations from the runs, for the reviewer: - Provider-only /search body 500s; pre-existing validation; PR leaves alone - Interception search failure still answers HTTP 200; pre-existing; PR leaves alone - Unknown search_provider passes proxy boot silently; pre-existing; PR leaves alone - Router drops extra yaml litellm_params (#37538); pre-existing; PR leaves alone - Guard refusals surface as HTTP 500 with tracebacks; pre-existing error shape; PR leaves alone - Gateway result dates occasionally nonsense ("April 12 2000"); upstream data; PR leaves alone ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Admin UI search-tool form has no `api_base` field, so UI setup needs `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL` - Cost map entry is $0 per query, AWS bills the gateway directly - `tool_name` and aws credential overrides work per request or via env vars, not yaml (#37538) ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR ## Changes `AgentCoreSearchConfig` (`litellm/llms/bedrock/search/transformation.py`) is a `BaseSearchConfig` that speaks MCP instead of a bespoke REST API: `transform_search_request` builds a JSON-RPC `tools/call` body, and `transform_search_response` accepts both a plain JSON reply and the Streamable HTTP SSE framing, picking the event that carries `result` or `error` so a progress notification can't shadow the response. ```python {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "web-search-tool___WebSearch", "arguments": {"query": query[:200], "maxResults": max_results}}} ``` Results are parsed from the tool result's text blocks first, falling back to `result.structuredContent` (the web-search connector 1.1.0+ can return machine-readable results there while the text blocks carry prose). Requests go out with `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-03-26`, the version a gateway with a default `protocolConfiguration` accepts, overridable via `AGENTCORE_MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION` for gateways pinning `supportedVersions`. Signing needed a new optional hook, because a SigV4 signature covers the exact bytes on the wire: ```python class BaseSearchConfig: def sign_request(self, headers, optional_params, request_data, api_base, api_key=None) -> tuple[dict, bytes | None]: return headers, None # default no-op ``` `BaseLLMHTTPHandler.search` / `async_search` call it and, when a signed body comes back, send it verbatim as `data=` rather than re-serializing it through `json=`. Three things the gateway makes easy to get wrong, all covered by tests: a caller-supplied `tool_name` must end in `___WebSearch`, so this provider can't be used to invoke unrelated tools on the same gateway with the proxy's credentials; server-managed credentials, both `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_TOKEN` and a SigV4 signature, only go to a trusted host (a real `*.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.<region>.amazonaws.com` hostname or the host in `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL`, which is how a custom or private gateway hostname gets authorized); and credentials only ride https, with plain http refused unless the host is localhost, so neither token nor signature is readable in transit. A `tools/call` that fails in-band, HTTP 200 with `result.isError`, raises instead of looking like a search with no results. The signing region comes from the gateway hostname, falling back to the AWS config chain and erroring out rather than guessing a region the gateway would reject. `api_key=""` is passed down to `BaseAWSLLM._sign_request` so the Bedrock Runtime `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` never leaks to an AgentCore endpoint. Also adds `agentcore/search` to the cost map (AWS bills the gateway directly) and an example proxy config wiring it into `websearch_interception` for Bedrock Claude Code. Search `pre_call` logs the headers as they were before signing, so a configured `logger_fn` never sees the SigV4 or bearer `Authorization` value; only the outbound request carries it Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/902d85f7efbc4becb45d3340ad7c6782 Requested by: @yassin-berriai - [x] 7744b9100ef68f43ab87ca8eb5b1b8d8b117ddc3 passes /live-pr-risk

signal.title: [Feature]: Add Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search as a native search provider (search_tools / websearch_interception backend)
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature ### The Feature Add `bedrock_agentcore` (web search connector) as a first-class LiteLLM **search provider**, so it can be used: - directly via `litellm.search()` / the `/search` endpoint, and - as a backend for the v1.81 **websearch_interception** feature (native `web_search` tool on Bedrock/Azure/Vertex Claude Code & Cowork). Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search is a fully managed, MCP-compatible web search connector (GA June 2026). It returns snippets, source URLs, titles, and publication dates — exactly the shape LiteLLM's `SearchResponse` expects. Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-target-connector-web-search-tool.html ### Motivation, pitch ### Motivation / Pitch Today every LiteLLM search provider (Perplexity, Tavily, Exa, Google PSE, SearXNG, …) is a third-party HTTP API requiring an external API key, and for AWS-hosted users it means search traffic and keys leave AWS. For teams running LiteLLM in front of **Bedrock**, AgentCore Web Search is the natural AWS-native option: - No third-party key — auth is AWS SigV4 via the AgentCore Gateway (IAM). - Search traffic stays within AWS / the account's trust boundary. - Completes the "web search across all providers" story: Claude Code / Claude Desktop (Cowork) on Bedrock could get the native `web_search` interception UX **without** onboarding an external search vendor. There is currently no way to do this via config, because search providers are gated by the hardcoded `SearchProviders` enum + `ProviderConfigManager`. This needs a small core addition. ### Current state (what already exists in the repo) - `litellm/search/main.py` — `search()` / `asearch()` dispatch. - `litellm/llms/base_llm/search/transformation.py` — `BaseSearchConfig` + `SearchResponse{results:[{title,url,snippet,date}]}`. - Example HTTP provider: `litellm/llms/tavily/search/transformation.py`. - Registration points: `SearchProviders` enum (`litellm/types/utils.py`) and `ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_search_config` (`litellm/utils.py`). - Interception hook: `litellm/integrations/websearch_interception/handler.py` (already calls `litellm.asearch()` with the configured provider — no change needed if the new provider registers cleanly). - Existing SigV4/MCP machinery to reuse: the AgentCore-hosted MCP SigV4 auth path (`docs/mcp_aws_sigv4`) and Bedrock's SigV4 signer. Note: the existing `bedrock/agentcore/<ARN>` provider is **agent runtimes (InvokeAgentRuntime) / A2A only** — unrelated to the web search connector. ### Proposed implementation The wrinkle vs. other providers: AgentCore Web Search is reached over **MCP (tools/call)** with **SigV4**, not a single plain HTTP POST. Two viable approaches: **Option A — self-contained provider (preferred).** New `litellm/llms/bedrock_agentcore/search/transformation.py` implementing `BaseSearchConfig`, that: - signs a SigV4 request (reuse the existing Bedrock signer + AWS credential chain), - performs the MCP `tools/call` for `WebSearch` against the configured AgentCore Gateway URL, - maps the connector result → `SearchResponse`. Register in `SearchProviders` + `ProviderConfigManager`; add cost-map + `provider_endpoints_support` metadata so it appears in the Search Tools UI. **Option B — bridge to the existing MCP server manager.** Special-case dispatch in `search/main.py` to invoke the WebSearch tool through LiteLLM's MCP client (which already does AgentCore SigV4), then map to `SearchResponse`. Less new protocol code, but more coupling in the core search path. Proposed config UX: search_tools: - search_tool_name: agentcore-search litellm_params: search_provider: bedrock_agentcore gateway_url: https://<gateway-id>.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.<region>.amazonaws.com/mcp aws_region_name: us-east-1 # credentials via standard chain / aws_role_name, mirroring the bedrock provider litellm_settings: callbacks: ["websearch_interception"] websearch_interception_params: enabled_providers: [bedrock] search_tool_name: agentcore-search ### Are you willing to contribute a PR? Yes — I'd like to author the PR (Option A) and would appreciate a maintainer sanity-check on the preferred approach (A vs B) and the SigV4/MCP helpers to reuse. ### Related - #14011 (web_search tool support, Responses API) - #30822 (websearch_interception tool_choice on Bedrock) - #25191 (interception agentic loop not triggered for Bedrock via /chat/completions) ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(proxy): randomize deadlock retry backoff in spend tracking
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #27989 Replace fixed exponential backoff (`2**i`) with randomized backoff (`random.uniform(2**i, 2**(i+1))`) in `update_end_user_spend` and `update_spend_logs` to prevent correlated retries from re-deadlocking. ### Problem When two transactions deadlock on the `LiteLLM_EndUserTable`, they are cancelled at the same time. With fixed backoff, both retry after the same delay, causing them to collide again. This pattern repeats until the retry limit is exceeded, resulting in `500 Internal Server Error`. ### Solution Use `random.uniform(2**i, 2**(i+1))` instead of `2**i`, which spreads retry times so concurrent transactions are less likely to collide. This matches the existing pattern in `db_spend_update_writer.py` (lines 1373-1379). ### Changes - `litellm/proxy/utils.py`: Add `import random`, replace fixed backoff at two sites (`update_end_user_spend` and `update_spend_logs`) - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/test_randomized_backoff.py`: Add tests verifying backoff values fall within randomized ranges and are not fixed ## Test plan - [x] Existing `test_update_spend_logs_exponential_backoff` still passes (range assertions already accommodate randomized values) - [x] New `test_update_spend_logs_backoff_is_randomized` verifies sleep times fall within `[2**i, 2**(i+1)]` ranges - [x] New `test_update_spend_logs_backoff_not_fixed` runs 10 trials and confirms sleep values vary (not identical)

signal.title: feat(proxy): auto-suppress the no-Redis banner for confirmed single-worker deployments
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Single-worker proxies still get the "No Redis configured" banner - Hiding it today needs an env var plus a full restart How it solves it: - Each worker upserts a heartbeat row into the database every 60s - Readiness counts live workers and hides the banner at exactly 1 - Two or more live workers, or an unknown count, still warn - Multi-pod and multi-worker are caught by the same census - LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING override behaves exactly as before ## User Flow Before: an admin running a single-worker proxy with no Redis sees a warning banner they can only hide with an env var and a restart 1. The admin starts the proxy with one worker, a Postgres database, and no Redis configured 2. They open http://localhost:4000/ui and the dashboard's call to GET http://localhost:4000/health/readiness/details comes back with `"show_no_redis_warning": true` 3. A red banner reads "No Redis configured. Redis is highly recommended" even though a single worker has nothing to share over Redis 4. The only way to hide it is to set `LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING=true` and restart the whole deployment After: the same single-worker deployment shows no banner at all, and the banner still comes back on its own the moment a second worker appears 1. The admin starts the proxy with one worker, a Postgres database, and no Redis configured 2. They open http://localhost:4000/ui and GET http://localhost:4000/health/readiness/details now returns `"show_no_redis_warning": false`, so no banner renders 3. They later scale to two workers, or a second pod sharing the same database, and within a couple of minutes a refresh shows the banner again, since limits and budgets now really are split across workers 4. They scale back down to one worker and the banner disappears again, with no env var and no restart ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All legs ran against a live proxy (`litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py`) on a fresh Postgres DB with no Redis, master key `sk-qa-1234`, and this config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY ``` The check in every leg is: ```bash curl -s localhost:$PORT/health/readiness/details -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-1234" ``` ### Before (b8d5139701) #### One worker, no Redis 1. Start the proxy with one worker and no Redis, then run the readiness check 2. `{"status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "show_no_redis_warning": true}`: the banner flag is stuck on with nothing to coordinate #### Two workers sharing one database, then scaling back to one 1. Boot a second replica process on another port against the same DATABASE_URL and check both 2. Replica A: `"show_no_redis_warning": true`, replica B: `"show_no_redis_warning": true` 3. Stop replica B with SIGTERM and check replica A again 4. Still `"show_no_redis_warning": true`: the flag never reflects the real worker count #### Two workers with LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING=true 1. Start one process with `--num_workers 2` and the env var set, then check 2. `{"status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "show_no_redis_warning": false}`: the env var is the only off switch ### After (31090d122e) #### One worker, no Redis 1. Start the proxy with one worker and no Redis, then run the readiness check 2. `{"status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "show_no_redis_warning": false}`: the flag turns off by itself, and the heartbeat table holds exactly 1 row 3. A real completion through that same proxy proves it still serves traffic (real OpenAI call, real $): `curl -s localhost:42731/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say OK"}]}'` returns "OK!" from `gpt-4o-mini` #### Two workers sharing one database, then scaling back to one 1. Boot a second replica process on another port against the same DATABASE_URL and check both 2. Replica A: `"show_no_redis_warning": true`, replica B: `"show_no_redis_warning": true`, and the heartbeat table holds 2 rows 3. The same holds for in-process workers: one process started with `--num_workers 2` also reports `"show_no_redis_warning": true` with 2 heartbeat rows 4. Stop replica B with SIGTERM and check replica A again 5. `"show_no_redis_warning": false` immediately, thanks to shutdown deregistration, and exactly 1 heartbeat row remains #### Two workers with LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING=true 1. Start one process with `--num_workers 2` and the env var set, then check 2. `{"status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "show_no_redis_warning": false}`: the existing escape hatch still wins UI verification steps (screenshots to be attached): 1. Start the proxy with one worker, a Postgres DATABASE_URL, no Redis, then run `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard` 2. Open http://localhost:3000/ui and confirm no red Redis banner appears anywhere on the dashboard 3. Restart the proxy with `--num_workers 2`, wait a minute, refresh, and confirm the banner appears with the new "more than one worker" wording 4. Set `LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING=true`, restart, refresh, and confirm the banner is gone again ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Suppression requires a connected database; DB-less proxies keep warning - A non-graceful scale-down converges within the 3-minute liveness window - Counting is fail-safe: any census error keeps the banner on - During a mixed-version rolling deploy, pre-heartbeat pods are invisible to the census until the rollout completes - Pods pointing at different databases each count only themselves ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] 31090d122e passes /live-pr-risk

signal.title: [Bug]: PostgresError "deadlock detected" at INSERT INTO EndUserTable ON CONFLICT SET spend...
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Approximately once a day, we get a slack alert due to a "deadlock detected" in postgres. The server logs say that both processes are trying to execute: ``` INSERT INTO "public"."LiteLLM_EndUserTable" ("user_id","spend","blocked") VALUES ($1,$2,$3) ON CONFLICT ("user_id") DO UPDATE SET "spend" = ("public"."LiteLLM_EndUserTable"."spend" + $4) WHERE ("public"."LiteLLM_EndUserTable"."user_id" = $5 AND 1=1) RETURNING "public"."LiteLLM_EndUserTable"."user_id", ... ``` Analysis by sonnet, abridged: In `_commit_spend_updates_to_db` — each table update runs in its own separate transaction: * End-user table (line 1170): db.tx() → upsert per end user — this is the deadlock source Three specific problems with update_end_user_spend vs the others: 1. upsert instead of update_many — the SQL is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, which takes heavier locks than a plain update. 2. No ordering — `end_user_list_transactions.items()` is iterated in arbitrary dict order. Different pods processing different orderings of the same end-user IDs will deadlock. The org table retry loop already has a comment about this and uses random.uniform; this one doesn't. 3. Fixed backoff — asyncio.sleep(2**i) (line 4907) vs random.uniform(2**i, 2**(i+1)) used by the org updates. Two pods that deadlock at the same time will sleep the exact same duration and deadlock again on retry. The _update_daily_spend function (db_spend_update_writer.py:1583) already has the fix pattern: it sorts by all indexed fields before processing, and uses random.uniform for backoff. The update_end_user_spend in utils.py predates that and never got the same treatment. ### Steps to Reproduce * 4 workers per pod, 4 pods, k8s, aurora * every job gets a new virtual key * most requests from claude code ### Relevant log output ```shell Message: DB read/write call failed: Error occurred during query execution: ConnectorError(ConnectorError { user_facing_error: None, kind: QueryError(PostgresError { code: "40P01", message: "deadlock detected", severity: "ERROR", detail: Some("Process 38532 waits for ShareLock on transaction 44389676; blocked by process 38611.\nProcess 38611 waits for ShareLock on transaction 44389672; blocked by process 38532."), column: None, hint: Some("See server log for query details.") }), transient: false }) [Non-Blocking]LiteLLM Prisma Client Exception - update spend logs: Error occurred during query execution ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? 1.84.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
