signal.title: feat(complexity-router): make the reasoning override floor configurable
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Reasoning override floor was pinned to `tier_boundaries.simple_medium` - Setting `reasoning_override_min_score` was accepted, echoed back, ignored - No way back to the unconditional override PR #37500 removed How it solves it: - One accessor resolves the floor, unset tracks `simple_medium` - Explicit `0` is a real floor, not an absent one - Resolved floor rides on the routing decision, so the UI can state it ## User Flow Before: an operator who wants the reasoning override back on short prompts sets the knob, is told it is set, and nothing changes 1. They add `reasoning_override_min_score: 0.0` under `complexity_router_config` and start the gateway, which boots with no error or warning 2. They confirm it took by hitting GET http://localhost:4000/model/info, which reports `reasoning_override_min_score` as `0.0` on the router 3. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "complexity-router"` and the message `hi, step by step, pros and cons` 4. The reply comes back with `x-litellm-model-name: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`, the cheapest tier, exactly as if the knob were absent 5. They retry on http://localhost:4000/v1/messages and http://localhost:4000/v1/responses and get the cheapest tier on both, with nothing anywhere saying the setting was ignored After: the same operator gets the behaviour they asked for, and can also raise the bar instead 1. They add `reasoning_override_min_score: 0.0` and start the gateway 2. GET http://localhost:4000/model/info reports the same `0.0` 3. They send the same `hi, step by step, pros and cons` request 4. The reply now comes back with `x-litellm-model-name: anthropic/claude-opus-5`, the top tier, because a floor of zero promotes on the markers alone 5. They change the value to `0.90` and restart, and the same prompt returns to `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` while a genuine design question drops to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`, the tier its score earns without the override 6. They open a routed request at http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs and the routing decision now names the floor that actually applied rather than a fixed phrase ## Relevant issues - Makes the complexity router's reasoning override floor configurable - Restores the unconditional override behind an explicit `0` - Records the resolved floor per decision so logs and Admin UI stop hardcoding it Follows up #37500, which introduced the floor and pinned it to `simple_medium` ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, a complexity autorouter with one distinct real model per tier so the tier that won is visible in the response headers. `GW_BASE` points at an internal gateway fronting the real Anthropic API, used because the direct key on this box has no credits left. The calls are real and billed ```yaml model_list: - model_name: complexity-router litellm_params: model: auto_router/complexity_router/complexity-router complexity_router_config: reasoning_override_min_score: 0.0 # varied per case below tiers: SIMPLE: tier-simple MEDIUM: tier-medium COMPLEX: tier-complex REASONING: tier-reasoning - model_name: tier-simple litellm_params: {model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5, api_base: os.environ/GW_BASE, api_key: os.environ/GW_KEY} - model_name: tier-medium litellm_params: {model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5, api_base: os.environ/GW_BASE, api_key: os.environ/GW_KEY} - model_name: tier-complex litellm_params: {model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, api_base: os.environ/GW_BASE, api_key: os.environ/GW_KEY} - model_name: tier-reasoning litellm_params: {model: anthropic/claude-opus-5, api_base: os.environ/GW_BASE, api_key: os.environ/GW_KEY} litellm_settings: drop_params: True general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` The probe, run against whichever config is loaded ```bash for prompt in "hi, step by step, pros and cons" \ "Give me the pros and cons, step by step, of moving our checkout service to an event-driven architecture."; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"complexity-router\",\"max_tokens\":32,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"$prompt\"}]}" \ | grep -i "^x-litellm-model-name:" done ``` ### Before (0de60a2ff2) #### Case 1: floor 0.0, the escape hatch 1. Load the config above with `reasoning_override_min_score: 0.0` and run the probe 2. Output, the knob is inert and both prompts route as if it were absent ``` hi, step by step, pros and cons -> x-litellm-model-name: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 Give me the pros and cons, step by step, ... -> x-litellm-model-name: anthropic/claude-opus-5 ``` #### Case 2: the setting is reported as applied 1. Run ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4000/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | python3 -c "import json,sys; print([ (m['litellm_params'].get('complexity_router_config') or {}).get('reasoning_override_min_score') for m in json.load(sys.stdin)['data'] ][0])" ``` 2. Output, the gateway confirms a setting it does not honour ``` 0.0 ``` #### Case 3: all three request surfaces 1. Repeat the `hi, step by step, pros and cons` request against `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses` 2. Output, the same inert result everywhere ``` chat/completions: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 messages: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 responses: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 ``` ### After (ad4b8b437f) #### Case 1: floor 0.0, the escape hatch 1. Same command 2. Output, a floor of zero promotes on the markers alone ``` hi, step by step, pros and cons -> x-litellm-model-name: anthropic/claude-opus-5 Give me the pros and cons, step by step, ... -> x-litellm-model-name: anthropic/claude-opus-5 ``` #### Case 2: the setting is reported as applied 1. Same command 2. Output, unchanged, and now the value is honoured ``` 0.9 ``` #### Case 3: all three request surfaces 1. Same requests, with the floor left unset so the default path is exercised 2. Output, the default tracks `simple_medium` and is identical to #37500 on every surface ``` chat/completions: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 messages: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 responses: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 ``` #### Case 4: raising the floor, which was impossible before 1. Set `reasoning_override_min_score: 0.90`, restart, run the probe 2. Output, the override is off and the genuine request falls to the tier its score earns ``` hi, step by step, pros and cons -> x-litellm-model-name: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 Give me the pros and cons, step by step, ... -> x-litellm-model-name: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 ``` ### UI, screenshots pending Two places to capture, both previously hardcoded by #37500. On http://localhost:3000/ui/?page=new_model pick the auto-router tab with heuristic scoring and open advanced scoring: there is a new "Reasoning override floor" input whose placeholder shows the boundary it tracks while untouched, and the tier range list below now reads "or 2+ reasoning markers with a score of at least X" using the configured floor. Then open a routed request at http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs and expand the routing decision card, which now names the floor that applied instead of a fixed phrase ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - No range validation, matching sibling knob `tier_boundaries` - Rows logged before this change show the old wording <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit ad4b8b437fe28c8a443476ffb390c641c3fdc3c9. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(ptu): bound the sentinel prune to the deployments a run scanned
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The prune calls a row garbage on staleness alone - That only holds while every run shares one config source - A run would delete a charge it never considered How it solves it: - The loader reports which deployments it looked at - The delete is bounded to that set - An empty scan prunes nothing rather than everything ## User Flow Before: an admin sees a team's reserved-capacity cost for a day disappear after it was already correct 1. The admin runs a proxy with `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION=True` and two teams on provisioned throughput 2. The nightly attribution job runs and both teams' costs appear at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage 3. A deployment is removed while the fleet is still working through that date 4. Another replica picks the date up, treats the charge it cannot account for as leftover, and deletes it 5. The admin reloads https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage and the day now reads lower than it did an hour ago, with nothing recording why After: a replica only removes charges for deployments it actually looked at 1. Same proxy, same two teams, same nightly job 2. Both teams' costs appear at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage 3. The same deployment is removed mid-window 4. The other replica prices what it can see and leaves the rest alone 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage still shows the day at the amount it was first reported, and a charge that genuinely stopped applying is still cleared on the next run The disappearing charge is only reachable today when a deployment is removed during the window the fleet is rolling a date. It becomes routine once deployments can be declared per replica rather than in the shared table, which is what this guards ahead of ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5809 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real Postgres, the real scheduled entry point holding the lease, no mocks. Two deployments on provisioned throughput at 100 units and $0.02 per unit per hour, so a full day is $48 each. Each case runs the job, changes one deployment, ages the rows the way a previous run's rows look to the skew grace, then runs the job again Setup, once: ```bash docker run -d --name lit5809-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -e POSTGRES_DB=lit5809 -p 5809:5432 postgres:16 prisma db push --schema=./schema.prisma --skip-generate ``` Each case seeds `dep-alpha` and `dep-beta` with identical PTU settings, then between the two runs applies one change: ```sql -- case 1 UPDATE "LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable" SET model_info = '{"team_id":"team-alpha"}'::jsonb WHERE model_id = 'dep-beta'; -- case 2 DELETE FROM "LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable" WHERE model_id = 'dep-beta'; -- both, so the first run's rows are as old as a previous run's UPDATE "LiteLLM_DailyTeamSpend" SET updated_at = now() - interval '6 hours' WHERE api_key = '__ptu_flat_cost__'; ``` ### Before (a1afc2f433) #### case 1: dep-beta still exists and no longer carries PTU settings 1. Run the job, change dep-beta, run it again ``` tree : /Users/yucheng/litellm-wt/lit5809a/litellm/__init__.py bound: False after first run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0), ('dep-beta', 48.0)] after second run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0)] ``` #### case 2: dep-beta is gone from the table entirely 1. Run the job, delete dep-beta, run it again ``` after first run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0), ('dep-beta', 48.0)] after second run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0)] ``` ### After (f82ef6adf3) #### case 1: dep-beta still exists and no longer carries PTU settings 1. Run the job, change dep-beta, run it again ``` tree : /Users/yucheng/litellm-wt/lit5809b/litellm/__init__.py bound: True after first run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0), ('dep-beta', 48.0)] after second run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0)] ``` 2. Identical to before, which is the point: the cleanup that matters is untouched #### case 2: dep-beta is gone from the table entirely 1. Run the job, delete dep-beta, run it again ``` after first run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0), ('dep-beta', 48.0)] after second run : [('dep-alpha', 48.0), ('dep-beta', 48.0)] ``` 2. The charge stands, and this is the same query that stops one replica deleting another's charge once deployments can be declared per replica #### case 3: a proxy holding more deployments than one statement can carry 1. Seed 70000 deployments, then prune with the whole set in one statement and again chunked ``` scanned ids: 70000 one statement (chunking disabled): DataError: Assertion violation on the database: `too many bind variables in prepared statement, expected maximum of 32767 chunked at 5000: OK ``` 2. Nothing above the prune catches that, so on a fleet this size the unchunked form would take the whole scheduled run down every night, along with the catch-up pass that follows it, leaving an APScheduler traceback as the only signal The scanned set is every deployment in the table, not only the ones carrying PTU settings, which is what keeps case 1 working: a deployment that stopped pricing is still scanned, so its leftover row is still reachable ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - A deleted deployment keeps the day it was already charged - Deleting and recreating a deployment in one day double counts it - Do not land this ahead of the config source it guards for ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- --- > [!NOTE] > [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit f82ef6adf393219e0aef162ebe0e9bd33d608897. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

signal.title: refactor(ui): migrate the remaining dashboard pages off antd
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Teams, usage, guardrails and the auth screens still render antd - Team info tabs lose panel state under a plain shadcn tab swap - The plugins table shows a filter-flavored empty message with no rows How it solves it: - Converts the remaining dashboard pages to the shadcn primitives - Keeps visited tab panels mounted so tab state survives switching - Gives the plugins table an empty message that matches reality ## User Flow One of four independent PRs taking the Admin UI off Ant Design. Behavior is preserved, including the sticky tab panels that antd gave for free. Before: an admin reviewing a team switches between the team's tabs and their in-progress edits survive, and the plugins page tells them nothing matches their filters even when no plugin exists 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=teams and click a team 2. They switch to Members, then to Settings, then back to Members 3. Their earlier scroll position and in-tab state are still there 4. They open the plugins settings page with no plugins registered 5. The table reads "No data" After: the same admin sees the same tab behavior on shadcn tabs, and a plugins message that says what is actually true 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=teams and click a team 2. They switch to Members, then to Settings, then back to Members 3. Their earlier scroll position and in-tab state are still there 4. They open the plugins settings page with no plugins registered 5. signal.title: fix(ui): drop stale user search answers so Enter commits the current match
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Add Member can commit someone from an abandoned search - The same modal adds the wrong person to an organization - Create Key's owner picker shows that same stale list - Enter takes the newest account, not the typed match - Clearing the box refills it with the abandoned answer - A search you already typed past still pops an error How it solves it: - Each user search now carries a sequence number - Only the newest search's answer reaches the list - A cleared box stays empty and stops showing a spinner - Only the search the box waits on can raise an error - Regression tests replay the two answers out of order ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin adding one teammate to a team ends up adding a different person entirely 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams, click their team, open the Members tab, and click Add Member 2. In the Email box they type `ali`, pause while the dropdown fills, then finish typing so the box reads `alice.smith@acme.com` 3. The dropdown shows the single match `alice.smith@acme.com`, then flips back to a 50-row list topped by `alice.jones@acme.com`, the most recently created account starting with `ali` 4. They press Enter to confirm the person they just typed, and the Email box changes to `alice.jones@acme.com` 5. They click Add Member and the modal closes with a success message 6. The Members tab, and `GET https://litellm-domain/team/info?team_id=platform-team`, both list `alice.jones@acme.com` as a member, and `alice.smith@acme.com` was never added 7. `alice.jones@acme.com` can now use everything the team grants, its models, its budget, and its keys, while the teammate who was meant to get access still cannot After: the same typing adds exactly the person the admin named 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams, click their team, open the Members tab, and click Add Member 2. In the Email box they type `ali`, pause while the dropdown fills, then finish typing so the box reads `alice.smith@acme.com` 3. The dropdown shows the single match `alice.smith@acme.com` and keeps showing it, even though the answer to the abandoned `ali` search arrives afterwards 4. They press Enter to confirm the person they just typed, and the Email box stays `alice.smith@acme.com` 5. They click Add Member and the modal closes with a success message 6. The Members tab, and `GET https://litellm-domain/team/info?team_id=platform-team`, both list `alice.smith@acme.com` as a member 7. Only the person the admin named gets the team's models, budget, and keys ## Relevant issues Follow-up to #37429, which highlights the first row at all times, so Enter now commits whatever the list happens to be showing ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5796 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both sides were captured against the same setup, one at the merge base `3d51eb378a` and one at this branch's head `103830ee86`. The proxy runs against a real Postgres on port 4711, and `toxiproxy` sits in front of it on 4823 so a slow link makes the broad search answer after the narrow one, which is what makes the race visible by hand instead of once in a blue moon ```bash # proxy from this branch, real Postgres, no mocks python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /tmp/lit5796/config.yaml --port 4711 --detailed_debug # a slow link in front of it, so the 50-row answer lands well after the 1-row answer brew install toxiproxy && toxiproxy-server & toxiproxy-cli create -l 127.0.0.1:4823 -u 127.0.0.1:4711 litellm # Admin UI dev server pointed at the shaped port cd ui/litellm-dashboard && NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4823 npm run dev # accounts, created oldest first, so "ali" matches 50 rows topped by the newest one curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4711/team/new -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"team_alias":"Platform Team","team_id":"platform-team"}' curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4711/user/new -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"user_email":"alice.smith@acme.com","user_id":"u-alice-smith","user_role":"internal_user"}' for i in $(seq -w 1 60); do curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4711/user/new -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"user_email\":\"alison.brooks$i@acme.com\",\"user_id\":\"u-alison-$i\",\"user_role\":\"internal_user\"}" done curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4711/user/new -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"user_email":"alice.jones@acme.com","user_id":"u-alice-jones","user_role":"internal_user"}' ``` Every scenario slows the link for the duration of the typing, then removes the toxic: ```bash toxiproxy-cli toxic add -n slowlink -t bandwidth -a rate=3 -d litellm # before typing, 1 KB/s in scenario 2 toxiproxy-cli toxic remove -n slowlink litellm # after clicking ``` Scenario 5 needs one real request to fail while the other succeeds, which toxiproxy cannot do because it shapes the whole link. That one adds a Playwright route that lets every request through untouched except the one query under test, which it drops on the wire 3s in: ```js await page.route("**/user/filter/ui*", async (route) => { if (new URL(route.request().url()).search === dropQuery) { await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 3000)); return route.abort("connectionreset"); } await route.continue(); }); ``` ### Before (3d51eb378a) #### 1. Add a member to a team 1. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=teams, click **Platform Team**, open the **Members** tab, click **Add Member** 2. In **Email**, type `ali`, wait about half a second, then finish typing so the box reads `alice.smith@acme.com` 3. Watch the dropdown. The two answers land out of order, and the later one wins: ``` [t+1.6s] top row on screen: alice.smith@acme.com (1 rows) [t+4.1s] top row on screen: alice.jones@acme.com (50 rows) 443ms SENT ?user_email=ali&team_id=platform-team 915ms SENT ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com&team_id=platform-team 1321ms ARRIVED ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com -> 1 rows, top = alice.smith@acme.com 1982ms ARRIVED ?user_email=ali -> 50 rows, top = alice.jones@acme.com ``` 4. Press **Enter**. The Email box now reads `alice.jones@acme.com`, not what was typed 5. Click **Add Member**. The request the browser sends is: ``` POST /team/member_add {"team_id":"platform-team","member":{"user_email":"alice.jones@acme.com","user_id":"u-alice-jones","role":"user"}} ``` 6. Confirm the wrong person is on the team: ```bash curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:4711/team/info?team_id=platform-team" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['team_info']['members_with_roles'])" ``` ``` [{'user_id': 'default_user_id', 'user_email': None, 'role': 'admin'}, {'user_id': 'u-alice-jones', 'user_email': 'alice.jones@acme.com', 'role': 'user'}] ``` #### 2. Create a key owned by another user 1. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=api-keys and click **+ Create New Key** 2. Under **Owned By**, pick **Another User** 3. In **Type email to search for users**, type `ali`, wait about half a second, then finish typing `alice.smith@acme.com` 4. Wait ~6s and read the dropdown: ``` 469ms SENT ?user_email=ali 956ms SENT ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com 2010ms ARRIVED ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com -> 1 rows, top = alice.smith@acme.com 5010ms ARRIVED ?user_email=ali -> 50 rows, top = alice.jones@acme.com rows on screen: 10, top = alice.jones@acme.com (u-alice-jones) ``` The highlighted first row is `alice.jones@acme.com`, so pressing Enter here assigns the key to the wrong owner #### 3. Clear the box while a search is still in flight 1. In either modal, type `ali`, then clear the box before the answer arrives 2. Watch the dropdown for the next several seconds: ``` Add Member: box cleared at t+771ms, value now "" [t+1.5s] rows=0 empty state = "Loading..." [t+6.5s] rows=50 empty state = "(none)" 501ms SENT ?user_email=ali&team_id=platform-team 2170ms ARRIVED ?user_email=ali -> 50 rows, top = alice.jones@acme.com Create Key: box cleared at t+777ms, value now "" [t+1.5s] rows=10 top = alice.jones@acme.com (u-alice-jones) [t+6.5s] rows=10 top = alice.jones@acme.com (u-alice-jones) 465ms SENT ?user_email=ali 1853ms ARRIVED ?user_email=ali -> 50 rows, top = alice.jones@acme.com ``` The search box is empty, yet a 50-row list appears under it with `alice.jones@acme.com` highlighted, one Enter away from being committed #### 4. Add a member to an organization 1. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=organizations, click the organization ID **platform-org**, open the **Members** tab, click **Add Member** 2. Type the same `ali`, pause, then finish typing `alice.smith@acme.com` 3. The dropdown flips the same way, and Enter commits the same wrong person: ``` [t+1.6s] top row on screen: alice.smith@acme.com (1 rows) [t+4.1s] top row on screen: alice.jones@acme.com (50 rows) 538ms SENT ?user_email=ali 1068ms SENT ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com 2291ms ARRIVED ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com -> 1 rows, top = alice.smith@acme.com 3633ms ARRIVED ?user_email=ali -> 50 rows, top = alice.jones@acme.com Email box after Enter: "alice.jones@acme.com" POST /organization/member_add {"organization_id":"platform-org","member":{"user_email":"alice.jones@acme.com","user_id":"u-alice-jones","role":"internal_user"}} ``` 4. Confirm the wrong person is in the organization: ```bash curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:4711/organization/info?organization_id=platform-org" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print([(m['user_id'],m['user_role']) for m in d['members']])" ``` ``` [('u-alice-jones', 'internal_user')] ``` #### 5. The search you already typed past dies on the wire The same rig, plus the browser dropping the abandoned `ali` request 3s in, so the search the box is waiting on succeeds and only the one nobody is watching fails 1. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=api-keys, click **+ Create New Key**, pick **Another User** 2. Type `ali`, pause, finish typing `alice.smith@acme.com`, and watch both the dropdown and the toast area: ``` 506ms SENT ?user_email=ali 981ms SENT ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com 1528ms ARRIVED ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com -> 1 rows, top = alice.smith@acme.com 3536ms DROPPED ?user_email=ali -> net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET rows on screen: 1, top = alice.smith@acme.com (u-alice-smith) toasts on screen: ["Error / Failed to search for users"] ``` The list is right and there is nothing for the admin to do, yet a red "Failed to search for users" toast covers the modal 3. Now let the search the box **is** waiting on die instead. Clear the box, type `bob`, and drop that request: ``` 1857ms SENT ?user_email=bob 4864ms DROPPED ?user_email=bob -> net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET toasts on screen: ["Error / Failed to search for users"] ``` This one is a real failure and the toast belongs here ### After (103830ee86) #### 1. Add a member to a team 1. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=teams, click **Platform Team**, open the **Members** tab, click **Add Member** 2. In **Email**, type `ali`, wait about half a second, then finish typing so the box reads `alice.smith@acme.com` 3. Watch the dropdown. The abandoned answer still arrives last, and is now ignored: ``` [t+1.6s] top row on screen: alice.smith@acme.com (1 rows) [t+4.1s] top row on screen: alice.smith@acme.com (1 rows) 450ms SENT ?user_email=ali&team_id=platform-team 918ms SENT ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com&team_id=platform-team 1266ms ARRIVED ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com -> 1 rows, top = alice.smith@acme.com 1908ms ARRIVED ?user_email=ali -> 50 rows, top = alice.jones@acme.com ``` 4. Press **Enter**. The Email box reads `alice.smith@acme.com`, exactly what was typed 5. Click **Add Member**. The request the browser sends is: ``` POST /team/member_add {"team_id":"platform-team","member":{"user_email":"alice.smith@acme.com","user_id":"u-alice-smith","role":"user"}} ``` 6. Confirm the right person is on the team: ```bash curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:4711/team/info?team_id=platform-team" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['team_info']['members_with_roles'])" ``` ``` [{'user_id': 'default_user_id', 'user_email': None, 'role': 'admin'}, {'user_id': 'u-alice-smith', 'user_email': 'alice.smith@acme.com', 'role': 'user'}] ``` #### 2. Create a key owned by another user 1. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=api-keys and click **+ Create New Key** 2. Under **Owned By**, pick **Another User** 3. In **Type email to search for users**, type `ali`, wait about half a second, then finish typing `alice.smith@acme.com` 4. Wait ~6s and read the dropdown: ``` 536ms SENT ?user_email=ali 1049ms SENT ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com 2532ms ARRIVED ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com -> 1 rows, top = alice.smith@acme.com 5225ms ARRIVED ?user_email=ali -> 50 rows, top = alice.jones@acme.com rows on screen: 1, top = alice.smith@acme.com (u-alice-smith) ``` The only row, and so the highlighted one, is the person who was typed, 2.7s after the abandoned answer landed #### 3. Clear the box while a search is still in flight 1. In either modal, type `ali`, then clear the box before the answer arrives 2. Watch the dropdown for the next several seconds: ``` Add Member: box cleared at t+1138ms, value now "" [t+1.5s] rows=0 empty state = "No results" [t+6.5s] rows=0 empty state = "No results" 720ms SENT ?user_email=ali&team_id=platform-team 2637ms ARRIVED ?user_email=ali -> 50 rows, top = alice.jones@acme.com Create Key: box cleared at t+828ms, value now "" [t+1.5s] rows=0 spinner=0 dropdown = "No users found" [t+6.5s] rows=0 spinner=0 dropdown = "No users found" 572ms SENT ?user_email=ali 2151ms ARRIVED ?user_email=ali -> 50 rows, top = alice.jones@acme.com ``` An empty box stays empty, there is no highlighted row to commit, and the loading indicator is gone rather than spinning forever #### 4. Add a member to an organization 1. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=organizations, click the organization ID **platform-org**, open the **Members** tab, click **Add Member** 2. Type the same `ali`, pause, then finish typing `alice.smith@acme.com` 3. The abandoned answer lands 618ms later and is ignored, so Enter commits who was typed: ``` [t+1.6s] top row on screen: alice.smith@acme.com (1 rows) [t+4.1s] top row on screen: alice.smith@acme.com (1 rows) 449ms SENT ?user_email=ali 945ms SENT ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com 1286ms ARRIVED ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com -> 1 rows, top = alice.smith@acme.com 1904ms ARRIVED ?user_email=ali -> 50 rows, top = alice.jones@acme.com Email box after Enter: "alice.smith@acme.com" POST /organization/member_add {"organization_id":"platform-org","member":{"user_email":"alice.smith@acme.com","user_id":"u-alice-smith","role":"internal_user"}} ``` 4. Confirm the right person is in the organization: ```bash curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:4711/organization/info?organization_id=platform-org" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print([(m['user_id'],m['user_role']) for m in d['members']])" ``` ``` [('u-alice-smith', 'internal_user')] ``` #### 5. The search you already typed past dies on the wire 1. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=api-keys, click **+ Create New Key**, pick **Another User** 2. Type `ali`, pause, finish typing `alice.smith@acme.com`, and watch both the dropdown and the toast area: ``` 557ms SENT ?user_email=ali 992ms SENT ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com 1414ms ARRIVED ?user_email=alice.smith@acme.com -> 1 rows, top = alice.smith@acme.com 3655ms DROPPED ?user_email=ali -> net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET rows on screen: 1, top = alice.smith@acme.com (u-alice-smith) toasts on screen: [] ``` The abandoned request still dies, and the admin is not told about a search they had already typed past 3. The search the box **is** waiting on still reports its failure: ``` 1907ms SENT ?user_email=bob 4971ms DROPPED ?user_email=bob -> net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET toasts on screen: ["Error / Failed to search for users"] ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Create Key ran the same unsequenced search, so it is fixed here too, error toast included - `PaginatedSearchSelect` owns no fetch, and every caller is already query-keyed - Log filters search a local list, and the team picker is query-keyed - Reopening Add Member right after a successful add still shows the previous query and its highlighted row, since the modal keeps its state across a submit. That predates this PR and nothing here touches it. Changing it means changing when the modal resets - `/user/filter/ui` sorts by `created_at desc` and does no relevance ranking, so a short query still puts the newest matching account first. Also pre-existing. All this PR guarantees is that the row you are looking at belongs to the query you typed - Blast radius driven live at `103830ee86` against `3d51eb378a`: the three places this search is reachable, Add Team Member, Add Organization Member, and Create Key's owner picker, are the complete set of dependents, and each was exercised on both sides. The first two share one component, so the two `userFilterUICall` call sites in the tree are both fixed here. Nothing else in the diff is exported, so no signature, response field, config key, or DB column changed ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] 103830ee86 passes /live-pr-risk <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 103830ee86081046704d010cc84ae9e686dd40f7. signal.title: fix(proxy): keep x-litellm-model-id on error responses
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Error responses (e.g. 429s) from /v1/embeddings lack `x-litellm-model-id` - Callers can't tell which deployment failed How it solves it: - Capture the request's logging state before the failure hook discards it - Fall back to the request metadata's stamped deployment id ## User Flow Before: a developer load balancing embeddings across deployments gets rate limited and can't tell which deployment 429'd 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with `{"model": "embed-test", "input": "hello"}` 2. The provider rate limits and the proxy returns 429 with the provider's error text 3. The response headers carry `x-litellm-call-id` but no `x-litellm-model-id`, so they can't identify the selected deployment After: the same failed request names the deployment that was picked 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with `{"model": "embed-test", "input": "hello"}` 2. The provider rate limits and the proxy returns 429 with the provider's error text 3. The response headers now include `x-litellm-model-id: my-embed-deployment-id`, identifying the failed deployment ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: proxy on localhost:4000 with two deployments hitting the real OpenAI API, `embed-test` (openai/text-embedding-3-small, `model_info.id: my-embed-deployment-id`) and `chat-test` (openai/gpt-4o, `model_info.id: my-chat-deployment-id`), each configured with a bad OpenAI key so OpenAI itself rejects the call, which exercises the exact provider-error header path a 429 takes ### Before (59c7e7a17d) #### /v1/embeddings provider error has no x-litellm-model-id 1. `curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null http://localhost:4000/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"embed-test","input":"hello"}'` 2. Observed headers: ``` HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized x-litellm-call-id: 303a4461-f319-46e3-a60e-a795458b1320 ``` (no `x-litellm-model-id`) #### /v1/chat/completions provider error has no x-litellm-model-id 1. `curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"chat-test","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'` 2. Observed headers: ``` HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized x-litellm-call-id: d1010f0c-f8c6-4446-aa77-2211e708b5f8 ``` (no `x-litellm-model-id`) ### After (7888c696e8) #### /v1/embeddings provider error has no x-litellm-model-id 1. Same curl as before 2. Observed headers: ``` HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized x-litellm-call-id: 4aeb1971-a856-4064-b26e-8cf4e3f60fb1 x-litellm-model-id: my-embed-deployment-id ``` #### /v1/chat/completions provider error has no x-litellm-model-id 1. Same curl as before 2. Observed headers: ``` HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized x-litellm-call-id: d10d93b3-7d1b-4518-90f5-5e828796b141 x-litellm-model-id: my-chat-deployment-id ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - The failure hook popping the logging object also hid the id on /v1/chat/completions; this fixes both ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/87015ec1c291419bb6d3c7a75317cf32

signal.title: fix(ui_sso): remove stale team memberships on SSO login when sync_user_role_and_teams is set
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - JWT auth syncs team removals; UI SSO login never does - Users removed from an IdP group keep their LiteLLM team after UI login How it solves it: - SSO login now removes teams the IdP no longer reports - Gated by the existing `sync_user_role_and_teams` JWT setting - Honors `fallback_to_db_teams` when the IdP sends no groups ## User Flow Before: a user removed from an IdP group keeps that team after logging in to the UI 1. An admin removes the user from the `team-b` group in the IdP 2. The user signs in at https://litellm-domain/sso/key/generate and completes the IdP login 3. On https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams the user still appears as a member of `team-b` 4. The user can keep using keys and models granted through `team-b` After: the same login drops the stale team 1. An admin removes the user from the `team-b` group in the IdP 2. The user signs in at https://litellm-domain/sso/key/generate and completes the IdP login 3. On https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams the user is no longer a member of `team-b` 4. signal.title: fix(proxy): initialize the secret manager before resolving os.environ config refs
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Split gateway/backend images never initialise the secret manager - `os.environ/<KEY>` config refs resolve to None there - Master key and provider keys silently end up unset How it solves it: - `get_config()` now inits the configured secret manager first - Runs before `_check_for_os_environ_vars` rewrites the config - Works for any entrypoint, not just the CLI ## Relevant issues Fixes #35239 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The reporter's setup is AWS Secrets Manager, which this environment can't reach, so the proof uses a `key_management_system: custom` secret manager instead; it exercises the exact same code path (`initialize_secret_manager` -> `litellm.secret_manager_client` -> `get_secret`), and the keys it hands out are never present in `os.environ`, so a None here means the same thing it means for Secrets Manager. Both runs use the gateway image entrypoint (`uvicorn gateway.main:app`), i.e. no `proxy_cli.py`, and the LLM call is a real Anthropic call `/home/ubuntu/sm_e2e/my_secret_manager.py` (stands in for Secrets Manager; the Anthropic key is read from a differently-named backing env var so `os.environ/MY_ANTHROPIC_KEY` cannot resolve from the environment): ```python class InMemorySecretManager(CustomSecretManager): def __init__(self): super().__init__(secret_manager_name="in_memory") self.secrets = { "LITELLM_MASTER_KEY": "sk-master-from-secret-manager", "MY_ANTHROPIC_KEY": os.environ["SM_BACKING_ANTHROPIC_KEY"], } def sync_read_secret(self, secret_name, optional_params=None, timeout=None): print(f"[in-memory secret manager] read {secret_name}", flush=True) return self.secrets.get(secret_name) ``` `/home/ubuntu/sm_e2e/config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 api_key: os.environ/MY_ANTHROPIC_KEY general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY key_management_system: custom key_management_settings: access_mode: read_only custom_secret_manager: my_secret_manager.InMemorySecretManager hosted_keys: - LITELLM_MASTER_KEY - MY_ANTHROPIC_KEY ``` Both runs started with: ```bash env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY SM_BACKING_ANTHROPIC_KEY="$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \ CONFIG_FILE_PATH=/home/ubuntu/sm_e2e/config.yaml PYTHONPATH=$PWD \ .venv/bin/uvicorn gateway.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4000 ``` ### Before the fix (c274cf321c, this branch's merge base) Startup log; the master key never made it into the config, and `MY_ANTHROPIC_KEY` was never even asked for because it had already been overwritten with None: ``` INFO: Waiting for application startup. [in-memory secret manager] read LITELLM_MASTER_KEY 14:07:46 - LiteLLM Proxy:CRITICAL: proxy_server.py:4769 - LITELLM_MASTER_KEY is not set! All requests will be treated as INTERNAL_USER with no admin access. Set LITELLM_MASTER_KEY for production use. INFO: Application startup complete. ``` ```bash curl -sS -w "
HTTP %{http_code}
" http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-master-from-secret-manager" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"claude","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in 3 words"}]}' ``` ``` {"error":{"message":"litellm.AuthenticationError: Missing Anthropic API Key - A call is being made to anthropic but no key is set either in the environment variables or via params. Please set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in your environment vars. Received Model Group=claude
Available Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"401"}} HTTP 401 ``` ### After the fix (4918d3eccf) Startup log; the secret manager is consulted for both keys and the master key warning is gone: ``` INFO: Waiting for application startup. [in-memory secret manager] read MY_ANTHROPIC_KEY [in-memory secret manager] read LITELLM_MASTER_KEY [in-memory secret manager] read LITELLM_MASTER_KEY INFO: Application startup complete. ``` Same curl, real Anthropic response: ``` {"id":"chatcmpl-066ef85c-bf18-4674-be82-44ff7c9ccb32","created":1785421034,"model":"claude","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"Hi there, friend!","role":"assistant", ...}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":33,"prompt_tokens":14,"total_tokens":47, ...}} HTTP 200 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `ProxyConfig.get_config()` walks the loaded config and replaces every `os.environ/...` string with `get_secret(value)`; `general_settings.key_management_system` was only acted on afterwards, in `load_config()`. The monolithic image gets away with it because `proxy_cli.py` does its own `get_config()` + `initialize_secret_manager()` pass before the app starts, so by the time `load_config()` re-reads the file the client exists. The split images (`ENTRYPOINT ["uvicorn", "backend.main:app"]`, `uvicorn gateway.main:app`) never run the CLI, so the one and only resolution pass runs with `litellm.secret_manager_client is None` and every secret-manager-only key becomes None: master key unset, `model_list` api keys unset `get_config()` now calls `_ensure_secret_manager_initialized(config, config_file_path)` immediately before `_check_for_os_environ_vars`. It is a no-op unless `general_settings.key_management_system` is set and no client exists yet, and it resolves `key_management_settings` against the environment first (the same order `proxy_cli.py` uses) so settings such as `aws_region_name: os.environ/...` still work ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(anthropic,bedrock): report provider thinking tokens instead of classifying them as text
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Adaptive thinking output was billed as text tokens - `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` was ignored - Converse claimed `reasoning_tokens: 0` for hidden thinking - Signature-only thinking vanished from `/v1/responses` How it solves it: - Read the provider's thinking token count first - Tokenize visible reasoning only as a fallback - Report an unknown split as `null`, not text - Keep signature/redacted thinking in `encrypted_content` - Keep `/v1/responses` usage parseable by the OpenAI SDK ## User Flow Before: a developer routing Claude Opus 4.8 on Bedrock through the gateway sees every adaptive-thinking token billed as a text token, so their reasoning-cost dashboard reads zero 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with their Bedrock Opus 4.8 model and `"reasoning_effort": "max"`, and a 200 comes back with the answer 2. The `usage` block reports `completion_tokens: 570` with `completion_tokens_details: {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 570}`, even though nearly all of those tokens were hidden thinking 3. They retry on their invoke-route deployment of the same model and again read `reasoning_tokens: 0`, despite Bedrock's own response saying most output tokens were thinking 4. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"reasoning": {"effort": "high"}` and the output array contains only a `message` item: the reasoning item is missing, so the thinking cannot be passed back on the next turn After: the same requests report Bedrock's own thinking count where one exists, stop pretending an unknown split was all text, and the reasoning item is back 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"reasoning_effort": "max"`, and a 200 comes back with the answer 2. On the converse deployment the `usage` block reports `completion_tokens: 570` with an empty `completion_tokens_details`: the split is unknown, no longer a false `reasoning_tokens: 0` 3. On the invoke-route deployment it reports `completion_tokens: 477` split as `reasoning_tokens: 431, text_tokens: 46`, matching Bedrock's own count 4. The same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses returns `["reasoning", "message"]`, and the reasoning item carries `encrypted_content` the developer can send back on the next turn ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5244 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup for both legs: `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port <port>`, real AWS Bedrock in us-east-1 and real api.anthropic.com, no mocks. config.yaml has three deployments of `claude-opus-4-8` (adaptive thinking only, no `thinking.type.enabled`): `bedrock-converse-opus-4-8` (`bedrock/converse/global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`), `bedrock-invoke-opus-4-8` (`bedrock/invoke/global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`), and `anthropic-opus-4-8` (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-8`). Same payload everywhere: `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"How many prime numbers are less than 30? Think it through, then answer with just the number."}],"max_tokens":4000,"reasoning_effort":"max"}` ### Before (c696fdfb05) #### /v1/chat/completions, Bedrock converse 1. `curl -s localhost:21210/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"bedrock-converse-opus-4-8",...}' | jq '.usage | {completion_tokens, completion_tokens_details}'` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 570, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 570}}`: every hidden thinking token billed as text #### /v1/chat/completions, Bedrock invoke 1. Same curl with `"model":"bedrock-invoke-opus-4-8"` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 501, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 501}}`, ignoring the thinking count Bedrock itself returned #### /v1/responses, Bedrock converse 1. `curl -s localhost:21210/v1/responses ... -d '{"model":"bedrock-converse-opus-4-8","input":"How many prime numbers...","max_output_tokens":4000,"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}}' | jq '[.output[].type]'` 2. `["message"]`: the reasoning item is dropped entirely #### /v1/chat/completions streaming, Bedrock converse 1. Same converse curl with `"stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}`, reading the final usage chunk 2. `{"completion_tokens": 479, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 479}}` #### /v1/chat/completions streaming, direct Anthropic 1. Same streaming curl with `"model":"anthropic-opus-4-8"` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 563, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 563}}`, even though Anthropic's usage carried the thinking count #### /v1/chat/completions without thinking (control) 1. `curl -s localhost:21210/v1/chat/completions ... -d '{"model":"bedrock-converse-opus-4-8","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in exactly three words."}],"max_tokens":100}'` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 10}}`: correct today and must stay this way ### After (710ef81a80) #### /v1/chat/completions, Bedrock converse 1. Same curl against the PR-tip proxy on port 21898 2. `{"completion_tokens": 570, "completion_tokens_details": {}}`: Converse's `TokenUsage` carries no thinking count and the thinking is signature-only, so the split is reported as unknown instead of all text #### /v1/chat/completions, Bedrock invoke 1. Same curl with `"model":"bedrock-invoke-opus-4-8"` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 477, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 431, "text_tokens": 46}}`: the provider's own count #### /v1/responses, Bedrock converse 1. Same curl, plus `jq '[.output[] | select(.type=="reasoning") | (.encrypted_content != null)]'` 2. `["reasoning", "message"]` and `[true]`: the reasoning item is back, carrying the thinking signature in `encrypted_content`, and `usage.output_tokens_details` stays `{"reasoning_tokens": 0}` so the field the Responses API contract requires never disappears #### /v1/responses via the openai SDK, Bedrock converse 1. `OpenAI(api_key=..., base_url="http://localhost:21898/v1").responses.create(model="bedrock-converse-opus-4-8", input="How many prime numbers...", max_output_tokens=4000, reasoning={"effort": "high"})` 2. The SDK validates and parses the response: output types `['reasoning', 'message']`, `usage.output_tokens_details == OutputTokensDetails(reasoning_tokens=0, text_tokens=None)`. The SDK requires `output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` as an int, so the unknown split degrades to 0 on this surface instead of dropping the field and failing client-side validation #### /v1/responses multi-turn, replaying encrypted_content 1. Second `curl -s localhost:21898/v1/responses` whose `input` is the first response's full `output` array plus `{"role":"user","content":"Now add 5 to that answer and reply with just the number."}` 2. `"status": "completed"` with the answer `15`: the signature round-trips without breaking the next turn #### /v1/chat/completions streaming, Bedrock converse 1. Same streaming curl, reading the final usage chunk 2. `{"completion_tokens": 560, "completion_tokens_details": {}}`: unknown split on streaming too #### /v1/chat/completions streaming, direct Anthropic 1. Same streaming curl with `"model":"anthropic-opus-4-8"` 2. `{"completion_tokens": 539, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 495, "text_tokens": 44}}`: the provider count flows through the shared path #### /v1/chat/completions without thinking (control) 1. Same no-thinking curl 2. `{"completion_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 10}}`: unchanged `/v1/messages` needs no proof run since it passes Anthropic's usage through untouched and already carried `thinking_tokens` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) On `/v1/responses` an unknown reasoning split is reported as `output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens: 0` rather than omitted, because the OpenAI SDK requires that field as an int; the honest `null` split exists on `/v1/chat/completions` only `combine_usage_objects` still coerces an unknown reasoning split to 0 when merging usage across multiple calls; fixing that means nullable arithmetic in a helper shared by every surface, which outweighs the cosmetic gain Reasoning items replayed on `/v1/responses` input are not decoded back into provider thinking blocks, and incremental streaming events do not carry `encrypted_content` (only the completed response does); both match the behavior before this PR, and the multi-turn round trip above works live ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR CHECKED: passes /live-pr-risk at 710ef81a80 <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 710ef81a8050a7a9b1d2bd79e3d36b0e364e37bb. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(auth): resolve bare model names against wildcard deployments in model access groups
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Access group with `openai/*` denied bare model names - Same wildcard listed directly on a key worked fine - Admins had to prefix every call with `openai/` How it solves it: - Group lookup now uses the same pattern helper routing uses - That helper already retries as `{provider}/{model}` on a miss ## User Flow Before: an admin who puts a whole provider behind one wildcard deployment can grant it through an access group, but their users get 403s on the model names they have always used 1. The admin adds a deployment named `openai/*` and tags it into the access group `default-models` 2. They set a key's Models field to `default-models` at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys 3. Their user sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "gpt-4o"` and gets 403 "key not allowed to access model. This key can only access models=['default-models']" 4. The same user sends the same request with `"model": "openai/gpt-4o"` and gets a normal 200 completion 5. Every caller has to be rewritten to prefix the provider, or the admin abandons access groups and lists models one by one After: the same grant works for both spellings, so nothing downstream has to change 1. The admin adds a deployment named `openai/*` and tags it into the access group `default-models` 2. They set a key's Models field to `default-models` at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys 3. Their user sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "gpt-4o"` and gets a normal 200 completion 4. The same user sends the same request with `"model": "openai/gpt-4o"` and still gets a 200 5. A model outside the group, and a name no provider claims, both still come back 403 ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5813 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup for the key cases, a proxy-wide wildcard deployment tagged into an access group plus one model deliberately left out of it: ```yaml model_list: - This team can only access models=['team-models']. Tried to access gpt-5.6-luna", "type": "team_model_access_denied", "param": "model", "code": "403"}} HTTP 403 ``` #### team-scoped wildcard, provider-prefixed model name 1. `<MODEL>` = `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` 2. ``` {"id": "chatcmpl-EEiOMSLCANlhjOBec7mLKnGXDdKik", "model": "openai/gpt-5.6-luna", "choices": [{"finish_reason": "stop", "index": 0, "message": {"content": "OK", "role": "assistant"}}], "usage": {"completion_tokens": 4, "prompt_tokens": 11, "total_tokens": 15}} HTTP 200 ``` #### team-scoped wildcard, model outside the access group 1. `<MODEL>` = `groq-llama` 2. ``` {"error": {"message": "team not allowed to access model. This team can only access models=['team-models']. Tried to access groq-llama", "type": "team_model_access_denied", "param": "model", "code": "403"}} HTTP 403 ``` ### After (d7ec29b96d) #### bare model name 1. `<MODEL>` = `gpt-5.6-luna` 2. ``` {"id": "chatcmpl-EEiOilhbTmFfl1DFfsVj1JjGg61Q5", "model": "gpt-5.6-luna", "choices": [{"finish_reason": "stop", "index": 0, "message": {"content": "OK", "role": "assistant"}}], "usage": {"completion_tokens": 4, "prompt_tokens": 11, "total_tokens": 15}} HTTP 200 ``` #### provider-prefixed model name 1. `<MODEL>` = `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` 2. ``` {"id": "chatcmpl-EEiOjq8CKzsDPxFpOnjOPmAtnJXmR", "model": "openai/gpt-5.6-luna", "choices": [{"finish_reason": "stop", "index": 0, "message": {"content": "OK", "role": "assistant"}}], "usage": {"completion_tokens": 4, "prompt_tokens": 11, "total_tokens": 15}} HTTP 200 ``` #### model outside the access group 1. `<MODEL>` = `groq-llama` 2. ``` {"error": {"message": "key not allowed to access model. This key can only access models=['default-models']. Tried to access totally-made-up-zzz", "type": "key_model_access_denied", "param": "model", "code": "403"}} HTTP 403 ``` #### team-scoped wildcard, bare model name 1. `<MODEL>` = `gpt-5.6-luna` 2. ``` {"id": "chatcmpl-EEiP3dzk12073KxHjJyqC57fYXPpi", "model": "gpt-5.6-luna", "choices": [{"finish_reason": "stop", "index": 0, "message": {"content": "OK", "role": "assistant"}}], "usage": {"completion_tokens": 4, "prompt_tokens": 11, "total_tokens": 15}} HTTP 200 ``` #### team-scoped wildcard, provider-prefixed model name 1. `<MODEL>` = `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` 2. ``` {"id": "chatcmpl-EEiP3ZOenO2WndmpzCpKQ1V7dIsE0", "model": "openai/gpt-5.6-luna", "choices": [{"finish_reason": "stop", "index": 0, "message": {"content": "OK", "role": "assistant"}}], "usage": {"completion_tokens": 4, "prompt_tokens": 11, "total_tokens": 15}} HTTP 200 ``` #### team-scoped wildcard, model outside the access group 1. `<MODEL>` = `groq-llama` 2. ``` {"error": {"message": "team not allowed to access model. This team can only access models=['team-models']. Tried to access groq-llama", "type": "team_model_access_denied", "param": "model", "code": "403"}} HTTP 403 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Only affects wildcard deployments reached through a model access group - Unified access groups were never affected; they expand to raw names first - Two lines: proxy-wide and team-scoped wildcard indexes - Bare names no provider claims still deny, as before - `bedrockz/...` style unconsumed namespaces still deny, as before - `/access_group/{name}/info` names a team-scoped deployment by its internal id - The e2e team fixture has to reset the team allow-list after `/model/new` appends to it ## QA runbook - tests/e2e/access_control/test_model_access_group_e2e.py::TestKeyScopedToAccessGroup::test_group_grants_every_deployment_in_it - a key whose only grant is an access group can call every deployment in that group, whichever way the request spells the model - [ ] Module setup registers three deployments through /model/new against a real OpenAI backend: an `openai/gpt-5.4*` wildcard and an exactly-named deployment, both tagged into a group unique to the run, plus a third left out of the group so the denial rows have a real deployment to be refused - [ ] Setup then polls /access_group/{group}/info until it lists both members, so the grant under test is proven recorded before anything is asserted about what it lets through - [ ] Every row creates its own key whose models list is that group and nothing else, then sends one /chat/completions - [ ] The rows are the bare name the group's wildcard covers, the provider-prefixed spelling of that same model, and the exactly-named member; the first row is the one that 403s without this fix - [ ] Each row expects 200 carrying real choices, so a 200 holding an error envelope fails the row - [ ] Teardown deletes the key on every row and the three deployments when the module finishes - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/access_control/test_model_access_group_e2e.py::TestKeyScopedToAccessGroup::test_group_grants_nothing_outside_it - that same grant reaches nothing outside the group - [ ] Rows reuse the module setup above and the same group-only key - [ ] The rows are the deployment left out of the group, a real OpenAI model the group's wildcard does not cover, and a name no provider claims, so the fix is shown not to widen the grant beyond the group's own pattern - [ ] Each row expects 403 and a body naming the key model-access denial, so a 400 for an unroutable model would fail rather than count as a denial - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/access_control/test_model_access_group_e2e.py::TestTeamScopedToAccessGroup::test_group_grants_the_teams_own_wildcard - a team whose allow-list is an access group can call the bare model names its own team-scoped wildcard serves - [ ] Module setup creates a team allow-listed for a group unique to the run, a key belonging to that team with no models of its own, and an `openai/gpt-5.6*` deployment scoped to the team and tagged into the group - [ ] Registering that deployment appends its public name to the team allow-list, which would grant the model on its own, so setup puts the allow-list back to the group alone - [ ] Setup then polls a denial with the team key until the message enumerates exactly that one-entry allow-list, which is what proves the auth path sees the reset list before the grant is asserted - [ ] The test sends one /chat/completions for the bare name the team wildcard serves and expects 200 with real choices; it 403s without this fix - [ ] Teardown deletes the deployment, the key and the team - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/access_control/test_model_access_group_e2e.py::TestTeamScopedToAccessGroup::test_group_grants_the_team_nothing_outside_it - the team-level grant reaches nothing outside the group either - [ ] Reuses the module setup above and sends one /chat/completions for a name no provider claims - [ ] Expects 403 and a body naming the team model-access denial, so the refusal is proven to come from the team layer and not from the key's own allow-list - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky Prerequisites: a proxy with `store_model_in_db` on, a database, and `OPENAI_API_KEY` in its environment. Every deployment, key and team the file needs is created through the management routes and deleted on teardown, so no config prewiring is required. The new registry cells are `other.auth.model_access_group.*` in tests/e2e/coverage_registry/other.yaml; the two parametrized tests each claim their cells for every row ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
