signal.title: feat(cli): add `lite login --config-claude` to wire Claude Code at login
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Claude Code users re-wire `~/.claude/settings.json` by hand after every login - `lite up` does it, but only while it runs, and reverts on exit - The apiKeyHelper `lite up` writes is malformed and returns nothing How it solves it: - `lite login --config-claude` writes that config persistently - Unrelated Claude Code settings preserved; plain `lite login` unchanged - Credential reached via apiKeyHelper, so re-login refreshes it - Fixes the helper's option order so it actually parses ## User Flow Before: a developer proxying Claude Code through LiteLLM has to re-point Claude Code at the proxy by hand every time their login expires 1. They run `lite --base-url https://litellm-domain login` and complete the browser sign-in 2. They open `~/.claude/settings.json` in an editor and paste the proxy URL and a token in themselves, or they keep a `lite up` process alive in a spare terminal for as long as they want Claude Code proxied 3. If they instead try `lite --base-url https://litellm-domain login --config-claude`, the CLI answers `Error: No such option: --config-claude` and exits 2 4. If they took the `lite up` route, closing that terminal restores the old settings and Claude Code goes straight back to Anthropic 5. Either way, tomorrow's login means doing it all again After: the same developer wires Claude Code up once, at login, and re-login keeps it working 1. They run `lite --base-url https://litellm-domain login --config-claude` and complete the same browser sign-in 2. The CLI prints `Login successful!` and then `Configured Claude Code: ~/.claude/settings.json now routes through https://litellm-domain.` 3. They open `~/.claude/settings.json` and see their theme, permissions and other env vars exactly as they left them, with the proxy URL added alongside 4. They run `claude` in any terminal, with no wrapper, and it answers through the proxy 5. When the login expires they run the same command again and Claude Code keeps working, with nothing to copy and no process to keep alive ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5817 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical for both sides: a live proxy on `:4817` backed by real Postgres and Redis, serving real Anthropic through `anthropic/*`, and a sandboxed `HOME` seeded with a pre-existing `~/.claude/settings.json` carrying a theme, permissions and an unrelated env var. `lite` is on `PATH` in both legs. The browser leg of the CLI SSO flow is stood in for by writing the completed session to the same Redis key `/sso/callback` writes; every other step is a real HTTP call against the running proxy. ```bash $ cat ~/.claude/settings.json { "theme": "dark", "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(git status)", "Read"], "deny": ["Bash(rm -rf *)"] }, "env": { "MY_TEAM_FLAG": "keep-me" } } ``` ### Before (133e72c8fd) #### The flag does not exist 1. Confirm the tree really lacks it, so the leg cannot pass for the wrong reason ``` $ grep -c "config-claude" litellm/proxy/client/cli/commands/auth.py 0 $ ls litellm/proxy/client/cli/commands/claude_settings.py absent ``` 2. Run the command ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 login --config-claude Usage: lite login [OPTIONS] Try 'lite login --help' for help. Error: No such option: --config-claude exit=2 ``` 3. The nearest thing that does exist offers nothing either ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 login --help Usage: lite login [OPTIONS] Login to LiteLLM proxy using SSO authentication Options: --help Show this message and exit. ``` #### The apiKeyHelper `lite up` writes is rejected by its own CLI 1. Run the exact command `lite up` puts in `~/.claude/settings.json` ``` $ lite auth print-token --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 Try 'lite auth print-token --help' for help. Error: No such option: --base-url exit=2 ``` 2. Claude Code gets an empty token from it, so the request is refused ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4817/v1/messages -H "x-api-key: " ... {"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, No api key passed in.","type":"auth_error","code":"401"}} ``` ### After (210ea7fe4d) #### Login writes the config and preserves everything else 1. Run the login ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 login --config-claude Opening browser to: http://127.0.0.1:4817/sso/key/generate?source=litellm-cli&key=cli-<login-id> Please complete the SSO authentication in your browser... Verification code: <code> Waiting for authentication... ``` 2. Complete the browser sign-in, then watch the CLI finish ``` Login successful! JWT Token: _somTPYtyB9DYmSKESqX... You can now use the CLI without specifying --api-key Configured Claude Code: ~/.claude/settings.json now routes through http://127.0.0.1:4817. Your other Claude Code settings were left untouched. Restart Claude Code to pick this up. ``` 3. Read the file back: theme, permissions and `MY_TEAM_FLAG` are untouched, the two proxy settings are added, and the mode tightened from `0644` to `0600` ``` $ cat ~/.claude/settings.json { "theme": "dark", "permissions": { "allow": [ "Bash(git status)", "Read" ], "deny": [ "Bash(rm -rf *)" ] }, "env": { "MY_TEAM_FLAG": "keep-me", "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:4817" }, "apiKeyHelper": "/.../bin/lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 auth print-token" } $ stat -f '%Sp' ~/.claude/settings.json -rw------- ``` #### The apiKeyHelper it wrote actually runs 1. Execute the helper string on its own, exactly as Claude Code does ``` $ /.../bin/lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 auth print-token _somTPYtyB9DYmSKESqXpzqd... (784 chars) ``` #### It refuses while another command owns the file 1. Simulate a running `lite autoroute up` session, which backs up to a different path than `lite up` does ``` $HOME/.litellm/autorouter/claude_settings_backup.json present $HOME/.litellm/claude_settings_backup.json absent ``` 2. Run the login and watch it refuse the settings write while still completing the login ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:4817 login --config-claude Login successful! JWT Token: tAELCbEebUGE-NDxfAIq... You can now use the CLI without specifying --api-key Error: Logged in, but could not configure Claude Code: `lite autoroute up` is currently managing ~/.claude/settings.json (backup at ~/.litellm/autorouter/claude_settings_backup.json) and will restore it when it stops. Run `lite autoroute down` first, then retry. ``` 3. Confirm the file was left alone ``` $ grep -c ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL ~/.claude/settings.json 0 $ grep -c apiKeyHelper ~/.claude/settings.json 0 ``` #### Real Claude Code reaches real Anthropic through the proxy 1. Launch Claude Code bare, with no wrapper and no env vars, so its only configuration is the file the login wrote ``` $ claude -p "Reply with exactly: LIT-5817 end to end" LIT-5817 end to end exit: 0 ``` 2. Confirm it went through the proxy rather than to Anthropic directly ``` $ grep -oE '"POST /v1/messages[^"]*" [0-9]{3}' proxy.log | sort | uniq -c 1 "POST /v1/messages HTTP/1.1" 401 <- the Before leg, with the malformed helper 5 "POST /v1/messages?beta=true HTTP/1.1" 200 ``` 3. Confirm the proxy booked real spend for it ``` $ psql -d litellm -c 'select model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, spend from "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" ...' anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 1180 | 18 | 0.00635000 anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 31116 | 12 | 0.19477250 anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 1180 | 1 | 0.00592500 anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 31116 | 12 | 0.19477250 anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 1180 | 1 | 0.00592500 anthropic/claude-opus-5 | 31116 | 12 | 0.19477250 $ psql -d litellm -c 'select count(*), sum(spend) from "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"' 7 | 0.60251750 ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix ## Review notes Greptile's P1 was real and is fixed. Its placement was better than mine: normalizing the read-side `OSError` inside `load_json_or_empty` rather than at my call site fixes `lite up` and `lite autoroute` at the same time, so I took its version. A regression test drives it by pointing the loader at a directory, and the mutation that narrows the catch back to `FileNotFoundError` fails that test. Round four was a CI red, not a review finding: the `lint` job's basedpyright gate rejected `owner: Final` bound inside the guard's loop (`A "Final" variable cannot be assigned within a loop`, `reportGeneralTypeIssues`, ceiling 0). Rather than drop the annotation, the registry now carries explicit `SettingsFileOwner(backup_path, start_command, stop_command)` records. That removes the loop-local binding, and with it a `== AUTOROUTE_BACKUP_PATH` identity check and a `.replace(' up', ' down')` string surgery that derived one command name from another. Same messages, no behaviour change, and the test for the autoroute case no longer has to patch a module constant to reach it. Round three came from a second reviewer and found the sharpest issue in the PR, which neither I nor Greptile had caught: the "another command owns this file" guard checked only `lite up`'s backup path, while `lite autoroute up` backs up to `~/.litellm/autorouter/claude_settings_backup.json`. So the exact hazard the guard existed for was still open through autoroute, which would have restored over this write with a success message. `claude_settings.py` now owns the registry of both owners and the guard iterates it, with a test that pins the registry against the path `autoroute` actually uses so the two definitions cannot drift. Two more from the same round, both specific to this write being persistent where `lite up`'s is backed up and reverted. `write_private_json` ends in `os.replace`, which swaps a symlinked `settings.json` for a regular file, silently detaching a dotfiles repo with nothing to restore from; the write now resolves a symlink and updates its target instead. And `merge_claude_settings` coerces a non-object `env` to `{}`, which is recoverable under `lite up` and permanent data loss here, so the persistent path refuses instead. That strictness is deliberately scoped to this path so `lite up` keeps its existing tolerance. Round two: Greptile then found that `UnicodeDecodeError` is a `ValueError`, not an `OSError`, so a settings file containing invalid UTF-8 still escaped the boundary the round-one fix had just built. Real, and confirmed by driving it. Rather than add a second `except`, the loader now reads bytes and hands them straight to the JSON validator, which removes the decode step altogether; a file that is not valid UTF-8 is not valid JSON, and it now reports as such. Mutating the read back to text fails the new test. Separately, while checking that round, I found a coverage gap the suite could not see: `lite up` calls `ctx.invoke(login)` on the real command object, but every `_ensure_fresh_login` test monkeypatches `up_module.login` with a fake, so no test would have noticed a login parameter `ctx.invoke` cannot supply. Adding `--config-claude` is exactly that kind of change. Two tests now drive the real command through `ctx.invoke` and assert both that it binds and that it leaves `~/.claude/settings.json` alone without the flag. Its P2 on the merge mutation is taken too; `env` is now built declaratively with no `pop`. That also removed the one LIT002 violation this PR added, so the `lint` budget gate goes from `total 26899 over limit 26886` to `OK: every LIT rule is within its codebase ceiling`. I have not taken the P2 asking for the docs to move to the `litellm-docs` repository. The section I added sits directly under the existing `lite up` section in the CLI's own README, and `lite up` is documented nowhere in `litellm-docs` (`grep -rn "lite up" litellm-docs/docs/` returns nothing), so that file is where this surface already lives rather than a customer-facing docs page I am bypassing. Happy to open a companion docs PR if the whole `lite up` / `lite autoroute` surface should be published there, but moving only the new subsection would split one section across two repositories. ## Caveats (if any) - Claude CLI only; VS Code and JetBrains are follow-ups - Shared settings handling moved out of `up.py` to break a cycle - Refuses while `lite up` or `lite autoroute up` holds the file - Forces the settings file to 0600; `lite up` leaves umask default - Proxy base URL disables Claude Code's MCP tool search by default ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(e2e): canonical content-based match keys for record-and-replay
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Replay matched verb + path in recorded order only - A changed request body silently replayed the stale recorded response - Reordering two independent calls broke replay entirely - Credential body/form fields landed in bundles verbatim How it solves it: - Canonical match keys: method, path, and a content hash - Volatile headers, credentials, markers, generated ids, and timestamps canonicalize out - A miss hard-fails naming the computed key, closest recorded key, and diff - Matching is order-independent across keys, FIFO within one key - Recording now redacts credential body and form fields on write - Replay pools build once at load; consumption is one atomic pop ## User Flow Before: an engineer replaying a recorded e2e run gets a stale response silently served for a request the suite no longer makes, and a harmless reorder of independent calls kills the replay with no hint of what was expected 1. They start a proxy on http://localhost:37526 and run the streaming chat suite with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record`; the test passes, hitting POST http://localhost:37526/model/new, GET /v1/models, POST /key/generate, POST /chat/completions (SSE), POST /key/delete, and POST /model/delete, and one JSON file per call lands in the bundle 2. They change the test's prompt and temperature, stop the proxy, blank `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and rerun with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay`: the run passes anyway, asserting against the old recording's streamed response as if the new request had been served 3. Kill the proxy; apply the same prompt + temperature mutation 3. Same replay command -> `1 failed in 15.14s` with `fixture_transport.ReplayMiss: replay miss for ...test_chat_stream_is_sse_and_ends_with_done: no recorded interaction matches key stream /chat/completions #e7ded1b5e0795c01; closest recorded key is stream /chat/completions #76ff084d9d1dd427 (0003-stream-chat-completions.json)` followed by a unified diff whose only hunks are `-"content": "Reply with the single word ok. <marker>"` / `+"content": "Reply with the single word HELLO in French. <marker>"` and `-"temperature": 0.0` / `+"temperature": 1.0`, and a re-record hint; proxy down and provider key blank, so no network call was possible #### Reordering independent calls breaks replay without naming keys 1. Restore the test; same replay command untouched -> `1 passed in 15.15s` with the proxy still down (clean replay needs no proxy and no provider key) #### Match keys across separate recordings 1. Record the same suite a second time into a separate bundle dir (`E2E_FIXTURE_DIR=<run2>`) -> `1 passed in 15.71s`, fresh OpenAI spend 2. Canonicalize every recorded request in both bundles and compare: both runs produce the same six keys (`get /v1/models #b582c5a565697d4d`, `post /key/delete #5e6c7d6ab75728c2`, `post /key/generate #1c98fef54321506b`, `post /model/delete #750972c5895baecc`, `post /model/new #d7d220d80dbafcc2`, `stream /chat/completions #76ff084d9d1dd427`) -> `IDENTICAL KEY SETS` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - signal.title: fix(batches): stop one bad output line from zeroing an entire batch's spend
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - One status-200 batch output line with an empty `body` raised inside batch costing - That error zeroed the whole batch's spend and made the cost poller re-error every cycle - A malformed or undecodable (invalid UTF-8) JSONL line in the output file had the same effect How it solves it: - Each output line is costed on its own; a line that cannot be costed is billed at $0 and warned - Malformed, undecodable, or non-object output lines are skipped with a warning instead of raising - The rest of the batch is billed normally and the poller marks the job done ## User Flow Before: a developer whose completed batch output carries one status-200 line with an empty body never sees that batch billed 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with `purpose=batch`, `target_model_names=gpt-4.1-mini`, and a two-line JSONL of chat requests; 200 back with a long scrambled file id 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with that `input_file_id`, `endpoint: /v1/chat/completions`, `completion_window: 24h`; 200 back, `status: validating`, a long scrambled batch id 3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it reads `status: completed`, `request_counts: 2/2`, `usage.total_tokens: 31` 4. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and see their two answers plus a third line whose `response.body` is `{}` 5. They check GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id}_batch_cost (or the Logs page) minutes later and still get `[]`: the batch sits at $0 spend indefinitely and the key, team, and daily spend totals never move for it After: the same batch is billed for its two healthy lines within a minute of completing 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with `purpose=batch`, `target_model_names=gpt-4.1-mini`, and a two-line JSONL of chat requests; 200 back with a long scrambled file id 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with that `input_file_id`, `endpoint: /v1/chat/completions`, `completion_window: 24h`; 200 back, `status: validating`, a long scrambled batch id 3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it reads `status: completed`, `request_counts: 2/2`, `usage.total_tokens: 31` 4. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and see their two answers plus a third line whose `response.body` is `{}` 5. Within a minute, GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id}_batch_cost returns one `aretrieve_batch` row for `gpt-4.1-mini` with 28 prompt and 3 completion tokens and `spend: 0.000008`; the empty-body line counts as $0 and the key, team, and daily spend totals move by the same amount ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5789 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, both legs: the proxy runs on port 35383 with Postgres, `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_INTERVAL=45`, master key `sk-1234`, and this deployment: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4.1-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4.1-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY api_base: http://127.0.0.1:45105 ``` Port 45105 is a tiny passthrough in front of `https://api.openai.com` that forwards every call unchanged except `GET /v1/files/{id}/content`, where it appends one extra line to the real output file: `{"custom_id": "request-poison-empty", "response": {"status_code": 200, "request_id": "inject-empty-body-1185", "body": {}}}`. That reproduces the customer's output file (one status-200 line with an empty body) on top of a real OpenAI batch. The batch is a real OpenAI batch, `batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189`, 2 chat requests on `gpt-4.1-mini`, completed 2/2: ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:35383/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -F purpose=batch -F target_model_names=gpt-4.1-mini -F file=@batch_input.jsonl {"id":"bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9vY3RldC1zdHJlYW07dW5pZmllZF9pZCwzZTljMDE0Ni0yNjJhLTQ3ZTItYjg5ZC0xNmNkNmU2ZjM2MjI7...","bytes":417,"created_at":1787129282,"filename":"modified_file.jsonl","object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"uploaded",...} $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:35383/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input_file_id": "<that file id>", "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions", "completion_window": "24h"}' {"id":"bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTttb2RlbF9pZDo1Nzg5YTExYjJjM2Q0ZTVmNjA3MTgyOTNhNGI1YzZkN2U4ZjkwYTFiMmMzZDRlNWY2MDcxODI5M2E0YjVjNmQ3O2xsbV9iYXRjaF9pZDpiYXRjaF82YTg1NmRjOWI0NWM4MTkwOTU2OGJiOTE5MGJmMTE4OQ","completion_window":"24h","created_at":1787129289,"endpoint":"/v1/chat/completions",...,"status":"validating",...} $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:35383/v1/batches/<batch id> -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" # ~3 minutes later {"status": "completed", "request_counts": {"completed": 2, "failed": 0, "total": 2}, "usage": {"total_tokens": 31, "input_tokens": 28, "output_tokens": 3, ...}, "output_file_id": "bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9qc29uO3VuaWZpZWRfaWQsODY0ODcwNjAtOWM5NS01ZmZlLTkzZDgtMDU5MGE1ZDIyNWM1O..."} $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:35383/v1/files/<output file id>/content -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"id": "batch_req_6a856e4862ac819093f9278db3ebb658", "custom_id": "req-1", "response": {"status_code": 200, ..., "body": {"id": "chatcmpl-EEWGweQMfHyv4lVQklDf116jkDUgE", "object": "chat.completion", "model": "gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14", "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hello!", ... {"id": "batch_req_6a856e486b0881909a103ac8f05144e2", "custom_id": "req-2", "response": {"status_code": 200, ..., "body": {"id": "chatcmpl-EEWHtka04uPUWZWaHOMz2mD1IUOwJ", "object": "chat.completion", "model": "gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14", "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Blue", ... {"custom_id": "request-poison-empty", "response": {"status_code": 200, "request_id": "inject-empty-body-1185", "body": {}}} ``` ### Before (ec6f1c1a56) 1. The cost poller picks the completed batch up and errors on the empty-body line, then keeps re-erroring on every 45s cycle (proxy log, three consecutive cycles): ``` 01:51:54 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: check_batch_cost.py:591 - Batch ID: batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 is complete, tracking cost and usage 01:51:55 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: check_batch_cost.py:881 - CheckBatchCost: failed to track cost for batch batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 (job 35332d3a-c1ad-4c82-954f-f4a9234f9755); leaving it unprocessed so the next poll retries: Model is None and does not exist in passed completion_response. Passed completion_response={} 01:53:08 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: check_batch_cost.py:591 - Batch ID: batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 is complete, tracking cost and usage 01:53:08 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: check_batch_cost.py:881 - CheckBatchCost: failed to track cost for batch batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 (job 35332d3a-c1ad-4c82-954f-f4a9234f9755); leaving it unprocessed so the next poll retries: Model is None and does not exist in passed completion_response. Passed completion_response={} 01:54:21 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: check_batch_cost.py:591 - Batch ID: batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 is complete, tracking cost and usage 01:54:22 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: check_batch_cost.py:881 - CheckBatchCost: failed to track cost for batch batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 (job 35332d3a-c1ad-4c82-954f-f4a9234f9755); leaving it unprocessed so the next poll retries: Model is None and does not exist in passed completion_response. Passed completion_response={} ``` 2. Three minutes after completion the only spend row tied to the batch is the $0 creation row; no cost row exists and the whole database still sums to $0: ``` $ curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:35383/spend/logs?request_id=<batch id>" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" [{"call_type": "acreate_batch", "model": "openai/gpt-4.1-mini", "spend": 0.0, "total_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens": 0, "startTime": "2026-08-19T08:48:09.332000Z"}] $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select call_type, model, spend, total_tokens from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" where request_id = '<batch id>' or metadata::text like '%batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189%';" call_type | model | spend | total_tokens ---------------+---------------------+-------+-------------- acreate_batch | openai/gpt-4.1-mini | 0 | 0 $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select count(*) as spend_rows, coalesce(sum(spend),0) as total_spend from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\";" spend_rows | total_spend ------------+------------- 18 | 0 $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select status, batch_processed from \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" where model_object_id='batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189';" status | batch_processed -----------+----------------- completed | f ``` ### After (608d749983) 1. Same DB, same batch, same passthrough still appending the empty-body line. The poller costs the batch on its first pass, warns about the one bad line, bills the rest, and later cycles do not touch it again: ``` 01:56:50 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: check_batch_cost.py:591 - Batch ID: batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189 is complete, tracking cost and usage 01:56:50 - LiteLLM:WARNING: batch_utils.py:135 - batch output line could not be costed, so it is billed at $0 and the rest of the batch is still billed. custom_id=request-poison-empty error=Model is None and does not exist in passed completion_response. Passed completion_response={}, model=None 01:56:50 - LiteLLM:DEBUG: batch_utils.py:227 - batch output aggregate: cost=8e-06 usage=Usage(completion_tokens=3, prompt_tokens=28, total_tokens=31, ...) models=['gpt-4.1-mini'] 01:58:02 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: scheduled_job_stagger.py:341 - Scheduled job check_batch_cost_job started ... (no further "failed to track cost" lines on this or any later cycle) ``` 2. The batch now has a spend row and the job is marked done: ``` $ curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:35383/spend/logs?request_id=<batch id>_batch_cost" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" [{"call_type": "aretrieve_batch", "model": "gpt-4.1-mini", "spend": 8e-06, "total_tokens": 31, "prompt_tokens": 28, "completion_tokens": 3, "startTime": "2026-08-19T08:56:50.332000Z"}] $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select status, batch_processed from \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" where model_object_id='batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189';" status | batch_processed ----------+----------------- complete | t $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select model, spend, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens from \"LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend\" where model = 'gpt-4.1-mini';" model | spend | prompt_tokens | completion_tokens --------------+-------+---------------+------------------- gpt-4.1-mini | 8e-06 | 28 | 3 ``` ### Re-run at the tip (5eeccf69b6) After merging `litellm_internal_staging` into the branch (51cafe4365), both scenarios were re-driven at the tip on fresh DBs with the same rig: the inline retrieve and the cost poller each warn on the injected lines and bill `8e-06 / 31 tokens`, the managed object reads `complete | t`, and `LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend` reads `gpt-4.1-mini | 8e-06 | 28 | 3` Cursor Bugbot then flagged that a batch output line that is not valid UTF-8 still aborted billing, since `json.loads` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` there, which `except json.JSONDecodeError` does not catch. 5eeccf69b6 catches `ValueError` instead and was A/B'd on the same rig with the passthrough also appending `{"custom_id": "request-bad-utf8", "note": "\xff"}` (a raw `0xff` byte). Before the fix the retrieve leaves no spend row and the proxy log shows the abort; at the tip the line is skipped and the batch still bills: ``` # before the fix (51cafe4365) UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 43: invalid start byte $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select request_id, spend, total_tokens from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\";" # no rows # at the tip (5eeccf69b6) 14:37:23 - LiteLLM:WARNING: batch_utils.py:430 - skipping malformed batch output line: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 43: invalid start byte $ psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "select request_id, spend, total_tokens from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\";" batch_6a856dc9b45c81909568bb9190bf1189_batch_cost | 8e-06 | 31 ``` A control retrieve at the tip with the passthrough disarmed bills the same `8e-06 / 31` with zero warnings ## Live PR risk (base vs head A/B) live-pr-risk: CHECKED at 5eeccf69b6. No breaking dependent path. One backward-incompatible contract change (intended, see below). Not verified: the Vertex `disable_vertex_batch_output_transformation` path. Changed surface: `_iter_batch_input_entries` renamed to `_iter_batch_output_entries` and it now skips malformed or non-object lines (raises change); `_get_file_content_as_dictionary` inherits that; `_iter_successful_output_line_stats` now isolates per-line costing failures (raises change); `dict` parameter annotations widened to `Mapping[str, Any]` (no runtime effect); `_parse_batch_output_line` catches `ValueError` rather than only `json.JSONDecodeError`, so an undecodable (invalid UTF-8) line is skipped like a malformed one instead of aborting the pass. Dependents reached from outside the module, ranked by reachability: (1) `GET /v1/batches/{raw_id}` and `litellm.aretrieve_batch` through `litellm_logging.async_success_handler` -> `_handle_completed_batch` (tests mock `_handle_completed_batch`, so untested live); (2) the enterprise cost poller `check_batch_cost._track_completed_batch_cost` -> `_get_file_content_as_dictionary` -> `calculate_batch_cost_and_usage` (tests mock `_get_file_content_as_dictionary`); (3) `_handle_completed_batch`'s Vertex branch -> `calculate_vertex_ai_batch_cost_and_usage(_get_file_content_as_dictionary(...))` (only the malformed-line skip reaches it; unit-tested at the helper level, not driven live). `batch_rate_limiter` uses the unchanged `_iter_batch_input_lines`, so it is not a dependent. No string dispatch, registry, config key, DB column, dashboard, SDK client, or docs reference to any changed symbol (grepped `litellm/`, `enterprise/`, `ui/`, `litellm/proxy/client/`, `~/Development/litellm-docs`). Rig: base ec6f1c1a56 (the merge base when the A/B first ran) and head on separate ports with separate fresh Postgres DBs, same config, `litellm.__file__` asserted per side. Real OpenAI upstream behind a passthrough that appends one empty-body line, one non-JSON line, and (since the 5eeccf69b6 leg) one invalid-UTF-8 line to every `GET /v1/files/*/content`. `origin/litellm_internal_staging` was later merged into the branch at 51cafe4365 (merge base now e126975468); the drift touches none of `batch_utils.py`, `check_batch_cost.py`, or `litellm_logging.py` and is annotation-only in `cost_calculator.py`, so the base legs stand, and the head legs were re-run at 51cafe4365 (both scenarios) and at 5eeccf69b6 (undecodable-line A/B plus a clean control), all passing. Scenario 1, inline retrieve of a completed raw batch id (path 1), poisoned file. Base: `LoggingWorker error: Model is None ... completion_response={}` from `_handle_completed_batch`, no `aretrieve_batch` spend row at all. Head: `WARNING batch_utils.py:135 ... custom_id=request-poison-empty`, `WARNING batch_utils.py:430 - skipping malformed batch output line`, `batch output aggregate: cost=8e-06 ... total_tokens=31`, spend row `aretrieve_batch | 8e-06 | 31`. Control with the passthrough disarmed: both sides aggregate `cost=8e-06`, identical response bodies, identical spend rows. Scenario 2, managed batch through the enterprise poller (path 2), one new gpt-4.1-mini batch per side, poisoned output. Base: `CheckBatchCost: failed to track cost for batch batch_6a857319a6a08190b360862029606fd1 ... leaving it unprocessed so the next poll retries: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` at 02:18:55 and again at 02:20:01, managed object `validating | batch_processed f`, no `aretrieve_batch` row. Head: both warnings, `batch output aggregate: cost=8e-06 ... models=['gpt-4.1-mini']`, spend row `aretrieve_batch | gpt-4.1-mini | 8e-06 | 31`, managed object `complete | t`, `LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend` `gpt-4.1-mini | 8e-06 | 28 | 3`, no error on later cycles. Backward incompatible: the poller's "leave unprocessed and retry" contract no longer covers a bad output line. Before, one uncostable or malformed line kept the job unprocessed forever (and bumped `litellm_check_batch_cost_errors_total{cost_tracking_error}` every cycle); now the healthy lines are billed once, the bad line is $0 with a WARNING, and the job is marked processed. Fetch failures and aggregate-level failures still retry. An unmapped model was already billed at $0 without raising on both sides, so the per-line try/except does not change that case. Not verified: Vertex batches with `disable_vertex_batch_output_transformation` (needs a Vertex batch job plus GCS output; the only behavior change on that path is the malformed-line skip, covered by `test_parse_jsonl_malformed_lines_skipped` and `test_iter_output_entries_skips_malformed_and_non_object_lines`). ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - A line that cannot be costed is billed at $0 with a warning, not retried; the cost poller no longer leaves such a batch unprocessed for a later retry (see Live PR risk) ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

The proxy admin configures a deployment with `model: vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-6` and `vertex_location: us-east5` 2. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see $0.0033 for that request 4. The Google Cloud billing export for the same request shows $0.00363, so every reconciliation is off by 10% and the gap grows with volume After: the same request is logged at the regional rate Google actually charges 1. The developer sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and gets the same 200 with 1000 prompt and 200 completion tokens 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows $0.00363, matching the billing export 4. They add `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` to their config and start the proxy 2. They GET http://localhost:4000/v1/model/info and the entry shows no `supports_tool_search` field 3. Their capability-based routing treats the model as unable to do tool search, and requests routed by that signal skip a model that Bedrock itself serves tool search on After: the same models advertise tool search and requests work end to end 1. Request body used for every /v1/messages call: ```json { "model": "<alias>", "max_tokens": 128, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Use tool discovery to find a tool that can add 2 and 3, then call it."}], "tools": [ {"type": "tool_search_tool_regex_20251119", "name": "tool_search_tool_regex"}, {"name": "add_numbers", "description": "Add two integers", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"a": {"type": "integer"}, "b": {"type": "integer"}}, "required": ["a", "b"]}, "defer_loading": true} ] } ``` ### Before (0de60a2ff2) #### /v1/model/info capability flag 1. `curl -s http://localhost:41412/v1/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` then print `model_info.supports_tool_search` per model 2. signal.title: [Bug]: search router silently drops provider-specific litellm_params from yaml search_tools entries
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a `search_tools` entry in the proxy config carries provider-specific keys in its `litellm_params` (for example `tool_name` for the agentcore provider, or `aws_access_key_id` / `aws_secret_access_key` overrides), those keys are silently dropped. The search router forwards only `search_provider`, `api_key`, and `api_base` from the tool's `litellm_params` to the underlying search call (`SearchAPIRouter.async_search_with_fallbacks_helper` in `litellm/router_utils/search_api_router.py`), so every other key is ignored with no warning, no boot error, and no request-time error Expected: either every `litellm_params` key is forwarded to the provider (the way `model_list` entries forward their `litellm_params` to completion calls), or the proxy rejects unknown keys loudly at boot so an admin finds out their knob is dead The same keys do work when passed per request in the body or set via provider env vars (for agentcore, `AGENTCORE_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME`), which is how the guard behind `tool_name` stays reachable. Only the yaml path is dead. The agentcore example config was corrected in #36331 to stop advertising the yaml knobs; this issue tracks fixing the plumbing itself, which affects all search providers ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a proxy admin whose AgentCore gateway target has a custom name configures it in yaml and every search silently uses the wrong tool name 1. They add a `search_tools` entry with `search_provider: agentcore`, their gateway `api_base`, and `tool_name: MyTarget___WebSearch` in `litellm_params`, then start the proxy; boot succeeds with no warning 2. They send POST http://litellm-domain/v1/search/agentcore-search with `{"query": "latest AI developments", "max_results": 5}` 3. The request goes out with the default `web-search-tool___WebSearch` instead of their configured name; on a gateway whose target really has a custom name this comes back as an MCP tool-not-found error, and on a gateway that also has a default-named target it silently searches through the wrong one 4. Nothing in the response or the logs says their yaml `tool_name` was ignored After a (hypothetical) fix: the same config works, or fails loudly 1. They add the same `search_tools` entry and start the proxy 2. They send the same POST http://litellm-domain/v1/search/agentcore-search request 3. The request goes out with `MyTarget___WebSearch` and returns results from their target, or, if the key is deliberately unsupported, the proxy refuses to boot naming the unsupported key ### Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with (proxy booted from PR #36331 at commit `70a4f9a73aabd327b9c06e52bf5d47b437b76430`; the router file involved is untouched by that PR and identical on `litellm_internal_staging`): ```yaml search_tools: - search_tool_name: agentcore-badtool litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: https://litellm-qa-agentcore-tez4ymmxfc.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp tool_name: my-target___ListFiles ``` The agentcore provider rejects any `tool_name` not ending in `___WebSearch`, so this request must fail. Instead it returns HTTP 200 with real web results, against a real AgentCore gateway: ``` curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/v1/search/agentcore-badtool \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \ -d '{"query": "anything", "max_results": 2}' -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' {"results":[{"title":"Anything","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anything", ...}],"object":"search"} HTTP 200 ``` The proxy debug log shows the outgoing JSON-RPC call used the default tool name, not the configured one, proving the yaml value never reached the provider: ``` -d '{'jsonrpc': '2.0', 'id': 1, 'method': 'tools/call', 'params': {'name': 'web-search-tool___WebSearch', 'arguments': {'query': 'anything', 'maxResults': 2}}}' ``` Control showing the guard itself works when the value arrives via env var: rebooting the same proxy with `AGENTCORE_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME=my-target___ListFiles` exported makes the same request refuse with ``` Invalid AgentCore search tool_name 'my-target___ListFiles': must end with '___WebSearch' (a web-search connector tool). Other gateway tools cannot be invoked through this provider. ``` Fix sketch: forward the tool's full `litellm_params` (minus `search_provider`, which becomes the positional provider) as kwargs from `SearchAPIRouter.async_search_with_fallbacks_helper` into the search call, mirroring how `model_list` `litellm_params` flow into completion calls, with request-body params winning over yaml on key collisions. Needs a check across all search providers that previously-ignored yaml keys don't change behavior for existing configs ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? litellm_internal_staging at 2059033352de (also present at PR #36331 tip 70a4f9a7) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(ci): stop Agent Shin reconsider from triggering on bot comments
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Agent Shin's own comments re-trigger the reconsider workflow - Every sweep close comment spawned a doomed unauthorized run How it solves it: - Job now skips comments authored by bots - Human authors and collaborators are unaffected ## User Flow Before: a maintainer watching the Agent Shin triage sweep gets a burst of pointless workflow runs, one per PR the sweep touched 1. The sweep posts its close comment on a PR, e.g. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/28399, and that comment tells the contributor to reply `@agent-shin reconsider` to bring the PR back 2. Because the comment body contains that phrase, the reconsider workflow triggers on the bot's own comment 3. The maintainer opens https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/workflows/triage_reconsider.yml and sees a run per closed PR, each one green but doing nothing except logging that `devin-ai-integration[bot]` is not authorized 4. The noise repeats on every sweep, so a real contributor reconsider is hard to spot in the run list After: the same sweep leaves the reconsider run list clean, so the only runs there are real contributor requests 1. The sweep posts the same close comment on the same PR, with the same `@agent-shin reconsider` instructions 2. No reconsider run is created at all, since the comment came from a bot 3. The maintainer opens the same Actions page and sees only runs triggered by humans 4. A contributor who actually comments `@agent-shin reconsider` still gets the 👀 reaction and a verdict, exactly as before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review No tests: the change is a GitHub Actions `if:` expression, which has no test harness in this repo. The trigger data below is from the real events ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix `issue_comment` workflows always run from the default branch, so the new gate cannot execute from a PR branch. Before is the live behavior on `litellm_internal_staging`, After is the same real event payload evaluated against the new condition ### Before (f4b46c81da) 1. List the reconsider runs from today's sweep ``` $ gh run list --workflow triage_reconsider.yml -L 200 --json conclusion,createdAt,displayTitle \ | jq -r '[.[] | select(.conclusion != "skipped")] | .[] | "\(.createdAt) \(.displayTitle)"' 2026-08-19T21:36:09Z proto(mcp): per-user env-var fields demo flow (UI mockup) 2026-08-19T21:36:06Z prototype(ui): per-user fields for MCP servers (mock/throwaway) 2026-08-19T21:36:03Z feat(mcp): per-server env vars with global + per-user scopes 2026-08-19T21:36:01Z feat(mcp): add admin-declared per-user fields for MCP servers 2026-08-19T21:35:58Z fix(proxy): make pass-through auth checks method-aware 2026-08-19T21:35:55Z fix(bedrock): forward clear_tool_uses context_management on Invoke route 2026-08-19T21:35:54Z fix(azure): preserve AD token refresh in v1 OpenAI client path 2026-08-19T21:35:52Z fix(proxy): keep the model-group alias through vector store credential merges ``` Eight runs in 17 seconds, all of them from the sweep's own comments rather than from any contributor 2. Read what one of those runs actually did ``` $ gh run view 32304710883 --log | grep -E "COMMENTER: |not authorized" COMMENTER: devin-ai-integration[bot] ##[notice]Commenter 'devin-ai-integration[bot]' (CONTRIBUTOR) is not authorized to trigger reconsider; skipping subsequent steps. ``` Every later step (reaction, checkout, Python setup, the LLM judge) was skipped, so the run could never have produced a verdict ### After (fe97a9d719) 1. Pull the triggering comment from the same run and check it against the new condition ``` $ gh api repos/BerriAI/litellm/issues/comments/5348285161 \ -q '{login: .user.login, type: .user.type, has_phrase: (.body | contains("@agent-shin reconsider"))}' {"has_phrase":true,"login":"devin-ai-integration[bot]","type":"Bot"} ``` `github.event.comment.user.type != 'Bot'` is false and `!endsWith(github.event.comment.user.login, '[bot]')` is false, so the job condition is false and no run is created for any of those eight comments 2. Confirm a human reconsider still passes the gate ``` $ gh api repos/BerriAI/litellm/issues/comments/5348285161 -q .author_association CONTRIBUTOR ``` The added clauses only look at the commenter's account type, so the existing author / OWNER / MEMBER / COLLABORATOR authorization step is what still decides human comments ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats (if any) - Takes effect once merged to the default branch - A bot-authored PR can no longer self-reconsider Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2e6fbd7ba56d4655b42601c88868a654

When the proxy fails a request (for example, an upstream provider timeout), it logs the exception with a full traceback but no request-correlating ID anywhere in that log line. The log entry only has a wall-clock timestamp and the exception text: ``` {"message": "litellm.proxy.proxy_server._handle_llm_api_exception(): Exception occured - litellm.Timeout: APITimeoutError - Request timed out. Error_str: Request timed out. - timeout value=33.0, time taken=33.0 seconds

timeout: None", "level": "ERROR", "timestamp": "2026-08-19T21:37:27.359154", "component": "LiteLLM Proxy", "logger": "common_request_processing.py:1837", ...} ``` With concurrent traffic, there's no way to tell which specific client request this error belongs to from the log line alone, so it can't be cross-referenced against the `x-litellm-call-id` response header, the spend logs table, or a client-side support ticket that references a request ID. I confirmed the same log call is unchanged as of the current `litellm_internal_staging` branch (`pyproject.toml` version 1.98.0): `_log_llm_api_exception` in `litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py` logs `e` with `verbose_proxy_logger.exception(...)` and never includes `litellm_call_id`, even though the caller (`_handle_llm_api_exception`) has `self.data` in scope, which carries that ID. I expected the error log line to include the request's `litellm_call_id` (or equivalent request ID) so it can be correlated with the request that failed. ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer operating a LiteLLM proxy gets a provider timeout error and can't tell which of their concurrent requests it belongs to 1. Their app sends many concurrent `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` requests, each returning an `x-litellm-call-id` response header 2. signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? We are not able to get proper routing behavior. We have tried / experimented with many options ‘default’ , fallbacks enabled/disabled, tag filtering on/off, with and without ‘default’ tags – never could get expected or consistent behavior. Our need is tags enabled, routing_strategy: latency-based-routing, Below are lots of details – we need to know what is the right combination of configuration to get basic routing behavior. model_list: # Existing, unmodified, working model group - model_name: reasoning-complex litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY max_tokens: 8192 tags: [default, provider:anthropic, paid] model_info: input_cost_per_token: 3.0e-06 output_cost_per_token: 1.5e-05 - model_name: reasoning-complex litellm_params: model: bedrock/amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 aws_region_name: us-east-1 max_tokens: 8192 tags: [provider:bedrock, private, local, paid] model_info: input_cost_per_token: 1.2e-06 output_cost_per_token: 4.8e-06 # New test model group -- same two deployments, tag filtering disabled per-group - model_name: reasoning-complex-notag litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY max_tokens: 8192 tags: [default, provider:anthropic, paid] model_info: id: reasoning-complex-notag-anthropic enable_tag_filtering: false input_cost_per_token: 3.0e-06 output_cost_per_token: 1.5e-05 - model_name: reasoning-complex-notag litellm_params: model: bedrock/amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 aws_region_name: us-east-1 max_tokens: 8192 tags: [provider:bedrock, private, local, paid] model_info: id: reasoning-complex-notag-nova enable_tag_filtering: false input_cost_per_token: 1.2e-06 output_cost_per_token: 4.8e-06 router_settings: routing_strategy: latency-based-routing enable_tag_filtering: true # proxy-wide defaul tag_filtering_match_any: false Proxy restarted after the config change; confirmed healthy before testing (/health showed 0 unhealthy endpoints across all model groups, a manual smoke-test call succeeded against Request sent (genuinely untagged) from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(api_key="...", base_url="http://localhost:4000/v1") client.chat.completions.create( model="reasoning-complex-notag", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "explain briefly"}], max_tokens=20, temperature=0, extra_body={"cache": {"no-cache": True}}, ) No tags field, no metadata field anywhere in the request. Expected behavior Per the described model_info.enable_tag_filtering: false semantics: the request should be routed via latency-based-routing across both deployments in reasoning-complex-notag, ignoreployments' own declared tags and any request-sidetags). Actual behavior openai.AuthenticationError: Error code: 401 - {'error': {'message': "Not allowed to access model due to tags configura model=reasoning-complex-notag and tags=['default', 'provider:anthropic', 'paid']", 'type': 'None', 'param': 'None', 'code': This is RouterErrors.no_deployments_with_tag_routi raised because zero deployments end up as validtag-matching candidates. Notably, the tags=[...] echoed in the error is the Sonnet deployment's own litellm_params.tags list (['default', 'provider:anthropic', 'paid']) — not anything the ugh, in this code path, a deployment's own declaredtags are being treated as the required request tags to satisfy, which the Nova Pro deployment in the same group (tags: ['provider:bedrock', 'private', 'local', 'paid'], ) can never match — resulting in animpossible-to-satisfy candidate set and a hard deny, even though the incoming request had no tags at all. We did not get to test a tagged request against this model group — it failed on the very first (untagged) call, before that could be tried. Source investigation We checked the installed package directly to under - litellm/router.py (Router.__init__): enable_tag_filtering is a constructor parameter stored as a single instance attribute (self.enable_tag_filtering = enable_tag_filtering)-deployment. - litellm/router_strategy/tag_based_routing.py (get_deployments_for_tag()): the very first check is if llm_router_instance.enable_tag_filtering is not Trs — reading the router-instance-level attribute, not anything from model_info. - We searched the entire installed package (grep -tering") and found zero references to aper-deployment/per-model_info tag-filtering override anywhere in the source of 1.93.0. Given that, we're not sure whether model_info.enable_tag_filtering is: (a) a real, newer feature not yet in 1.93.0, (b) a doc/support inaccuracy, or (c) real but implementeied (e.g. requires additional config we're missing), which would also explain the specific 401 we're hitting rather than a clean no-op. Why we were trying this in the first place (context, not required to reproduce the bug above) Separately, and probably relevant background: with router_settings.enable_tag_filtering: true (the global default) and no request tags at all, latency-based-routing consistently sends to 1 model group to one deployment (Anthropic, tagged default) and 0% to the other (Bedrock Nova Pro, no default tag) — even though we've directly measured Nova Pro as meaningfully faster per completion token on this eia matched back-to-back timing, ~2-5x faster, consistent across 6 pairs). Explicitly tagging requests works as expected and lets the faster deployment compete and win the majority of the time (confirmed: a shared tag both Pro selected 60% of the time; a Nova-exclusive taggets it selected 100% of the time). Setting router_settings.enable_tag_filtering: false globally also restores genuine latency-based competition for untagged traffic (coreached Nova Pro with this global flag off, versus0/10 with it on). We were trying model_info.enable_tag_filtering: false specifically to get this same effect for one model group without disabling tag filtering proxy-wide, since ng (e.g. private/local tags for data-residencyconstraints) elsewhere. Ask 1. Is model_info.enable_tag_filtering a real, supported config key in 1.93.0? If so, what are we missing that causes this specific 401 instead of the documented behavior? 2. If it's not supported in this version, is there a different documented way to get "tag filtering enabled globally, disabled for one specific model group" without hitting this error ### User Flow from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(api_key="...", base_url="http://localhost:4000/v1") client.chat.completions.create( model="reasoning-complex-notag", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "explain briefly"}], max_tokens=20, temperature=0, extra_body={"cache": {"no-cache": True}}, ) No tags field, no metadata field anywhere in the request. Expected behavior Per the described model_info.enable_tag_filtering: false semantics: the request should be routed via latency-based-routing across both deployments in reasoning-complex-notag, ignoreployments' own declared tags and any request-sidetags). Actual behavior openai.AuthenticationError: Error code: 401 - {'error': {'message': "Not allowed to access model due to tags configura model=reasoning-complex-notag and tags=['default', 'provider:anthropic', 'paid']", 'type': 'None', 'param': 'None', 'code': This is RouterErrors.no_deployments_with_tag_routi raised because zero deployments end up as validtag-matching candidates. ### Proof the bug occurs - Image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-latest - Version: 1.93.0 (via importlib.metadata, since litellm.__version__ isn't exposed) - Image built: 2026-07-02 ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? signal.title: fix(model_prices): correct gemini 3.1 flash image and deepseek v4 pricing, add openai deprecation dates
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Gemini 3.1 Flash Image billed at batch price, not standard - DeepSeek V4 prices match no published DeepSeek tier - Six retired OpenAI models carry no deprecation date How it solves it: - Standard and batch fields set from Google's pricing table - DeepSeek V4 set to the official peak rates - Announced shutdown dates added to the six entries ## User Flow Before: a developer calling `gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-image` and `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` through the gateway is billed roughly half of what the provider actually charges, and sees nothing telling them the OpenAI moderation and instruct models are already shut down 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-image"` 2. The response header `x-litellm-response-cost` and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs report input billed at $0.25 per 1M tokens, while Google charges $0.50 for the same standard-tier call 3. They repeat with `"model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"` and get $0.435 per 1M input tokens logged against DeepSeek's actual $1.32 4. They GET https://litellm-domain/model/info and the entries for `text-moderation-latest`, `babbage-002`, `davinci-002` and `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct` come back with no shutdown date, so nothing warns them these models are retired After: the same calls are billed at the provider's published rate, and the retired models report their shutdown dates 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-image"` 2. `x-litellm-response-cost` and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now report input at $0.50 per 1M tokens, matching Google's standard tier, and batch requests stay at $0.25 3. The same `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` call is logged at $1.32 per 1M input tokens and $3.96 per 1M output tokens 4. GET https://litellm-domain/model/info returns `"deprecation_date": "2025-10-27"` for the three `text-moderation-*` models and `"deprecation_date": "2026-09-28"` for `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`, `babbage-002` and `davinci-002` ## Relevant issues Supports #26900 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5849 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Sources for every changed value ### Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing#gemini-3.1-flash-image That table gives, for the Standard tier, input $0.50 per 1M tokens (text/image) and output $3 per 1M (text and thinking), with the Batch tier at $0.25 and $1.50. Both `gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-image` and `gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` had the batch numbers sitting in the standard fields and half-batch in the `_batches` fields, so every tier was understated by 2x | field | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | `input_cost_per_token` | 2.5e-07 | 5e-07 | | `output_cost_per_token` | 1.5e-06 | 3e-06 | | `input_cost_per_token_batches` | 1.25e-07 | 2.5e-07 | | `output_cost_per_token_batches` | 7.5e-07 | 1.5e-06 | Cross-check inside this same file: the `vertex_ai/gemini-3.1-flash-image` entries already use 5e-07 and 3e-06. The image-token and per-image fields (6e-05, and 0.045 for a 0.5K image) already match the page, so they are untouched ### DeepSeek V4 Source: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing Peak rates from that table: `deepseek-v4-flash` is $0.014 cache-hit input, $0.44 cache-miss input, $1.32 output per 1M tokens, and `deepseek-v4-pro` is $0.044, $1.32 and $3.96. Off-peak is exactly half of peak, which this file cannot express, so the peak (list) rate is used, matching how the existing `deepseek-chat` entry carries DeepSeek's list price. The values in the registry ($0.14 / $0.28 for flash, $0.435 / $0.87 for pro) match neither the peak nor the off-peak column Updated `input_cost_per_token`, `output_cost_per_token`, `cache_read_input_token_cost` and `input_cost_per_token_cache_hit` on `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro` and their `deepseek/` prefixed twins. Context length (1M) and max output (384K, stored as 393216) already matched the page ### OpenAI deprecations Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations | model | shutdown date on the page | added | | --- | --- | --- | | `text-moderation-007`, `text-moderation-latest`, `text-moderation-stable` | 2025-10-27 | `"deprecation_date": "2025-10-27"` | | `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`, `babbage-002`, `davinci-002` | 2026-09-28 | `"deprecation_date": "2026-09-28"` | The key name and ISO format match the 335 entries that already carry `deprecation_date`, which is what `litellm/proxy/common_utils/model_deprecation.py` parses. Azure, `vercel_ai_gateway/*` and `github_copilot/*` copies of these models are left alone because those platforms publish their own lifecycle dates, and the `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct-0914` snapshot is not on OpenAI's table ## Also audited, nothing verifiably wrong Anthropic (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations), Gemini deprecations (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations), Groq (https://console.groq.com/docs/deprecations) and Mistral (https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/models/models_overview/) all agree with the dates already in the registry, including the Gemini rows where a fetch-tool summary disagreed with the live page ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a proxy started with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` and `master_key: sk-1234`, serving `gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-image`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `text-moderation-latest`, `babbage-002`, `davinci-002` and `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`, run once from a worktree at the merge base and once from the branch tip so each process loads the intended registry. The Gemini and DeepSeek calls are real provider API calls that cost real money. `/spend/logs` was unavailable on this box (the configured database has no `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` table), so the spend evidence is the `x-litellm-response-cost` header plus the usage block from the same response. The DeepSeek runs used DB-less proxies on random free ports (41783 before, 43498 after) ### Before (c696fdfb05) #### Deprecation metadata for the six OpenAI models 1. Query the deprecation route: ```bash curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ 'http://localhost:4000/model/deprecations?warn_within_days=90' | jq '{deprecated: [.deprecated[] | select(.model_name == "text-moderation-latest" or .model_name == "babbage-002" or .model_name == "davinci-002" or .model_name == "gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct") | {model_name,deprecation_date,days_until_deprecation,status}], imminent: [.imminent[] | select(.model_name == "text-moderation-latest" or .model_name == "babbage-002" or .model_name == "davinci-002" or .model_name == "gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct") | {model_name,deprecation_date,days_until_deprecation,status}], upcoming: [.upcoming[] | select(.model_name == "text-moderation-latest" or .model_name == "babbage-002" or .model_name == "davinci-002" or .model_name == "gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct") | {model_name,deprecation_date,days_until_deprecation,status}]}' ``` 2. Nothing is reported, so an operator gets no warning that these models are retired or 40 days from shutdown: ```json { "deprecated": [], "imminent": [], "upcoming": [] } ``` #### Billed cost of a real Gemini 3.1 Flash Image generation 1. Send the request: ```bash curl -sS -D /tmp/before.headers -o /tmp/before.body \ -X POST 'http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{"model":"gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-image","prompt":"A small red circle on a white background"}' ``` 2. The response is billed at the batch rates that were sitting in the standard fields: ```text HTTP 200 x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0674 ``` ```json {"usage":{"total_tokens":1260,"input_tokens":8,"output_tokens":1252, "output_tokens_details":{"image_tokens":1120,"text_tokens":132}}} ``` 3. That is `8 x 2.5e-7 + 132 x 1.5e-6 + 1120 x 6e-5 = 0.067400`, i.e. input charged at $0.25 per 1M and output text at $1.50 per 1M, half of Google's standard tier #### Billed cost of a real DeepSeek V4 Pro chat completion 1. Send the request: ```bash curl -sS -D /tmp/lit5849_before.headers -o /tmp/lit5849_before.body \ -X POST 'http://localhost:41783/v1/chat/completions' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{"model":"deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly the word: pong"}]}' ``` 2. The response is billed at the old registry rates that match no published DeepSeek tier: ```text HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 6.3945e-05 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 3.9585e-05 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 2.436e-05 ``` ```json {"usage":{"completion_tokens":28,"prompt_tokens":91,"total_tokens":119, "completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":25}, "prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0}, "prompt_cache_hit_tokens":0,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":91}} ``` 3. That is `91 x 4.35e-7 + 28 x 8.7e-7 = 0.000063945`, i.e. input at $0.435 per 1M and output at $0.87 per 1M, roughly a third of DeepSeek's published $1.32 / $3.96 peak rates ### After (dcd8bb3f38) #### Deprecation metadata for the six OpenAI models 1. Same query as before: ```bash curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ 'http://localhost:4000/model/deprecations?warn_within_days=90' | jq '<same filter as above>' ``` 2. The announced dates now come back, with `text-moderation-latest` already past shutdown and the three instruct/completion models flagged 40 days out: ```json { "deprecated": [ {"model_name": "text-moderation-latest", "deprecation_date": "2025-10-27", "days_until_deprecation": -296, "status": "deprecated"} ], "imminent": [ {"model_name": "babbage-002", "deprecation_date": "2026-09-28", "days_until_deprecation": 40, "status": "imminent"}, {"model_name": "davinci-002", "deprecation_date": "2026-09-28", "days_until_deprecation": 40, "status": "imminent"}, {"model_name": "gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct", "deprecation_date": "2026-09-28", "days_until_deprecation": 40, "status": "imminent"} ], "upcoming": [] } ``` #### Billed cost of a real Gemini 3.1 Flash Image generation 1. Same request: ```bash curl -sS -D /tmp/after.headers -o /tmp/after.body \ -X POST 'http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{"model":"gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-image","prompt":"A small red circle on a white background"}' ``` 2. The response is now billed at the standard tier: ```text HTTP 200 x-litellm-response-cost: 0.068263 ``` ```json {"usage":{"total_tokens":1481,"input_tokens":8,"output_tokens":1473, "output_tokens_details":{"image_tokens":1120,"text_tokens":353}}} ``` 3. That is `8 x 5e-7 + 353 x 3e-6 + 1120 x 6e-5 = 0.068263`, i.e. input at $0.50 per 1M and output text at $3.00 per 1M, matching Google's standard tier. The model returns a different number of thinking/text tokens on every call, so compare the per-token rates in the arithmetic rather than the two totals #### Billed cost of a real DeepSeek V4 Pro chat completion 1. Same request: ```bash curl -sS -D /tmp/lit5849_after.headers -o /tmp/lit5849_after.body \ -X POST 'http://localhost:43498/v1/chat/completions' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{"model":"deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly the word: pong"}]}' ``` 2. The response is now billed at DeepSeek's published peak rates: ```text HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00022308 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.00012012000000000001 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 0.00010296 ``` ```json {"usage":{"completion_tokens":26,"prompt_tokens":91,"total_tokens":117, "completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":23}, "prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0}, "prompt_cache_hit_tokens":0,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":91}} ``` 3. That is `91 x 1.32e-6 + 26 x 3.96e-6 = 0.00022308`, i.e. input at $1.32 per 1M and output at $3.96 per 1M, exactly DeepSeek's peak column. The model returns a different number of reasoning tokens per call, so compare the per-token rates rather than the two totals QA observations from the DeepSeek legs: - DeepSeek routes these calls to api.deepseek.com/beta; unrelated to this PR - Reasoning tokens bill inside output cost; this PR leaves that alone - Both calls had zero cached tokens, so cache-hit rates stay doc-verified only ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - DeepSeek input/output rates proven live; cache-hit rate doc-verified only - No batch variant of `output_cost_per_image_token` exists in the schema, so Gemini batch image pricing stays inexpressible (pre-existing gap) - V4 Pro previously held a discounted price from #26709, now list price - Updated the two DeepSeek V4 assertions in `tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py` - `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image`, `gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview`, `gemini-omni-flash` still missing - Google serves no static token limits for those, so adding them means guessing - Same for Bedrock `amazon.nova-reel-v1:0/v1:1` and `amazon.nova-sonic-v1:0` - xAI docs are unreachable from this box, so Grok entries went unaudited ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/9d0d242e58ed4a5b8fc2f892bf2713e9 - [x] dcd8bb3f38 passes /live-pr-risk

signal.title: fix(model_prices): add provider-announced deprecation_date to 205 registry entries
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - 205 registry entries lack provider-announced `deprecation_date` - `/model/deprecations` (#26900) therefore reports them as healthy - Operators get no warning for Azure, Anthropic, Vertex, OpenAI retirements How it solves it: - Adds `deprecation_date` from each provider's official retirement doc - Purely additive: no existing value or field is changed - Skips ambiguous alias/version mappings rather than guessing ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin who deploys `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `azure/gpt-5`, `vertex_ai/claude-opus-5` and `babbage-002` gets no retirement warning even though all four have published retirement dates 1. They call `GET https://litellm-domain/model/deprecations` with their master key 2. The response comes back `{"deprecated": [], "imminent": [], "upcoming": []}` 3. They see nothing to act on, and the Anthropic Sonnet 4.5 deployment silently stops working after its retirement date After: the same call lists every deployment whose provider has announced a retirement date 1. They call `GET https://litellm-domain/model/deprecations` with their master key 2. `upcoming` now contains `legacy-babbage` (2026-09-28), `sonnet-4-5` (2026-09-29), `vertex-opus-5` (2027-01-24) and `azure-gpt-5` (2027-02-09), each with `days_until_deprecation` 3. They plan migrations ahead of each date, and Slack deprecation alerts fire for the same deployments ## Relevant issues Supports #26900 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5850 ## What changed, by source Every date below comes from the provider's own retirement/deprecation doc. Only entries that had **no** `deprecation_date` were touched; where a provider doc was ambiguous (unversioned Azure alias covering versions with differing dates, `azure_ai/model_router`, Gemini-API dates for models exposed under `vertex_ai`, conflicting rows for `gpt-realtime-mini-2025-10-06`) the entry was left alone | Group | Entries | Source | | --- | --- | --- | | Azure OpenAI + Azure AI Foundry (`azure/*`, `azure_ai/*`) | 96 | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/model-retirement-schedule | | OpenAI (`openai`, `text-completion-openai`, incl. image-size variants) | 45 | https://platform.openai.com/docs/deprecations | | Vertex AI Gemini / Imagen / Veo / embeddings | 24 | https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/model-versions | | Vertex AI Claude partner models | 24 | https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/partner-models/use-claude | | Anthropic direct (`claude-*`) | 15 | https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/model-deprecations | | Gemini API (`gemini/gemini-robotics-er-1.6-preview`) | 1 | https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations | Representative values: ```diff "claude-sonnet-4-5": { + "deprecation_date": "2026-09-29" # Anthropic: not sooner than Sept 29, 2026 "claude-opus-5": { + "deprecation_date": "2027-07-24" # Anthropic: not sooner than July 24, 2027 "vertex_ai/claude-opus-5": { + "deprecation_date": "2027-01-24" # signal.title: feat(ui): add Ultra Lite heuristic auto-router preset
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - No bundled preset skips the classifier call - Every cross-provider template bills per-request classification How it solves it: - Adds an Ultra Lite template on the heuristic scorer - Tiers cost-ascending across four providers ## User Flow Before: an admin who wants cross-provider cost routing has to accept a classifier call on every request 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=llm-playground and start Add Auto Router 2. The Template dropdown offers Anthropic Family, Lite, OpenAI Family, Custom Configuration 3. Lite is the only mixed-provider option, and it routes through an LLM classifier, so every request pays a classification call before it reaches a model 4. To avoid that call they pick Custom Configuration and fill in all four tiers by hand After: the same admin picks a mixed-provider template that classifies locally 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=llm-playground and start Add Auto Router 2. The Template dropdown now also offers Ultra Lite 3. Selecting it fills SIMPLE with deepseek-v4-flash, MEDIUM with minimax-m3, COMPLEX with deepseek-v4-pro, REASONING with kimi-k3, and leaves the classifier set to heuristic 4. They save, and routed requests reach a model with no classification call ahead of them ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Setup: run the dashboard dev server with `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard` against a proxy on port 4000, with deployments registered for deepseek-v4-flash, minimax-m3, deepseek-v4-pro, and kimi-k3 so the template is selectable rather than greyed out ### Before (4d57bf0bdd) 1. Open http://localhost:3000/ui/?page=llm-playground and start Add Auto Router 2. Open the Template dropdown, observe exactly Anthropic Family, Lite, OpenAI Family, Custom Configuration, with no Ultra Lite entry ### After (2bf5c60184) 1. Open http://localhost:3000/ui/?page=llm-playground and start Add Auto Router 2. Open the Template dropdown, observe Ultra Lite listed after OpenAI Family and selectable 3. Select Ultra Lite, expand Detailed Configuration, observe the four tiers filled with deepseek-v4-flash, minimax-m3, deepseek-v4-pro, kimi-k3 and the classifier left on heuristic 4. Save the router, send a chat completion through it, and observe the request reaching a model with no classifier call logged at http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Heuristic tiering is weaker than the LLM classifier - Needs all four model groups registered to select - kimi-k3 group must be named exactly: FW- prefix blocks auto-match ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
