signal.title: fix(anthropic adapter): keep tool_result blocks that render no text
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #37462. Same class of defect as #36540 (there: `/v1/messages` → Responses API; here: the shared Anthropic→OpenAI adapter that the Gemini path goes through). ## The bug `translate_anthropic_messages_to_openai` only recognised `text` and `image` blocks inside a `tool_result` list. Anything else produced **no `role:"tool"` message at all**, so the `tool_call` it answers lost its result. Two spots, both in `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/transformation.py`: - single-item list — the `text` / `image` `if/elif` chain had no `else` - multi-item list, and `[]` — `if combined_content_parts:` skipped the append when nothing rendered Claude Code's deferred tool loading (`ToolSearch`) hits this on every use: its tool result is a list of `tool_reference` blocks with no text. ```json { "type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "call_1", "content": [{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "Read"}] } ``` Downstream is innocent — `convert_to_gemini_tool_call_result` has no empty-content skip and `_gemini_convert_messages_with_history` appends 1:1; the tool message simply never arrives. Vertex sees N `functionCall` parts answered by N-1 `functionResponse` parts and rejects the whole `contents`: ``` Please ensure that the number of function response parts is equal to the number of function call parts of the function call turn. ``` The turn is already in history, so retries replay it and the session stays broken. Verified against a proxy on `v1.98.0-rc.1` → `vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash`: two `tool_use` blocks, two `tool_result` blocks, only the first result's shape varying. | first `tool_result.content` | before | |---|---| | `"20C"` | 200 | | `[{"type": "text", "text": "20C"}]` | 200 | | `[{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "Read"}]` | 400 | | `[]` | 400 | A single-call turn hides it: with one `tool_use` and one dropped result the response turn collapses entirely and Gemini never runs the pairing check. It needs parallel tool calls where at least one sibling result does render. ## The change Every `tool_result` now emits exactly one tool message. Unknown blocks degrade to text instead of vanishing: - `tool_reference` → `[Loaded tool: <name>]` - any other unrecognised type → `[<type> block]` A placeholder rather than a JSON dump on purpose — unknown blocks may carry base64 payloads, and dumping a `document` block's `source.data` into a tool result would be its own bug. Their semantics don't need to survive: Claude Code re-injects the discovered tool schemas into `tools` itself, so the block is a history marker. What must survive is the item. Behaviour kept identical for everything already handled: single text block still yields string content (backward compat), single image still yields a one-element list, mixed lists still combine into one message. ## Tests Added to `tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/test_anthropic_experimental_pass_through_adapters_transformation.py`: - `test_translate_anthropic_messages_to_openai_tool_result_without_text_still_emits_tool_message` — parametrized over `tool_reference`, `[]`, and an unknown block type - `test_translate_anthropic_messages_to_openai_parallel_tool_results_keep_pairing` — the exact shape that 400s on Gemini Both fail on `main`, pass with this change. ``` tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/ 51 failed, 1319 passed same suite at the parent commit 51 failed, 1315 passed ``` The 51 failures are pre-existing and unrelated (`files/`, `count_tokens/`); the delta is the 4 added tests. `ruff check` on the changed file reports the same 3 pre-existing findings before and after. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix
signal.author: arthurh4

signal.title: fix(anthropic_responses): translate_tool_choice_to_responses_api returns invalid objects instead of string literals
signal.text: ## Bug `translate_tool_choice_to_responses_api` in the Anthropic→Responses API adapter returns `{"type": "auto"}` and `{"type": "required"}` (object form) where the OpenAI Responses API requires string literals `"auto"` and `"required"`. This causes 400/422 errors from vLLM (and potentially other OpenAI-compatible backends) when an Anthropic `/v1/messages` client sends `tool_choice` and the request is routed through the Responses API path. ## What happened LiteLLM v1.91.0 proxy receiving Anthropic `/v1/messages` requests for an `openai/`-provider model (e.g. vLLM backend) routes through the Responses API adapter (`litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/responses_adapters/`). The `tool_choice` translation produces invalid objects: | Anthropic `tool_choice` | Current output (broken) | Correct output | |---|---|---| | `{"type": "auto"}` | `{"type": "auto"}` | `"auto"` | | `{"type": "any"}` | `{"type": "required"}` | `"required"` | | `{"type": "none"}` | `{"type": "auto"}` ← **also wrong: enables tools when user asked to disable** | `"none"` | | `{"type": "tool", "name": "foo"}` | `{"type": "function", "name": "foo"}` | `{"type": "function", "name": "foo"}` (correct already) | ## Error from vLLM backend ``` litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - {"error":{"message":"13 validation errors: {'type': 'literal_error', 'loc': ('body', 'tool_choice', "literal['none','auto','required']"), 'msg': "Input should be 'none', 'auto' or 'required'", 'input': {'type': 'auto'}} {'type': 'missing', 'loc': ('body', 'tool_choice', 'ToolChoiceAllowed', 'mode'), 'msg': 'Field required', 'input': {'type': 'auto'}} ... (11 more validation errors) POST /v1/responses ``` vLLM's `ToolChoiceAllowed` Pydantic union tries `Literal["none","auto","required"]` (fails: dict not str), then `ToolChoiceAllowed` (fails: missing `mode`), then `ToolChoiceFunction` (fails: missing `name`), etc. ## Root cause **File:** `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/responses_adapters/transformation.py:198` ```python @staticmethod def translate_tool_choice_to_responses_api( tool_choice: AnthropicMessagesToolChoice, ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Convert Anthropic tool_choice to Responses API tool_choice.""" tc_type = tool_choice.get("type") if tc_type == "any": return {"type": "required"} # ← should be "required" (string) elif tc_type == "tool": return {"type": "function", "name": tool_choice.get("name", "")} return {"type": "auto"} # ← should be "auto" (string); also swallows "none" ``` The OpenAI Responses API `tool_choice` field accepts: - String literals: `"none"`, `"auto"`, `"required"` - Fully-typed objects: `{"type": "function", "name": "..."}`, `{"type": "web_search_preview"}`, etc. But **not** `{"type": "auto"}` or `{"type": "required"}` — these are neither valid string literals nor valid typed objects. ## Two bugs, one function 1. **`auto`/`any` return objects instead of strings** — causes 400/422 from backends that strictly validate the Responses API schema (vLLM, potentially others). 2. **`none` is silently mapped to `auto`** — `{"type": "none"}` (explicit tool-disable) falls through to the default `return {"type": "auto"}` (tool-enable). This is a safety issue: a client that explicitly disables tools gets tools enabled silently. ## Existing codebase already does this correctly Two sibling functions in the same codebase already handle this translation correctly, returning string literals: 1. **`LiteLLMCompletionResponsesConfig._transform_tool_choice`** in `litellm/responses/litellm_completion_transformation/transformation.py:104` — the chat-completions bridge. Returns `"auto"`, `"none"`, `"required"` as strings. Its docstring even cites Cursor IDE sending `{"type": "tool"}` as motivation. 2. **`translate_anthropic_tool_choice_to_openai`** in `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/transformation.py:702` — the Anthropic→Chat Completions adapter. Returns `"auto"`, `"none"`, `"required"` as strings, and raises `ValueError` for unknown types. The Responses API adapter was apparently never given the same treatment. ## Proposed fix ```python @staticmethod def translate_tool_choice_to_responses_api( tool_choice: AnthropicMessagesToolChoice, ) -> Union[str, Dict[str, Any]]: """Convert Anthropic tool_choice to Responses API tool_choice. The Responses API accepts string literals ("auto", "none", "required") or fully-typed objects (e.g. {"type": "function", "name": ...}). Returning {"type": "auto"} or {"type": "required"} as objects is rejected by the Responses API (and vLLM's Pydantic schema) — the string form is required. """ tc_type = tool_choice.get("type") if tc_type == "auto": return "auto" if tc_type == "none": return "none" if tc_type == "any": return "required" if tc_type == "tool": return {"type": "function", "name": tool_choice.get("name", "")} return "auto" ``` The existing tests in `tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/responses_adapters/test_responses_adapters_transformation.py` assert the buggy behavior and need to be updated. ## Environment - LiteLLM version: v1.91.0 (also affects v1.88.1+) - Backend: vLLM serving GLM-5.2 (OpenAI-compatible, `/v1/responses` endpoint enabled) - Client: Anthropic `/v1/messages` format (ZCode desktop agent, `kind=anthropic`) - Routing: `_should_route_to_responses_api` returns `True` for `openai` provider → dispatches to Responses API adapter ## Reproduction ```bash # vLLM backend with /v1/responses endpoint curl -X POST 'http://<vllm>:8000/v1/messages' \ -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "glm-5.2", "max_tokens": 48, "stream": true, "tools": [{"name": "test", "description": "test", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}], "tool_choice": {"type": "auto"}, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}] }' # → 400: 13 validation errors on tool_choice ```

signal.title: Responses API transformer strips cache_control unconditionally, unlike Chat Completions' custom-endpoint carve-out
signal.text: ### What happened? When a model is configured with `custom_llm_provider: openai` and a self-hosted `api_base` (an OpenAI-compatible gateway that understands Anthropic-style `cache_control` markers — e.g. a local proxy bridging to Claude via OAuth), the **Chat Completions** transformer preserves `cache_control` for that self-hosted endpoint, but the **Responses API** transformer strips it unconditionally, with no equivalent carve-out. `litellm/llms/openai/chat/gpt_transformation.py` has `_should_preserve_cache_control_for_endpoint()`: ```python def _should_preserve_cache_control_for_endpoint( self, custom_llm_provider: str | None, api_base: str | None, ) -> bool: """ The generic `openai` provider also reaches OpenAI-compatible endpoints (a LiteLLM proxy, vLLM, an Anthropic-compatible gateway) via a custom api_base. Those can understand cache_control, so it must survive there. Real OpenAI cannot, so it is still stripped for an openai.com host. """ ``` This is called from `transform_request`/`transform_request` async path, and when `custom_llm_provider == "openai"` with a non-`api.openai.com` `api_base`, `cache_control` on messages/tools is preserved. `litellm/llms/openai/responses/transformation.py` has no equivalent check. `transform_responses_api_request` (and the sync counterpart) unconditionally calls `remove_cache_control_flag_from_input_and_tools`, regardless of `custom_llm_provider`/`api_base`: ```python """Strip Anthropic-only `cache_control` markers before sending to OpenAI. OpenAI's Responses API rejects unknown fields on input content blocks with HTTP 400 ("Unknown parameter: 'input[0].content[0].cache_control'"). Chat Completions strips these in `remove_cache_control_flag_from_messages_and_tools`; mirror that here. """ ``` Net effect: a client sending Anthropic `cache_control` breakpoints (e.g. Claude Code, which enables extended thinking by default and in our setup causes LiteLLM to route through the Responses API transformer rather than Chat Completions) through a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible + Anthropic-capable backend gets its `cache_control` silently dropped on the Responses path, while the same request would have survived on the Chat Completions path. Prompt caching (`cache_read_input_tokens`) never fires — measured 0% hit rate across all live traffic in our deployment — even though the pricing config (`cache_read_input_token_cost` etc.) and the downstream bridge both support it correctly when the field is present. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.96.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response*

signal.title: [Bug]: `cache_control_injection_points` incorrectly invokes Dotprompt prompt management and requires `prompt_id`
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Requests to `/v1/chat/completions` return HTTP 500 when a cloud model is configured with: ```yaml cache_control_injection_points: - role: system location: message ``` This has been observed with `gemini-3.6-flash`, `claude-opus-4.8`, and other cloud models configured in a local LiteLLM deployment. The same model and request work when `cache_control_injection_points` is removed. When this parameter is enabled, LiteLLM unexpectedly calls the Dotprompt prompt-management integration while constructing the chat prompt. The request is an ordinary chat-completion request and does not reference a managed prompt, so it does not contain a `prompt_id`. `PromptManagementBase.get_chat_completion_prompt()` consequently raises: ```text ValueError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` LiteLLM wraps this local preprocessing exception as an `APIConnectionError`, retries it five times, attempts fallback handling, and ultimately returns HTTP 500. This appears to occur because cache-control injection is incorrectly activating, or being handled by, the Dotprompt prompt-management callback. Configuring cache-control injection should not cause an unrelated prompt-management integration to require `prompt_id`. ### Expected behavior LiteLLM should add the requested cache-control metadata to the matching system message and submit the completion to the provider without requiring prompt-management fields. If the selected provider or model does not support cache-control injection, LiteLLM should return an appropriate validation or unsupported-feature error. It should not invoke prompt management or require `prompt_id`. ### Actual behavior An ordinary completion enters the Dotprompt prompt-management path and fails before a provider response can be obtained because the request has no `prompt_id`. ### User Flow - Run a local LiteLLM Proxy deployment with a cloud-backed model such as `claude-opus-4.8` or `gemini-3.6-flash`. - Configure the model with `cache_control_injection_points` under `litellm_params`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-opus-4.8 litellm_params: model: <provider/model> api_key: os.environ/PROVIDER_API_KEY cache_control_injection_points: - role: system location: message ``` - Send a normal request containing a system message, without specifying `prompt_id` or any managed-prompt parameters: ```bash curl http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "claude-opus-4.8", "messages": [ { "role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant." }, { "role": "user", "content": "Hello" } ] }' ``` - Observe that the request returns HTTP 500 with: ```text prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` - Remove the following configuration: ```yaml cache_control_injection_points: - role: system location: message ``` - Restart or reload the proxy and repeat the same request. - Observe that the prompt-management error no longer occurs. ### Proof the bug occurs | Test Result | Outcome | | --- | --- | | Cloud model without `cache_control_injection_points` | Request proceeds without this error | | Same model and request with `cache_control_injection_points` | HTTP 500 | | Request without any managed-prompt fields | Dotprompt is still invoked | | Models observed | `gemini-3.6-flash`, `claude-opus-4.8`, and other configured cloud models | The stack trace proves that an ordinary completion unexpectedly enters Dotprompt prompt management: ```text litellm.main.completion -> litellm_logging_obj.get_chat_completion_prompt -> custom_logger.get_chat_completion_prompt -> dotprompt_manager.get_chat_completion_prompt -> PromptManagementBase.get_chat_completion_prompt -> ValueError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` Relevant trace excerpt: ```text File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/main.py", line 5076, in completion ) = litellm_logging_obj.get_chat_completion_prompt( File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py", line 701, in get_chat_completion_prompt ) = custom_logger.get_chat_completion_prompt( File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/integrations/dotprompt/dotprompt_manager.py", line 201, in get_chat_completion_prompt return PromptManagementBase.get_chat_completion_prompt( File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/integrations/prompt_management_base.py", line 168, in get_chat_completion_prompt raise ValueError("prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class") ValueError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` The error is then incorrectly surfaced as a provider connection failure: ```text 500 litellm.APIConnectionError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` LiteLLM retries the deterministic preprocessing failure: ```text LiteLLM Retried: 5 times, LiteLLM Max Retries: 5 ``` Fallback handling cannot recover from it: ```text No fallback model group found for original model_group=claude-opus-4.8 Error doing the fallback: litellm.APIConnectionError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` This evidence shows that: 1. The exception originates in LiteLLM prompt preprocessing rather than in the cloud provider. 2. Dotprompt is invoked even though the request does not use a managed prompt. 3. Enabling `cache_control_injection_points` makes `prompt_id` incorrectly mandatory. 4. The issue is provider-independent because it occurs with multiple cloud models. 5. Retries and fallbacks cannot resolve the issue because every attempt encounters the same local preprocessing error. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.2 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: [Bug]: /v1/messages → vertex_ai/gemini drops tool_result blocks with no text (tool_reference, empty list) → Vertex 400 function-response part count
signal.text: ### What happened Any Claude Code turn that calls `ToolSearch` (deferred tool loading) dies against a Gemini model routed through `/v1/messages`: ``` litellm.BadRequestError: Vertex_aiException BadRequestError - { "error": { "code": 400, "message": "Please ensure that the number of function response parts is equal to the number of function call parts of the function call turn.", "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT" } } . Received Model Group=claude-gemini-flash ``` Retries cannot help — the malformed turn is already in history, so every retry replays it and the session is stuck until the user clears it. The error message is misleading: the client's Anthropic request is well-formed. Every `tool_use` block has exactly one matching `tool_result` block. The mismatch is introduced by LiteLLM's own translation. ### Root cause `ToolSearch` returns a `tool_result` whose content is a list of `tool_reference` blocks, with no text anywhere: ```json { "type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "call_1", "content": [{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "Read"}] } ``` `translate_anthropic_messages_to_openai` only recognises `text` and `image` blocks inside a `tool_result` list. Anything else produces **no `role:"tool"` message at all**, so the `tool_call` it belongs to loses its result. Two places, both in `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/transformation.py`: - single-item list — the `if c.get("type") == "text" / elif ... == "image"` chain has no `else`, so nothing is appended - multi-item list / `[]` — `if combined_content_parts:` skips the append when nothing rendered Downstream is innocent: `convert_to_gemini_tool_call_result` has no empty-content skip, and `_gemini_convert_messages_with_history` appends 1:1 over whatever messages it is handed. It simply never receives the tool message. Vertex then sees N `functionCall` parts answered by N-1 `functionResponse` parts and rejects the whole `contents`. An empty *string* `content: ""` is handled correctly (`elif isinstance(content.get("content"), str)` matches and appends) — only the list form drops. ### Reproduction No credentials needed — the defect is in the adapter: ```python from litellm.llms.anthropic.experimental_pass_through.adapters.transformation import ( LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter, ) messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "search"}]}, {"role": "assistant", "content": [ {"type": "tool_use", "id": "call_1", "name": "ToolSearch", "input": {"q": "read"}}, {"type": "tool_use", "id": "call_2", "name": "get_weather", "input": {"city": "Paris"}}, ]}, {"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "call_1", "content": [{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "Read"}]}, {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "call_2", "content": "20C"}, ]}, ] out = LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter().translate_anthropic_messages_to_openai(messages=messages) print([m["tool_call_id"] for m in out if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("role") == "tool"]) # actual: ['call_2'] <- call_1 has no result # expected: ['call_1', 'call_2'] ``` End to end against a proxy with `model: vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash`, POST `/v1/messages` with that same body → 400 as above. ### Evidence Sent to a LiteLLM proxy `v1.98.0-rc.1` → `vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash`. Two `tool_use` blocks, two `tool_result` blocks, only the first result's shape varies: | `tool_result.content` of the first result | outcome | |---|---| | `"20C"` (plain string) | 200 | | `[{"type": "text", "text": "20C"}]` | 200 | | `[{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "Read"}]` | **400 function-response part count** | | `[]` | **400 function-response part count** | Replaying a real failing Claude Code request reproduces it, and rewriting *only* the `tool_reference` block of that body into text — leaving everything else byte-identical — makes the same request return 200. Same failure on `vertex_ai/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. A single-call turn hides the bug: with one `tool_use` and one dropped result, the response turn collapses entirely and Gemini never runs the pairing check. It only surfaces on parallel tool calls where at least one sibling result does render. ### Suggested fix Guarantee the invariant at the adapter: **every `tool_result` block emits exactly one tool message**, and unknown blocks degrade to text instead of disappearing. `tool_reference` renders as `[Loaded tool: <name>]`; other unrecognised types get a `[<type> block]` placeholder rather than a JSON dump, since they may carry base64 payloads. Their semantics do not need to survive — Claude Code re-injects the discovered tool schemas into `tools` itself, so the block is a history marker. What must survive is the item. PR follows. ### Relevant log output ``` File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/anthropic_endpoints/endpoints.py", line 97, in anthropic_response result: Final = await base_llm_response_processor.base_process_llm_request( File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/litellm_core_utils/exception_mapping_utils.py", line 1205, in _map_vertex_exception raise BadRequestError( litellm.BadRequestError: Vertex_aiException BadRequestError - {"error": {"code": 400, "message": "Please ensure that the number of function response parts is equal to the number of function call parts of the function call turn.", "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT"}} ``` ### Related - #36540 — same `tool_reference` blocks dropped on the `/v1/messages` → Responses API transform. Same class of defect, different downstream path; that report's "any unknown block inside a `tool_result` should degrade, not delete" applies verbatim here. - #22841 — `v1/messages` tool_result messages lost. ### Environment - LiteLLM proxy `v1.98.0-rc.1`; code paths above verified unchanged on `main` (`1.99.0`) - Route: `model: vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash`, `vertex_location: global`; also `vertex_ai/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` - Claude Code against the proxy with tool search active (deferred tool loading — needs `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=1` on non-first-party hosts) and enough MCP servers to trigger deferral - Non-streaming `/v1/messages`

signal.title: feat(elevenlabs): diarized_json transcription and multi-channel speaker support
signal.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ([Greptile review: Confidence Score 5/5](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/31324#issuecomment-4802230806)) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Tested against the real ElevenLabs `scribe_v2` speech-to-text API through `litellm`, with transcript text redacted. Diarization via `response_format=diarized_json` on a mono recording with two speakers: ``` $ curl -s http://PROXY:4000/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \ -F "model=elevenlabs/scribe_v2" \ -F "response_format=diarized_json" \ -F "file=@call.ogg" keys: ['text', 'usage', 'task', 'duration', 'segments', 'language'] usage: {'type': 'duration', 'seconds': 70.5} duration: 70.5 language: por num_segments: 5 [speaker_1] 58.4-59.0: <redacted> [speaker_0] 59.0-59.0: <redacted> [speaker_1] 59.0-60.1: <redacted> [speaker_0] 62.1-65.5: <redacted> [speaker_1] 66.9-69.1: <redacted> ``` Stereo audio with one person per channel, via `use_multi_channel=true` and `multichannel_output_style=combined`: ``` $ curl -s http://PROXY:4000/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \ -F "model=elevenlabs/scribe_v2" \ -F "use_multi_channel=true" \ -F "multichannel_output_style=combined" \ -F "file=@stereo_call.wav" num_segments: 7 | speakers: ['speaker_0', 'speaker_1'] | duration: 40.0 [speaker_1] 2.9-3.8: <redacted> [speaker_0] 3.6-5.8: <redacted> [speaker_1] 6.6-6.9: <redacted> [speaker_0] 7.1-9.1: <redacted> ... ``` A plain request with no diarization is unchanged and still returns the flat transcript with word-level timestamps. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes ElevenLabs speech-to-text previously supported only `language` and `temperature`, so a client requesting `response_format=diarized_json` either hit `UnsupportedParamsError` or, with `drop_params` enabled, had the format silently dropped. Even when diarization was turned on through the `diarize` passthrough, the response transformer flattened the output to `text` plus word timings and discarded each word's `speaker_id`, so speaker information never reached the caller. `response_format=diarized_json` now maps to ElevenLabs `diarize=true`, and the response is shaped into OpenAI's `diarized_json` form with `segments` that carry a `speaker` label, alongside `usage` and `duration`. The shape is decided from what the provider returned rather than from request flags, because the audio-transcription response transformer only receives the raw response. A `transcripts[]` body (`use_multi_channel=true`) or words with a non-null `speaker_id` (`diarize=true`) produce segments; a plain response keeps the existing flat `words` output untouched, so non-diarized callers see no change. For multi-channel audio such as a stereo call with one person per side, the channel index is used as the speaker, since ElevenLabs assigns `speaker_id` independently per channel and the two sides would otherwise collide on the same label. ElevenLabs rejects `diarize` and `use_multi_channel` together, and the OpenAI client API exposes a single knob (`response_format=diarized_json`). To bridge that, a `diarized_json` request reads the channel count from the audio header (via `soundfile`, already a dependency) and picks the mechanism: multi-channel audio switches to `use_multi_channel` with combined output and drops `diarize`, while mono keeps acoustic diarization. An explicit `use_multi_channel` from the caller wins over detection, and an unreadable header falls back to mono. One client call shape covers both mono and stereo without the caller knowing which it sent The untyped ElevenLabs JSON is validated through Pydantic models in `litellm/types/llms/elevenlabs.py` before use instead of being indexed as raw dicts, which also lowers the file's basedpyright error count. This depends on the fractional `usage.seconds` fix from #30996; the diarized_json `usage` carries a fractional duration, so this is branched off `litellm_oss_staging` where that fix landed.

They send `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` with the same prompts 6. A blocking collector returns HTTP 400 `Violated guardrail policy` with `trace_id` / `request_id` only. Model is `mock_response`, so there is no OpenAI spend. TrustGuard evaluate calls are live ### Before (973329e986) 1. `GET http://127.0.0.1:4000/ui/?page=guardrails` → Guardrail Garden → search NeuralTrust 2. signal.title: fix(cache): InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl returns remaining seconds (gh-37261)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #37261. When `provider_budget_config` is used without Redis, `GET /provider/budgets` reports `budget_reset_at` ~57 years in the future because `InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl` returned an absolute expiry timestamp instead of remaining seconds. ## Root cause `InMemoryCache` stores absolute expiry timestamps in `ttl_dict` (`time.time() + ttl`), but `async_get_ttl` returned that raw value. `budget_limiter.py` then added it directly to `datetime.now()`, producing `now + ~56.7 years`. `RedisCache.async_get_ttl` correctly returns remaining seconds, so the mismatch only manifests when no Redis is configured. ## Fix `InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl` now converts the stored absolute expiry to remaining seconds: ```python expiry = self.ttl_dict.get(key, None) if expiry is None: return None return max(0, expiry - time.time()) ``` This aligns both cache backends on the same contract (`remaining seconds`), matching the Redis behavior and what `budget_limiter.py` expects. ## Test plan - Unit test for `InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl` returning remaining seconds - Unit test for `_get_current_provider_budget_reset_at` without Redis: `budget_reset_at` is now `now + time_period`, not `now + 56.7 years` - Existing budget-limiter tests pass; no behavior change for Redis deployments Fixes #37261

signal.title: fix(router): add NotFoundErrorRetries to RetryPolicy (gh-36896)
signal.text: ## Summary - Add `NotFoundErrorRetries` to `RetryPolicy` and wire it into `get_num_retries_from_retry_policy()`. - Previously a 404 (`litellm.NotFoundError`) could not be pinned to 0 retries and fell back to `num_retries`, so the router retried 404s. Each retry also triggers an immediate cooldown, so retrying across the deployment pool cools every deployment and can cascade into a fleet-wide 5xx storm (see #36896). - Operators can now set `NotFoundErrorRetries: 0` to surface 404s to the client immediately. ## Test plan - tests/router_unit_tests/test_router_helper_utils.py::test_get_num_retries_from_retry_policy_notfounderror_zero - tests/router_unit_tests/test_router_helper_utils.py::test_get_num_retries_from_retry_policy_notfounderror_falls_back_to_num_retries Fixes #36896

signal.title: fix(gemini): use systemInstruction (camelCase) for native Gemini REST (gh-37028)
signal.text: ## Summary - Fixes #37028. When using native Gemini (`custom_llm_provider == "gemini"`) with a custom `api_base`, LiteLLM serializes a system message with the snake_case key `system_instruction`. Some Gemini-compatible proxies reject this and require the canonical `systemInstruction` (camelCase), returning HTTP 400 with a protobuf oneof error. ## Root cause In `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/transformation.py`, the `system_instruction` key was hardcoded regardless of provider. Vertex AI rejects `system_instruction` alongside `cachedContent`, so this was intentional for Vertex — but it breaks native Gemini REST endpoints that require camelCase. ## Fix Introduce a `system_instruction_key` variable: - `"systemInstruction"` for native Gemini - `"system_instruction"` for Vertex AI `RequestBody` is a `dict` at runtime, so setting `data[system_instruction_key]` works for both paths. ## Test plan - Native Gemini + custom `api_base` with a `system` message now sends `systemInstruction` in the JSON body. - Vertex AI path unchanged: still sends `system_instruction`. - Docstring-only behavioral change; no unit test needed beyond verifying the key in the serialized request. Fixes #37028

signal.title: fix(proxy): strip extra_headers/headers/aws_session_token from GET /health (gh-36898)
signal.text: ## Summary - `GET /health` already stripped `api_key` from each deployment row via `ILLEGAL_DISPLAY_PARAMS`, but `extra_headers`, `headers`, and `aws_session_token` were never added to that list, so `GET /health` leaked provider credentials (Azure `api-key`, Google `x-goog-api-key`, Bearer tokens, AWS session tokens) in plaintext to any caller — even without a master key. - Add those three fields to `ILLEGAL_DISPLAY_PARAMS` so `_clean_endpoint_data()` omits them for all callers, matching how `api_key` is already handled. ## Test plan - tests/test_litellm/proxy/health_endpoints/test_health_endpoints.py::test_clean_endpoint_data_strips_extra_headers_and_aws_session_token Fixes #36898

signal.title: [Bug]: /v1/audio/speech returns HTTP 500 for client-side (4xx) errors while /v1/audio/transcriptions returns the correct status
signal.text: ### Note on root cause The status-code mechanism below is **verified by reading the code** on `upstream/main`. The concrete trigger (an Azure `gpt-audio` deployment rejecting the speech operation) is **verified from live proxy tracebacks and access logs**. The generalization to "all client-side errors on this route" is **inferred** from the code path; I directly observed only the `BadRequestError` / `OperationNotSupported` case. ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues Searched several angles (`audio/speech 500`, `gpt-audio OperationNotSupported`, `aspeech status code`, `tts 500 instead of 400`, `audio speech BadRequest`); no existing issue or PR covers this. The `stream_chunk_builder` 500 on `/v1/messages` (#32951) is unrelated (different route and root cause). ### What happened A `POST /v1/audio/speech` request whose underlying provider call fails with a client error (HTTP 4xx) is surfaced to the caller as **HTTP 500** with a generic body: ```json {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"internal_server_error"}} ``` The same underlying error on `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` is correctly surfaced as **HTTP 400** with the real provider message. So the two sibling audio routes disagree on status mapping, and the speech route both returns the wrong class (5xx for a client error, which inflates server-error metrics/alarms) and hides the actionable message from the caller. Root cause, verified by reading `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py` on `upstream/main`: - `audio_speech`'s `except` block ends with a bare `raise e` (v1.92.0 tree: `proxy_server.py:9106`). A raw `litellm.BadRequestError` is not a `ProxyException`/`HTTPException`, so it falls through to the catch-all `@app.exception_handler(Exception)` -> `otel_unhandled_exception_handler` (`proxy_server.py:1391`), which hardcodes `status_code=500` and the generic "Internal server error" body. - `audio_transcriptions`'s `except` block instead wraps the error: `raise ProxyException(message=..., code=getattr(e, "status_code", ...))` (`proxy_server.py:9161`). That is caught by `@app.exception_handler(ProxyException)` (`proxy_server.py:1337`), which emits the real status code (400). ### Steps to reproduce Observed case (production): an Azure `gpt-audio` deployment (the `gpt-audio` / `gpt-audio-mini` / `gpt-audio-1.5` family are realtime/chat audio models, not TTS/STT) returns `400 OperationNotSupported` for the speech operation. The proxy logged it as `litellm.BadRequestError` (status_code 400) but returned 500. The identical rejection on `/v1/audio/transcriptions` returned 400. Minimal LiteLLM-side repro (any provider that raises a 4xx on the speech call works; the point is a `litellm.BadRequestError` reaching the `audio_speech` handler): ```bash # Route /v1/audio/speech to a model whose provider rejects the request with a 400 # (e.g. a model that does not support the speech operation, or an invalid `voice`). curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:4000/v1/audio/speech \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"<model-that-provider-rejects-for-speech>","input":"hello","voice":"alloy"}' # Actual: 500 (generic "Internal server error") # Expected: 400 (provider's BadRequest message), matching /v1/audio/transcriptions ``` ### Relevant log output ```shell # app layer (litellm.BadRequestError, status_code 400) - speech litellm.proxy.proxy_server.audio_speech(): Exception occured - litellm.BadRequestError: AzureException - The audioSpeech operation does not work with the specified model, gpt-audio. Please choose different model and try again.. Received Model Group=<redacted> # access log - same underlying error, two different statuses - "POST /v1/audio/speech HTTP/1.1" 500 - "POST /v1/audio/transcriptions HTTP/1.1" 400 ``` ### What part of LiteLLM Proxy ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_ ### Version `v1.92.0`. Confirmed the bare `raise e` in `audio_speech` is still present (unfixed) on `upstream/main`, `litellm_internal_staging`, and `litellm_oss_staging_06_06_2026` as of 2026-07-12. ### Suggested fix (for maintainers) Assuming the hypothesis holds, make `audio_speech`'s `except` mirror `audio_transcriptions`: replace the bare `raise e` with a `ProxyException` that carries the upstream status, e.g. ```python raise ProxyException( message=getattr(e, "message", str(e)), type=getattr(e, "type", "None"), param=getattr(e, "param", "None"), code=getattr(e, "status_code", 500), ) ``` That returns 400 for client errors and unmasks the real provider message, at parity with the transcriptions route.

signal.title: fix(anthropic-messages): suppress reasoning_content→thinking block when thinking is absent/disabled
signal.text: ## Summary When a client omits the Anthropic `thinking` request parameter (or sends `{type: disabled}`), the Anthropic Messages contract is that thinking is off. The experimental pass-through adapter's translation of a non-Anthropic backend's `reasoning_content` into a `thinking` content block previously ignored this entirely, unconditionally converting any `reasoning_content` into a `thinking` block regardless of what the client asked for. Backends that reason unconditionally (e.g. vLLM-served Qwen3/DeepSeek-R1 without an explicit `enable_thinking=false` at the inference-server layer) would therefore produce unexpected `thinking` blocks that Anthropic-SDK-based clients (including Claude Code) do not expect and can reject with `Content block is not a thinking block` errors. ## Changes - **handler.py**: Compute `thinking_disabled` boolean from the `thinking` param in both async and sync handler entry points, thread through all 4 call sites (async/sync × streaming/non-streaming). - **transformation.py**: Accept `thinking_disabled: bool = False` on 7 functions in the translation call chain; gate 4 `reasoning_content`→`thinking` conversion branches on `not thinking_disabled`. - **streaming_iterator.py**: Accept `thinking_disabled` in `AnthropicStreamWrapper.__init__`, thread through all 3 internal call sites (`__next__`, `__anext__`, and the direct call inside `_should_start_new_content_block` that bypasses the main translation entry point). - **Tests**: 21 new regression tests (5 for classifier/emitter gating, 16 for handler-level computation truth table). Default `False` on every new parameter preserves existing behavior for any caller that doesn't pass it explicitly. ## Files - `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/handler.py` - `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/transformation.py` - `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/streaming_iterator.py` - `tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/test_anthropic_experimental_pass_through_adapters_transformation.py` - `tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/test_handler_thinking_disabled.py` (new)

signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Mixed-type metadata sets break JSON log serialization - A TypeError prevents the log record from being emitted How it solves it: - Sort serialized set values by their JSON representation - Preserve deterministic output across heterogeneous values ## User Flow Before: a Python developer using JSON logs loses a record when metadata contains mixed set values 1. They enable JSON logging in their Python application 2. They emit an INFO record with label metadata containing `"beta"`, `7`, and `None` 3. Logging raises `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'NoneType'` After: the same record is emitted as valid JSON with every label preserved 1. They enable JSON logging in their Python application 2. They emit the same INFO record with label metadata containing `"beta"`, `7`, and `None` 3. signal.title: test: invalidate memoized model-cost lookups between unit tests
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Pricing unit tests flake on cost-map values - `get_model_info` memoization survives cost-map swaps between tests - CI saw exactly-2x Vertex batch cost mismatches How it solves it: - Invalidate model-cost memoization around every unit test - Makes test order irrelevant for pricing assertions ## User Flow No user-facing behavior changes, this only touches the unit test isolation fixture, so there is no before/after flow for an end user ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## CI evidence `tests/test_litellm/batches/test_batch_utils.py::test_handle_completed_vertex_batch_computes_cost_usage_and_models` failed in "Unit Tests: MCP, Secrets, Containers & Misc" with ``` assert 3.9375e-05 == 7.875e-05 ± 7.9e-11 ``` on https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/32213874586 (attempt 2, SHA 2e1d4077) and again on https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/32235776332, while the same test at the same and adjacent SHAs passed elsewhere in the window and passes locally with no edits ## Mechanism The misc unit workflow does not set `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP`, so `litellm.model_cost` is fetched over the network at import. `litellm.get_model_info` memoizes `ModelInfo` in `_cached_get_model_info`, keyed only on model, provider, and api_base, and the only invalidation hook is `_invalidate_model_cost_lowercase_map`, which nothing calls when a test rebinds `litellm.model_cost` itself. Around a dozen tests in the same workflow paths do exactly that, `litellm.model_cost = litellm.get_model_cost_map(url="")`, so they prime the memo from the packaged map, then `isolate_litellm_state` restores the network-fetched map attribute and leaves the memo pointing at the other map. Under `-n 2 --dist loadscope` the ordering decides whether a pricing test lands after such a polluter, so the Vertex batch test computed cost from the packaged map's batch rates while its expectation read the network map, and the two differed by exactly the 2x Vertex price halving that had landed on the branch but not yet on the map served from `main`, hence `3.9375e-05` vs `7.875e-05` ## Fix ```py def isolate_litellm_state(): ... _reset_module_level_aws_auth_caches() + litellm_utils_module._invalidate_model_cost_lowercase_map() ... yield ... litellm_utils_module._runtime_registered_model_cost.update(original_runtime_registered_model_cost) + litellm_utils_module._invalidate_model_cost_lowercase_map() ``` Every test now starts and ends with the memoized model info consistent with whatever `litellm.model_cost` currently is, which makes ordering irrelevant instead of hiding the mismatch. No test assertion was relaxed, no rerun, marker, skip, or sleep was added ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A test-isolation leak has no proxy-visible surface, so this is a deterministic library-level reproduction of the leaked state rather than a live LLM call, plus a mutation check that the covered behavior is still enforced ### Before (c696fdfb05) #### The memo keeps pricing from a swapped-out cost map 1. Run ```bash LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync python -c ' import copy, litellm m = copy.deepcopy(litellm.model_cost) e = m["vertex_ai/gemini-3.6-flash"] for f in ("input_cost_per_token", "output_cost_per_token", "input_cost_per_token_batches", "output_cost_per_token_batches"): e[f] *= 2 orig = litellm.model_cost litellm.model_cost = m litellm.get_model_info(model="gemini-3.6-flash", custom_llm_provider="vertex_ai") litellm.model_cost = orig print("memo ", litellm.get_model_info(model="gemini-3.6-flash", custom_llm_provider="vertex_ai")["input_cost_per_token_batches"]) print("live map", litellm.model_cost["vertex_ai/gemini-3.6-flash"]["input_cost_per_token_batches"])' ``` 2. Observed, the two sources disagree by 2x, which is what the CI failure asserted on ``` memo 7.5e-07 live map 3.75e-07 ``` 3. Reproduced inside pytest as an ordering flake, a preceding test that swaps the cost map and prices a Vertex batch line leaves the next test computing `7.875e-05` where the live map says `3.9375e-05` ### After (2fb04fd7e2) #### The memo keeps pricing from a swapped-out cost map 1. Same pytest ordering repro, the following test now computes `3.9375e-05` against a live map that says `3.9375e-05`, and the leak cannot cross a test boundary because the fixture invalidates on both sides 2. Mutation check that the assertion still bites, changing `batch_cost_calculator` to bill batch lines at the standard input rate makes the Vertex batch test fail with `assert 5.0625e-05 == 3.9375e-05`, and reverting restores it ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Three unrelated failures in that suite predate this branch ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/032cc679b3934ebbb3ff7a2d90b4d1ab

signal.title: fix(fireworks): strip pattern, title, default:null from tool param schemas
signal.text: ## Summary Fireworks AI rejects tool parameter schemas containing `pattern`, `title`, or `default: null`, returning 400 errors: - **`pattern`**: `"Conflict in schema definitions for key 'pattern'"` — occurs when LiteLLM's Anthropic→OpenAI translation injects a second `pattern` on a field that already has one from the client (e.g. Claude Code sends `^[^\n\r]*$`, LiteLLM adds `^[\s\S]{0,300}$`). Fireworks' grammar compiler sees two conflicting patterns and rejects the request. Reported by a Fireworks customer using Claude Code + LiteLLM + `kimi-k3`. - **`title` / `default: null`**: `"JSON Schema not supported: could not understand the instance {'default': None, 'title': 'Page Size'}"` — auto-emitted by Pydantic models from MCP servers. See #27821 and #28149. The existing `_transform_tools` only popped `strict` and inlined legacy `$ref` defs. The Anthropic path already strips these keywords (`filter_anthropic_output_schema` in #22447 / #21045 / #34319), but the Fireworks path had no equivalent recursive sanitizer. ## Changes **`litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/chat/transformation.py`**: - Added `_FIREWORKS_TOOL_SCHEMA_STRIP_KEYS` class constant (`pattern`, `title`) - Added `_sanitize_tool_schema` static method that recursively walks `properties`, `items`, `anyOf`/`allOf`/`oneOf`, and `$defs` to strip: - `pattern` (always removed — Fireworks compiles it into a constrained-decoding grammar; conflicts arise when multiple patterns land on the same field) - `title` (always removed) - `default` (only when value is `None`; non-null defaults preserved) - Wired into `_transform_tools` after the existing `unpack_legacy_defs` call **`tests/test_litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/chat/test_fireworks_schema_sanitize.py`**: - 20 new unit + integration tests covering: top-level removal, nested properties, array items, anyOf/allOf/oneOf, $defs, deeply nested schemas, field preservation, non-null default preservation (including falsy `False`), no-op on clean schemas, non-function tools, tools without parameters, and combined strict+pattern stripping ## Design decisions - **Fireworks-only**: The sanitizer lives on `FireworksAIConfig`, not in shared utils, so no other provider's tool schemas are affected. - **Preserves non-null defaults**: Only `default: null` is stripped. `{"default": 10}` and `{"default": False}` survive (Fireworks specifically chokes on null defaults). - **Recursive**: Handles arbitrarily nested schemas (MCP tools and Claude Code often produce complex schemas). - **Consistent with Anthropic path**: The Anthropic sanitizer already strips `pattern`, `title`-adjacent keywords, and other constrained-decoding constraints. This brings the Fireworks path to parity. ## Related issues - Closes #27821 - Closes #28149 - Related: #26692 (legacy `$ref` defs — already fixed), #22447 / #21045 / #34319 (Anthropic path schema filtering) ## Test plan - [x] `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/chat/test_fireworks_schema_sanitize.py` — 20 passed - [x] `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/fireworks_ai/chat/` — 108 passed (16 pre-existing caplog failures deselected, unrelated to this change) - [x] Black formatted Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signal.title: [Bug]: provider_budget_config reports budget_reset_at ~57 years in the future without Redis
signal.text: ### What happened? With `provider_budget_config` and **no Redis configured**, `GET /provider/budgets` reports a `budget_reset_at` roughly 57 years in the future, so a monthly budget effectively never resets. Config: ```yaml router_settings: provider_budget_config: openrouter: budget_limit: 5 time_period: 30d ``` Response: ```json {"providers":{"openrouter":{"budget_limit":5.0,"time_period":"30d", "spend":4.8888e-06,"budget_reset_at":"2083-05-04T16:04:00.635943+00:00"}}} ``` Same result with `time_period: 1mo` (`2083-05-05T15:39:32`), so it is not specific to the period format. Today's date when this was captured: 2026-08-18. ### Root cause `async_get_ttl` means different things in the two cache backends, and `_get_current_provider_budget_reset_at` assumes the Redis meaning: - `RedisCache.async_get_ttl()` returns **remaining seconds** (Redis `TTL`). - `InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl()` returns `self.ttl_dict.get(key)` — and `ttl_dict` stores an **absolute expiry timestamp**: `self.ttl_dict[key] = time.time() + float(kwargs["ttl"])` (`litellm/caching/in_memory_cache.py`). `litellm/router_strategy/budget_limiter.py`: ```python if self.dual_cache.redis_cache: ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.redis_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key) else: ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key) if ttl_seconds is None: return None return (datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(seconds=ttl_seconds)).isoformat() ``` Without Redis, `ttl_seconds` is an absolute unix timestamp (~1.79e9), so the result is `now + ~56.7 years` — which matches the observed 2083. The budget limit itself works; only the reported reset time (and therefore the reset window for in-memory deployments) is wrong. ### Suggested fix Either make `InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl` return remaining seconds like the Redis backend does, or convert at the call site: ```python ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key) ttl_seconds = ttl_seconds - time.time() # in-memory stores absolute expiry ``` The first option is preferable — `async_get_ttl` returning different units per backend is a trap for any other caller. ### Relevant log output ``` LiteLLM.LoggingError: [Non-Blocking] Exception occurred while success logging File ".../litellm/router_strategy/budget_limiter.py", line 412, in async_log_success_event raise ValueError("custom_llm_provider is required") ValueError: custom_llm_provider is required ``` Separate but related observation while testing the same feature: every request through a `pass_through_endpoints` route raises the above in `budget_limiter.async_log_success_event`, so pass-through traffic is not counted toward provider budgets at all. Happy to file that separately if useful. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: feat(cost): support time-based off-peak pricing in cost calculation
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Some providers discount per-token rates during a daily window - The cost map only modeled one static rate per model - Logged spend therefore overstates cost inside that window How it solves it: - A model entry can carry an `off_peak_pricing` block - `hours_utc` takes one `"HH:MM-HH:MM"` window or a list - Windows may wrap past midnight; unset rates fall back - An off-peak rate replaces the tier or threshold rate - Timezone-aware timestamps are normalized to UTC before comparing ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin serving a provider that discounts by time of day sees the same spend logged around the clock, so their cost dashboard overstates what the provider actually invoices 1. They add the deployment to their config with a single `input_cost_per_token` and `output_cost_per_token` 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with that model at 18:00 UTC, inside the provider's published discount window 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see the request billed at the full daytime rate 4. They send the same request again at 12:00 UTC and see an identical spend figure, so the discount never shows up anywhere After: the same two requests bill differently, so logged spend tracks the provider invoice 1. They add `off_peak_pricing` to the deployment, giving `hours_utc` plus the discounted per-token rates 2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions at 18:00 UTC 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows that request at the discounted rate 4. They send it again at 12:00 UTC and see the standard rate, so the two windows are visibly different ## Relevant issues Fixes #31606 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The feature is time-gated, so the only thing that changes between two otherwise identical calls is the clock. Captured at 7621e0df4e, asking the cost calculator for the same usage at four different times: ```python from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone import litellm from litellm.litellm_core_utils.llm_cost_calc.utils import _get_token_base_cost from litellm.types.utils import Usage litellm.register_model( { "offpeak-demo": { "litellm_provider": "openai", "mode": "chat", "input_cost_per_token": 1e-6, "output_cost_per_token": 2e-6, "off_peak_pricing": { "hours_utc": "16:30-00:30", "input_cost_per_token": 5e-7, "output_cost_per_token": 1e-6, }, } } ) info = litellm.get_model_info(model="offpeak-demo") usage = Usage(prompt_tokens=100, completion_tokens=50, total_tokens=150) for label, when in [ ("18:00 UTC (inside window)", datetime(2026, 1, 1, 18, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)), ("12:00 UTC (outside window)", datetime(2026, 1, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)), ("00:15 UTC (past midnight wrap)", datetime(2026, 1, 1, 0, 15, tzinfo=timezone.utc)), ("02:00 UTC+8 (same instant as 18:00 UTC)", datetime(2026, 1, 2, 2, 0, tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=8)))), ]: print(label, _get_token_base_cost(info, usage, current_time=when)[:2]) ``` ``` 18:00 UTC (inside window) (5e-07, 1e-06) 12:00 UTC (outside window) (1e-06, 2e-06) 00:15 UTC (past midnight wrap) (5e-07, 1e-06) 02:00 UTC+8 (same instant as 18:00 UTC) (5e-07, 1e-06) ``` The last row is the timezone case: an aware timestamp in UTC+8 lands on the same instant as 18:00 UTC and gets the discount, rather than being compared as a bare 02:00 wall clock and missing the window To see it end to end, put the same `off_peak_pricing` block on a deployment in your proxy config, set `hours_utc` so it covers the current UTC time, send a real request to /v1/chat/completions, and check the spend on /ui/?page=logs against the same request made outside the window ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Windows are UTC only, no named timezones - Naive timestamps are treated as already being UTC - Not exposed yet on deployment-level custom pricing params - Boundary-crossing requests bill at completion time, not request start - Off-peak replaces tier rates rather than discounting them proportionally ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(mcp): tolerate invalid content blocks in tools/call results
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A single malformed content block fails an entire MCP `tools/call` result - Client returns a raw `ValidationError` traceback instead of any content How it solves it: - Degrade only the invalid content block to text instead of raising - Every valid content block in the result is left untouched ## User Flow Before: a developer calling a tool on a non-compliant upstream MCP server through the gateway gets an error instead of the tool's real output 1. They send a `tools/call` JSON-RPC request for a tool backed by an Azure DevOps MCP server to the gateway's MCP endpoint 2. The upstream server's response includes a resource content item using a relative path instead of a full URI, which the MCP client library rejects 3. The gateway's response comes back with `"isError": true` and a single `text` block containing a raw pydantic `ValidationError` traceback, not the tool's actual output After: the same call returns the tool's real output even though the upstream's response is still not fully spec-compliant 1. They send the same `tools/call` JSON-RPC request for the same tool to the same MCP endpoint 2. The upstream server's response still contains that same non-compliant resource content item 3. The gateway's response now comes back with `"isError": false` and the tool's actual output as `text` content ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review The lint/format/unit-test box is left unchecked deliberately: this repo's build backend (`maturin`, compiling `litellm-rust`) requires a local Rust toolchain that wasn't available in the environment this PR was written in, so `make lint` / `make test-unit` could not be run locally. The new test was verified with a standalone script exercising the same `mcp==1.28.1` model classes and the same `_ScriptedUpstream`/`_ScriptedClient` harness logic used in the actual test file, not through `pytest` itself. Flagging this explicitly rather than checking a box I couldn't verify; happy to fix anything CI turns up. ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This is not the live-proxy curl proof this template normally asks for. A local proxy could not be built for the same Rust-toolchain reason noted above. What follows is real evidence gathered against a live, non-compliant upstream MCP server, plus a real run of this fix's exact logic against that captured payload, at the commit above. **Before (parent commit `423b791ee0395815050998dd73542445350ab792`): the real failure, captured live** An MCP `tools/call` request for a `repo_file` tool backed by an Azure DevOps MCP server (`mcp.dev.azure.com`), sent with a real, valid upstream token, returns this content block verbatim: ```json {"type":"resource","resource":{"uri":"/templates/ev.job/template/docker-compose.yml","mimeType":"text/plain","blob":"dmVyc2lvbjogJzIuNCcK..."}} ``` Feeding that exact block into `mcp==1.28.1`'s `CallToolResult.model_validate` (the same call `ClientSession.call_tool` makes internally) raises: ``` pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 14 validation errors for CallToolResult content.0.TextContent.type Input should be 'text' [type=literal_error, input_value='resource', input_type=str] ... content.0.EmbeddedResource.resource.TextResourceContents.uri Input should be a valid URL, relative URL without a base [type=url_parsing, input_value='/templates/ev.job/template/docker-compose.yml', input_type=str] ... ``` This is exactly the `ValidationError` that `MCPClient.call_tool`'s except-block turns into the `isError: true` text block described above. **After (this PR, commit `3b7d9e74cbd8561bf62041c5888168ec64a0779c`): the same payload, run through the new model** ``` $ python -c " from litellm.experimental_mcp_client.tolerant_result import TolerantCallToolResult payload = {'content': [{'type': 'resource', 'resource': { 'uri': '/templates/ev.job/template/docker-compose.yml', 'mimeType': 'text/plain', 'blob': 'dmVyc2lvbjogJzIuNCcK', }}], 'isError': False} result = TolerantCallToolResult.model_validate(payload) print(result.content[0].type, repr(result.content[0].text)) " text "version: '2.4'\n" ``` No exception. `isError` stays `False`. The content that used to be silently discarded behind a traceback comes through as the actual decoded text. The new test in this PR, `TestCallToolToleratesMalformedContentBlocks::test_relative_uri_resource_degrades_to_text_instead_of_raising`, asserts this same outcome through the real `ClientSession`-derived class and real anyio streams via `_ScriptedUpstream`/`_ScriptedClient`, not a hand-built result object; it could not be executed via `pytest` here for the Rust-toolchain reason above, so this is not a substitute for CI actually running it, only evidence that the logic it exercises behaves as asserted. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - `make lint` / `make test-unit` not run locally; blocked on this repo's Rust/maturin build requirement - `TolerantClientSession.call_tool` mirrors `mcp==1.28.1`'s method body verbatim (no override seam exists); a later `mcp` release changing that method won't automatically propagate - Uses `Any`/`Mapping[str, Any]`/`object` for the genuinely untyped external data at this one boundary; flagging in case `reportAny` disagrees ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

Real Vertex Agent Platform calls, real video generation, no mocks. The real project (`my-real-project` here) only ever lives in the deployment config, never in the caller's URL. 1. Create, short form, no project or location in the URL (same shape as `generateContent`): ``` $ curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:4000/vertex_ai/v1beta1/interactions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gemini-omni-flash-preview","background":true,"input":[{"type":"text","text":"A red balloon over a city at sunset"}],"generation_config":{"video_config":{"task":"text_to_video"}},"response_format":{"type":"video","aspect_ratio":"16:9","duration":"5s"}}' {"id": "", "status": "in_progress", "object": "interaction"} ``` The returned id is opaque; decoding it shows it carries the project and location litellm resolved from the body's model, plus the raw Vertex id: ``` litellm_proxy:vertex_interaction;project,my-real-project;location,global;raw_id,video- ``` The proxy `--detailed_debug` log confirms litellm filled in the resolved project and location for the projectless URL: ``` updated url https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/my-real-project/locations/global/interactions ``` 2. Poll, short form, still no project in the URL, using the opaque id: ``` $ curl -sS "http://localhost:4000/vertex_ai/v1beta1/interactions/" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" {"id": "", "status": "completed", ... "steps":[{... "content":[{"type":"video", "data":""}]}], "usage":{"total_tokens":29292}} ``` It reaches `completed` and returns the video. The debug log shows the poll routed back to the originating project with the raw id restored: ``` updated url https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/my-real-project/locations/global/interactions/video- ``` The response `id` is byte-for-byte the opaque id the caller already holds, so polling is stable. 3. The full form also works, and a wrong or placeholder project in the URL is corrected from the body's model (this is the exact case that fails today). `POST /vertex_ai/v1beta1/projects/whatever/locations/global/interactions` with the real model in the body is rewritten to `projects/my-real-project/...` just like the short form above. 4. Negative control: with `vertex_interactions_passthrough_auto_routing` off, a create whose URL project is not a configured passthrough credential fails, reproducing today's behavior: ``` $ curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:4000/vertex_ai/v1beta1/projects/not-configured/locations/global/interactions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{...}' HTTP 401 [{"error":{"code":401,"message":"Request had invalid authentication credentials. Expected OAuth 2 access token, login cookie or other valid authentication credential ...","status":"UNAUTHENTICATED"}}] ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes On the Vertex AI pass-through route, a `generateContent` request auto-corrects the GCP project and location from the model id embedded in the URL, so callers can send a placeholder project and still reach the right backend. The Interactions API cannot use that path: on create the model lives in the request body, and get/delete/cancel carry neither a model nor a body. Because the pass-through is stateless and selects credentials purely from the URL's `{project}-{location}`, an async interaction created under one project fails to poll unless the caller reconstructs the exact same project in every follow-up URL. This adds opt-in auto-routing behind `general_settings: vertex_interactions_passthrough_auto_routing` (default off). A stateless base64 codec encodes the project, location, and raw provider id into the interaction id returned to the caller. On create, the project and location are resolved from the body's model through the router; a decoded `previous_interaction_id` is used as a fallback. On get/delete/cancel, the opaque id is decoded to route back to the originating project, and the raw id is restored before forwarding upstream. The encoding is deterministic, so a poll re-encodes to the identical id the caller already holds. There is no database, no tenant isolation, and no enterprise dependency; when the flag is off the route behaves exactly as it does today. Both URL forms are supported: the full `.../projects/{p}/locations/{l}/interactions` and, like `generateContent`, the short `/vertex_ai/v1beta1/interactions` with no project or location in the path (litellm fills them in from the resolved deployment, or from the opaque id on a follow-up call). ## Review follow-up Rebased onto the current `litellm_internal_staging` and addressed the request-body preservation review finding. If `request.json()` fails, interactions routing now returns without writing `LITELLM_PASS_THROUGH_CUSTOM_BODY_STATE_KEY`, so the original payload remains available to the pass-through handler. The regression test asserts that the state key is absent on this path. Local verification after the rebase: `make pre-commit` passed, and 136 focused Vertex interactions/common-utils tests passed.

signal.title: fix(proxy): preserve timezone offsets when resetting multi-window budgets
signal.text: ## Summary `ResetBudgetJob.reset_budget_windows()` drops the timezone offset stored in `budget_limits[].reset_at`, then compares it with a naive UTC timestamp. This delays resets for non-UTC configured budget timezones. ## Current code In `litellm/proxy/common_utils/reset_budget_job.py`: ```python reset_at = datetime.fromisoformat(reset_at_str.replace("Z", "+00:00")).replace(tzinfo=None) if reset_at > now: return False # ... now = datetime.utcnow() ``` ## Reproduction Configure a non-UTC budget reset timezone, for example `Asia/Shanghai` / `Asia/Singapore` (UTC+8), and create a multi-window budget: ```json { "budget_duration": "24h", "max_budget": 100, "reset_at": "2026-08-20T00:00:00+08:00" } ``` At `2026-08-19 16:00:00 UTC`, the window is due, because this is exactly `2026-08-20 00:00:00+08:00`. The current code removes `+08:00`, yielding `2026-08-20 00:00:00` (naive), then compares it to `2026-08-19 16:00:00` (naive UTC). It considers the window unexpired and delays the reset until `2026-08-20 00:00:00 UTC` (08:00 local time). ## Impact This affects `budget_limits` / Budget Windows for Keys and Teams. A daily or monthly window configured for local midnight may continue enforcing the previous window for up to the timezone offset after its intended reset boundary. ## Expected behavior - Preserve the parsed offset for `reset_at`. - Use `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` for `now`. - Convert both values to aware UTC before comparing. - Define a compatibility policy for legacy offset-less values (for example, interpret them as UTC and log a warning). - Reset only the expired window; other windows (e.g. `30d`) must remain untouched. ## Suggested tests 1. `2026-08-20T00:00:00+08:00` does not reset at `2026-08-19 15:59 UTC`. 2. The same window resets immediately at `2026-08-19 16:00 UTC`. 3. A `Z` timestamp resets at the correct UTC boundary. 4. Legacy offset-less timestamps follow the documented compatibility behavior. 5. With `24h` and `30d` windows, expiring `24h` only clears its matching memory/Redis counter. The current test coverage constructs only `Z` timestamps and therefore does not cover this offset-preservation case.

signal.title: fix(ui): gate the pass-through guardrail field inputs when the section is disabled
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Disabling the guardrails section left two inputs fully typeable - Every prop crossed to those inputs except the enforcing one - `TagsInput`'s own `disabled` prop had no test at all How it solves it: - Pass `disabled` to both field-targeting `TagsInput` controls - Add a test that types into the control, not one asserting an attribute - Enabled cases act as the liveness gate for the disabled ones ## User Flow This gate is latent today. Neither call site passes `disabled`, so no end user can currently reach either flow. Both lists below describe the flow a caller gets the moment it passes the prop, which is what this PR changes. Before: an admin viewing a read-only pass-through endpoint sees a greyed-out guardrails section and can still edit the parts of it that matter 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints, click the "Pass-Through Endpoints" tab and open an endpoint whose guardrails section is rendered disabled 2. The guardrail picker is greyed out and the "+ query", "+ documents[*]" and "+ results[*]" buttons are all unclickable, so the section reads as locked 3. They click into the "Request Fields (pre_call)" box, type `query` and press comma 4. The tag is accepted and appears as a chip, and the same works in "Response Fields (post_call)" 5. The section reports itself as locked while still taking edits, so what is on screen no longer matches what is enforced After: the same section refuses every edit, matching what it says about itself 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints, click the "Pass-Through Endpoints" tab and open the same endpoint 2. The guardrail picker is greyed out and the three quick-add buttons are unclickable, exactly as before 3. They click into the "Request Fields (pre_call)" box and type `query` followed by a comma 4. Nothing is entered, no chip appears, and the same holds for "Response Fields (post_call)" 5. Typing, pressing Enter and clicking away all leave the field untouched, so the section is locked in the way it already looked ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Reaching this needs a one-line local edit, because no call site passes `disabled` yet, so there is no route that shows it today. Steps for both sides: ### Before (c94d692864) #### Request and response field targeting accept input while the section is disabled 1. Open http://localhost:3000/models-and-endpoints, click the "Pass-Through Endpoints" tab, then "+ Add Pass-Through Endpoint" 3. Pick any guardrail so the "Field Targeting (Optional)" card appears 4.
