signal.title: [Bug]: Responses API `reasoning: {"summary": ...}` crashes ollama_chat with `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'`
signal.text: ## What happened? Calling `/v1/responses` against an `ollama_chat/*` model with a `reasoning` object that contains a `summary` key fails with `litellm.APIConnectionError: unhashable type: 'dict'`. This makes **Codex CLI (`wire_api = "responses"`) unusable against a LiteLLM proxy backed by Ollama** — Codex sends `reasoning: {"summary": "auto"}` on every request, so every call fails and the client falls into a reconnect loop (`ERROR: Reconnecting... 1/5 … 5/5`). ## Root cause Two pieces of code disagree about the type of `reasoning_effort`. **1. The Responses→Chat bridge deliberately keeps the whole dict when `summary` is present** (`litellm/responses/litellm_completion_transformation/transformation.py`, ~L259-274): ```python if isinstance(reasoning_param, dict): # reasoning can be {"effort": "low|medium|high", "summary": "detailed"} # Keep the full dict when summary is set so the responses API bridge can # forward it; otherwise use the effort string for chat completion (e.g. Gemini). if "summary" in reasoning_param: reasoning_effort = reasoning_param # <-- dict elif "effort" in reasoning_param: reasoning_effort = reasoning_param.get("effort") # <-- str ``` **2. `OllamaChatConfig.map_openai_params` assumes it is always a string** (`litellm/llms/ollama/chat/transformation.py`, ~L172-176): ```python if param == "reasoning_effort" and value is not None: if model.startswith("gpt-oss"): optional_params["think"] = value else: optional_params["think"] = value in {"low", "medium", "high"} # <-- set membership ``` `value in {...}` hashes `value`. When `value` is the preserved dict, this raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'`. Note this is **not** the same as #15059 / PR #15465 (which corrected *which* `think` value is produced for a valid effort string). Those touch the same lines but assume `value` is a string; this report is about `value` being a `dict` at all. PR #15465's mapping would hit the identical crash. ## Reproduction Minimal matrix against an `ollama_chat/*` model. Only the presence of `summary` matters — `tools`, `stream`, `store`, `include`, and `text` are all irrelevant. | Request body (`/v1/responses`) | Result | |---|---| | `{"model": M, "input": "say OK"}` | OK | | `{"model": M, "input": "say OK", "reasoning": {"effort": "medium"}}` | OK | | `{"model": M, "input": "say OK", "reasoning": {"summary": "auto"}}` | **`unhashable type: 'dict'`** | | `{"model": M, "input": "say OK", "reasoning": {"effort": "medium", "summary": "auto"}}` | **`unhashable type: 'dict'`** | ```bash curl -s -X POST http://<proxy>/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"my-ollama-alias","input":"say OK","reasoning":{"summary":"auto"}}' ``` `config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: my-ollama-alias litellm_params: model: ollama_chat/<any-model> api_base: http://127.0.0.1:11434 ``` ## Relevant log output ``` litellm.proxy.proxy_server._handle_llm_api_exception(): Exception occured - litellm.APIConnectionError: unhashable type: 'dict' Traceback (most recent call last): File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/main.py", line 5314, in completion optional_params = get_optional_params(**optional_param_args, **non_default_params) File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/utils.py", line 4146, in get_optional_params optional_params = litellm.OllamaChatConfig().map_openai_params( File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/llms/ollama/chat/transformation.py", line 176, in map_openai_params optional_params["think"] = value in {"low", "medium", "high"} ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict' ``` ## Suggested fix Guard the dict case in `OllamaChatConfig.map_openai_params` — pull `effort` out when a dict arrives, and treat a summary-only object as "no explicit effort": ```python if param == "reasoning_effort" and value is not None: if isinstance(value, dict): value = value.get("effort") if value is None: pass elif model.startswith("gpt-oss"): optional_params["think"] = value else: optional_params["think"] = value in {"low", "medium", "high"} ``` Other providers that read `reasoning_effort` off the Responses bridge likely need the same guard, since the bridge can hand any of them a dict. ## Workaround Drop the parameter before it reaches the mapper, per model: ```yaml - model_name: my-ollama-alias litellm_params: model: ollama_chat/<any-model> api_base: http://127.0.0.1:11434 additional_drop_params: ["reasoning_effort"] ``` This runs before `map_openai_params`, so the crash site is never reached. Downside: callers lose `reasoning_effort` entirely for that alias (thinking reverts to the model default, and for Qwen3 the thinking text then leaks into `content` — we pair it with `think: false`). ## Are you a ML Ops Team? No. ## What LiteLLM version are you on? `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable` (image `468c25f35f3e`, pulled 2026-08-19). Both code paths quoted above are unchanged on `main` at time of filing. Backend: Ollama 0.32.14, model `Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL`. Client: Codex CLI 0.148 with `wire_api = "responses"`.

signal.title: fix(ui): rebuild nested and list paths in the mounted-field projection
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The mounted-field projection emitted one flat key per registered name - Credential paths and field-array rows both flattened, so the payload lost them - Splitting every name on `.` fixed that but diverged from antd - antd nests only for an array name, never for a dotted string How it solves it: - `name` accepts `string | readonly string[]` - An array nests, with a numeric segment as an array index - A string stays one literal key, dots included - 8 unit tests, including the flat-string case that pins the divergence ## User Flow Before: an admin saves an MCP server that authenticates with AWS SigV4, and the credentials never arrive 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and edit a server 2. They set Auth Type to AWS SigV4 and fill in region, access key and secret 3. They click Save Changes and the request returns 200 4. They reopen the same server and every credential field is empty again After: the same edit round-trips 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and edit a server 2. They set Auth Type to AWS SigV4 and fill in region, access key and secret 3. They click Save Changes and the request returns 200 4. They reopen the same server and the credentials they entered are still there ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The user flow above is the reproduction. The projection is a pure function, so behaviour is pinned by unit tests and the round-trip is what an admin would see once the MCP form graph consumes it. ``` MountedFormField.test.ts 8 passed create_key_button.integration.test.ts 65 passed ``` The second number is the one that matters. The create key form is the existing consumer of this projection, so it is the regression surface for a change to shared form plumbing. A passing count on a behaviour-preserving change cannot tell two trees apart, so that green was liveness-gated rather than trusted. With the projection gutted to return `undefined` for every value, the consumer suite goes red on a payload diff, `models` from `[]` to `undefined` and `team_id` from `null` to `undefined`, which is an assertion failure rather than a crash. The tree was restored byte-identical afterwards. That converts "their suite passed" into "their suite can detect this". ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) Behaviour that is not visible in the diff and that the next change here can undo silently. A numeric path segment is an array index, so `["env_vars","0","name"]` rebuilds an array holding one row rather than an object keyed `"0"`. A sparse index keeps its position instead of shifting later rows down. A mounted-but-unset field is emitted as a key holding `undefined` rather than omitted, which is what antd's own submit does, and the payload builder distinguishes an absent key from an explicitly undefined one. Nesting is opt-in because antd's `getNamePath` is `toArray`. `check_openapi_schema` registers names taken from a live `/openapi.json`, so its field set is a runtime input rather than source, and a spec property containing a dot would silently nest under an unconditional split. ## HANDOVER: the MCP form graph port is NOT in this PR This PR is the primitive only. The 92-field port of the MCP server form graph is not started beyond two fields, and this section exists so the next person does not rediscover any of it. **Measured surface.** 92 `<Form.Item` opens, 89 named, 3 unnamed, 57 distinct name literals, across 14 files under `mcp-servers/_components/`. Counting raw `Form.Item` occurrences gives 187 because it counts closing tags too. Use a brace-aware scan, not a regex: a `name=` on a continuation line and a `name={expr}` both defeat the obvious pattern. **Do the roots first.** This is the ordering constraint and it is not negotiable. `OpenAPIFormSection` takes an antd `FormInstance` and calls `setFieldsValue` and `resetFields` imperatively, and siblings thread the same instance, so children cannot move before their root provides react-hook-form equivalents. The two roots, `mcp_server_edit.tsx` and `CreateMCPServer.tsx`, are also the two largest files. **The graph is one atomic unit.** A half-ported form is two stores that do not merge: fields still on antd submit through `onFinish`, fields moved to react-hook-form submit through the projection, and the payload silently carries one set or the other. Two fields, `DcrBridgeToggle` and `TokenEndpointAuthMethodField`, are ported but deliberately NOT committed for this reason. Redo them with their root. **The port pattern.** `MountedFormField` is not a drop-in. Its children are a render prop receiving `{id, name, value, onChange, onBlur, aria-*}`, so every call site has its JSX children rewritten rather than its tag swapped. Every antd `Form.Item` child was receiving `value` and `onChange` it never declared, so a child that reads them without declaring them compiles fine and silently receives `undefined`. Nested names become arrays, not dotted strings. **Eight inversions need individual attention.** Six `valuePropName` and two `getValueProps`/`getValueFromEvent`. A reversed boolean does not fail to compile. `available_on_public_internet` is both an inversion and a coalesced key, which makes it the single most dangerous field in the graph. **Five keys cannot be proven by any payload assertion in the obvious way.** `allow_all_keys`, `available_on_public_internet`, `delegate_auth_to_upstream`, `oauth_passthrough` and `dcr_bridge` all resolve as `Boolean(raw ?? mcpServer.x)`. The `??` falls back to the stored server value when a binding is absent, so on a fixture where submitted equals stored, a deleted binding is invisible and a payload test passes either way. Any test covering the first two must set the stored value to the OPPOSITE of what the form submits; an equal-valued run is INVALID, not GREEN. Three of those five are forced to a constant by the payload builder and are therefore usable as harness controls rather than as coverage. `delegate_auth_to_upstream` is forced false when `auth_type` is not `oauth2`, `dcr_bridge` unless `isClientForwardedTokenMode`, and `oauth_passthrough` unless the server is none-auth with an `Authorization` extra header. On an `api_key` scenario all three are forced regardless of the submitted value, so deleting those bindings cannot move the payload and a red on them localises the defect to the harness. **The verification instrument changes when the code does.** Against antd, delete the `name` attribute: antd tolerates it by not registering the field, so the payload loses the key and the battery measures bindings. After the port that operator is degenerate, because `Controller` throws and the battery becomes a crash detector that reads as a clean sweep. Post-port, drop the binding from the mounted projection while the field still renders and validates. **Cost model, measured under contention so treat as upper bounds.** The edit suite is 19 tests at 43s, the create suite 71 tests at 214s. A per-binding battery rerunning a full suite is about 6.35 hours. `--bail=1` collapses a red mutation from 214s to 5s because only the first failure is needed for the verdict, so cost is dominated by survivors rather than by sweep size. Root scoping by import closure saves a further 18%: 19 edit-only fields, 21 create-only, 52 reachable from both. **One trap that cost real time.** The edit root binds all seven AWS credentials inline at `mcp_server_edit.tsx`, while `AwsSigV4Fields.tsx` is the create root's separate copy of the same seven. Same logical fields bound twice in two places, so a component-level import closure is blind to the edit root's copy. Port both and keep them consistent. **There are two field-array sites, not one.** `env_vars` in `EnvVarsSection` and `static_headers` in `MCPPermissionManagement`. The second feeds `reduceStaticHeaders`, so missing it is the same silent loss. **A port can turn a latent test defect into an intermittent one without touching it.** Measured by another lane on a byte-identical component, 6 runs per harness on the same machine and base: the antd `Form` harness failed 0 of 6, a native form with plain `useState` failed 1 of 6, and a native form with a react-hook-form `Controller` failed 5 of 6. The cause is not the port. Two cases were already racing the Base UI select popup, because `findByText` resolves as soon as the option text is in the DOM while the popup still carries `pointer-events: none` until its open transition settles, so a click landing in that window is rejected by user-event. The antd harness was hiding the race rather than avoiding it, and what moves the failure rate is render count, which a `Controller` raises. Any suite in this graph that drives a Base UI popup, select, dropdown, combobox or tooltip and asserts with `findBy*` before clicking carries the same latent race. The port will make it intermittent, it will present as "the port broke these tests", and the diff will look innocent. So: measure a popup-driving suite with REPEATED runs before concluding anything, because neither a single green nor a single red is evidence. Measure the pre-port harness too, which is how the component was shown not to have changed. The fix is `PointerEventsCheckLevel.Never` on the offending interaction, which relaxes only user-event's assertion about a CSS property jsdom never animates; look for a sibling case in the same file already using it for the same interaction, which is corroboration rather than invention. Then gate the fix: removing the click must turn the case red, and stubbing the callback must turn it red. A fix that makes a case vacuous leaves both gates green and tells you so. ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: PUT /v1/mcp/server silently nulls authorization_url, token_url, oauth2_flow when delegate_auth_to_upstream=true
signal.text: ### What happened? When an MCP server is configured with `auth_type: oauth2`, `oauth2_flow: authorization_code`, and `delegate_auth_to_upstream: true`, any subsequent update via `PUT /v1/mcp/server` silently discards `authorization_url`, `token_url`, and `oauth2_flow` — even when those exact fields are explicitly present with non-null values in the request body. The response (and the persisted record, confirmed via a follow-up `GET /v1/mcp/server`) always comes back with these three fields set to `null`. This breaks the Admin UI's own "Authorize & Fetch Token" convenience button (used to fetch a test token for a server's Tools tab), since that feature depends on `authorization_url`/`token_url` being present. It fails with: \`\`\` {"detail":"MCP server authorization url is not configured. OAuth endpoint discovery against the configured server url did not resolve it; the url may be misconfigured. Check the proxy logs for 'MCP OAuth' warnings from server load, verify the server url, or set Authorization URL and Token URL manually, or set Issuer to discover them from the identity provider (RFC 8414)."} \`\`\` Setting `issuer` instead (for RFC 8414 discovery) does not help either — discovery does not appear to run on-demand, and `authorization_url`/`token_url` remain `null` regardless. Importantly, this only affects the UI test button. The actual delegated/passthrough OAuth flow works correctly for real traffic: a client that authenticates against the upstream IdP directly and passes its own bearer token via `x-mcp-<server_name>-authorization`, alongside a valid LiteLLM virtual key in `Authorization`, successfully reaches the upstream MCP server and receives a real tool list. So the runtime behavior of `delegate_auth_to_upstream` is sound — only the persisted config for `authorization_url`/`token_url`/`oauth2_flow` is being wiped on save. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create/register an MCP server with `auth_type: oauth2`, `oauth2_flow: authorization_code`, `authorization_url`, `token_url`, and `delegate_auth_to_upstream: true`. 2. Send a `PUT /v1/mcp/server` with the full server object, explicitly including `authorization_url`, `token_url`, and `oauth2_flow: "authorization_code"` (and `issuer` cleared to `""`): \`\`\`bash curl -X PUT 'https://your-litellm-proxy.example.com/v1/mcp/server' \ -H 'authorization: Bearer <admin-key>' \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "server_id": "<server_id>", "server_name": "example_mcp_server", "url": "https://your-mcp-server.example.com/mcp", "transport": "http", "auth_type": "oauth2", "oauth2_flow": "authorization_code", "issuer": "", "authorization_url": "https://your-idp.example.com/realms/your-realm/protocol/openid-connect/auth", "token_url": "https://your-idp.example.com/realms/your-realm/protocol/openid-connect/token", "delegate_auth_to_upstream": true, "oauth_passthrough": false, "dcr_bridge": false }' \`\`\` 3. Inspect the response, or immediately follow up with `GET /v1/mcp/server` and find the same `server_id`. ### Expected behavior `authorization_url` and `token_url` should be persisted exactly as submitted, and `oauth2_flow` should remain `"authorization_code"`. ### Actual behavior The response (and subsequent GET) shows: \`\`\`json { "issuer": "", "authorization_url": null, "token_url": null, "oauth2_flow": null, "delegate_auth_to_upstream": true } \`\`\` All three fields are nulled despite being explicitly sent as non-null in the request. ### Relevant log output N/A on our end — we don't have access to the proxy's server-side logs in this deployment, only client-observable request/response pairs (above). ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: refactor(ui): port the create key form off antd Form onto react-hook-form
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Create Key was the last big antd `Form` in the dashboard - antd `Form.Item` submits only mounted fields; nothing else reproduces that - Blocks removing antd, and the payload shape is easy to break silently How it solves it: - Moves the form onto react-hook-form with a mount registry - Registry records mounted field names and projects the store at submit - Submit payload is unchanged in both directions, key for key ## User Flow The contract here is zero functional change, so the two lists are identical on purpose. That identity is the deliverable, not a shortcut. Anything that differs between them is a bug in this PR. Before: a proxy admin creates a virtual key and the request carries exactly the fields that were on screen 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click "+ Create New Key" 2. They type a key name, leave every collapsible section closed, and click "Create Key" 3. The browser sends POST /key/generate carrying only the always-visible fields: team, key name, models, key type, user, duration, metadata 4. They repeat with "Optional Settings" expanded, and the same POST now also carries the budget, rate limit, guardrail, tag and access-group fields, each empty 5. They type a max budget, collapse "Optional Settings", and submit; the budget is not on the request at all, rather than being sent as an empty value 6. They expand "Optional Settings" again and the budget they typed is still in the box After: the same admin sees the same screens and the proxy receives the same requests 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click "+ Create New Key" 2. They type a key name, leave every collapsible section closed, and click "Create Key" 3. The browser sends POST /key/generate carrying only the always-visible fields: team, key name, models, key type, user, duration, metadata 4. They repeat with "Optional Settings" expanded, and the same POST now also carries the budget, rate limit, guardrail, tag and access-group fields, each empty 5. They type a max budget, collapse "Optional Settings", and submit; the budget is not on the request at all, rather than being sent as an empty value 6. They expand "Optional Settings" again and the budget they typed is still in the box ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, done once and left running for both sides: 1. Start the proxy: `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log` 2. Start the dashboard dev server: `cd ui/litellm-dashboard && npm run dev` 3. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=api-keys, open DevTools, go to the Network tab and filter on `key/generate` ### Before (8941f2a622) #### Every section closed 1. Click "+ Create New Key", type `proof-key` into Key Name, leave every section collapsed, click "Create Key" 2. In Network, open the `/key/generate` request and record its full Request Payload #### Optional Settings open 1. Click "+ Create New Key", type `proof-key-2` into Key Name, expand "Optional Settings", click "Create Key" 2. Record the full Request Payload #### Budget typed then collapsed 1. Click "+ Create New Key", type `proof-key-3` into Key Name, expand "Optional Settings", type `150.75` into Max Budget (USD) 2. Collapse "Optional Settings", expand it again, and confirm `150.75` is still in the box 3. Collapse "Optional Settings" once more, click "Create Key", record the full Request Payload ### After (4748856403) #### Every section closed 1. Same steps as Before 2. Record the full Request Payload and compare it key for key against the Before capture #### Optional Settings open 1. Same steps as Before 2. Record the full Request Payload and compare it key for key against the Before capture #### Budget typed then collapsed 1. Same steps as Before 2. Confirm `150.75` still survives the collapse and re-expand 3. Record the full Request Payload and compare it key for key against the Before capture The three After payloads should match the three Before payloads exactly, including which keys are absent rather than sent empty ## How the mounted set is reproduced antd hands `onFinish` exactly the fields mounted at submit time, and it keeps the values of unmounted ones so re-expanding a section restores what was typed. react-hook-form reaches only one of those per `shouldUnregister` setting: true reproduces the payload and destroys re-expansion, false reproduces re-expansion and ships keys the antd form omitted. Neither flag reaches both, so the store is kept whole and projected down to the mounted set through a registry that records which fields are currently mounted. Validation needs no equivalent, because RHF already skips unmounted fields, which is the same rule antd applies. Two smaller pieces of the `Form.Item` contract mattered to the payload. Defaults come from each field's own declaration rather than a blanket empty value, so a key that antd sent as `undefined` is not turned into `null` or `""`. And antd's `help` prop replaces the rule's message rather than sitting beside it, including when it is the empty string, so a field carrying help never shows a validation message even while `aria-invalid` is set. The shared `FormField` in this repo always renders `FieldError`, which is why it could not be reused here. The registry counts by name and the projection emits flat keys, so it holds only static literal names. A `Form.List` row, and the per-row sub-fields under it, generates its name at runtime, never lands in the mounted set, and would go missing from the payload without a sound. No such field exists in this form, so nothing here is broken today, but the next form to adopt this needs the registry taught about generated names first. That constraint used to sit in a comment at the export and is recorded here instead, so there is only one place to keep in sync with the code. ## What the tests prove The 60-case submit differential from #37405 runs unedited, and the port passed it on the first run with no gesture repair. Five cases were added for the classes a payload net misses by construction: a writer that lives outside the submit path, validation following the mounted set, Enter to submit, switch coercion, and a required message on a field carrying no help. Every binding was then checked individually by dropping it from the mounted projection, leaving the field rendered, bound and validating, so the key vanishes from the payload the way a real porting defect would. 29 mutants, each suite running all 65 cases, 28 killed on payload assertions with no crashes, and one survivor predicted in advance: `mcp_tool_permissions`, which the payload builder drops unconditionally, so removing it cannot change the request. Five bindings turned out to be held by exactly one case each, which is worth recording because it is a general trap rather than a quirk of this form. A payload builder that defaults, coalesces or unconditionally stamps a key hides that key's binding from every fixture that does not defeat the default. `duration` is coalesced to `null`, `metadata` defaults to `"{}"`, `disable_global_guardrails` is dropped when falsy, and `user_id` is stamped from the signed-in user for one owner type. That last one had no coverage at all before this PR: all sixty inherited cases pass whether or not the form's own `user_id` binding reaches the payload. ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats - antd widgets stay; only `Form` and `Form.Item` were replaced - `MountedFormField` is new and reusable for the remaining antd forms - Advanced Settings fields still come from the live `/openapi.json` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: MCP auto-execute (require_approval "never") hijacks client-side tool_use from agentic clients like Claude Code, breaking all non-MCP tools with "Error executing tool"
signal.text: ## What happened? A model configured with an MCP tool reference using `require_approval: "never"` (so the proxy auto-executes it server-side) is deployed behind an agentic client that sends its own tools in the same request, such as Claude Code sending Read/Bash/Edit. The auto-execute loop takes over the entire tool_use turn and tries to execute every tool_use block the model emits, including the client's own non-MCP tools. Those tools are not in the MCP server map, so the proxy raises a KeyError that gets swallowed into `Error executing tool: '<tool_name>'` and fed back to the model. The model retries, fails again, and eventually gives up. From the client's perspective all of its native tools (Read, Bash, etc.) are broken for any request routed to that model What I expected: when `require_approval: "never"` is set, the proxy should auto-execute only the MCP tools it injected. A tool_use whose name does not resolve to a known MCP server should be passed through to the client unchanged so the client can execute it locally, the way a normal tool_use turn works when no MCP tool is present ## User Flow Before a fix 1. A user creates a virtual key and a team in the LiteLLM proxy UI, then registers an HTTP MCP server (say `image_understand`) and grants the team access to it 2. The user attaches the MCP tool to a model via the model's LiteLLM Params, e.g. `{"tools": [{"type": "mcp", "server_url": "litellm_proxy/mcp/image_understand", "require_approval": "never"}]}` 3. The user points an agentic client (Claude Code) at `POST /v1/messages` on the proxy, using that model and that virtual key. The client sends its own tools (Read, Bash, Edit, ...) alongside whatever the proxy injects 4. The model decides to call Read on a local file. The proxy's auto-execute loop intercepts that tool_use, fails with `Error executing tool: 'Read'`, and returns the error text to the model instead of handing the tool_use back to the client 5. The model retries with Bash, gets `Error executing tool: 'Bash'`, and eventually stops with a message saying the tools are unavailable. The user sees tool call failures and the client's native tooling is dead for that model After a fix 1. Same setup as above: MCP server registered, team granted access, MCP tool attached to the model with `require_approval: "never"` 2. The user points Claude Code at `POST /v1/messages` with that model and key, sending its own tools 3. The model calls Read on a local file. The proxy recognizes Read is not one of its MCP tools, returns the tool_use block to the client in the response, and lets the client execute it locally 4. When the model calls the injected MCP tool (`image_understand`), the proxy auto-executes it server-side as before and feeds the result back 5. Both the client's native tools and the injected MCP tool work in the same turn ## Proof the bug occurs I verified the root cause by reading the current main branch (v1.98.0-dev.2). I was not able to capture a full Claude Code trace against my own proxy in time for this report, so the proof below is the code path plus the user-visible symptom. I can add a full end-to-end curl reproduction if the maintainers want one Config / setup: a model with an MCP tool attached via LiteLLM Params ```json {"tools": [{"type": "mcp", "server_url": "litellm_proxy/mcp/image_understand", "require_approval": "never"}]} ``` Version or commit: v1.98.0-dev.2 on main Commands and their full output The auto-execute loop in `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/mcp_handler.py` extracts every tool_use block without checking whether it belongs to an MCP server ``` # line 38-40 def _extract_tool_use_blocks(response): return tuple(block for block in _get_response_content(response) if block.get("type") == "tool_use") # line 139-158 (abridged) for _ in range(MAX_MCP_TOOL_USE_ITERATIONS): if _get_stop_reason(response) != "tool_use": break tool_use_blocks = _extract_tool_use_blocks(response) if not tool_use_blocks: break tool_results = await LiteLLM_Proxy_MCP_Handler._execute_tool_calls( tool_server_map=tool_server_map, tool_calls=list(tool_use_blocks), ... ) ``` `tool_server_map` is built only from the injected MCP tools (in `_process_mcp_tools_without_openai_transform`). When `_execute_tool_calls` looks up a client-side tool name that is not in that map, it throws KeyError ``` # litellm/responses/mcp/litellm_proxy_mcp_handler.py line 675 server_name = tool_server_map[tool_name] ``` That KeyError is caught by the broad except at line 891-905 and turned into the user-visible error string ``` # line 891-905 (abridged) except Exception as e: ... tool_results.append({ "tool_call_id": tool_call_id, "result": f"Error executing tool: {e}", "name": tool_name, }) ``` So a model emitting `tool_use` for `Read` produces `Error executing tool: 'Read'`, which matches what I observed in the proxy spend logs and what Claude Code surfaced as "tool call failed" The symptom from the agentic client side (Claude Code talking to the proxy over `/v1/messages`): the model attempts Read on a file that exists, gets `Error executing tool: 'Read'` back, tries Bash, gets `Error executing tool: 'Bash'`, then tells the user it cannot read files or run commands. A plain curl client that sends no tools of its own works perfectly against the same model, because then every tool_use resolves to an MCP tool. This is why the bug is specific to agentic clients that bring their own tools ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ## What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.98.0-dev.2 ## Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(responses-bridge): decrypt proxy-managed previous_response_id for session lookup
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Stateful `/v1/responses` chaining through the chat-completions bridge loses all prior context when Responses ID security is enabled - The client-facing `resp_...` ID is encrypted, while spend logs are keyed by the internal chat-completion request ID - `previous_response_id` therefore resolves to no session and the follow-up starts a fresh conversation How it solves it: - Decrypt the proxy-encrypted response ID before decoding the LiteLLM-managed ID - Use the resulting request ID for the spend-log lookup - Keep the lookup testable without importing the proxy server - Enforce the same ownership check on `/v1/responses/compact` before the shared decoder runs ## User Flow Before: a developer sends a two-turn stateful conversation and the second turn forgets the first 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with `"input": "My favorite color is blue."` and receive `resp_...` and HTTP 200 2. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` again with `previous_response_id` set to that ID and `"input": "What is my favorite color?"` 3. The proxy returns HTTP 200, but the model answers as if it has no memory of the first turn After: the same two-turn flow keeps the conversation 1. They send the same first `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` 2. They send the same follow-up with `previous_response_id` 3. The model recalls the first turn and answers correctly, e.g. `"Blue"` ## Relevant issues No GitHub issue filed yet. ## Linear ticket <!-- leave blank if no Linear ticket --> ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (lint/format/unit passed locally; CI re-running on the rebased head) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 (re-review triggered on the final head) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proof against the running proxy (real DeepSeek V4 calls). Before (stock container, no fix): ```json { "status": "incomplete", "output": [ {"type": "reasoning", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "We need answer user asks favorite color, but we don't know..."}]}, {"type": "message", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": ""}]} ], "usage": {"input_tokens": 95, "output_tokens": 256} } ``` After (original capture at commit `73384cce13`; same behavior rebased onto `litellm_internal_staging` as `173124f8a9` with the compaction ownership and DI fixes, spend-log row flushed before the follow-up): ```json { "status": "completed", "output": [ {"type": "reasoning", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "We previously said favorite color is blue. So answer just \"Blue\"."}]}, {"type": "message", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "Blue"}]} ], "usage": {"input_tokens": 135, "output_tokens": 45} } ``` Note: the session handler reads the prior turn from the spend-log row, so the follow-up must be sent after the spend-log write has landed. Security coverage: `ResponsesIDSecurity.async_pre_call_hook` now treats `acompact_responses` like `aresponses`, checking ownership of an encrypted `previous_response_id` before the shared decoder runs. Local suites: `67 passed` for the targeted responses/security tests; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on the changed files; all three repo gates pass locally. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `ResponsesAPIRequestUtils.decode_previous_response_id_to_original_previous_response_id` decrypts the proxy-encrypted layer before the LiteLLM-managed decode - `ResponsesSessionHandler.get_all_spend_logs_for_previous_response_id` uses the decoder so spend-log lookups receive the original request ID, with injectable Prisma client/decoder seams for tests - `ResponsesIDSecurity.async_pre_call_hook` now checks ownership on `acompact_responses` requests - Tests cover proxy decryption, the Prisma seam, the no-Prisma path, and compaction ownership ## QA runbook N/A — this PR adds mocked unit tests, not e2e tests. The live proof above was captured manually. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(bedrock): add cost map entries for gpt-5.6 on Bedrock Converse
signal.text: ## Problem The gpt-5.6 family (luna / sol / terra) is registered in the cost map **only** as `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-*`. Calling these models over the regular Bedrock Converse route silently loses tool calling and reasoning. That route matters because `bedrock_mantle` authenticates with a Bearer Bedrock API key, while `bedrock/converse/...` goes through SigV4 and honours `aws_role_name`. Anyone doing cross-account role assumption (per-tenant billing, tag routing) has to use the Converse route. ## Root cause `AmazonConverseConfig.get_supported_openai_params()` appends `tools` only when `base_model` starts with `anthropic`/`mistral`/`cohere`/`meta.llama3-1|3-2|3-3`/`meta.llama4`/`amazon.nova`, or when `supports_function_calling()` resolves True from the cost map. `BedrockModelInfo.get_base_model("bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna")` returns `openai.gpt-5.6-luna`, which matches no prefix and has no cost map entry. So `tools`, `tool_choice`, `thinking` and `reasoning_effort` are all excluded, and with `drop_params: true` the request returns 200 with the model answering as if no tools were offered. Reproduced on 1.97.0: ```python from litellm.llms.bedrock.chat.converse_transformation import AmazonConverseConfig p = AmazonConverseConfig().get_supported_openai_params(model="bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna") "tools" in p # False "reasoning_effort" in p # False ``` Through a proxy, `tool_choice: "required"` also gets dropped: `finish_reason` comes back `stop` with `tool_calls: null`, while `claude-sonnet-5` with the identical schema returns `finish_reason: tool_calls`. This is not a Bedrock limitation. A direct call works: ``` aws bedrock-runtime converse --model-id us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna \ --messages '[{"role":"user","content":[{"text":"..."}]}]' \ --tool-config file://tools.json # stopReason: tool_use ``` ## Fix Adds bare, `us.` and `global.` prefixed entries with `litellm_provider: bedrock_converse` and `mode: chat`. This matches how every other Bedrock model is keyed, including `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` and the existing `openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0` entries. Pricing mirrors the published `bedrock_mantle/` values, including the above-272k tiers and cache costs. Data-only change. No logic touched, and the existing `bedrock_mantle/` entries are unchanged, so the Responses-path behaviour is unaffected. ## Verification With the patched map on 1.97.0: | model | tools | tool_choice | reasoning_effort | |---|---|---|---| | `bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | `bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | `bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-5.6-terra` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | `get_model_info()` resolves `litellm_provider: bedrock_converse`, `mode: chat`, and the correct per-token pricing. Both `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and the bundled backup are kept in sync. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: feat(ui): add mounted-field projections for the MCP server form graph
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - antd submits only mounted fields; react-hook-form submits the whole store - The MCP server form graph gates 89 bindings behind 22 conditions - Four of those gates are invisible when reading the roots' JSX - Porting the graph without them written down silently changes the payload How it solves it: - Adds pure mounted-field projections for both MCP server roots - Covers all 22 gates with unit tests, one case per gate - Pins three antd behaviours measured by probe, not assumed - Touches no JSX; nothing imports the module yet ## User Flow No user-visible change, so the two flows below are identical by construction. The new module is not imported anywhere; it is groundwork the form port will consume. Before: an admin edits an MCP server and saves 1. They open the MCP Servers page and edit a server 2. They change a field and click Save Changes 3. The server updates After: unchanged, step for step 1. They open the MCP Servers page and edit a server 2. They change a field and click Save Changes 3. The server updates ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix There is no runtime behaviour to demonstrate. The module is not imported by any component, so no request an end user can make reaches it and a live proxy would show nothing either way. Recording that plainly rather than presenting a test run as a proof of fix. What the change is verified by instead is a per-field deletion battery over the projections, which is the instrument that decides whether each of the 89 bindings is load-bearing. Each of the 80 emitted field-name sites is deleted one at a time and the suite must go red for it. The harness gates every entry on the mutation applying, the file still compiling, and the suite running the expected test count, and reports INVALID rather than a verdict when any gate fails. Result, at the tip of this branch: ``` RED 80 GREEN 0 INVALID 0 tree restored byte-identical: true ``` The first run of that battery was 46 RED / 32 GREEN / 9 INVALID. Every survivor was investigated individually rather than banked. Thirty-two were real coverage holes, closed by pinning the exact mounted set per auth configuration instead of spot-checking membership. The nine INVALID were the harness correctly refusing to score a mutation of a gate's comparison value, plus one output-parsing bug in the harness itself that mislabelled a genuine red. That one is worth naming: it failed safe, but it means the first run's greens were the finding and its invalids were not. A kill rate of 80 out of 80 is only worth something if the battery can also let something live, so it is checked against a mutation that provably cannot matter: swapping two names inside one credential array. The projected object holds the same keys, and key order is not observable in the payload, so that mutation has to survive. It did not. It went red, and the two assertions it tripped turned out to compare the returned array against a source-order literal, pinning order rather than membership. Those two now sort both sides like the other fifteen already did. Deleting any of the eighty names still fails the suite, reordering two of them no longer does. The last survivor to fall was `token_exchange_endpoint` on the Entra OBO branch. Deleting it left the suite green because the Entra case asserted the two fields that drop and never asserted the endpoint that stays. signal.title: fix(responses-bridge): preserve reasoning input items as reasoning_content
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Responses `/v1/responses` requests that replay `type: "reasoning"` input items are mishandled by the chat-completions bridge - Plaintext reasoning leaks into ordinary message content or is silently dropped - DeepSeek V4 and Kimi K2.6 reject or lose context when prior `reasoning_content` is not passed back How it solves it: - Reasoning input items are converted to assistant `reasoning_content` - Standalone reasoning merges into the following assistant turn, or is preserved before a user turn - Opaque encrypted-only items are skipped instead of polluting the prompt - Guardrail text extraction and redaction now cover reasoning content and summary blocks ## User Flow Before: a developer reuses a prior response's reasoning item in a new stateless `/v1/responses` request and the model loses its chain of thought 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with an `input` array containing a `type: "reasoning"` item followed by a user message 2. LiteLLM forwards the reasoning text as ordinary message content, or drops it 3. The model answers without the prior reasoning, and DeepSeek V4 can return HTTP 400 with `reasoning_content must be passed back` After: the same request preserves the reasoning as `reasoning_content` 1. They send the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` body 2. LiteLLM emits the reasoning on an assistant `reasoning_content` field, merging it with the following assistant turn when one exists 3. The model receives the prior chain-of-thought and answers correctly ## Relevant issues - #36197 — reasoning items (including `encrypted_content`) are silently dropped for non-native Responses providers - Related PR: #27630 (drop-based alternative handling of the same input item) ## Linear ticket <!-- leave blank if no Linear ticket --> ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (lint/format/unit passed locally; CI re-running on the rebased head) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 (5/5 on the latest head) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live smoke after the fix (original capture at commit `f6c0cbb49a`; same code rebased onto `litellm_internal_staging` as `2d4e6afe1c` with the guardrail coverage fix): ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "BLSC/DeepSeek-V4-Flash", "input": [ {"type": "reasoning", "id": "rs_1", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "The secret word is BLUEBERRY."}]}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is the secret word? Answer with one word."} ], "store": true, "max_output_tokens": 256, "stream": false }' ``` Result: HTTP 200, `status: "completed"`, no provider rejection. Guardrail regression coverage: `iter_message_text`, `walk_user_text`, and `build_inspection_messages` now see reasoning `content` and `summary` text; the new tests assert both inspection and in-place redaction. Full local suite: `54 passed` for the targeted guardrail + reasoning bridge tests; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on the changed files; all three repo gates pass locally. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `_transform_responses_api_input_item_to_chat_completion_message` handles `type: "reasoning"` explicitly - `_extract_reasoning_text_from_input_item` extracts plaintext from `content` or `summary` blocks - `_merge_reasoning_only_assistant_messages` merges standalone reasoning into the following assistant turn, preserving chronology when that turn already has `reasoning_content` - `litellm/proxy/guardrails/_content_utils.py` inspects and rewrites reasoning content/summary text so guardrails see every plaintext shape the bridge forwards - New unit tests cover item shapes, merging, preservation, non-reasoning regressions, and guardrail coverage ## QA runbook N/A — this PR adds mocked unit tests, not e2e tests. The live proof above was captured manually. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(proxy): record estimated input tokens in spend logs for failed dispatched requests
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Requests that fail after reaching the provider log 0 tokens - The provider bills the input anyway, so spend cannot be reconciled How it solves it: - Failure rows now carry tokenizer-estimated input token counts at $0 spend - Only dispatched call types with countable text input get estimates - Image inputs count at the default per-image token estimate; the image is never fetched - Recovered mid-stream usage keeps priority over the estimate - /v1/messages and /v1/embeddings failure rows now see the request's usage data at all - The raw request body backfills the top-level `system` / `instructions` prompt when a bridged endpoint (e.g. /v1/messages served by a chat-completions provider) never fills it in internally ## User Flow Before: a platform admin reconciling their AWS Bedrock bill against the gateway's spend logs finds every failed request logged at zero tokens, even though the provider billed the input 1. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a ~2900 token prompt for a Bedrock model and it times out, returning 408 "litellm.Timeout: Connection timed out" 2. Another request comes back 400 "BedrockException: The maximum tokens you requested exceeds the model limit of 128000" 3. The same timeout happens on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses after the provider has already started reading the prompt 4. A POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages call with a large top-level `system` prompt for a Gemini model (which the gateway serves by translating to the provider's chat API) times out the same way with a 408 5. A POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings call for a Bedrock embedding model times out the same way with a 408 6. A chat request carrying an image attachment (an `image_url` content block) also times out with a 408 7. The admin opens https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and every one of those failure rows shows 0 input, 0 output, and 0 total tokens 8. The provider's console shows billed input processing for those same calls, so the two reports cannot be reconciled After: the same failed requests log an estimated input token count, so the spend logs line up with what the provider billed 1. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a ~2900 token prompt for a Bedrock model and it times out, returning 408 "litellm.Timeout: Connection timed out" 2. Another request comes back 400 "BedrockException: The maximum tokens you requested exceeds the model limit of 128000" 3. The same timeout happens on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses after the provider has already started reading the prompt 4. A POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages call with a large top-level `system` prompt for a Gemini model (which the gateway serves by translating to the provider's chat API) times out the same way with a 408 5. A POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings call for a Bedrock embedding model times out the same way with a 408 6. A chat request carrying an image attachment (an `image_url` content block) also times out with a 408, and the proxy never downloads the image while logging it 7. The admin opens https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and each of those failure rows now shows the input tokens that were sent (2917 on the chat and responses calls, 2913 on the messages call, 728 on the translated Gemini messages call with its 720 token system prompt included, 263 on the image call as text plus a default per-image allowance, 21 on the embeddings call) with 0 output tokens at $0 spend 8. A request that never reached a provider, like an unknown model name, still logs 0 tokens, so only provider-dispatched failures carry counts ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5690 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical for both runs: a live proxy against real AWS Bedrock and OpenAI (us-east-1, real $$$), fresh Postgres, `router_settings: {num_retries: 0}`, deployments `bedrock-sonnet-5` (`bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`, no timeout), `bedrock-sonnet-5-timeout-2s` (same model, `litellm_params.timeout: 2`, so the call is cut off after Bedrock starts reading the prompt), `bedrock-sonnet-5-timeout-50ms` (same model, `timeout: 0.05`), `bedrock-embed-timeout-50ms` (`bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`, `timeout: 0.05`), `gemini-timeout-50ms` (`gemini/gemini-3.7-flash`, `timeout: 0.05`), and `gpt-timeout-50ms` (`openai/gpt-5.6`, `timeout: 0.05`); the last two exercise the /v1/messages bridges (Gemini goes through the chat-completions bridge, OpenAI through the responses bridge). probe_gemini.json and probe_gpt.json are Anthropic messages bodies with a ~720 token top-level `system` string and a one-word user message. signal.title: fix(proxy): scope auth token cookie path to SERVER_ROOT_PATH
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #32249 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The token cookie was written without a `path`, so it defaulted to `/`. When two LiteLLM deployments are served on the same host under different root paths (`a.com` with no `SERVER_ROOT_PATH` and `a.com/prefix` with `SERVER_ROOT_PATH=/prefix`), logging into one overwrote the browser's `token` cookie for the other, which bounced the user to `/sso/key/generate` To observe the fix, set `SERVER_ROOT_PATH=/prefix`, log in through the UI, and inspect the login response headers. The `Set-Cookie` for `token` now carries `Path=/prefix` instead of `Path=/`, so the two deployments no longer clobber each other's cookie. With `SERVER_ROOT_PATH` unset the path stays `/`, matching prior behavior Because the cookie is now scoped to the server root path, logout has to clear it at that same path; a cookie set at `Path=/prefix` is not removed by a delete at `Path=/`. `clearTokenCookies` now also clears the token cookie at the server root path derived from the UI location, so logging out reliably invalidates the session on path-mounted deployments Regression tests cover both sides: `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_utils.py` locks in the cookie path derivation, and `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/utils/cookieUtils.test.ts` verifies the token cookie is cleared at the server root path ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Added `get_cookie_path_from_server_root_path` in `litellm/proxy/utils.py`, which normalizes `SERVER_ROOT_PATH` into a cookie path (defaulting to `/` when unset). Passed `path=get_cookie_path_from_server_root_path()` to every `set_cookie(key="token", ...)` call in the login and SSO flows (`login`, `login_v2`, `login_v3_exchange` in `proxy_server.py` and the SSO callback in `ui_sso.py`) so the auth cookie is scoped to the deployment's root path On the frontend, `clearTokenCookies` now also clears the token cookie at the server root path (derived by stripping the trailing `/ui` from the UI cookie path), so logout clears the newly scoped cookie

signal.title: fix(ui): stop alerting settings writing unusable values into stored config
signal.text: > **Deferred, not ready to merge.** Everything here changes behaviour rather than migrating it, and the current mandate is migration with today's behaviour preserved. Parked as a draft until the behaviour fixes are picked up as their own piece of work. The branch and its tests are complete; see the known-behaviour note below ## Known behaviour this would change, measured at staging `3f15dc3287` Both of these are shipped today and are longstanding, not recent regressions: - `dynamic_form.tsx:52` sends `null` when a numeric alerting field is emptied - `dynamic_form.tsx:57` sends the whole React change event, not the typed text The `null` is the one with real consequences. `/config/field/update` stores it because `ConfigGeneralSettings` types `alerting_args` as a plain dict and never checks contents, and `SlackAlertingArgs` then rejects the stored value on every config reconcile. Reachable with an ordinary two-field edit, and it survives a reload. The change event is inert in practice. `renderControl` only reaches that branch for a `field_type` outside `Integer` and `Boolean`, and `/alerting/settings` hard-codes all nine fields to those two, so the branch never renders against a real proxy. Forced open in a test it does not corrupt anything either, because the event's circular fiber reference makes `JSON.stringify` throw before the request is built, so the save is dropped rather than written. ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Emptying a numeric alerting field stored an unusable value - The proxy then rejected its own stored alerting settings on every reload - The page claimed success even when the save was refused How it solves it: - Emptied fields are dropped instead of sent as null - Both saves are awaited, and a refusal now surfaces as an error - The text control reports the typed text, not the raw event ## User Flow Before: an admin who clears a numeric alerting field silently poisons the proxy's saved alerting settings 1. Sign in and open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=settings, then the Alerting tab 2. Empty the `daily_report_frequency` box and switch `slack_alerting` on 3. Click Update Settings and see "Wait 10s for proxy to update." 4. Reload the page; `daily_report_frequency` shows its old value, so it looks like nothing happened 5. From here on the proxy log reports the saved alerting settings as invalid on every refresh, and later changes on the same page stop taking effect until the saved settings are cleared by hand 6. If the proxy refuses the save outright, the page still shows the same "Wait 10s for proxy to update." and no error After: the same edit saves cleanly, and a refusal is visible 1. Sign in and open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=settings, then the Alerting tab 2. Empty the `daily_report_frequency` box and switch `slack_alerting` on 3. Click Update Settings and see "Wait 10s for proxy to update." 4. Reload the page; `daily_report_frequency` shows the proxy default, which is what emptying it asks for 5. The proxy log stays quiet and later changes on the same page keep taking effect 6. If the proxy refuses the save, the page shows the refusal instead of claiming success ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats - Deferred; behaviour change, and the mandate is migration only - Backend still accepts any `alerting_args` shape; API callers can reproduce it - The text control never renders today; that part is hygiene - Saving still requires changing at least one field, unchanged ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: test: skip a streaming test that passes and fails on the same commit
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - One streaming test passes and fails on the same commit - Its failures make CircleCI unusable as a merge signal How it solves it: - Skips that one test, with the evidence in the reason - No other test is touched ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) No tests are added: this removes one from the run rather than adding behavior. The other two are not yet knowable, since CI has not run on this branch and Greptile reviews on open ## Skipped test, failure rate, and evidence `tests/local_testing/test_streaming.py::test_openai_stream_options_call_text_completion` **Observed failure rate: 1 of 8 runs (12.5%).** That is every run CircleCI retains for this project, so it is a small sample and worth reading as such The evidence is a same-commit disagreement rather than the rate. On commit `3c0b1db6` the job `local_testing_part2` failed in workflow `556313cc-e2d8-41b2-8da2-8513c8dc83a2` (job `a2a70857`), and the rerun of that same commit, workflow `8665db04-a372-4ab6-bfbb-5f7cce696ff5` (job `8eefa345`), passed. Same tree, same test, opposite outcomes. It passed in the other six runs `ModelResponseStream.model_dump()` raises `TypeError: 'MockValSer' object is not an instance of 'SchemaSerializer'` at `litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py:1768`, and the stream wrapper remaps it through `MidStreamFallbackError` into an `InternalServerError` **The cause is not confirmed, and that is the open question here.** `MockValSer` is pydantic's placeholder for a model whose schema was never built, which can come from cross-test pollution in an xdist worker or from a provider response shape that reaches an un-rebuilt model. Commit `e8356c18d0` fixed a MockValSer crash in this same handler by normalizing provider logprobs, so the second reading has direct precedent and this test calls the live OpenAI API That matters because skipping a real product bug is worse than living with a flaky test. If it turns out to be the serialization bug, the fix belongs in `streaming_handler.py` and this skip should come off rather than stay ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This change has no runtime surface. It adds no endpoint and no provider behavior, and touches nothing the proxy serves, so there is no request to curl against a live instance. What it does, captured at `2d118fc562`: ``` $ python -m pytest "tests/local_testing/test_streaming.py::test_openai_stream_options_call_text_completion" -rs tests/local_testing/test_streaming.py s [100%] SKIPPED [1] tests/local_testing/test_streaming.py:1810: LIT-TBD: ModelResponseStream.model_dump() intermittently raises "'MockValSer' object is not an instance of 'SchemaSerializer'" ... 1 skipped in 0.06s ``` The file carries 139 pre-existing ruff errors on both sides of this change, so the nine added lines introduce none: ``` base: Found 139 errors now : Found 139 errors ``` ## Type ✅ Test ## Changes One `@pytest.mark.skip` on `test_openai_stream_options_call_text_completion`, nine lines in one file. The reason carries the ticket, the failing and passing workflow ids for the same commit, and the competing explanation for the cause, so whoever picks it up does not have to re-derive any of it `LIT-TBD` is a placeholder. It needs the real ticket before this merges ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR This change cannot alter product behavior, so it cannot introduce a customer-facing regression. It does remove one test from the signal, which is the cost being accepted here

signal.title: ci: run the proxy search_endpoints tests in the endpoints shard
signal.text: ## What `tests/test_litellm/proxy/search_endpoints` is named by no job's test path. Adds it to the `proxy-endpoints` shard, alongside the 24 sibling `*_endpoints` directories it belongs with, and creates the directory as a package. ## Why `assert_ci_coverage` fails any PR that adds a test file under that directory — it is currently red on #36063 for exactly this reason: ``` ERROR: test files that no CI job invokes - tests/test_litellm/proxy/search_endpoints: 2 test file(s) invoked by no job ``` The gate is correct: without a shard entry those tests would be committed and then never run. Splitting the wiring out here so #36063 stays a behaviour change and this stays a CI change. ## Why the empty `__init__.py` The shard runs `pytest <paths...>`, and pytest exits 4 on a path that does not exist. `tests/test_litellm/proxy/search_endpoints` does not exist on `litellm_internal_staging` yet, so adding the path alone would turn `proxy-endpoints` red on this branch and make the two PRs merge-order dependent. Creating the directory as a package makes this PR green on its own and lets the two land in either order. It also closes a real gap: every other `*_endpoints` test directory carries an `__init__.py` and this one did not, so its `test_endpoints.py` would have been imported as a top-level `test_endpoints` module rather than a qualified one. ## Verification Run locally against this branch: - `python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py` → exit 0, `OK: 2363 test files and 10 Dockerfiles ...` - `pytest <the 26 shard paths> --collect-only` → exit 0, 6945 tests collected, every path resolves - With #36063's test files present, `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/search_endpoints` → 20 passed; run alongside `video_endpoints`, `google_endpoints` and `agent_endpoints` (which each also have a `test_endpoints.py`) → 263 passed, no import collision

signal.title: test(ui): pin the MCP server edit save payload before the form migration
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Nothing asserts the MCP server edit save payload - No `toStrictEqual` anywhere, so key changes stay invisible - Upcoming form migration would change it silently How it solves it: - 19 cases pin the exact object sent to the server - Values captured from live behaviour, not read off the source - Six-mutant battery proves the net actually bites ## User Flow There is no user-visible change here, by design. This PR adds tests only, and the point of it is that the flow below stays byte-identical before and after. Both lists are therefore the same list Before: an admin edits an MCP server and saves 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and click an existing server 2. They change a field, say the auth type or the alias, and press Save Changes 3. The server updates and the row reflects the change After: unchanged 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and click an existing server 2. They change a field, say the auth type or the alias, and press Save Changes 3. The server updates and the row reflects the change ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This PR changes no runtime behaviour, so there is no live-proxy before and after to show. Stating that plainly rather than staging a run that would look identical on both sides The evidence that matters for a characterization net is whether it fails when the thing it pins changes. That is the mutation battery below, run at `9df4cafcfb`, six mutants applied one at a time to the payload builder in `mcp_server_edit.tsx`, each reverted before the next Every anchor was asserted unique before substitution, and every run was checked to have executed all 19 tests, so a mutant that silently failed to apply or broke the file would report as a harness fault instead of a kill. Two earlier mutants did exactly that and were caught by those guards | mutant | payload change | tests red | | --- | --- | --- | | M1 | leaks `created_by` into the body | 19 / 19 | | M2 | drops `logo_url` from `mcp_info` | 18 / 18 strict cases | | M3 | emits `allowed_tools` with the gate removed | 17 | | M4 | turns a flat key into a lodash path | 18 / 18 strict cases | | M5 | sends `null` where today it sends `undefined` | 18 / 18 strict cases | | M6 | sends `null` where today it sends `[]` | 18 / 18 strict cases | Kill rate 6/6. M3 spares the two allowlist cases because `allowed_tools` is present either way in one and the gate is the subject of the other. M1 is the only mutant the leak-guard case catches, which is what it exists for M5 is the one worth reading twice. It is caught only because the file uses `toStrictEqual`; `toEqual` treats a key holding `undefined` as absent, and that is precisely the distinction that separates a gated-off field from a mounted-but-empty one in this form today ## Type ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Records current behaviour, including anything currently wrong - `alias` assignment is dead, shadowed by `...restValues` - `mcp_access_groups` mapping is a no-op only while antd yields strings - Do not delete either during the migration; the second can revive - Integration tier, so roughly two seconds per case ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(cost): match streamed Messages usage cost to the recorded spend
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Streamed `usage.cost` disagreed with the logged spend - Cached input tokens were billed as $0 input - 1h cache writes were billed at the 5m rate - Custom deployment pricing was ignored, streaming sticker price How it solves it: - Rebuild streamed usage with the non-streaming Anthropic transformation - Price the chunk through the call's own cost calculator - Fall back to model-name pricing when unavailable ## User Flow Before: a developer streaming Anthropic Messages through the gateway gets a per-request cost in the stream that does not match the spend the gateway records, so their in-app cost meter and their invoice disagree 1. Their proxy admin configures a Bedrock Sonnet deployment with negotiated per-token prices, plus `include_cost_in_streaming_usage: True`, and restarts the proxy 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"stream": true` and a large cached system prompt 3. The final `message_delta` frame reports `"input_tokens": 14, "cache_read_input_tokens": 3202` alongside `"cost": 0.00118866` 4. The same request is recorded at `0.0003742` spend, roughly a third of what the stream claimed, so the two numbers cannot be reconciled 5. They retry with a 1 hour cache TTL, the frame claims `0.016660875` while the request is recorded at `0.008068`, off by about 2x After: the same requests report the same cost in the stream as the gateway records, so the in-app meter reconciles 1. Their proxy admin configures the same deployment and restarts the proxy 2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"stream": true` and a large cached system prompt 3. The final `message_delta` frame reports the same token counts alongside `"cost": 0.0003742` 4. The request is recorded at `0.0003742` spend, matching the stream 5. They retry with a 1 hour cache TTL, the frame reports `0.008068` and the request is recorded at `0.008068` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4902 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live AWS Bedrock, real spend, `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` in `us-east-1`, through a proxy on localhost:4000. The deployment carries custom per-token prices, about a third of Sonnet sticker, standing in for a negotiated discount, and a 1h cache write rate distinct from the 5m one `lit4902_config.yaml` ```yaml model_list: - model_name: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 aws_region_name: us-east-1 aws_access_key_id: os.environ/AWS_BEDROCK_TEST_ACCESS_KEY_ID aws_secret_access_key: os.environ/AWS_BEDROCK_TEST_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY input_cost_per_token: 0.000001 output_cost_per_token: 0.000005 cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.0000001 cache_creation_input_token_cost: 0.00000125 cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_1hr: 0.000002 general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 litellm_settings: include_cost_in_streaming_usage: True callbacks: ["lit4902_cb.proxy_handler_instance"] ``` `lit4902_cb.py`, a logging callback that records the spend the gateway attributes to each request, so the streamed number can be compared against it ```python from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger class Lit4902CostLogger(CustomLogger): async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time): cost = kwargs.get("response_cost") with open("/home/ubuntu/lit4902_callback_cost.txt", "a") as f: f.write(f"CALLBACK response_cost={cost!r}\n") proxy_handler_instance = Lit4902CostLogger() ``` `msg_payload.json` streams a ~3.2k token cached system prompt with a 5m TTL. `msg_1h_<tag>.json` streams a ~4k token system prompt carrying `"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}` with a unique prefix per run, so each run is a fresh 1h cache write Both sides run the same proxy command ```bash PYTHONPATH=/home/ubuntu python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /home/ubuntu/lit4902_config.yaml ``` Expected values under the configured prices, for reference. Cache read: `14*0.000001 + 3202*0.0000001 + 8*0.000005 = 0.0003742`. 1h cache write: `14*0.000001 + 4007*0.000002 + 8*0.000005 = 0.008068` ### Before (c94d692864) #### Cache read with a discounted deployment 1. Stream the cached request ```bash curl -s -m 120 -N -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "content-type: application/json" \ --data @/home/ubuntu/msg_payload.json | grep '"type": "message_delta"' ``` ``` data: {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "end_turn", "stop_sequence": null, "stop_details": null}, "usage": {"input_tokens": 14, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0, "cache_read_input_tokens": 3202, "output_tokens": 8, "cache_creation": {"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens": 0, "ephemeral_1h_input_tokens": 0}, "cost": 0.00118866}} ``` 2. Read the spend the gateway recorded for that same request ```bash cat /home/ubuntu/lit4902_callback_cost.txt ``` ``` CALLBACK response_cost=0.0003742 ``` 3. The stream says `0.00118866`, the gateway recorded `0.0003742`, so they disagree by about 3.2x. The streamed figure is Sonnet sticker rather than the configured discount, and it also drops the 14 non cached input tokens #### 1 hour cache write 1. Stream a fresh 1h cached request ```bash python /home/ubuntu/gen_1h_payload.py before1 curl -s -m 150 -N -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "content-type: application/json" \ --data @/home/ubuntu/msg_1h_before1.json | grep '"type": "message_delta"' ``` ``` data: {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "end_turn", "stop_sequence": null, "stop_details": null}, "usage": {"input_tokens": 14, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 4007, "cache_read_input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 8, "cache_creation": {"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens": 0, "ephemeral_1h_input_tokens": 4007}, "cost": 0.016660875000000002}} ``` 2. Read the spend the gateway recorded ```bash cat /home/ubuntu/lit4902_callback_cost.txt ``` ``` CALLBACK response_cost=0.008068 ``` 3. The stream says `0.016660875`, the gateway recorded `0.008068`, so they disagree by about 2.1x. The frame reports all 4007 tokens as 1h writes, yet the streamed cost charged them at the 5m sticker rate ### After (6f4844bfd9) #### Cache read with a discounted deployment 1. Stream the cached request ```bash curl -s -m 120 -N -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "content-type: application/json" \ --data @/home/ubuntu/msg_payload.json | grep '"type": "message_delta"' ``` ``` data: {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "end_turn", "stop_sequence": null, "stop_details": null}, "usage": {"input_tokens": 14, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0, "cache_read_input_tokens": 3202, "output_tokens": 8, "cache_creation": {"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens": 0, "ephemeral_1h_input_tokens": 0}, "cost": 0.0003742}} ``` 2.
