signal.title: feat(images): support ChatGPT OAuth image APIs
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - ChatGPT OAuth could not call GPT Image endpoints - JSON data URL image edits failed at the proxy How it solves it: - Add ChatGPT image generation and edit transformations - Decode JSON image edit inputs with configurable limits - Auto-route unconfigured GPT Image models through ChatGPT ## User Flow Before: a developer using ChatGPT OAuth cannot generate or edit GPT images through the proxy 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations with `"model": "gpt-image-2"` 2. The request cannot resolve a configured image provider, so no image is returned 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/edits with base64 data URLs in `images` 4. The proxy does not accept the JSON image payload, so the edit fails After: the same requests use ChatGPT OAuth and return image responses 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations with `"model": "gpt-image-2"` 2. The request uses their ChatGPT OAuth session and returns a generated image 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/edits with base64 data URLs in `images` 4. The proxy decodes the images and returns the edited image response ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? signal.title: fix(types): map nested prompt_tokens_details.cache_creation_input_tokens to cache_write_tokens
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - DashScope nests `cache_creation_input_tokens` inside `prompt_tokens_details` - LiteLLM never reads it, so cache-write tokens bill at the input rate - Spend logs and `/v1/responses` also drop the cache-write count How it solves it: - Map the nested key onto canonical `cache_write_tokens` when usage is parsed - Cost calculation, spend logs, and `/v1/responses` all read that field already ## User Flow Before: a proxy user calling a DashScope qwen model with prompt caching gets billed at the wrong rate and sees no cache-write data in their logs 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `dashscope/qwen3.7-plus` with a long system prompt marked `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}` and tiered pricing configured with a `cache_creation_input_token_cost` 2. The response usage shows `prompt_tokens_details.cache_creation_input_tokens: 7456` of 7472 prompt tokens 3. The `x-litellm-response-cost-input` header reads 0.0029888, which is all 7472 tokens at the plain input rate; the configured cache-creation rate is ignored and no cache-creation cost header appears 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs records that wrong spend and no cache-creation token count After: the same request bills cache-write tokens at the configured cache-creation rate 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions request 2. The response usage now also carries `cache_write_tokens: 7456` alongside the provider's nested field 3. The cost headers split correctly: `x-litellm-response-cost-cache-creation: 0.003728` (7456 tokens at the cache-creation rate) and `x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.0000064` (the 16 uncached tokens at the input rate) 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the corrected spend with `cache_creation_input_tokens: 7456` recorded ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5757 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both legs hit the real DashScope International API (`https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`) with a real key through a local Postgres-backed proxy, Before at the merge base and After at the PR tip. Every request used a fresh ~7.4k-token system corpus with a unique nonce marked `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}`, so each call is a fresh cache write and token counts differ slightly between calls. Spend rows are looked up by the provider response id (the `chatcmpl-*` body id), not the `x-litellm-call-id` header Proxy model config (both legs): ```yaml - model_name: qwen3.7-plus-real litellm_params: model: dashscope/qwen3.7-plus api_key: os.environ/DASHSCOPE_API_KEY api_base: https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 model_info: tiered_pricing: - range: [0, 128000] input_cost_per_token: 4e-7 cache_read_input_token_cost: 1.6e-7 cache_creation_input_token_cost: 5e-7 output_cost_per_token: 1.6e-6 ``` ### Before (d9e9270574) #### /v1/chat/completions 1. `curl -sD s1_headers.txt http://localhost:31817/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @s1_payload.json` 2. The provider returns the nested field, but usage carries no canonical cache keys: ```json "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 7472, "completion_tokens": 29, "total_tokens": 7501, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 7472, "cache_creation": {"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens": 7456}, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 7456, "cache_type": "ephemeral"}} ``` 3. Cost headers bill all 7472 prompt tokens at the input rate (7472 * 4e-7 = 0.0029888), with no cache-creation line: ```text x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0030352 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.0029888 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 4.64e-05 ``` #### /v1/responses (cache_control on the content part) 1. `curl -sD s2a_headers.txt http://localhost:31817/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @s2a_payload.json` 2. Usage shows zero cache signal and billing is full input rate (7472 * 4e-7 = 0.0029888), even though this same call's spend-row raw fields prove the provider cached 7456 tokens: ```json "usage": {"input_tokens": 7472, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 7472}, "output_tokens": 23, "total_tokens": 7495} ``` ```text x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0030256 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.0029888 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 3.68e-05 ``` 3. Two other shapes (cache_control on the message object, corpus via `instructions`) never reach DashScope as cacheable on either side, so the content-part shape is the canonical case #### /v1/messages 1. `curl -sD s3_headers.txt http://localhost:31817/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @s3_payload.json` (Anthropic format, `cache_control` on the system block) 2. Every row bills the wrong full-input-rate figure and `additional_usage_values` has no top-level `cache_creation_input_tokens`, even for the two calls where the provider demonstrably cached: ```text chat spend 0.0030352 top-level cache_creation_input_tokens: ABSENT prompt_tokens_details: {"cache_type": "ephemeral", "text_tokens": 7472, "cached_tokens": 0, "cache_creation": {"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens": 7456}, "cache_creation_input_tokens": 7456} responses spend 0.0030256 top-level key ABSENT; nested 7456 present (provider cached) messages spend 0.0030352 top-level key ABSENT; no cache fields (provider never cached) ``` ### After (490079e7df) #### /v1/chat/completions 1. `curl -sD s1f-headers.txt http://localhost:33619/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @s1f-payload.json` 2. signal.title: fix(pass_through): don't override client-forwarded Anthropic OAuth with server x-api-key
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `/anthropic` passthrough always sent the server's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as `x-api-key` - Anthropic authenticates off `x-api-key` when both it and `Authorization` are present - A client forwarding its own OAuth token (e.g. Claude Code Max) got silently ignored How it solves it: - Skip injecting the server `x-api-key` when the request already carries a client OAuth token - The client's own `Authorization` header then reaches Anthropic unmodified ## User Flow Before: a developer routing a Claude Code Max subscription through the `/anthropic` passthrough gets authenticated as the proxy's own configured key instead of their subscription 1. They set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000/anthropic` and run Claude Code with their Max subscription OAuth token 2. Claude Code sends `POST http://localhost:4000/anthropic/v1/messages` with `Authorization: Bearer sk-ant-oat...` 3. The proxy also attaches `x-api-key: <the operator's configured ANTHROPIC_API_KEY>` to the upstream request 4. Anthropic authenticates off `x-api-key`, so every request runs as the proxy's own key, not the developer's Max subscription (probing with a deliberately invalid client token still returns "API key is invalid" instead of an OAuth-token error, proving the client's identity never reached Anthropic) After: the same flow authenticates as the developer's own subscription 1. They set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000/anthropic` and run Claude Code with their Max subscription OAuth token 2. Claude Code sends `POST http://localhost:4000/anthropic/v1/messages` with `Authorization: Bearer sk-ant-oat...` 3. The proxy forwards only that `Authorization` header; it no longer attaches its own `x-api-key` 4. Anthropic authenticates the request as the developer's own Max subscription ## Relevant issues Relates to #37344 (the `/anthropic` passthrough auth-substitution finding in that report; the report's separate 429 rate-limit observation on the router/provider path is not reproduced or explained by this change and remains open) ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Ran the real proxy (`litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py`) with `ANTHROPIC_API_BASE` pointed at a local echo listener standing in for `api.anthropic.com`, so the actual outbound headers can be inspected directly, the same technique the issue reporter used to diagnose this. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-server-configured-fakekey` simulates the operator's configured key; the request carries a fake Claude Code Max OAuth token (`sk-ant-oat01-...`) as the client's own `Authorization` header. ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4111/anthropic/v1/messages \ -H "x-litellm-api-key: Bearer sk-test-master-key-1234" \ -H "authorization: Bearer sk-ant-oat01-fake-claude-code-max-oauth-token" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-4-5","max_tokens":10,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' ``` ### Before (41de13aa0c) 1. Ran the command above against the proxy on the merge-base commit 2. The echo listener recorded both headers on the outbound request: ```json { "authorization": "Bearer sk-ant-oat01-fake-claude-code-max-oauth-token", "x-api-key": "sk-ant-server-configured-fakekey" } ``` 3. Anthropic would authenticate this request off `x-api-key`, i.e. as the proxy operator, not the client ### After (abf911ec19) 1. Ran the identical command against the proxy rebuilt from this branch's tip 2. The echo listener recorded only the client's own header: ```json { "authorization": "Bearer sk-ant-oat01-fake-claude-code-max-oauth-token" } ``` 3. `x-api-key` is no longer sent, so Anthropic has only the client's own credential to authenticate with ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Does not address the report's separate 429 rate-limit observation on the router/provider `/v1/messages` path; that needs reproduction against a real Claude Max subscription, which wasn't available here - Testing used a local echo listener instead of the live Anthropic API since no Anthropic OAuth subscription or API key was available in this environment ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: test(ui): characterize the create key form payload contract
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The create-key suite mocked antd wholesale - Its fake form store submitted every value ever typed - Real antd submits only currently mounted fields - So the suite passed whatever the form actually sent - A form-library port could regress it undetected How it solves it: - Renders the real tree, stubs only the network boundary - Pins the exact submitted body with `toStrictEqual` - Covers each collapsible section closed, alone, and open - Splits the genuinely unit-level logic into a unit test ## User Flow This PR changes no runtime behaviour, so the two lists below walk the same admin through the same task with a plausible form regression applied, showing what reaches the proxy today versus what CI would let ship Before: a regression in the create-key form silently wipes a setting the admin never touched, and the suite stays green 1. An admin opens https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys and clicks Create New Key 2. They type a Key Name, expand Advanced Settings to read the options, change nothing there, and click Create Key 3. The key comes back created, but its soft budget has been explicitly cleared rather than left at whatever the team or default policy would have given it 4. CI is green, so nothing stops the change from shipping After: the same regression turns CI red before it can reach an admin 1. An admin opens https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys and clicks Create New Key 2. They type a Key Name, expand Advanced Settings to read the options, change nothing there, and click Create Key 3. The key comes back created with its soft budget untouched, exactly as before this PR 4. signal.title: feat(openai): add gpt-5.6 model family to registry
signal.text: TLDR The GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models were released in July 2026 but were never added to the LiteLLM model registry. Because of this: * Cost tracking returns $0 for these models. * Using `tool_choice` results in an `UnsupportedParamsError`. This PR adds all three models to the required registry files with their pricing, context window, and supported capabilities. Pricing Pricing is based on the OpenAI documentation: * gpt-5.6-sol: $5/M input, $30/M output, $0.50/M cached input * gpt-5.6-terra: $2/M input, $12/M output, $0.20/M cached input * gpt-5.6-luna: $0.20/M input, $1.20/M output, $0.02/M cached input All three models support: * 1M+ context * Vision * tool_choice * Reasoning * Prompt caching Problem LiteLLM currently does not have registry entries for these three GPT-5.6 models. As a result, LiteLLM does not have the model metadata required for pricing and capability detection. For example, when a developer sends a request using `gpt-5.6-sol` with: ``` { "model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "tool_choice": "auto" } ``` LiteLLM currently returns: ``` 400 BadRequestError: UnsupportedParamsError ``` This happens because `tool_choice` is not recognized as a supported parameter for the model. Requests using these models can also appear in the LiteLLM logs with $0 spend because the pricing information is missing from the registry. What this PR changes This PR adds `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-luna` to both LiteLLM registry JSON files. Each entry includes: * Input token pricing * Output token pricing * Cached input pricing * Context window information * Vision support * Tool choice support * Reasoning support * Prompt caching support No unrelated behavior is changed. User flow before this PR A developer sends: ``` POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions ``` with: ``` { "model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "tool_choice": "auto" } ``` LiteLLM returns an `UnsupportedParamsError` because the model is missing from the registry. The request can also be logged with $0 spend because LiteLLM does not know the model's pricing. User flow after this PR The developer sends the same request. LiteLLM recognizes that `gpt-5.6-sol` supports `tool_choice`, forwards the request to OpenAI, and returns the response normally. The request is also logged using the correct token pricing instead of $0 spend. Relevant issues There is currently no open issue for this. The models were released in July 2026 but were not added to the LiteLLM registry. Testing This change can be tested locally without making live OpenAI API requests because the changes are limited to model registry metadata. For example: ``` python -c "import litellm; info = litellm.get_model_info('gpt-5.6-sol'); print(info)" ``` Before this PR: ``` python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.get_model_info('gpt-5.6-sol'))" ``` returns: ``` NotFoundError: gpt-5.6-sol not found ``` And: ``` python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.supports_tool_choice(model='gpt-5.6-sol', custom_llm_provider='openai'))" ``` returns: ``` False ``` After this PR: ``` python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.get_model_info('gpt-5.6-sol'))" ``` returns the model metadata, including values such as: ``` input_cost_per_token: 5e-06 max_input_tokens: 1050000 ``` And: ``` python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.supports_tool_choice(model='gpt-5.6-sol', custom_llm_provider='openai'))" ``` returns: ``` True ``` The registry tests also pass: ``` python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/openai/test_gpt56_registry.py -v ``` Result: ``` 8 passed ``` Type New Feature Caveats * Pricing is based on OpenAI documentation as of August 2026 and may need to be updated if OpenAI changes its pricing. * There is no live end-to-end API test because access to the GPT-5.6 models is not universally available. Pre-Submission Checklist * I have added meaningful tests. * The PR passes the relevant lint, formatting, and unit tests. * The scope is isolated to adding support for these three models. * I have received the required Greptile confidence score before requesting maintainer review. Final Attestation The tests cover model registration, pricing metadata, and `tool_choice` support for the new models. The change is limited to the model registry and is intended to prevent regressions in these behaviors.

signal.title: fix(proxy): allow internal users to view their own spend-log detail
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Non-admins get 401 clicking any row on the Logs page - A missing spend-log row silently authorized reading someone else's payload How it solves it: - Allow `/spend/logs/ui/{request_id}` for internal-user roles - Deny the ownership check when the log row is absent ## User Flow Before: an internal user can list their logs but cannot open any of them, and a missing row leaks another user's payload 1. They sign in at https://litellm-domain/ui/ with role `internal_user` or `internal_user_viewer` 2. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the table loads with their own requests 3. They click any row to open the detail drawer 4. Nothing renders: `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/ui/<request_id>?start_date=...` comes back 401 with "Only proxy admin can be used to..." 5. Another user who knows a `request_id` whose row has aged out of the database still gets that request's messages and response back from the configured log store After: the same user opens any of their own rows, and rows they do not own stay closed 1. They sign in at https://litellm-domain/ui/ with role `internal_user` or `internal_user_viewer` 2. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the table loads with their own requests 3. They click any row to open the detail drawer 4. The drawer renders: the same GET returns 200 with that request's detail 5. signal.title: fix(cost): stop double-billing cached tokens that overlap a modality
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Providers report cached and image tokens as overlapping counts - Billing treats them as separate slices of the prompt - Cached image tokens are therefore charged twice - Synthetic case in the issue bills 109e-6 instead of 39e-6 How it solves it: - Cap each modality at what the cache did not cover - Billed components sum back to prompt_tokens again - Uncached tokens keep their own modality rate ## User Flow Before: a team sending image prompts with prompt caching turned on sees spend far above what the provider invoices, so their dashboard cannot be trusted for chargeback 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with an image prompt, to a provider that reports `cached_tokens` and `image_tokens` as overlapping subsets of `prompt_tokens` 2. The provider serves most of that prompt from cache and reports it in `usage` 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see the request logged at roughly 2.8x the price the provider actually charged 4. Sending the same prompt again makes the gap worse, because a warmer cache means more overlap After: the same request is logged at the price the provider charges, so cached image prompts get cheaper instead of more expensive 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same image prompt 2. The provider serves most of it from cache and reports the same `usage` 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows the cached portion at the cache-read rate and the rest once at the ordinary rate 4. Sending it again lowers the logged spend, matching what caching is supposed to do ## Relevant issues Fixes #37281 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Reproducing the issue's synthetic case at cd7cdb3e3a, using a model with no explicit image rate so image tokens fall back to the ordinary input rate: ```python usage = Usage( prompt_tokens=100, completion_tokens=10, total_tokens=110, prompt_tokens_details=PromptTokensDetailsWrapper( text_tokens=None, cached_tokens=90, image_tokens=80, ), ) generic_cost_per_token(model=model, usage=usage, custom_llm_provider="openai") ``` Before: ``` prompt=89.0e-6 completion=20.0e-6 total=109.0e-6 ``` After: ``` prompt=19.0e-6 completion=20.0e-6 total=39.0e-6 ``` The 70 tokens counted as both cached and image were previously billed at the cache rate and again at the input rate. Now the 90 cached tokens bill at 1e-7 and the 10 uncached tokens bill once at 1e-6 ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Overlap is assumed maximal, since providers do not report it - Only applies when a cached or cache-creation count is present

signal.text: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). Every release is signed with the same key introduced in [commit `0112e53`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0). **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: ```bash cosign verify \ --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \ ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-dev.1 ``` **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: ```bash cosign verify \ --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.99.0-dev.1/cosign.pub \ ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.99.0-dev.1 ``` Expected output: ``` The following checks were performed on each of these signatures: - The cosign claims were validated - The signatures were verified
